headline: BPCL commissions integrated lube blending plant, base oil terminal in Maha
content: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) has commissioned an integrated lube oil blending plant and base oil terminal at Rasayani in Maharashtra, strengthening its manufacturing and supply-chain infrastructure as the state-run energy major seeks to expand its MAK Lubricants business.The facilities, inaugurated on November 21 by BPCL chairman and managing director Sanjay Khanna, bring together base oil receipt and storage, lubricant blending, product filling, warehousing and dispatch within a single integrated operational complex, according to a company statement.The new infrastructure is expected to improve manufacturing flexibility, inventory management and supply reliability, while allowing BPCL to respond more efficiently to changing customer requirements and market demand.The development is strategically significant for BPCL's lubricants business, where efficient sourcing, blending, packaging and distribution are important to maintaining product availability and competing across automotive and industrial lubricant markets.The Rasayani facility incorporates a range of automated manufacturing and warehouse management technologies, including recipe-based blending through a Plant Control System (PCS), piggable pipelines, automated filling and palletising, an Automated Storage and Retrieval System (ASRS), a Warehouse Management System (WMS) and automated gantry operations.These systems are designed to improve process control, product traceability and inventory visibility while reducing manual handling and enhancing workplace safety.The integration of manufacturing and logistics operations is also expected to improve the efficiency of material movement across the facility, potentially reducing operational bottlenecks and strengthening the consistency of supply to customers and distribution channels.The commissioning marks a significant step in BPCL's efforts to strengthen the manufacturing backbone of MAK Lubricants, its lubricants brand, as the company seeks to build scale and improve its competitive positioning.Addressing the inauguration, Khanna congratulated the Exploration and Production (E&P) and Lubes business teams and stressed the importance of effectively managing and leveraging the facility's advanced automation and integrated systems.BPCL Director (Finance) V.R.K. Gupta highlighted the transition from the company's earlier Wadilube operations to Rasayani, saying the new facility offered opportunities to increase business volumes and improve profitability.Director (Marketing) Subhankar Sen emphasised the need to translate the investment in smart manufacturing and warehousing into a stronger customer value proposition through better service delivery.Business Head (Lubes) S. Kannan described Rasayani as a strategic platform for the next phase of expansion."The golden era of MAK Lubricants has truly begun!" he said.Calling the facility "the launchpad for MAK's next phase of growth, excellence and leadership," Kannan urged the team to leverage the new infrastructure and convert its technological capabilities into a competitive advantage and stronger business performance.The facility's combination of automated blending, filling and warehousing systems reflects the growing importance of technology-led manufacturing in the lubricants industry.Lubricant production involves the blending of base oils with performance-enhancing additives to meet specifications for different automotive and industrial applications. Consistency in formulation, process control, storage and product handling is therefore critical to maintaining quality and operational efficiency.By integrating these activities at Rasayani, BPCL aims to strengthen control over the manufacturing and distribution process, improve traceability and enhance its ability to manage a wider range of products and customer requirements.The automated storage and retrieval infrastructure, coupled with digital warehouse management, is expected to provide better inventory visibility and streamline dispatch operations.The company, however, did not disclose the plant's production capacity, investment outlay or expected contribution to MAK Lubricants' revenue and profitability.The Rasayani project involved extensive coordination between BPCL's E&P and Lubes teams, along with the Central Procurement Organisation, Information Systems and Infrastructure teams.The commissioning adds to BPCL's existing lubricants manufacturing infrastructure and supports its broader strategy of strengthening operational capabilities across its refining, marketing and downstream businesses.BPCL, which operates refineries at Mumbai, Kochi and Bina with a combined crude processing capacity of around 35.3 million tonnes per annum, is India's second-largest oil marketing company.Its wider marketing network includes more than 25,300 fuel stations, over 6,250 LPG distributorships and around 440 lubricants distributors, providing an extensive distribution platform for its petroleum and lubricant products.

headline: Nomura raises December RBI rate hike call to 50 bps, BoB sticks to 25 bps
content: Nomura Holdings on Friday raised its forecast for the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI’s) December policy rate hike to 50 basis points (bps) from 25 bps, citing a sharper-than-expected rise in food prices. Bank of Baroda (BoB), however, expects a smaller 25 bps increase when the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) announces its decision on December 4. Nomura expects the repo rate to rise to 6 per cent, assigning a 60 per cent probability to a 50 bps hike and a 40 per cent chance of a 25 bps increase, which is also the consensus expectation. Its base case is a 50 bps hike, with a 5-1 vote split and the policy stance remaining at “calibrated tightening”. BoB also expects a rate increase but sees the MPC opting for 25 bps, citing an improvement in the geopolitical situation following the US midterm elections. The divergence stems largely from their inflation assessments. Nomura’s daily food price trackers have recorded some of the sharpest monthly increases in the past couple of years, driven by persistent price pressures in cereals and pulses. It expects consumer price index (CPI)-based inflation to rise to around 6.4 per cent in November from 6.1 per cent in October, taking the October-December quarter average to 6.3 per cent, above the RBI's forecast of 6 per cent. The brokerage expects headline inflation to remain above 6 per cent for at least two quarters, against the RBI’s earlier projection of one quarter. Core inflation momentum has also picked up as companies pass on higher input costs, it said. BoB, meanwhile, flagged October’s 6.1 per cent retail inflation, 8.5 per cent food and beverages inflation and 4.5 per cent core inflation. Lower reservoir levels, at 61.6 per cent as of November 19, and slower rabi sowing of wheat, pulses and oilseeds also pose risks to the inflation outlook. The bank expects inflation to remain in line with the RBI's projections of 6 per cent for the third quarter and 5.7 per cent for the fourth quarter. However, the share of goods and services recording inflation above 4 per cent rose sharply in October, indicating a broadening of price pressures. On growth, Nomura expects gross domestic product (GDP) data due on November 30 to show growth of more than 7.5 per cent, against the RBI’s forecast of 7.2 per cent. It expects the central bank to raise its FY27 GDP growth projection by 40 bps to around 7.5 per cent and its CPI inflation forecast by 10 bps to 5.3 per cent. Its core inflation forecast is unchanged at 4.4 per cent. BoB expects GDP growth of 7.4 per cent in the second quarter and 7.2 per cent for the full financial year, with an upward bias. Both institutions see scope for further tightening, though their projections differ. Nomura's base case is for the RBI to pause at 6 per cent after December, although another 25 bps increase in February or April remains a risk. It said the timing and communication of the December hike would be crucial: a front-loaded increase would reduce the likelihood of another hike in February, while a move framed as a catch-up could leave that possibility open. It also cautioned that basing policy decisions on headline rather than core inflation could risk overtightening. BoB expects another 25 bps hike in February and possibly one more in April, depending on inflation trends. This would take the terminal repo rate to 6.25 per cent, implying a real return of around 1 per cent, with inflation remaining above 5 per cent for the year. Liquidity is another area where both expect RBI intervention. Nomura said the central bank could lower the minimum daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) maintenance requirement to 90 per cent from 99 per cent and signal foreign exchange buy-sell swaps. BoB said liquidity remained tight, with the RBI relying on variable rate repo (VRR) auctions. Faster credit growth than deposit growth, liquidity absorption following the FCNR(B) deposit mobilisation scheme, higher CRR maintenance requirements and elevated government cash balances were weighing on the system. It expects open market operation (OMO) purchases and forex swaps, under which the RBI buys dollars from banks, to ease liquidity and check the rupee’s appreciation. The rupee has strengthened to around ₹92.50 per dollar from ₹94.87 at the beginning of November. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) invested $16.4 billion during the month, while Brent crude averaged $93.5 per barrel in the 16 days since the US elections, against $120.2 per barrel in the preceding 16 days, BoB said. The 10-year government bond yield has held in the 7.20-7.25 per cent range in recent sessions, suggesting markets have priced in a 25 bps hike. Yields had been approaching 7.50 per cent before the US midterm elections. The US 10-year Treasury yield has eased to 4.85-4.90 per cent, while the Federal Reserve is expected to raise rates at least twice more by 25 bps each, BoB said. Nomura said markets were pricing in only a 25 bps increase and would be surprised by a 50 bps hike. The brokerage has raised its conviction on its March 2027 one-year versus five-year overnight indexed swap (OIS) flattener trade to 4/5 from 3/5. The spread is currently at minus 12 bps, against a target of minus 35 bps by end-February.

headline: Drought’s bitter harvest of debt
content: Trigger warning: the following article contains references to suicide; please avoid reading if you are disturbed by the subject. Four days after her husband died by suicide, 38-year-old Neelagiri Laxmi has barely had time to grieve. With two children to raise, a debt of over ₹10 lakh hanging over the family and her own health failing, she must somehow find the strength to keep the household going. Her husband, Neelagiri Ashanna, 43, was a tenant farmer in Thalamadugu village of Adilabad district. He had borrowed the money from a private moneylender in Adilabad town at a high rate of interest to cultivate cotton on 20 acres of leased land, hoping that a good harvest would help secure his family’s future. But the rains failed, the crop withered and his hopes unravelled. On November 14, Ashanna stepped out of his house after dinner. “I thought he had gone out to relieve himself. But he never came back. About half an hour later, I started looking for him, and we found his body,” says his 19-year-old son Abhilash, a second-year undergraduate student. “There was no rain. The crop failed. He must have feared he wouldn’t be able to repay the loan,” says Laxmi, who must now manage the debt and household on her wages, despite health complications.

headline: Telangana SAFE discards 858 kg spoiled fish, prawns at Hyderabad markets
content: HYDERABAD The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) seized and discarded approximately 858 kg of spoiled fish and prawns, valued at ₹1.56 lakh, during inspections at Ram Nagar and Begum Bazaar fish markets in Hyderabad on Friday (November 27, 2026). https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/fssai-licences-suspended-of-two-karachi-bakery-units-in-hyderabad-four-meat-outlets-over-food-safety-violations/article71721101.ece Nineteen enforcement teams comprising Food Safety Officers, TG SAFE police personnel, State Food Laboratory technicians and GHMC veterinary officials inspected 19 establishments and street vendors across the two markets. List of violations detected at Hyderabad fish markets The inspections revealed several violations, including operating without FSSAI licences or registration, storing and selling fish in unhygienic conditions, using unclean water and ice, and failing to monitor the temperature of chilled fish. The officials also found fresh and old stock stored together, rotten fish, rodent infestation and poor personal hygiene among food handlers. Several establishments failed to maintain stock registers, employee health records and pest control records. Plastic crates and thermocol boxes used to store fish were also found in unclean condition. Spot tests for formalin in fish and other seafood Technicians from the State Food Laboratory conducted spot tests to detect adulterants such as formalin in fish and seafood products. Food Safety Officers and GHMC veterinary officials also examined the physical characteristics of fish and prawns, including the colour of the gills, clarity of the eyes, firmness and texture, to assess their freshness and suitability for consumption. The spoiled and deteriorated stock was seized and discarded using GHMC sanitation vehicles. The establishments inspected included JBS Fish Company, GBK Fish Company, SMS Fish Trades, Arjun Fish Mart, SVR Wholesale Fish Merchant, KLM Fish Merchants, Laxminarayana Wholesale Fish Shop, Siva Karthikeya Fish Merchants, Thirumala Fish Company, GNB Sri Srinivasa Fish Merchant, Bonson’s Fishery, SSNR Wholesale Fish Merchant, JDB Fish Merchant, CNR Enterprises, SSS Rajesh Fish Mart and Balakrishna Fish Mart in Ram Nagar. Aryan Fisheries, Chandu Fisheries, Gopal Fisheries and Jaideep Fisheries were among those inspected at Begum Bazaar. headline: Quacks in Karnataka: Health Minister U T Khader vows strict laws, action against fake doctors
content: Shivamogga: Karnataka's Health Minister U T Khader stated that the existing rules are not strong enough to tackle quacks menace. So the government would frame strong laws and take stringent action against them.Speaking to media persons here on Friday, he said many unqualified people are working as doctors in the state and many have come from northern states. "I ask them to leave Karnataka and return to their states.".'How else are we to seek justice?': ASHA workers continue indefinite protest.On ASHA workers strike, the minister said he has already written a letter to Union Health Minister JP Nadda asking him to give incentives of Rs 1,500 to ASHA workers' as announced earlier. I have even attached a copy of resolution passed in parliament."He reiterated that private hospitals must display charts of treatment fees on their notice boards without fail. Information would be gathered from hospitals that have already published their treatment price charts, and these lists would be examined. Based on this, steps will be taken to ensure that all other hospitals also display their price charts.He noted that a shortage of medicines has occurred in government hospitals due to delays in the tender process for the procurement of certain drugs. This delay is attributed to the time required for the manufacturing, supply, and quality verification of the medicines. Instructions have been issued to procure and provide essential medicines under the 'Ayushman Bharat-Aarogya Karnataka' scheme to ensure that patients do not face hardships. He added that the department will conduct reviews to prevent any such shortages in the future.When questioned on dearth of medicine for snake bite cases, he stated that a minimum of 10 vials must be available at primary health centres (PHCs), 30 vials taluk hospitals, and an adequate quantity at district-level medical stores. In the event of a shortage, arrangements must be made to ensure immediate supply from the medical stores. He stated that this is the first time the issue of a medicine shortage for snake bites in Shivamogga has come to his attention, and that it will be investigated.On separate district general hospital, he said McGann hospital has been handed over medical education department. So, the government is considering establushing separate district general hospital. "We are yet to decide whether it should be constructed in Shivamogga or in any other town in the district that would prove beneficial for people of the entire district." He clarified that Ayurvedic practitioners must prescribe only those medicines permitted under the regulations. They are not permitted to exceed their legal scope of practice by administering injections or employing other treatment methods outside their authorized domain.

headline: Mirwaiz says he was put under house arrest over Vande Mataram issue, decries action against Maulana Qasimi
content: Srinagar Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq on Friday (November 27, 2026) said he was placed under house arrest and another prominent cleric, Maulana Rehmatullah Qasimi, was summoned to a police station over their opposition to the playing of Vande Mataram at a J&K Waqf Board function in Srinagar. “I had anticipated that I would be punished this Friday by being put under house arrest. I also raised concerns over the recitation of Vande Mataram at the religious function of the J&K Waqf Board, as well as people’s grave concerns over the disaster-in-waiting in the ecologically fragile region of Sheshnag after the viral visuals,” the Mirwaiz said in a statement. The Mirwaiz alleged he was “prevented from proceeding to Jama Masjid, Srinagar, to deliver the Friday sermon and offer congregational prayers.” J&K clerics apologise, offer ‘repentance prayers’ for standing during Vande Mataram at Waqf Board function J&K clerics apologise, offer ‘repentance prayers’ for standing during Vande Mataram at Waqf Board function After Vande Mataram was played at the first Waqf Day function, clerics say they recited the ‘kalima’ in repentance; Muttahida Majlis-e-Ulama may seek legal opinion J&K clerics apologise, offer ‘repentance prayers’ for standing during Vande Mataram at Waqf Board function storyline 1 “It has become a precedent that every time I raise people’s issues and concerns, I am not allowed to go to Jama Masjid on that Friday,” the Mirwaiz said. The chief cleric also expressed “deep regret” over the summoning of Mr. Qasimi, head of Kashmir’s largest seminary, Darul Uloom Raheemiyyah, in Bandipora. Mr. Qasimi also spoke about the playing of Vande Mataram during the J&K Waqf Board Day on November 23 in Srinagar, which was attended by local imams and religious scholars. MMU objects to ‘Vande Mataram’ singing competition in J&K MMU objects to ‘Vande Mataram’ singing competition in J&K The religious body Muttahida Majlis-e-Ulema cites faith concerns; seeks sensitivity in official outreach on the issue MMU objects to ‘Vande Mataram’ singing competition in J&K storyline 1 “Yesterday (Thursday), Kashmir’s renowned Islamic scholar and patron of the Mutahida Majlis-e-Ulama, Maulana Rehmatullah Qasimi Sahib, was summoned to the police station and reprimanded. Can we no longer raise our voices to safeguard our religious beliefs and sentiments? Do we not even have the right to express our religious concerns?” the Mirwaiz said. He added that those in power must understand that “we will not tolerate any coercion in matters of faith, particularly when it comes to our fundamental belief in Tawheed.” “It would serve the ruling regime much better if, instead of applying pressure on me, it understands the sensitivity and impact these issues have on the people of J&K. It should desist from imposing things that cause people hurt and concern,” the Mirwaiz said. Such actions should not be defended under any circumstances.” Earlier, a number of Muslim clerics tendered apologies and offered special repentance prayers for attending the Waqf function where Vande Mataram was played.

headline: Delimitation row: Centre approves bill for 50% more Lok Sabha seats for every state, freeze on representation till 2051
content: The Union Cabinet on Friday has cleared a new women's reservation bill linked to delimitation which proposes a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats in all states.This bill is likely to be brought before the special sitting of the Parliament which is set to begin next week.The Union Cabinet gave its nod to the new bill with amendments in order to ensure no state loses its share of representation in the Lok Sabha in proportion to others after the delimitation exercise is carried out, PTI reported citing sources.The bill also proposes a freeze on the number of seats till 2051, with the sources telling PTI that the uniform 51 per cent increase has been mandated in order to address the concerns southern states have expressed earlier.The new bill is reportedly using the 2011 Census in order to redraw the increased seats. If this proposed amendment passes, India will see an increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats from 543 to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. The government's opinion is that this move will allow for the implementation of the 33 per cent quota for women in the Parliament as well as state assemblies ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. The government has called for a four-day special sitting -- November 30 and December 1 in Lok Sabha, and December 2 and 3 in Rajya Sabha. "When the government calls a session or a special session, that means there are very important bills or business for the nation," Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said, as per PTI. How Opposition parties are reacting The opposition INDIA bloc is against the legislation and will be meeting on Saturday to discuss its strategy. Non-INDIA bloc parties like the DMK, AAP, and the BJD have also been invited for the meeting, PTI reported citing sources. Speaking with reporters, Congress general secretary in-charge organisation K C Venugopal said, "PM (Narendra) Modi and (Home Minister) Amit Shah want to set a big trap against the people of India. That is the design of this entire episode."Notably, Supriya Sule of the NCP(SP) has said that she will not be attending the meeting since her father, party patriarch Sharad Pawar, is unwell. This comes amid buzz that the NCP(SP) might decide to side with the BJP on the delimitation issue. MK Stalin has warned that under no circumstances should the 7.18 per cent seat share of Tamil Nadu in the Lok Sabha should be reduced. "No change in position, no compromise, the DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu's interests; nor will it depart from its principles," Stalin said in a statement. Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) Rajya Sabha MP Mahua Majhi questioned how the government could proceed with the bill without any update data, accusing the ruling party of renewed attempts of political poaching. "If they don’t even have the necessary data, how can they carry out a delimitation exercise? This suggests that the politics of poaching has begun once again. We have several apprehensions regarding this: a session was called for just a single day,” Majhi told ANI. Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut slammed the proposed bill on Friday, calling it “anti-national and anti-democratic” “Realising they are set to lose in 2029, they have devised a new ploy: they intend to bring in 860 MPs and carry out a delimitation exercise. This bill is anti-national and anti-democratic; it must be opposed. Those who vote in favour of this bill will be traitors to the nation. Their names will be recorded in history as traitors,” Raut was quoted as saying by ANI.

headline: 'Who is lying': Akhilesh questions U.P. CM, CEO over conflicting missing voter figures
content: Lucknow Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Friday (November 27, 2026) questioned the conflicting figures cited by Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and the state's Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa over missing voters, wondering who was telling the truth. Akhilesh, the Ambedkarite storyline 1 https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/other-states/who-is-yogi-adityanath/article61804668.ece The former Chief Minister also alleged that attempts were being made to manipulate electoral rolls ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. SP, Congress seat-sharing talks turn bumpy in U.P., as Akhilesh declares candidates for five seats SP, Congress seat-sharing talks turn bumpy in U.P., as Akhilesh declares candidates for five seats Congress leaders slammed the decision to make a unilateral announcement while talks are still underway; reject SP’s initial 26-seat proposal; SP leaders say Congress must set aside ego, understand realities SP, Congress seat-sharing talks turn bumpy in U.P., as Akhilesh declares candidates for five seats storyline 1 Addressing a press conference in Lucknow, Mr. Yadav referred to Mr. Adityanath's claim in a media interview that 1.27 crore Hindu voters were missing from the electoral rolls and a subsequent statement by Rinwa in a separate interview that around 2.5 crore voters' names were missing in Uttar Pradesh. "One figure is being given by the Chief Minister, who says 1.27 crore Hindu voters are missing, while the chief electoral officer says 2.5 crore voters are missing. So who is lying," he asked. Mr. Yadav pointed out that the Election Commission had stated on November 17 that it did not release voter data on the basis of religion or caste. "The Election Commission says it does not provide figures based on religion or caste. Then how did the Chief Minister arrive at the figure of 1.27 crore Hindu voters," he further asked. In his interview, CEO Rinwa had clarified that his use of the word "missing" did not necessarily mean that these names had earlier existed on the electoral rolls and were subsequently deleted, but referred to people who could be eligible voters but whose names were absent. 13.58 crore voters in U.P. draft electoral roll; 18 lakh added since SIR 13.58 crore voters in U.P. draft electoral roll; 18 lakh added since SIR Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa says Election Commission does not keep religion-wise data on voters; Akhilesh questions CM Yogi’s recent claim that 1.27 crore Hindu voters were removed 13.58 crore voters in U.P. draft electoral roll; 18 lakh added since SIR storyline 1 Mr. Yadav alleged that the BJP, in collusion with the ECI, was preparing to add crores of bogus voters to the final electoral rolls while creating a narrative about missing voters to pre-empt questions over a sudden increase. "The BJP is creating an atmosphere by spreading the narrative that crores of voters are missing, so that nobody questions how crores of voters suddenly get added to the final electoral list," he alleged. He also questioned an alleged 22-fold increase in Form 6 applications for voter registration, asking, "Has the manpower increased, or has the power of the system increased? Has some machine started working faster?" Presenting what he described as an analysis of the November 17 draft electoral rolls, Mr. Yadav alleged that 2.84 lakh fake and duplicate voters had been added, mostly in urban constituencies where names had been deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). He further claimed that 55,584 names of alleged fake voters deleted during the SIR had been restored, and another 52,000 entries had been added where voter identity cards carried only titles such as 'Shri' and 'Shrimati' instead of names. The SP chief said his party submitted complaints to the ECI but has received no information on how many duplicate entries have been removed. "If our complaints are not heard, we will be forced to launch an agitation," he said. Mr. Yadav demanded that voter identity cards be linked to Aadhaar and that biometric verification be introduced to prevent bogus voting. He also sought metal voter ID cards, alleging that fake cards could otherwise be manufactured on polling day. He further demanded that at least 50% of administrative and police officers deployed for election duty belong to the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) communities. Independent SIR Commission asks CM Adityanath for proof of his statement that 1.27 crore Hindus excluded Independent SIR Commission asks CM Adityanath for proof of his statement that 1.27 crore Hindus excluded In its letter to the Chief Minister, the Commission said his statement was directly relevant to its mandate of examining whether eligible electors were unfairly removed from the rolls during the SIR exercise Independent SIR Commission asks CM Adityanath for proof of his statement that 1.27 crore Hindus excluded storyline 1 The press conference was held after several prominent people from different parts of Uttar Pradesh, including Noida, joined the Samajwadi Party. Mr. Yadav also said his party would address the distinct urban challenges of Noida, Ghaziabad and other rapidly urbanising areas of western Uttar Pradesh, promising a district-wise development roadmap. "Urban issues are different. Air pollution may not be an issue in rural areas, and traffic congestion may not affect people in villages, but these are major concerns in cities," he said, citing pollution, traffic and infrastructure challenges. Mr. Yadav also promised improved government school infrastructure, trained teachers and better facilities, saying government schools would be developed to match or surpass private institutions. "The BJP has an enmity with education," he alleged, accusing the government of neglecting infrastructure created during the SP regime.

headline: West Bengal consumer commission directs momo outlet to pay  ₹50,000 for charging  ₹10 extra for packaging
content: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, West Bengal, held a Kolkata food outlet liable for deficiency in service and unfair trade practices for charging Rs. 10 extra for packaging, according to a report by The Indian Express. The bench comprising President Manoj Kumar Rai and member Gopal Chandra Roy observed and directed the food outlet to pay Rs. 50,000. “OP no. 1 has failed to prove that the complainant requested him to provide packaging and agreed to provide cost for the same. So, deficiency in service on the part of OP no 1 is proved,” the order read. The customer had bought two plates of chicken momos, each priced at Rs. 109, from the outlet on October 29, 2024. The customer was charged an additional Rs. 10 on the bill, leading to an altercation between the two. The customer demanded that the extra amount be refunded; however, the outlet outright refused. Triggered by the incident, the consumer moved the consumer court, seeking a refund and compensation.The food outlet rejected the allegations, claiming that the customer had requested extra packaging to ensure the food remained safe and hygienic and did not spill while he travelled on a motorcycle. It further maintained that the packaging fee had been disclosed to the customer before the order was placed and that he had agreed to pay it.However, the commission found that the outlet had not submitted any evidence showing that the customer had asked for the momos to be packed separately.Why did the consumer court hold the Kolkata food outlet liable?Referring to Section 36(5) of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, the commission said that the seller is responsible for bearing the expenses involved in making goods ready for delivery, unless there is a different agreement between the parties.“Section 36 (5) of the Sale of Goods’ Act, 1930 provides that unless otherwise agreed, the expenses of and incidental to putting the goods into a deliverable state shall be borne by the seller. Therefore, in view of the aforesaid provision, it is duty of the OP No. 1 as seller, to provide packaging of the goods sold by them for taking it away and the OP No. 1 shall have to bear the cost of such packaging,” the order read, according to The Indian Express report.The commission also pointed out that the food outlet had failed to establish that the customer had been informed about the additional ₹10 packaging fee before placing the order.What compensation did the consumer court order the food outlet to pay?Concluding that the outlet was guilty of deficiency in service, the commission directed it to return the ₹10 packaging charge to the customer. It also ordered the company to pay ₹100 as compensation and ₹2,000 towards litigation expenses.In addition, the food outlet has been directed to deposit ₹50,000 into the Consumer Legal Aid Account of the Commission.

headline: For the second time this year, Guindy Children’s Park closed as birds die of suspected flu
content: CHENNAI Guindy Children’s Park in Chennai will remain closed to the public until November 30 following the death of birds at the facility on Friday (November 27, 2026). The cause of the deaths is yet to be established, a press release issued by the Forest Department said on Friday. Samples have been sent to the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal, for testing. The results are awaited. The closure is a precautionary measure, officials said. The park will be closed from November 28 to 30, or until further orders. The Forest Department said preventive measures were being implemented in accordance with the Union government’s guidelines. #Guindy Children’s Park in #Chennai will remain closed to visitors for three days from November 28 to November 30, 2026 (or until further orders) as a precaution following bird deaths in its waterbirds enclosure. Photo: B. Velankanni Raj (@VelankanniRaj6) https://t.co/vFgcT6EtQp— The Hindu - Chennai (@THChennai) November 27, 2026 These include isolating the affected enclosure, disinfecting and sanitising the premises, and intensifying biosecurity measures. The health of other birds and animals in the park is also being closely monitored. Avian influenza concerns The latest incident comes amid avian influenza concerns at zoological facilities in Tamil Nadu. Wetland bird enclosures at Arignar Anna Zoological Park in Vandalur were also temporarily closed to visitors after the virus was detected among birds. They reopened on November 18 after two rounds of samples, collected 15 days apart from the affected bird group, tested negative for avian influenza at NIHSAD, Bhopal. This is the second time this year that Guindy Children’s Park has been closed following bird deaths suspected to be linked to avian influenza. In March, nearly 40 birds died at the Vedanthangal Aviary inside the park. Samples sent to NIHSAD confirmed the presence of the H5N1 virus, prompting the closure of the park from March 20. headline: ‘Willfully disobeyed order’: Supreme Court pulls up Tamil Nadu govt amid Karthigai Deepam row
content: The Supreme Court on Friday held that the Tamil Nadu government and Madurai district administration had prima facie “wilfully and flagrantly disobeyed” its November 20 order directing the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram hill, and described the Madurai District Collector's preliminary status report as one that was “shedding crocodile tears.”The Court directed that the lamp be lit at the Deepathoon on Saturday, November 28, four days after the Karthigai Deepam festival was celebrated on November 24. It permitted “all devotees” to light the lamp at the designated spot, at least 50 metres away from the dargah, and directed the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to take necessary steps to protect the dargah.A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and VM Pancholi Tissued show-cause notices of contempt against the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, HR&CE Commissioner, Board of Trustees, Chairperson and the Trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thiruparankundram, and the Madurai collector Nishant Krishna, asking why contempt proceedings should not be initiated against them. Also Read | ‘Complete failure’: SC suspends temple trustees amid Deepathoon row, appoints retired judgesCourt suspends board of trustees of templeThe Court also suspended the Board of Trustees of the Temple, appointed two former Madras High Court judges as receivers to administer the temple, and directed the CRPF to take over security of the temple premises.The Apex Court appointed former Madras High Court judges Justices S Vaidyanathan and V Parthiban as receivers to take immediate charge of the temple administration from the suspended Board of Trustees.It further directed the receivers to ensure that the lamp is lit at the Deepathoon “using the flame from the lamp at the Uchipillaiyar temple.”“The first thing which comes to our mind is to express the word alas! As it would be relevant and appropriate to express in the present scenario. We say so for reasons assigned hereinafter and we say so with pain and anguish. The time has come to deal with the situation with an iron hand,” the Court said, adding that one must remember that its orders were not something that can be negotiated upon by anyone.The bench also noted that the Madurai district collector had personally undertaken before the Madras High Court to implement the Apex Court’s November 20 order of lighting the lamp on the Deepathoon. However, he failed to do so and blamed the temple authorities for such failure. Such conduct, the Court said, could lead to “constitutional chaos.”“District Collector has filed a preliminary report that the order couldn't be complied with. He has tendered a formal apology that he took all steps and has attempted to shift the blame entirely to the temple administration. We are surprised that the collector could take a stand. His powers are wide, and hands are long to implement the order,” the Court said.Also Read | SC orders lighting of lamp atop disputed ‘Deepathoon’ tomorrow, issues contempt notice to top Tamil Nadu officials‘Order of Court is not invitation to negotiation,’ says benchThe Court made the scathing observations while hearing contempt petitions alleging non-compliance with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order directing that the lamp be lit at the Deepathoon.“An order of this Court is not an invitation to negotiation until the Court itself modifies it,” the bench said.It further warned that any attempt to undermine the constitutional mandate or interfere with the administration of justice would be dealt with firmly.The Supreme Court also said that the extraordinary intervention could have been avoided had the authorities “demonstrated bona fide compliance and purged the contempt.”It said that after hearing all parties, it had found that the temple's Board of Trustees had purportedly overreached the Supreme Court's directions by passing a resolution to light the lamp at the Uchipillaiyar temple, where it had traditionally been lit, instead of at the Deepathoon.SC observed that the trustees had effectively taken a stand that they would not implement its November 20 order.The Court also directed the TN Chief Secretary to furnish details of “all communications, messages and call records to ascertain whether executive authorities had acted at the behest of political superiors.” It directed the Chief Secretary to file a personal affidavit confirming that notices had been served on all the concerned persons.All the persons issued notices must file their affidavits within 10 days of service and appear personally before the Court on the next hearing date, December 15.What happened in courtDuring the hearing, the State sought permission for the Chief Secretary and other officials to appear virtually at the next hearing. The bench, however, directed them to appear in person first, indicating that it would consider requests for exemption from personal appearance subsequently.During the hearing, Senior Advocate Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), submitted that its officials had been prevented by the police from proceeding beyond the dargah to reach the Deepathoon and ascertain the location for lighting the lamp.He argued that the police administration had effectively prevented compliance with the Supreme Court's directions and urged the Court to entrust the exercise to an independent agency.Senior Advocate Sai Deepak, appearing for one of the devotees, submitted that the November 20 order was an unequivocal direction and did not leave room for the temple administration or the State authorities to exercise discretion over whether the lamp should be lit at the Deepathoon.He argued that the appointment of the Board of Trustees shortly before the Supreme Court's order and its subsequent resolution to light the lamp at Uchipillaiyar indicated a premeditated attempt to frustrate the Court's directions.Senior Advocate Guru Krishna Kumar, also appearing for the devotees, contended that the Collector had failed to discharge the responsibility entrusted to him and had deliberately avoided consulting the Board of Trustees until it became an obstacle to implementing the order.Opposing the allegations, Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the Collector, submitted that several coordination meetings had been held with the relevant authorities and that the Collector had taken all necessary steps to implement the Supreme Court's directions. He maintained that the Collector could not independently direct the lighting of the lamp without the necessary authorisation from the temple administration.Senior Advocate Siddharth Luthra, appearing for the Madurai Commissioner of Police, said that nearly 5,800 police personnel had been deployed to maintain law and order and facilitate the exercise.Senior Advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for the temple's Executive Officer, argued that the Executive Officer could not override a religious decision taken by the Board of Trustees.Also Read | Karthigai Deepam row: SC issues contempt notice to Tamil Nadu chief secretary, DGP and collectorAnd Senior Advocate Manu Abhishek Singhvi, appearing for the HR&CE Commissioner, submitted that the Supreme Court's November 20 order had been carefully calibrated and had left some leeway to the temple trustees.Rejecting that interpretation, the Apex Court clarified that it had not granted any such leeway.The bench also referred to Article 144 of the Constitution, which mandates that all civil and judicial authorities in India shall act in aid of the Supreme Court, and said that “any attempt to undermine that constitutional mandate would not be tolerated.”SC will hear the matter next on December 15 this year.

headline: CSIR-CCMB’s LaCONES G. Umapathy elected as Fellow of National Academy of Agricultural Sciences
content: HYDERABAD G. Umapathy, from CSIR–Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CSIR–CCMB)-Laboratory for the Conservation of Endangered Species (LaCONES), has been elected as Fellow of the National Academy of Agricultural Sciences (NAAS), New Delhi. The fellowship recognises his work in wildlife conservation biology. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/csir-ccmbs-govindswamy-umapathy-elected-as-fellow-of-national-academy-of-sciences-2025/article70120930.ece The scientist uses reproductive physiology, genetics, genomics and eDNA tools to help conserve endangered species such as the mouse deer, pygmy hog and lion-tailed macaque. headline: Telangana’s new pattadar passbooks to have unique code,  land maps
content: HYDERABAD The Telangana Government has embarked upon a first-of-its kind exercise in the country to issue pattadar passbooks to farmers with embedded maps of the respective lands. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/pattadar-passbooks-only-solution-to-land-problems-govt/article71405058.ece The new pattadar passbooks, the design of which is in final stages of preparation, will include the map of the land owned by the respective farmers along with its coordinates, enabling its exact location. It will contain a unique code on the lines of the QR code which can be scanned to know the information pertaining to that particular land. “Latest information of the land will be there in the passbook. It is likely to be used for multiple purposes as departments like Agriculture will use the coordinates,” a senior Revenue official told The Hindu. The development assumes significance as the State Government has taken up resurvey of the 10,900 revenue villages in a phased manner with 2,500 villages selected in the first phase. The Revenue department had completed survey exercise pertaining to 2.35 crore land holdings so far in the pilot villages. The process to issue passbooks is likely to start soon in over 530 villages where survey work has been completed and time has been given for claims and objections in anticipation that a section of farmers could raise objections over the extent of land they own once the survey process is completed. The passbooks to be issued after the land survey, considered as complementary to the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) of the Central Government, are likely to help farmers in streamlining several functions. It will help create a comprehensive digital registry which is likely to be entrusted to a nodal agency to affectively utilise the survey outcomes for delivery of schemes. Accordingly, the digital registry will help in targeted reach of fertilisers, urea and seed as the nature and use of land will be recorded. It will also help in effective implementation of payment of minimum support price and settle crop insurance claims as and when needed. (eom)

headline: Himachal BJP demands re-exam after Sikh candidate barred entry over ‘kara’, ‘kirpan’
content: Himachal BJP on Friday demanded a re-examination for the patwari post exclusively for an Amritdhari Sikh candidate who was allegedly barred from appearing in the exam over 'kara' and 'kirpan'.Addressing the media in Poanta Sahib in Sirmaur district, state BJP Minority Morcha chief Gurmeet Singh sought an explanation from the Congress government over the incident at the 'Devbhoomi Online Examination Centre' in Solan.He demanded that the state government conduct an inquiry, hold a special patwari (revenue official) examination for the affected candidate, and make necessary amendments to the examination guidelines so that no candidate is deprived of taking an exam due to their religious beliefs.Also read: BJP’s Samrasta Sankalp Yatra to enter Himachal todayHe stated that this matter concerns not only the future of a student but also his religious freedom and constitutional rights. Gurmeet Singh said that he spoke to the candidate, who said he had been asked to remove his kara (iron/steel bangle) and kirpan (ceremonial sword).Gurmeet Singh said the Sikh youth told him that the examination centre operator cited "government instructions" for disallowing those articles. However, when asked for the relevant notification, the authorities failed to provide a copy, the party's minority chief added.Also read: Haryana allows Sikh candidates to wear kirpan, married women mangalsutra in examsThe candidate's father, Sardar Vichitra Singh, who was also present at the press conference, demanded that the government clarify the specific order under which the candidate was barred from the examination.Gurmeet Singh said that a father invests his hard-earned money in his child's education, dreaming of a bright future for him, but being barred from the examination has come as a severe blow to the family.Referring to Article 25 of the Constitution, which guarantees the right to religious freedom, Gurmeet Singh pointed out that carrying a kirpan is an integral part of the Sikh faith. He emphasised that while establishing security protocols for examinations, constitutional rights and religious beliefs must be respected.Also read: Rajasthan allows Sikh candidates to wear religious symbols in competitive examsGurmeet Singh also raised concerns regarding alleged restrictions on mangalsutras (sacred necklaces) and bangles worn by women, as per the examination guidelines. He urged the government to review such directives that interfere with religious and cultural practices.The patwari recruitment examinations began on November 23 and are scheduled to conclude on November 30.

headline: Srikakulam farmers own the land but not the manganese Vedanta wants beneath it
content: SRIKAKULAM (A.P.) It was early October, and farmers across Punnam and Bathuva villages, gram panchayats of G. Sigadam mandal in Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh, were busy preparing their fields for the next crop. In the red sandy loam soil, they worked alongside the pairs of oxen they had raised and cared for over the years. For many families, these fields had been passed down through generations. Women followed the oxen as they ploughed the land, bending over to sow maize seeds. Though it was Gandhi Jayanti, a government holiday, they were determined to finish sowing on time. Around noon, things changed with the arrival of a team of experts from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Bhubaneswar, at Punnam with survey equipment. They soon began work in the fields where farmers were already sowing maize, leaving the villagers puzzled and alarmed. The team carried a No Objection Certificate (NOC) issued by the G. Sigadam Tahsildar, permitting it to conduct a Differential Global Positioning System (DGPS) survey and install boundary pillars on 30 acres of government land. IIT-Bhubaneswar had been engaged by Vedanta Limited to carry out the survey. Vedanta had commissioned the survey to identify the geographical coordinates of the Punnam Manganese Block (PMB) and mark its boundaries ahead of the proposed mining operations. In September 2025, the Andhra Pradesh Department of Mines and Geology conducted an e-auction for the block, following which the State Industries and Commerce Department issued a Letter of Intent (LoI), declaring Vedanta Limited the preferred bidder.

headline: ‘Panthic’ politics: SAD-BJP renewed alliance could reignite Akali Dal’s core base ahead of 2027 Punjab polls
content: CHANDIGARH Even as ‘Panthic’ politics, a political mobilisation surrounding the Sikh community’s collective identity, continues to be the cornerstone in Punjab’s electoral space, the restitching of an alliance between the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), could work in favour of the century-old SAD, which has been struggling to stage a political comeback in the State. If the Akali Dal’s “core support base” sees a genuine prospect of returning to power in 2027, through this alliance with the BJP, that itself could become a rallying point drawing voters back to the SAD led by Sukhbir Singh Badal, who has served as Deputy Chief Minister in two separate stints.

headline: Voter data at risk? Election Commission website flaw—now fixed—left personal details and IDs exposed, probe finds
content: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has fixed a security vulnerability in its website that exposed sensitive personal information and identity documents of registered voters. The flaw was discovered by Reuters during a month-long investigation and reported to the poll body on October 26, 2026. The weakness meant that information such as voters' names, phone numbers, email addresses, date of birth, residential addresses and file paths to uploaded voter identification documents could be accessed via the developer tool of a browser.The security gap was fixed on Thursday, November 26, after Reuters repeatedly sought a response from the Election Commission. This development comes one month before assembly polls in pivotal states such as Uttar Pradesh, and at a time when the ECI is facing intense questioning on its voter list verification drive. The vulnerability could've been used to harvest voters' personal data in large numbers, security researchers said.How the ECI website flaw exposed voter informationThe flaw was connected to the website's call-booking system, which was unveiled in June 2025, according to Reuters. Voters logged in to their accounts and asked for a call from their electorate officer; the browser network tab on the website showed a reference number from their voter registration or information update form.Using these reference numbers to book calls, Reuters found that the website exposed additional personal details that were not displayed on the main webpage. These comprised personal details, home addresses and file paths to voter-registered ID documents.The security flaw has been verified by Indian security researchers Karan Saini and Ehraz Ahmed, who studied the report. They said the reference numbers were in a predictable sequence that could enable an attack to guess the numbers and automate the process of gathering sensitive information.Researchers warn of possible bulk data theftThe researchers said cybercriminals could have used publicly available web tools and basic coding knowledge to download identity documents, including passports and national identity cards.Reuters said that one of its reporters was able to follow the steps to download a copy of his national identity document. It seems the server was trying to check if someone was logged in but failed to verify whether they were allowed to access a certain document, Saini said.However, Reuters said it could not establish whether anyone had exploited the vulnerability, how long it had existed or how many voters may have been affected.ECI fixes vulnerability after Reuters raises concernsReuters first contacted the Election Commission and its three commissioners on October 26, seeking comments on the findings. The institution did not respond to repeated requests.On Thursday, November 26, an ECI spokesperson told Reuters that the commission's IT division had been asked to examine the issue. Hours later, a review by Reuters and the researchers confirmed that the vulnerability had been addressed. The same approach was no longer available to access sensitive information or document file paths.Congress spokesman Pawan Khera said the revelations were "deeply alarming" and warned that such exposure could allow for voter information to be targeted for intimidation, profiling and voter suppression.Former election commissioner Ashok Lavasa told Reuters that the exposure was accidental. The ECI's website privacy statement also notes that no system is 100% secure.The incident follows a similar security concern reported in 2019, when researcher Karan Saini found that the commission's online voter search portal was exposing personal information through the browser's network tab.

headline: CPI(M) leader P. Rajeeve urges police to register case against Keralam CM over remarks at Youth Congress event
content: KOCHI Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] leader P. Rajeeve has urged the police to register a case against Keralam Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan on the charge of inciting violence in connection with his alleged remarks made at the conclusion of the Gen India campaign of the Youth Congress in Kannur on November 20. He urged the Governor to examine the speech, alleging that the Chief Minister has violated the oath of office and rule of law by making “a provocative speech” at the event. Mr. Rajeeve accused Mr. Satheesan of making threatening remarks while referring to the alleged attacks and police atrocities against Youth Congress workers and student activists during the previous Left front government regime during his speech. Mr. Rajeeve questioned the legality of the formation of the Special Investigation Teams (SITs) after the United Democratic Front government came to power. He alleged that the SITs were formed as part of the government’s “vengeance against its rivals”, going by the remarks made by the Chief Minister himself during his speech in Kannur. The Home Minister should explain whether the SITs have been formed to protect the political interests of the government, he said. Mr. Rajeeve rejected the remarks by Chief Minister that the government was unable to fulfil the demand of the striking Lower Primary School Teacher rank holders to reduce the prescribed pupil-teacher ratio as the average ratio in government lower primary schools is already 1:19 and lowering it further was impractical. He said that the ratio was fixed as per the head count in each class and not by estimating the total number of pupil-teacher ration district-wise.
