headline: From 9 percentile in CAT section to IIM Kozhikode: Kolkata man shares how father's sacrifice changed his life
content: A 26-year-old man from Kolkata, who once scored just 9 percentile in a section of the Common Admission Test (CAT), has shared how he overcame repeated failures and financial struggles to secure admission to the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Kozhikode. His journey was far from easy, with his father struggling to keep the family's grocery business running and giving him ₹20,000 for one final attempt at the entrance examination.(Also read: ₹5 crore net worth">25-year-old IIM Bangalore student says ‘money is fuel’ after building ₹5 crore net worth)Speaking to Hindustan Times, Hemant Tulsan, who graduated from IIM Kozhikode in 2025, recalled the challenges he faced while pursuing his MBA dream, including losing money to an online scam, spending major festivals alone while preparing for CAT and receiving unexpected financial assistance from entrepreneur Ankur Warikoo.Tulsan, who now lives in Bengaluru, scored approximately 44 percentile in his first CAT attempt in 2020. Although his overall score improved to 85.5 percentile the following year, he managed just 9 percentile in the Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning (DILR) section. However, his third attempt in 2022 changed everything. He scored 97.84 percentile overall, including 98.8 percentile in DILR, eventually making it to IIM Kozhikode.Growing up in a family facing financial difficultiesTulsan grew up in a Marwari joint family in Kolkata. His father ran a grocery shop, while his mother was a homemaker. He began helping at the family business when he was in Class 8.According to Tulsan, the family was financially comfortable during his early childhood, but things began to change after his father suffered a slipped disc. The grocery business subsequently faced losses, and by 2015-16, the family was struggling financially.Despite his medical condition, his father continued working to support the family. Tulsan said his father would leave home at 8 am and return around 10 pm.He completed his schooling at Shri Jain Vidyalaya and later pursued a BCom degree at St Xavier's College, Kolkata.Describing himself as an average student, Tulsan recalled failing examinations during his school years and struggling academically in college. His interest in pursuing an MBA developed after attending a workshop during graduation, where he learnt about the career opportunities and professional growth offered by management education.Two CAT attempts and a difficult decisionTulsan first appeared for CAT in 2020. He had enrolled at a coaching institute, paying approximately ₹60,000 to ₹70,000, but the Covid-19 pandemic forced classes online.He admitted that he relied heavily on coaching and lacked a preparation strategy of his own. His first attempt ended with a score of around 44 percentile.In 2021, he improved considerably, scoring 85.5 percentile overall. However, his DILR performance dropped to just 9 percentile after he selected two difficult sets during the examination.Although he also appeared for other management entrance examinations, securing admission to his preferred institution remained difficult.After his second unsuccessful CAT attempt and rejections from several colleges, people around him suggested that he should consider joining a private institution or finding a job.One of his mentors, however, offered him a different perspective: "Either go for a job or go all in."Tulsan decided to attempt CAT one final time, despite knowing that his family could barely afford another year of preparation.Father's ₹20,000 and an unexpected setbackOne of the biggest challenges was arranging money for college application forms. Tulsan estimated that he needed approximately ₹50,000 to apply to all the institutions he was targeting.When he approached his father, he received ₹20,000, the maximum amount his father could arrange at the time. According to Tulsan, his father gave him the money without informing anyone else in the family.However, before leaving for Dhanbad to prepare for CAT, he handed the money to his younger brother for safekeeping. His brother subsequently lost it in an online scam.Another relative offered financial help, but that money was eventually used during a family emergency.Left with limited options, Tulsan began asking teachers, acquaintances and even strangers to pay their own application fees using his credit card, allowing him to collect cashback.Over two months, he managed to save approximately ₹3,000 through this arrangement, which he used to apply to MDI.Preparing alone in DhanbadDetermined not to repeat his previous mistakes, Tulsan moved to Dhanbad and dedicated himself entirely to CAT preparation.He spent Durga Puja and Diwali alone, following a strict daily schedule that included reading articles, practising questions from all three CAT sections and taking mock tests.He also created a colour-coded accountability sheet to track his progress and identify areas requiring improvement.His biggest focus was DILR, the section that had affected his performance in previous attempts. Instead of attempting the most difficult questions, he developed a strategy to identify sets he could solve accurately.The approach worked.In CAT 2022, Tulsan scored 97.84 percentile overall and 98.8 percentile in DILR.Recalling the day he checked his response sheet, Tulsan said he was sitting beside his father. He had been particularly worried about his performance in quantitative aptitude.When he realised he had performed well, he began crying and hugged his father. Although his father did not fully understand the significance of the score, he became emotional seeing his son's reaction.Tulsan also shared his CAT result in a LinkedIn post. A memorable IIM Kozhikode interviewDespite his improved score, Tulsan continued to face challenges during the admission process.He eventually received offers from IIM Shillong and other management institutes, but his interview at IIM Kozhikode remained particularly memorable.Scheduled for March 3 at a hotel in Kolkata, it was his first offline admission interview. Running late, he arrived on a motorcycle with his hair dishevelled.The interview began with a question: "What is the difference between correlation and regression?"Tulsan admitted that he did not know the answer.The interviewers later noticed his hair and jokingly asked whether it was a new trend. When he mentioned using anti-dandruff shampoo, the conversation unexpectedly turned to the causes of dandruff.His response, "sir, mummy told me", left both professors laughing.The discussion subsequently moved to economics, government finances and current affairs. Despite struggling with some questions, Tulsan said he maintained his composure and continued interacting naturally with the panel.He eventually secured admission to IIM Kozhikode in the first merit list.How Ankur Warikoo helped him secure admissionHowever, receiving the admission offer brought another financial challenge.Tulsan needed ₹1 lakh to confirm his seat, but his education loan had been delayed.According to Tulsan, entrepreneur and content creator Ankur Warikoo stepped in and paid the amount directly to IIM Kozhikode, allowing him to complete the admission formalities.He said he later repaid the entire amount in two instalments of ₹90,000 and ₹10,000. Life after IIM KozhikodeTulsan graduated from IIM Kozhikode in 2025, a milestone he celebrated in another LinkedIn post.He subsequently worked with Snapsight, Juniper Green Energy and Pocket FM while also building a YouTube channel focused on MBA preparation and interview guidance.According to Tulsan, around 300 students he has mentored have collectively secured more than 1,000 admission offers from management institutions.His family's circumstances have also improved. His parents and younger brother have moved into a separate rented three-bedroom apartment, while his father has retired after years of working despite persistent back pain.Having received financial assistance during his own journey, Tulsan said he now tries to help other aspirants. He has paid a junior's ₹1 lakh IIM admission fee and supported several students with their CAT application fees.(Also read: ₹74 lakh to quit government job for IIM-A, explains how">Man claims it cost him ₹74 lakh to quit government job for IIM-A, explains how)Looking ahead, he hopes to expand his business and establish an NGO that teaches communication and professional skills to underprivileged children.Reflecting on his journey, Tulsan acknowledged that pursuing his dream without a fallback plan was risky, particularly given his family's financial situation. However, he believes consistency, accountability and the willingness to ask for help played an important role in changing his circumstances.

headline: Traffic disrupted as truck carrying liquor overturns on ORR near Avadi
content: CHENNAI A truck carrying liquor bottles, estimated to be worth ₹56 lakh, overturned on the Vandalur-Minjur Outer Ring Road (ORR) near Avadi on Friday (November 27, 2026), spilling a large quantity of liquor on the road and disrupting vehicular traffic. The accident attracted a large number of motorists and passersby, who gathered at the spot to watch the liquor spill from the truck. A senior officer from the Avadi Police Commissionerate said the truck was transporting liquor from a Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) warehouse at Kakkalur in Tiruvallur district to Red Hills. The driver reportedly lost control of the vehicle while it was proceeding along the ORR near Morai village in Avadi. Four persons, including the driver, sustained injuries in the accident and were admitted to the Tiruvallur Government Hospital for treatment. Liquor bottles shattered on impact, causing alcohol to spill across the road. The acccident drew crowds to the spot, resulting in a traffic jam. Tasmac employees were engaged in retrieving the liquor bottles, while police personnel provided protection and assisted in clearing the stretch, the officer added.

headline: Odisha’s interest must be protected: BJD on delimitation bill
content: BHUBANESWAR The Biju Janata Dal on Friday (November 27, 2026) said it would decide its stand on the amended delimitation bill in the Rajya Sabha after receiving complete information, asserting that Odisha’s interests would remain its sole priority in taking a call on the issue. The party issued a statement saying that discussions on delimitation had once again begun following the announcement of special sessions of the Lok Sabha on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2, 2026. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/government-to-reconvene-parliament-from-november-30-to-december-3-kiren-rijiju/article71747089.ece Union Cabinet clears delimitation bill Union Cabinet clears delimitation bill A similar attempt by the government was rejected in the Lok Sabha during the Monsoon session in April Union Cabinet clears delimitation bill storyline 1 Manas Mangaraj, Leader of the BJD Parliamentary Party in the Rajya Sabha, said the party had not yet received any information regarding the specific issues to be discussed during the upcoming special sessions. “After receiving detailed facts and information in this regard, the Parliamentary Party will take further steps as per the directions of BJD supremo Naveen Patnaik. The BJD has always given priority to the interests of the State and will never deviate from this principle in the future either,” Mr. Mangaraj said, without divulging the party’s position on the different formulas being speculated upon for delimitation. Meanwhile, BJD Rajya Sabha member Santrupta Mishra, while speaking to the media, said the party had always maintained that Odisha’s present proportion of representation in Parliament must be protected. Why Delimitation Bill failed to pass in Parliament in April 2026 Why Delimitation Bill failed to pass in Parliament in April 2026 Why the Delimitation Bill failed in Parliament in April 2026 and how the political arithmetic changed since then; here’s what to know Why Delimitation Bill failed to pass in Parliament in April 2026 storyline 1 The proposed 50% increase in the number of seats in Parliament for different States, which was being discussed in various forums, did not necessarily ensure equity, he pointed out. Mr. Mishra said Odisha’s interests, or those of smaller States, should not be compromised. Until the details of the bill were made available, it would be difficult for the BJD to take a stand, the Rajya Sabha MP said. At present, the BJD has five MPs in Rajya Sabha while it has no representation in Lok Sabha.

headline: Sebi clarifies no change proposed to managing director age limit at MIIs
content: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Friday clarified that its consultation paper on strengthening governance of market infrastructure institutions (MIIs) does not propose any change to the maximum age limit of 65 years for their managing directors (MDs). MIIs include stock exchanges, depositories, and clearing corporations. The regulator said that the proposals floated on November 20 regarding MDs concern only their term and tenure within a single MII and across MIIs. Incumbent public interest directors, MDs, and executive directors would continue till the end of their ongoing terms. Sebi has proposed that a single term for a managing director (MD) would not exceed five years, with a maximum of two terms and eight years in one MII. The proposed changes include lower age and term limits for public interest directors (PIDs), a 12-year cap on the combined tenure of managing directors across MIIs, and a board seat for the Association of Mutual Funds in India’s (Amfi’s) chief executive at the repo clearing corporation. The regulator has proposed cutting the maximum age of PIDs from 75 to 70 years and the cap on terms from three to two. A PID would serve two terms of three years each across MIIs. The regulator said the role is quasi-regulatory and more demanding than that of an ordinary non-executive director, and that a narrow pool of individuals can circulate between MIIs.

headline: Nudged by Centre, Tamil Nadu begins ration card data clean-up
content: CHENNAI Nudged by the Union government, the Tamil Nadu government has begun removing ineligible beneficiaries from the categories of the Priority Household (PHH) and Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) ration cards. This follows two lists of such persons sent by the Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD) at the Centre to the State. After due verification, the State government has removed most of the persons mentioned in the first list. The process is under way with regard to the second, says a senior official in the State Co-operation, Food and Consumer Protection Department. The fiscal cost of cash-transfer schemes The fiscal cost of cash-transfer schemes A social policy is often based on expected electoral gain, and is implemented without any ex ante appraisal; since cash transfers and subsidies are perpetual in nature and politically hard to reverse, such continuous commitment of financial resources demands prior evaluation and real-time monitoring to address potential shortcomings The fiscal cost of cash-transfer schemes storyline 1 The Centre’s action was, in turn, a sequel to a study commissioned by the DFPD to assess the effectiveness, inclusiveness, operational efficiency, and beneficiary experience of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013, and the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) across all States and Union Territories. Called the Concurrent Evaluation and Monitoring of NFSA-PMGKAY (2025-26), the study covered 51,303 beneficiary households, 4,939 fair price shops (FPS), 2,036 vigilance committee members, 245 godowns, and all 36 States and Union Territories across rural and urban areas. On average, 550 beneficiaries were covered in every State. High inclusion error Even as Tamil Nadu fared well on many parameters, the “high inclusion error” was glaring. Clubbed with West Bengal, Tripura, and Meghalaya, Tamil Nadu’s score for inclusion error is 38.7%. Though the evaluation took into account the AAY category too, the report showed that the degree of inclusion error was higher in the PHH category than in the AAY category. The study has highlighted the need for continued strengthening of eligibility validation, Aadhaar seeding, and periodic reviews of beneficiary databases. Udhayanidhi alleges free ration rice being polished and sold at ₹30 per kg across T.N. Udhayanidhi alleges free ration rice being polished and sold at ₹30 per kg across T.N. He alleges that people have also been returning the rice in several places Udhayanidhi alleges free ration rice being polished and sold at ₹30 per kg across T.N. storyline 1 As for Tamil Nadu, the rules notified by the State government in July 2017 point out that families living in pucca houses with three or more rooms, those owning an air-conditioner, and those with an annual income of ₹1 lakh or more must be excluded while preparing lists of PHH cards. The study has identified non-adherence to these three stipulations as the major contributing factor to the inclusion error. The rules also say that families owning a car or having at least one income tax payer among their members cannot be brought under PHH. Data purification After the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led government assumed office on May 10, the authorities removed, as part of the data purification of ration cards, around 3.08 lakh beneficiaries from the rolls as on July 31. On July 28, the Centre informed the Rajya Sabha that about 10.46 lakh beneficiaries in Tamil Nadu had been identified for removal. Onions to be sold at ₹35 per kg through urban fair price shops: T.N. Minister in Assembly on price control measures Onions to be sold at ₹35 per kg through urban fair price shops: T.N. Minister in Assembly on price control measures Mr. Venkataramanan said the increase in onion prices was owing to a shortage in supply in major onion-producing States such as Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. Onions are currently being sold at ₹56 to ₹60 per kg in the open market. Onions to be sold at ₹35 per kg through urban fair price shops: T.N. Minister in Assembly on price control measures storyline 1 At the end of July, the number of AAY cards was approximately 18.6 lakh and that of PHH cards was 99.4 lakh. Together, these categories accounted for about 3.6 crore beneficiaries, or about 52% of the beneficiaries in the State. The State has three more categories: Non-Priority Household (NPHH) cards, NPHH cards for those drawing sugar and other commodities except rice, and NPHH cards for those drawing no commodities. There were nearly 2.29 crore cards, falling under all the five categories. Under the NFSA and the PMGKAY, the entitlements of the AAY and PHH cardholders are covered. Every member of a family holding a PHH card is entitled to 5 kg of rice free of cost, while a family holding an AAY card is entitled to 35 kg of rice free of cost. The Union government bears the primary financial responsibility for distribution. The State government has been providing free rice to all ration card holders, regardless of their category, and incurring a huge food subsidy bill of ₹14,000 crore. It also distributes sugar, tur dal, and palm oil at highly subsidised rates through fair price shops.

headline: Blackbuck-inspired mascot unveiled for Khel Mahakumbh Haryana-2026; 18,000 to compete in 30 disciplines
content: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini on Friday unveiled the mascot of ‘Khel Mahakumbh Haryana-2026’. Inspired by the blackbuck, the state animal of Haryana, the mascot symbolises the state’s identity and cultural heritage, along with the agility, alertness, balance and unwavering commitment of Haryana’s sportspersons towards their goals.On the occasion, former Indian hockey captain Sardar Singh, Asian Games medallist Parveen Hooda and boxer Narender were also felicitated. The Chief Minister extended his best wishes to the members of the junior hockey team travelling to Egypt.Addressing the sportspersons, Saini said the passion and enthusiasm of Haryana’s athletes were the state’s greatest strengths. He said it was a matter of pride that Haryana consistently figured among the top states in medal tallies. Congratulating the sportspersons, he said Khel Mahakumbh would provide them with a major platform to hone their talent and bring laurels to the state.The Chief Minister said the blackbuck was known for its remarkable speed, agility, alertness, balance and grace, qualities that were also reflected in Haryana’s sportspersons. He said that on entering the sporting arena, they demonstrated the agility, concentration and determination to achieve their targets that characterised the blackbuck.He added that the mascot also conveyed a message of environmental conservation, sensitivity towards wildlife and preservation of natural heritage to the youth and people of the state.A total of 18,000 sportspersons will showcase their talent, skills and sporting spirit across 30 disciplines during the state-level competitions of Khel Mahakumbh. The competitions will be organised in two phases across 11 cities in the state.Saini said Khel Mahakumbh was a visionary initiative of the state government aimed at providing appropriate opportunities, guidance and modern facilities to budding sporting talent in villages, towns and small cities. He said these young athletes had the potential to bring glory to the Tricolour at the Olympic Games, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games in the future.As per the annual sports calendar, activities under Khel Mahakumbh commenced on November 16. District-level selection trials were conducted across the state ahead of the state-level competitions. The enthusiastic participation of youngsters in these trials reflected the growing sporting culture in Haryana, he said.The Chief Minister said that over the past 12 years, 17,676 sportspersons from the state had been awarded cash prizes amounting to Rs 931 crore. Advance financial assistance was also being provided to sportspersons representing the country in international competitions to support their preparations.A monthly scholarship of Rs 1,500 is being provided to sportspersons in the 8-14 age group, while those in the 15-19 age group receive Rs 2,000. The Sports Gradation Policy has also been amended to extend the benefits of sports gradation to participants in the Haryana State Games, enabling them to access government employment and other opportunities.Saini said recipients of the Khel Ratna, Dronacharya, Arjuna, Dhyan Chand and Tenzing Norgay Awards were now being provided a monthly honorarium of Rs 20,000, while Bhim Award recipients were receiving Rs 5,000 per month.He said village grounds, school playgrounds and early training played a crucial role in the success of every sportsperson. With this objective, 2,000 sports nurseries had been established across the state, where around 40,000 children were undergoing training in morning and evening sessions.In addition, 25 residential sports academies had been established, where sportspersons were being provided diet money at the rate of Rs 500 per day.The Chief Minister said around Rs 1,100 crore had been spent on sports infrastructure over the past nearly 12 years to provide modern facilities to athletes.To ensure better treatment, training and rehabilitation facilities for injured sportspersons, a national-level ‘A-STAR’ Advanced Scientific Training and Rehabilitation Centre had been established at the Tau Devi Lal Sports Complex in Panchkula at a cost of around Rs 10 crore. He said it was the first and most advanced centre of its kind in North India.

headline: Ahead of Parliament sitting, Supriya Sule, Sanjay Raut likely to miss INDIA bloc’s strategy meet tomorrow
content: Two prominent Opposition leaders from Maharashtra, NCP (SP)’s Supriya Sule and Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Sanjay Raut, are likely to miss a key INDIA bloc meeting in Delhi on Saturday, ahead of Parliament’s special sitting on November 30, people aware of the matter said.Sule is unlikely to attend the meeting, called by the Congress to discuss the Opposition’s strategy for the special session on delimitation, due to the ill health of her father and party chief Sharad Pawar, the people said. The NCP (SP) will be represented by other MPs, they said, adding that Sule is expected to reach Delhi on Sunday night, ahead of the Lok Sabha sitting. Shiv Sena (UBT) will also be represented by other lawmakers, they said.ALSO READ: ‘Can’t comment without reviewing it’: Supriya Sule on possible support for delimitation billMeanwhile, the ruling alliance is preparing its own floor strategy. Deputy chief minister and Shiv Sena chief Eknath Shinde has called a meeting of all the party’s Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs at his Nandanvan bungalow in Mumbai at 2pm on Saturday, the people said. The meeting will discuss the party’s stand and floor strategy for the special session, and attendance has been made mandatory. The Shiv Sena has also issued a whip directing all its MPs to be in Delhi by November 29.

headline: Six restaurants, including KFC, sealed in Dehradun for violating environmental norms
content: The Uttarakhand Pollution Control Board has sealed six restaurants in Dehradun, including a KFC outlet, for violating environmental norms, an official said on Friday.Naresh Goswami, a regional officer for the board, said authorities issued show-cause notices to six restaurants located on Rajpur Road a month ago regarding the violations. Since the outlets didn't give any satisfactory response, the administration sealed the establishments on November 25," he said.ALSO READ | Uttarkashi fire guts 39 houses, school, panchayat building in Pawani village; relief work stepped upGoswami said the officials disconnected electricity connections to the establishments following directives from the board and then sealed KFC (Safeyure Food India), Mojo Resto Bar & Party Lounge, Lifestyle (Playboy), Level One Resto, AS 4 Integrated Facility Management Services Pvt Ltd, and Diablo Restaurant & Bar.

headline: 4 Jharkhand school boys kill fellow student for reporting them to principal, detained
content: Four boys have been detained for allegedly strangling to death a fellow student of a government residential school in Jharkhand's Chatra district after they were reported to the principal for possessing tobacco products, police said on Friday.The principal expressed shock over the reason police gave for the murder, and denied having ever received any complaint from the victim about the accused's tobacco addiction.A student of Class 7 at Eklavya Model Residential School in Charu was found dead in his hostel on November 24, with his father alleging that the boy was murdered.ALSO READ | Jharkhand couple held for killing 14-year-old daughter over mobile phone use, making reelsAn investigation was initiated, which found that four fellow students, aged between 14 and 16 years, were involved, Chatra Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Sunny Vardhan said.He said the probe revealed the accused used to consume chewing tobacco and smoke cigarettes. The victim had reported them to the school principal and hostel warden multiple times, the police officer said.Infuriated, the four accused strangled the victim to death using a scarf, the SDPO said, adding that of the four detained, three were students of Class 8 and the other of Class 7.ALSO READ | Jharkhand’s Congress ally JMM keeps options open on delimitation bill, says ‘we will decide once we see it’Manoj Hembram, the uncle of the victim, said he received a call from the school that his nephew was in serious condition and admitted to hospital on November 24 morning."I immediately rushed to Chatra from Giridih. As I reached Koderma, I was informed that my nephew had died. Upon arriving at the hospital, I noticed blood stains on his ears and nose, and a mark on the neck. I immediately suspected that he was strangled to death," Hembram said.School principal Pradip Thakur, however, denied receiving any complaint against the accused from the victim.Thakur claimed he was not in the district when the incident occurred, and was made aware of it on the phone, following which he returned to the school the next day.ALSO READ | Wedding turns into shootout in Jharkhand's Hazaribagh; one dead, another critical"I have not received a single complaint against the accused boys. Had I been aware of this, I would have taken action. I was shocked when police informed me of reasons behind the murder," he told PTI.The principal said he has initiated an inquiry to ascertain if the victim had reported the accused to any teacher or school official. "I am also trying to ascertain if the victim was tortured by fellow students," he said.The Eklavya Model Residential School in Charu has 220 students, including girls, housed in 50 hostel rooms on campus. "Four students are housed in a room. But the accused boys and the victim were not sharing a room," Thakur said.The other three students who shared a room with the victim told police that they did not hear anything on the night of the incident as they were asleep.According to the school principal, the school does not have adequate security guards. Only one guard was manning the 50 hostel rooms on the night of the incident, he added.A psychiatrist at Central Institute of Psychiatry (CIP) in Ranchi called for regular counselling of students to prevent such incidents from recurring."What was actually going on in the accused's minds could be ascertained only after one-to-one discussion. But regular counselling of students is required in schools, particularly the residential ones," Dr Umesh said.

headline: Special session a political ploy to push delimitation, raise number of LS seats: HP minister
content: Shimla, The Union government's decision to convene a special session of Parliament is a political strategy to push delimitation and increase the number of Lok Sabha seats under the pretext of women's reservation, Himachal Pradesh Agriculture Minister and former MP Chander Kumar said on Friday.He said the Women's Reservation Bill has already been passed by Parliament and it could be implemented using the 2011 Census as a basis.He also questioned the need for creation of new districts in Himachal Pradesh, arguing that it is far more important to strengthen the existing administrative framework. Talking to reporters here, the minister said the Centre has called for the special session from November 30 to December 3 following pressure from the Opposition, but it primarily aims to accelerate the delimitation process.Kumar, who was a member of the relevant committee during the 2011 delimitation process, recalled that at the time, assembly constituencies were adjusted based on population, with some designated as reserved and others as general categories.He said the Centre aims to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats to 850, granting greater representation to North Indian states, to the potential disadvantage of southern states.Expressing concern that states that have controlled their population could end up with a lower share of seats, he said it is inappropriate to discuss an increase in parliamentary seats before the constitutional processes of Census and delimitation are completed.The Centre is seeking political gain through delimitation, a move that could create a political imbalance between North and South India, he said.Kumar said women's reservation could be implemented using the 2011 Census as a basis and there is no need to increase the number of parliamentary seats under the pretext of delimitation to achieve this.On creation of new districts in Himachal Pradesh, Kumar said an informed decision on this could only be taken once the Census is completed and the population data becomes available.Questioning the need for new districts, he pointed out that it would increase administrative expenditure and consume a larger share of the budget.People are already receiving significant services through tehsils, blocks and various departmental offices, and the expansion of digital services now allows them to access many government services from the comfort of their homes, he argued.He said it is far more important to strengthen the existing administrative framework than to create new districts, emphasising the need to carefully consider the actual, tangible benefits new districts would provide to the common people.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Keralam Assembly session from Nov 30 to Dec 10; nine bills to be taken up
content: Thiruvananthapuram, Speaker Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan on Friday said the third session of the 16th Keralam Legislative Assembly would be held from November 30 to December 10, with nine bills slated for consideration.The House would sit for nine days, of which eight were earmarked for legislative business and one for non-official members' business, he told reporters.The bills slated for consideration are the Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Bill, 2026; the Kerala Public Service Commission Amendment Bill, 2026; and the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Bill, 2026. The remaining Bills are the University Laws Bill, 2026; the Kerala Private Universities Bill, 2026; the Kerala Sidharthan Anti-Ragging and Student Welfare Bill, 2026; and the Kerala Sports Persons' Welfare and Sports Development and Administration Bill, 2026.Radhakrishnan said the second session was convened exclusively for legislative business, and the third session, too, would be devoted exclusively to it, a month after the previous session concluded.During the second session, the Assembly passed a resolution seeking the return of the Kerala Private Universities Bill, 2025, which had been passed by the 15th Keralam Assembly and sent to the governor for assent.Following the resolution, the governor referred the Bill to the President for consideration and returned it to the Assembly with a message.A motion seeking withdrawal of the Bill would be moved in the House during the forthcoming session, the Speaker said.He announced new restrictions on the movement of visitors within the Assembly complex, citing a rise in their numbers during sessions.The curbs have been introduced to ensure the smooth functioning of the House without restricting visitors' access to facilities, he said.Under the revised arrangement, visitors, irrespective of the type of pass they hold, will not be allowed to move around the Assembly hall area until the conclusion of Zero Hour, except those authorised to enter the House.Those wishing to meet ministers can continue to visit their chambers, where watch-and-ward personnel, including women staff, will assist them.The decision was taken after consultations with Chief Minister V D Satheesan, the Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan, and leaders of various political parties, the Speaker added.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: ICAR-CRIDA, Hyderabad Strengthens Climate-Resilient Agricultural Interventions under OADMP in Odisha
content: A multidisciplinary team from ICAR–Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture, Hyderabad, visited Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, from 18 to 20 November 2026 under the Odisha Agriculture Drought Mitigation Programme (OADMP) to review project progress and strengthen the implementation of climate-resilient agricultural technologies and livelihood interventions across three Gram Panchayats (GPs)—Bhanjakia, Godapalsa and Tilakuti. During the visit, the team held consultations with farmers, community representatives, block-level officials from the Agriculture, Engineering and Veterinary Departments, and project field staff to assess ongoing activities and finalize implementation strategies. As part of efforts to strengthen community-based farm mechanization, meetings were held in all three GPs with the respective Sarpanches, block officials and Custom Hiring Centre (CHC) committee members. Office bearers, including Presidents, Secretaries and Treasurers, were elected from the existing committees, and resolutions were passed to operationalize the CHCs. Land allocation for CHC infrastructure in Bhanjakia GP was also finalized. Based on consultations with farmers and stakeholders, 108 agricultural implements were identified for procurement through the Odisha Agro Industries Corporation (OAIC), comprising 24 for Bhanjakia, 38 for Godapalsa and 46 for Tilakuti. Operational modalities for machinery management, maintenance and custom hiring were also discussed. The team reviewed livelihood promotion and natural resource management interventions, including the identification of beneficiaries for Azolla cultivation units, farm bunding and composite pisciculture in farm ponds. Discussions were also held on mobilizing Women’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs) through a corpus-fund model to promote agroforestry-based livelihood opportunities. To promote crop diversification and nutritional security, the team assessed interventions across nine OADMP villages, covering non-paddy crop diversification (4 beneficiaries), agroforestry models (3 beneficiaries) and backyard nutrition gardens (8 beneficiaries). A questionnaire-based survey was also initiated to assess the nutrition-garden interventions aimed at improving household dietary diversity and addressing malnutrition.

headline: YSRCP supports delimitation because it seeks to protect Andhra’s representation: Party MP
content: Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party (YSRCP) parliamentarian P V Midhun Reddy has said their party supports the proposed delimitation legislation because it favours women’s reservation and seeks to protect Andhra Pradesh’s representation, not because it is aligning with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). In an interview with HT, he said they have criticised the BJP, including the way elections are conducted, and raised concerns about EVMs. Edited excerpts:YSRCP supported the delimitation bill in April after receiving assurances from the government. Has that position changed?No, we voted in favour last time. The reason was the 50% proportionate increase in seats. The Centre assured us of this. This time, they have included it in the bill. In principle, we are okay with it, but we want to raise one more concern: further regional imbalances should not arise. YSRCP has been critical of the Centre, particularly over promises made to Andhra Pradesh that remain unfulfilled. By supporting this legislation, are you not emboldening the government?There are two things. One is women’s reservation, which we support. Whether the BJP is in power or not, we have always supported the reservation. When we were in power in Andhra Pradesh, we provided 50% reservation for women in all local bodies, which was within the state’s powers. As long as there is a 50% increase in seats, our state is protected. If the exercise is entirely based on population, we will suffer a loss. We believe the proportionate 50% increase is reasonable for Andhra Pradesh.The Opposition Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) opposed the bill. What do you make of its position?That is their political call, and we do not want to comment on it. Earlier, the DMK [Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam] and Congress were together. Now they are not. That is their decision. We are concerned about the interests of our state. We do not want to get into [ruling] NDA [National Democratic Alliance] or INDIA bloc politics.We have criticised the BJP on several issues, including the way elections are conducted. We have raised concerns about EVMs on the floor of the House. It is not that we are aligning with the BJP. But this is about women’s reservation, which we have always supported. We thought it should happen at least now.Does YSRCP’s position on the bill mark a departure from the broader Opposition’s stand?We are not too concerned with central politics. We are worried about our state and anything that affects its interests. Once we have numbers, the Centre will talk to us. There is no point trying to do central politics without having the numbers. Hopefully, we will get better numbers.Has the government reached out to you to discuss the bill?The government has reached out. We had detailed discussions last time as well, and I think we will speak to them tomorrow or the day after. The Opposition has not reached out.What are the specific concerns you want the Centre to address?Andhra Pradesh has three regions — Rayalaseema, Coastal Andhra and Uttarandhra. We want the same proportion of seats to be maintained. We do not want the representation of drought-prone areas to decline because of population shifts.Southern states have also faced drought concerns this year. Are you discussing these issues with the Centre alongside delimitation?We are not linking the two issues. But we have been fighting for Andhra Pradesh’s interests. Despite being part of the NDA, Andhra Pradesh has not received adequate funds. There is also a lot of alleged embezzlement of funds in the name of the capital. For example, construction in Delhi costs around ₹3,500-4,000 per square foot, while the state government is spending ₹20,000 per square foot in Amaravati.The Centre has also floated a tender for a building next to the one being constructed by the state government in Amaravati at around ₹3,500 per square foot. The state government’s project is costing ₹18,000-20,000 per square foot. We have been raising these issues and will continue to do so. There are several corruption-related concerns in Andhra Pradesh.

headline: 5.6% Nagaland women in 20-24 year age group entered into wedlock before 18: Social Welfare Secy
content: Kohima, Child marriage prevalence in Nagaland was concerning, with 5.6 per cent of women in the 20 to 24 years age bracket having entered into wedlock before turning 18, Social Welfare Secretary Limawabang Jamir said on Friday, citing National Family Health Survey-5 data.It was higher in the state's rural areas, with 7.3 per cent such cases, while urban settlements have a 2.4 per cent incidence, the officer said at an event here to mark the first International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage.He said teenage pregnancy remained a major concern alongside child marriage and called for sustained community-level awareness and preventive action.Jamir said Child Marriage Prohibition Officers had been designated in all 17 districts, while Mission Shakti's 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' initiative was promoting girls' education, checking school dropout rates and challenging discriminatory social practices.The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, was under process for formal adoption by the state government, but its principles were being implemented through departmental interventions, the officer said.The government's Social Welfare Advisor and MLA Wangpang Konyak said protecting women and girls was a fundamental human rights issue and essential for ensuring equality, justice and sustainable development.Appealing to people to treat every girl with dignity, he asked how they would feel if their daughters were forced into marriage, deprived of education or denied the freedom to choose their future.Konyak expressed concern over teenage pregnancy, particularly in rural areas, and cautioned that the absence of formally solemnised or officially reported child marriages should not lead to complacency when pregnancies among very young girls remained a concern.He called for stronger coordination among government agencies and urged churches, tribal and community leaders, educational institutions, NGOs and civil society to headline: ManipalCigna Addresses Evolving Health Insurance Needs with INFINIX, Offering Unlimited Sum Insured and Greater Flexibility
content: INFINIX combines Unlimited Sum Insured with hospital-network choices, city-based pricing and a One-Time Aggregate Deductible Mumbai, Maharashtra, India (NewsVoir) As healthcare costs, treatment choices and family needs continue to evolve, choosing the right health insurance is becoming a more nuanced decision. Customers need to consider not only how much health cover is adequate, but also where they want to access healthcare, how they balance coverage with affordability, and whether their protection can remain relevant as their needs change. Against this backdrop, ManipalCigna Health Insurance’s INFINIX brings together Unlimited Sum Insured, city-based pricing, a choice of hospital networks and differentiated affordability features, giving customers greater flexibility to structure their health cover around their healthcare preferences and financial priorities. A key feature of INFINIX is its One-Time Aggregate Deductible, which needs to be exhausted only once during ten policy years, while the associated premium discount continues throughout the decade. Customers can also choose from three Smart Care Network options, Classic, Premier and Premier+, based on their preferred hospitals, location and financial comfort. Commenting on how health insurance needs are evolving, Joydeep Saha, MD & CEO, ManipalCigna Health Insurance, said “The way people think about health insurance is changing. Customers are looking for more than a sum insured; they want confidence that their health cover can remain relevant as healthcare costs, family needs and life stages evolve. At the same time, every family has different preferences around where they access healthcare and how they balance protection with affordability. INFINIX responds to these changing needs by bringing together unlimited coverage, hospital-network choices and a differentiated affordability model, giving customers greater flexibility to structure health protection around their needs and financial priorities.” Different needs, greater choice INFINIX is available in two variants designed around different customer needs. INFINIX CORE is designed for first-time health insurance buyers seeking unlimited health coverage at a value-oriented price, with the flexibility to reduce applicable waiting periods. INFINIX NOW is designed for customers who already have health insurance and want to upgrade to unlimited health coverage from Day 1. Both variants offer a choice of INR10 lakh or Unlimited Sum Insured, with policy tenures of one, two or three years and optional covers that allow customers to tailor protection according to their requirements. Looking beyond hospitalisation Changing health needs also extend beyond hospital treatment alone. Through Emotional Quotient and NutriBoost, INFINIX provides unlimited e-consultations with psychologists and nutritionists, along with mental-wellbeing tools, dietary guidance and lifestyle support. The New Beginnings maternity benefit comes with just a one-year waiting period. The opted coverage grows by 100% every year after the second policy year, up to 1,000% of the selected amount. An eligible male insured can also extend the benefit to his spouse even if she is not covered under the policy. INFINIX also offers coverage for specified advanced diagnostic tests, including PET-CT, PET MRI, Coronary Angiography and Endoscopic Ultrasound, when medically prescribed and undertaken at a hospital, subject to policy conditions. Eligible NRI and OCI customers opting for Unlimited Sum Insured can also avail additional premium discount, while the No Claim Discount rewards claim-free years through progressive renewal premium discounts. For more information on key features, eligibility, exclusions and terms and conditions, please refer to the product brochure here Note: Unlimited Sum Insured is subject to policy terms, conditions, underwriting guidelines and applicable exclusions. About ManipalCigna Health Insurance Company Limited ManipalCigna Health Insurance Company Limited is a joint venture between the Manipal Group and Cigna Healthcare and has been operating in India since 2014. The company's mission is to improve the health, well-being and peace of mind of those it serves. It believes that expertise in health insurance begins with understanding health, a belief reflected in the India Health Quotient, its annual study with YouGov India on how Indians manage their well-being. ManipalCigna’s retail portfolio provides individuals and families with comprehensive health coverage for different life stages and evolving health needs. Its group business partners with SMEs, corporates, banks and NBFCs to deliver health and wellness solutions for their employees and customers. ManipalCigna has 125 branches across 500+ cities, an ecosystem of 1 lakh+ agents and 500+ distribution partners, and over 17,500 network hospitals. The company ended FY26 with a claim settlement ratio of 96% and gross written premium growth of about 30%. With an employee base of 3,500+ people, ManipalCigna is a certified Great Place To Work. To learn more, visit www.manipalcigna.com. (Disclaimer: The above press release comes to you under an arrangement with Newsvoir and PTI takes no editorial responsibility for the same.). headline: Calcutta HC sets aside TMC rebel Ritabrata Banerjee’s appointment as Bengal LoP
content: The Calcutta high court on Friday set aside the West Bengal Assembly speaker's appointment of rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) leader Ritabrata Banerjee as leader of opposition, while directing him to reconsider the appointment within 10 days.The HC order came following a petition by TMC's Mamata Banerjee faction leader Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay, wherein he challenged the Speaker's decision to appoint Ritabrata as LoP, Live Law reported.Justice Krishna Rao also set aside the appointment of Akhruzzaman as the chief whip of the TMC in the Assembly. The court ruling comes even as rival factions of the TMC – led by Ritabrata and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee – are expected to present their claims before the Election Commission of India on Friday.The HC said both appointments were not sustainable under law, news agency PTI reported. In his petition, Chattopadhyay had claimed that his nomination as LoP was finalised by the TMC before the Speaker recognised Ritabrata as the LoP.Following TMC's defeat in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly polls, in early June 2026, Ritabrata Banerjee, TMC MLA from Uluberia, claimed support of nearly 60 of the party's 80 MLAs. He was recognised as LoP, following which the decision was challenged the decision in court.Meanwhile, the ECI allotted interim identities to the two factions—naming one camp the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (symbol: football player) and the other Democratic Trinamool Congress (symbol: envelope).May 6 AITC meeting, forgery claims: How did the LoP dispute begin?According to the petition, in a meeting held at the All India Trinamool Congress headquarters on May 6, 2026, Chattopadhyay's nomination as the LoP was confirmed. Around 70 party leaders, including Ritabrata, allegedly attended the meeting.Following this, a signed resolution dated May 19, 2026, endorsing Chattopadhyay's nomination, was submitted to the Speaker along with the attendance sheet of the meeting, the petition said, according to Live Law.However, Ritabrata late approached the Speaker and alleged that several signatures on the resolution were forged. The Speaker subsequently directed the registration of a police complaint against AITC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee over alleged falsification of signatures. Soon after this, Ritabrata and 59 other leaders broke away from the Mamata-led AITC and sought claim to the post of the LoP. The Speaker then recognised Ritabrata for the position.What did the two factions argue in court?Appearing for Chattopadhyay, senior advocate Kalyan Bandopadhyay questioned the legality of Ritabrata's appointment and alleged that the speaker had acted in a partisan manner.He further claimed that the Speaker had deliberately delayed recognising Chattopadhyay as the LoP while waiting for the dissident MLAs to break away from TMC, Live Law reported. Bandopadhyay argued that defence under Article 212 of the Constitution, which protects legislative proceedings from judicial scrutiny on grounds of procedural irregularity, could not be invoked here.Meanwhile, senior advocate Jaydip Kar, representing Ritabrata, argued that a dispute regarding the symbols of both the factions is still pending before the ECI, submitting that the legitimate TMC faction is yet to be established, according to Live Law.To this, Justice Rao highlighted that the TMC had not split into factions on the day the Speaker had announced the decision. Kar argued that no specific statutory provision or procedure regarding the Speaker's appointment of the LoP, and therefore, his decision could not be challenged. Additional advocate general Billwadal Bhattacharyya, appearing for Speaker Rathindra Bose, addressed the alleged delay in recognising the LoP initially, arguing that Chattopadhyay's nomination could not have been finalised at the May 6 meeting as the Speaker had not yet assumed office in the Assembly.

headline: Infosys sees eightfold rise in US H-1B approvals as Texas prepares to change visa policy: Report
content: Infosys received 2,088 approvals for new H-1B employment in the US in fiscal 2026, compared with 257 a year earlier, marking an increase of more than eight times, according to federal immigration records analysed by The Dallas Express.The figures place the Indian IT company among the employers recording significant growth in new H-1B employment approvals over the two-year period. Infosys identifies Richardson, Texas, as its petitioner city in the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) database, although the records do not establish where all the approved employees will work.The increase is being reported at a time when Texas is reconsidering its approach to the visa programme. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has announced plans to withdraw restrictions introduced by outgoing Governor Greg Abbott, which currently limit new H-1B sponsorship by certain state institutions.For Infosys, however, the state directive is not a direct restriction. Abbott's order applies to specified government agencies and public higher-education institutions, rather than private-sector employers. This means companies such as Infosys are outside the categories covered by the directive.USCIS data also shows that the increase was not limited to Infosys. KPMG recorded 234 approvals for new employment in FY2026, up from 75 in FY2025. Texas Instruments increased from 50 to 125, while American Airlines rose from 60 to 69, as cited by The Dallas Express.The pattern differed among public institutions. UT Southwestern Medical Center recorded 102 new-employment approvals in FY2026, down from 124 in the previous year. Dallas Independent School District also saw its figure fall, from 73 to 39. Its approvals for continuing employment, however, increased from 155 to 210.The distinction between private employers and public institutions is central to the policy debate in Texas. Under Abbott's January 27 directive, agencies led by gubernatorial appointees and public universities must secure written clearance from the Texas Workforce Commission before filing new H-1B sponsorship petitions. The requirement is due to remain in effect until May 31 next year.The directive also asks covered institutions to maintain records of attempts to recruit qualified Texas applicants and provide information about their visa sponsorship activity.Hinojosa has said she intends to reverse the restrictions. Speaking to The Texas Tribune on November 18, she acknowledged concerns about misuse of the H-1B programme but opposed applying a broad freeze to public institutions. She also cited the difficulties school districts face in recruiting teachers.Her proposed reversal could change the process followed by state agencies and public universities, although she has not yet detailed what oversight measures would replace Abbott's requirements.You use AI every day. headline: CSR not just legal obligation but investment in India’s future: Karnataka Guv
content: Bengaluru, Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav on Friday said CSR should not be viewed merely as a legal obligation, but as an investment in society's future and in building a developed India.She said industries must cultivate a spirit of giving back to society the wealth they earn from it.The governor was speaking at the BCIC CSR Conclave-2026, organised by the Bengaluru Chamber of Industry and Commerce here as part of its Golden Jubilee celebrations, officials said.She said the vision of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas' could be realised only through the active participation of society and the corporate sector, alongside government efforts.Collective efforts involving all sections of society would be the driving force behind building a new India, she added.Quoting renowned industrialist J R D Tata, Yadav said the fundamental principle of Corporate social responsibility should be to give back to society many times over what businesses receive from it, according to a statement issued by Lok Bhavan.She stressed the importance of integrating social responsibility with business objectives and ensuring that corporate initiatives contribute to sustainable social development."Profit is the fuel that keeps the engine running, but purpose is the compass that gives it direction," she said.Noting that India had made significant strides in CSR, she flagged several challenges, such as the uneven distribution of CSR funds, limited participation by Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises , and inadequate assessment of the long-term impact of projects.She called on industry bodies and business organisations to work together to address these concerns.The governor said industries were undertaking commendable CSR initiatives in areas such as women's empowerment and health, education, school infrastructure and tree plantation. However, she emphasised that launching projects was not enough; they had to be sustained and responsibly managed until the intended outcomes were achieved.Referring to school infrastructure projects in rural areas and tree plantation drives, she said many saplings failed to survive due to inadequate maintenance.She also pointed out that several regions continued to lack basic infrastructure and adequate development opportunities.Yadav said greater attention should be paid to improving the living standards, education and social progress of tribal communities.She urged industries and business organisations to look beyond their immediate areas of operation and contribute to the development of backward and remote regions of the state.Instead of undertaking isolated projects independently, industries could join hands to identify priority areas and implement comprehensive development programmes, she said.Yadav suggested that industries adopt specific regions, assess their needs, set clear development goals and implement projects in a phased manner.Regularly assessing a project's baseline, the progress made and the number of beneficiaries reached would help ensure that CSR initiatives delivered measurable results. Such an outcome-oriented approach was essential to fulfil the true purpose of CSR, she said.The governor called on the corporate sector to recognise its social responsibility and make meaningful contributions through CSR initiatives towards the vision of a developed India."At a time when India is achieving new development milestones, it is the collective responsibility of all stakeholders to build a nation that offers future generations better opportunities, equality and sustainable development," she added.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Kerala launches students savings scheme: Deposit and withdrawal records, SMS alerts for parents | Key features explained
content: Kerala has launched a “first-of-its-kind”, fully integrated online portal to digitise the state government's Students Savings Scheme and promote habit of saving among school children, PTI reported citing officials.The portal, developed by the Kerala Infrastructure and Technology for Education, was inaugurated by Chief Minister VD Satheesan on 19 November. KITE is the technical arm of the state's General Education Department.As part of the launch celebrations, the chief minister handed over digital passbooks to three students from the Government Lower Primary School, Vilappil — Hrishikesh AR, Anigha R Sooraj and Harshitha Kiran S, as per the statement.Students Savings Scheme digitisation: Key featuresThe Students Savings Scheme aims to inculcate financial discipline and the habit of saving among students from Classes 1 to 12 in government and government-aided schools across Keralam.It is the country's largest statewide digital initiative dedicated exclusively to school-level student savings, officials said.The portal enables end-to-end digital management of student savings accounts, with access extending from class teachers to the Director of National Savings, it added.The portal offers several features, such as digital passbooks that automatically record deposits, withdrawals and accrued interest, SMS alerts to parents for every transaction, digital generation of treasury pay-in slips, fixed deposit tracking and online account closure facilities. To facilitate seamless adoption without adding to teachers' data-entry workload, schools can access the platform using their existing login credentials for the state's educational e-governance portals-Sampoorna (school management system), HSCAP (Higher Secondary Centralised Admission Process) and VHSCAP (Vocational Higher Secondary Centralised Admission Process). Teachers-in-charge can also log in by scanning a QR code through the 'KITE Key' mobile application, which is integrated with the portal to facilitate SMS-based one-time password (OTP) verification. Real-time dashboards provide district and state-level administrative offices with access to school-level financial transactions and consolidated reports, the statement said. Kudumbashree campus initiative to help college students Further, Kerala's all-women network Kudumbashree on 19 November also launched a new initiative to help female college students earn an income and develop entrepreneurial skills alongside their studies, PTI reported.Inaugurating the state-level launch of the 'Kudumbashree @ Campus' project at Kozhikode beach, Local Self-Government Minister KM Shaji said the organisation would guide youngster in the right direction to achieve their aspirations. He explained that the project was conceived as a collective platform shaped by students' ideas and suggestions and would seek to move away from the conventional approach of pursuing employment only after completing education by enabling students to gain work experience and generate income while studying. Under the initiative, entrepreneurship clubs will be formed in colleges to nurture innovative ideas and help students translate them into viable ventures. The programme will provide opportunities for internships, mentorship, business planning, digital marketing and financial literacy, besides opening up avenues in start-ups, hospitality and tourism. The project will cover students of arts and science as well as professional colleges, offering training and entrepreneurial support in creative, production and service, and IT and technology sectors. The areas covered include filmmaking, digital marketing, content writing, designing, editing, software development, app building, start-ups, micro-enterprises, agriculture, handicrafts, tourism, fashion and beauty. Special Kudumbashree groups comprising female students will be formed in colleges to implement the project. The organisation will extend support at every stage, from developing business ideas and providing training to facilitating financial assistance and marketing support. (With inputs from PTI)

headline: Big win for Mamata: HC sets aside Ritabrata Banerjee's appointment as Bengal LoP
content: NEW DELHI: The Calcutta high court on Friday quashed the appointment of Ritabrata Banerjee as the leader of opposition in the West Bengal assembly.A bench of justice Krishna Rao called the decision unsustainable under law and directed the speaker to reconsider and pass a reasoned order.The bench also asked the speaker to reach a fresh decision within 10 days.Following the West Bengal assembly elections earlier this year, assembly speaker Rathindra Bose had recognised Ritabrata Banerjee, leader of the rebel Trinamool Congress faction, as the leader of the opposition and Akhruzzaman as the chief whip.Challenging the speaker's decision, veteran Trinamool Congress MLA Sovandeb Chattopadhyay, a senior leader of the faction led by former chief minister Mamata Banerjee and her nephew Abhishek Banerjee, moved the Calcutta high court.Earlier, a division bench of the high court had allowed Ritabrata Banerjee and Akhruzzaman to continue in their respective positions on an interim basis for two months.After the interim period expired on October 18, Chattopadhyay approached the high court again, arguing that neither legislator had any legal right to continue in the posts as the interim arrangement had not been extended.He also alleged that both legislators continued to enjoy state-provided privileges attached to the offices of the leader of the opposition and chief whip despite having no legal authority to hold them.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: 'Deepam to be lit tomorrow': Furious SC suspends temple trust, asks CRPF to step in
content: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday ordered that the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp will be lit again on Saturday atop the Deepathoon. It also suspended the Tamil Nadu temple's board of trustees, appointed two retired Madras High Court judges as receivers to manage the temple, and handed over security of the temple and Thiruparankundram hill to the CRPF.This order came days after Karthigai Deepam lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple, instead of Deepathoon as ordered earlier by the Supreme Court.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said it would take action against anyone attempting to create constitutional chaos.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), told the bench that temple trustees had informed the agency that they had received no instructions from higher officials regarding the entry.Also read: 'Time to deal with iron hand' - SC comes down heavily on Vijay government over Deepam rowHere's what SC ordered:Lamp to be lit at Deepathoon on SaturdayThe Supreme Court directed that the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit atop the disputed Deepathoon pillar on Saturday, using the flame lit at the Uchaipillaiyar mandapam. The court had earlier permitted the ritual as a one-time interim measure on November 24, but the lamp was lit only at the customary mandapam and not at Deepathoon.Temple trustees suspended, CRPF to handle securityThe Supreme Court suspended the board of trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and appointed two retired Madras High Court judges, Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthipan, as receivers to take over its management. It also handed over security of the temple and Thiruparankundram hill to the CRPF.Contempt notices to top Tamil Nadu officialsThe bench issued contempt notices to Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, Director General of Police (DGP), Madurai Collector and other officials over the alleged violation of its November 20 order permitting the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon. Observing that the state executive authorities appeared to have acted on the "diktats of their political bosses", the court directed the chief secretary to appear personally and file an affidavit detailing the emails, phone calls and messages exchanged between officials in connection with the matter.The bench said, "The wilful non-compliance of orders of the Court, especially by the executive authorities, cannot go unnoticed and it has to be dealt with an iron hand." It also observed that the conduct of the officials prima facie indicated administrative chaos in the state. Describing the alleged actions as "a brazen and wilful disobedience" of its order and "a calculated affront to the authority of both constitutional courts", the court warned that attempts to undermine the course of justice would not be tolerated. It further clarified that its orders were binding on the state, its officials and every religious institution, and were not an invitation to negotiate.SC warns against constitutional chaosExpressing "pain and anguish" over the failure to implement its earlier order, the bench said, "The time has come to deal with the situation with an iron hand as it will lead to constitutional chaos."It also warned that it would "set right anybody trying to create constitutional chaos", making it clear that its directions could not be diluted.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
