headline: Tamil Nadu introduces 15 days of paternity leave for married government employees
content: CHENNAI In a significant move, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has announced 15 days of paternity leave for married male employees of the State government. Should men get paternity leave in India? storyline 1 According to an official release issued on Thursday (November 26, 2026), the paternity leave can be availed by male employees either 15 days before the birth of the child or within six months from the date of birth. Should men get paternity leave in India? Should men get paternity leave in India? PARLEY Should men get paternity leave in India? storyline 1 While female employees working in the Tamil Nadu government are currently provided 365 days of maternity leave, the government has introduced paternity leave for male employees following requests from government employees. To aid sharing of childcare responsibilities The provision of 365 days of maternity leave to female government employees reflects the importance attached to motherhood and the welfare of the child, the release said. Similarly, extending paternity leave to male government employees would help them share family responsibilities and ensure the father’s involvement in raising the child, it added. Maternity leave for third child of Tamil Nadu government employees raised to 365 days storyline 1 According to a G.O. issued by the Human Resources Management Department in this regard, the paternity leave on full pay for a period of 15 days would be for married men government servants with less than three surviving children during the confinement of their wife for childbirth. Necessary amendments to the Tamil Nadu Fundamental Rules in this regard would be issued separately, the G.O. said. What did the Supreme Court say about paid maternity leave? What did the Supreme Court say about paid maternity leave? Why did the Supreme Court strike down Section 60(4) of the Social Security Code, 2020? What did it say about maternity leave for adoptive mothers? What did the Court recommend that the Union government do regarding paternity leave? What did the Supreme Court say about paid maternity leave? storyline 1 Doctors and government employees’ associations have welcomed the decision. A. Jaishree Gajaraj, Head of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, MGM Healthcare, Chennai, said paternity leave extends the father’s involvement during pregnancy, labour, and delivery into the post-natal period. Early involvement also helps establish parent-child bonding and shared responsibility for childcare. She suggested that the duration of the leave be extended to a month. Pavithra Ramakrishnan, Consultant, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Reproductive Medicine, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Chennai, said the post-natal period involves physical recovery from childbirth and adjustment to newborn care. Fathers’ support during this phase allows mothers to get adequate rest and can help address emotional difficulties, including post-partum depression. Anna Kuberan, State president, Tamil Nadu Government Employees’ Association, and R. Arulraj, State president, Tamil Nadu Village Administrative Officers’ Association, also welcomed the decision. Mr. Arulraj said a representation in this regard was submitted to the government on various occasions. He said the paternity leave would be beneficial to the employees staying away from family for their work.

headline: ‘Complete failure’: SC suspends temple trustees amid Deepathoon row, appoints retired judges
content: The Supreme Court on Friday suspended the board of trustees of the Uchipillayar Temple in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai, days after the ceremonial ‘Karthigai Deepam’ was lit at its usual spot instead of the disputed stone pillar.During a hearing on Friday, the apex court said it was a “complete failure” on the Devasthanam’s part and ordered the suspension of the board of trustees.Also Read | SC orders lighting of lamp atop disputed ‘Deepathoon’ tomorrow, issues contempt notice to top Tamil Nadu officialsThe top court also appointed the retired judges as receivers."There is complete failure of the Devasthanam, and therefore we immediately suspend the board of trustees," the court said, according to Live Law.Furthermore, the Court handed over the security of the temple to CRPF, citing the failure of the Tamil Nadu Police to implement its orders.Also Read | Karthigai Deepam row: SC issues contempt notice to Tamil Nadu chief secretary, DGP and collectorSC orders lighting of lamp atop 'Deepathoon' tomorrowThe Supreme Court has ordered the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon on Saturday, November 28. This came days after its earlier order to do the same was disobeyed. The apex court was hearing contempt petitions over the controversy surrounding the location where the Karthigai Deepam was lit.Taking a strong stance on the matter, the Court warned that such situations must be dealt with an "iron hand" to prevent constitutional chaos."Time has come to deal with such situations with an iron hand; otherwise, it will lead to constitutional chaos," the Court said, according to news agency PTI.Contempt notices were issued to senior officials, including the Tamil Nadu chief secretary and the Madurai collector."The executive authorities in Tamil Nadu seem to have acted on diktat of their political bosses," the apex court added.Also Read | We will set right anybody trying to create constitutional chaos: SC on Karthigai Deepam rowTamil Nadu govt apologises, blames temple authoritiesEarlier on Wednesday, the Tamil Nadu government apologised to the top court over the failure to light the ceremonial lamp at Deepathoon, holding the temple authorities responsible for it.Despite the SC's permission, the Karthigai Deepam was lit only at its customary Uchipillayar mandapam at Thirupparankundram on November 24 and not at Deepathoon.(with inputs from PTI)

headline: Himachal records 82% rainfall deficit in Nov; min temperature dips to -5.1°C
content: Himachal Pradesh has recorded an 82 per cent rainfall deficit in November, with dry-cold conditions prevailing across the state and minimum temperatures dropping below the freezing point in tribal and high-altitude areas.The weather remained dry across the state on Friday, while dense fog was reported in Bilaspur.The state received 3.1 mm of rainfall against the normal of 17.1 mm during the month, marking a deficit of 82 per cent, according to weather data.Bilaspur, Hamirpur, Sirmaur and Una recorded a 100 per cent rainfall deficit, while Kangra reported 99 per cent, Kullu and Mandi 98 per cent, Solan 96 per cent, Shimla 91 per cent, Chamba 87 per cent, Lahaul and Spiti 66 per cent and Kinnaur 52 per cent.The Shimla meteorological centre on Friday issued a yellow warning of moderate to dense fog at isolated places in the low hills and plains of Bilaspur, Hamirpur and Mandi districts during late-night and early-morning hours till December 1.Tabo in Lahaul and Spiti district was the coldest place in the state, recording a minimum temperature of minus 5.1 degrees Celsius.Doctors have advised people to stay hydrated and warm and maintain adequate moisture indoors, warning that dry cold conditions could trigger respiratory problems, throat irritation, dry skin and seasonal infections.

headline: SC orders lighting of lamp atop disputed ‘Deepathoon’ tomorrow, issues contempt notice to top Tamil Nadu officials
content: The Supreme Court on Friday ordered the lighting of a ceremonial lamp atop a disputed pillar in Thirupparankundram in Madurai district of Tamil Nadu, three days after its previous order to do the same was defied. The court directed the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam atop the pillar, ‘Deepathoon’, once again on Saturday, November 24, observing that there was a "brazen and willful disobedience" of its November 20 order.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and VM Pancholi T asked the authorities to ensure that the devotees were allowed to participate in the ceremony, unlike before.Taking strong exception to the defiance of its order, the Supreme Court said, “Time has come to deal with such situations with iron hand, otherwise it will lead to constitutional chaos.”The Supreme Court issued contempt notice to Tamil Nadu's top officials, including the chief secretary, the director general of police (DGP), HR&CE department secretary, HR&CE commissioner, Madurai district collector, Madurai superintendent of police, temple CEO, and the chairperson and trustees of the temple board of trustees.ALSO READ: 'Complete failure’: SC suspends temple trustees amid Deepathoon row, appoints retired judgesIn a dressing down to the officials, the apex court said, “The executive authorities in Tamil Nadu seem to have acted on diktat of their political bosses.”The court was hearing contempt petitions amid row over the spot at which the Karthigai Deepam was lit in Thirupparankundram. The petitions, filed against the Madurai District Collector and other Tamil Nadu State authorities, alleged that they “willfully” disobeyed the Supreme Court's order to light the lamp atop the disputed stone pillar. “We cannot sit in silo if our order is not complied with: SC on Karthigai Deepam row. The order of this court is not invitation to negotiate; it binds State, its officers and every institution,” news agency PTI quoted the apex court as saying.The top court also suspended the board of trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thiruparankundram and superseded the temple administration through a committee comprising two judges.Ahead of the order, the Supreme Court said, “We will set right anybody trying to create constitutional chaos.”ALSO READ: 'Age-old customs': Temple board defends lighting of Karthigai Deepam at usual spot despite SC orderThe chief minister Vijay-led Tamil Nadu government has been accused of pre-planned defiance to the November 20 order issued by the apex court. Earlier on Wednesday, the state government apologised to the Supreme Court and blamed the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple authorities for the lighting of the lamp at the usual spot instead of the pillar.The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), which is one of the petitioners, told the top court on Friday that its officials were prevented by the Tamil Nadu Police from going near the ceremonial lamp at the disputed pillar atop the hill.Earlier in the day, the apex court clarified that today's hearing would be confined to the non-compliance of its November 20 order and not the main matter of the dispute over the stone pillar.(With PTI inputs)

headline: 'One community being favoured': Ex-CJI Gavai writes to President Murmu, cites low OBC, SC and ST representation in judiciary
content: NEW DELHI: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai on Friday wrote to President Droupadi Murmu alleging that judicial appointments increasingly favour candidates from a particular community, raising concerns over inadequate representation of OBCs, SCs, STs, minorities and women in the higher judiciary.Gavai expressed concern over a "growing disregard for diversity, inclusion and merit in judicial appointments and transfers", and sought presidential intervention to ensure equitable representation.In a letter dated November 27, Gavai alleged that a community comprising less than 5% of the country's population had accounted for more than 40% of Supreme Court judges in recent years, without naming the community."I am increasingly becoming concerned that recommendations are being made with a focus on appeasing and rewarding a single community," he said."A community that is under 5% of the country's population has had over 40% representation in the Supreme Court which has risen manifold in the recent past. While I admit that this is not something new and that is precisely why it is increasingly becoming unforgivable," he added.Clarifying that he was not opposed to candidates from forward communities being considered for judicial appointments, Gavai said his endeavour had always been to ensure a balance between different sections of society.Citing parliamentary data, Gavai said the representation of marginalised communities in the higher judiciary remained inadequate.According to figures presented by Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal in the Rajya Sabha in March 2025, only 22 Scheduled Caste, 16 Scheduled Tribe, 89 OBC and 37 minority candidates were among the 715 High Court judges appointed since 2018.He said roughly three out of every four appointees belonged to the general category, reflecting an imbalance in judicial appointments.Gavai further cited figures for appointments between January 2021 and January 2026, stating that nearly 80% of judicial appointments were from forward communities, while OBC representation remained below 14%."The Other Backward Classes, perhaps 40 to 50% of our people, have received under 14%. Within that pool, one community has been preferred at the Apex Court," he said.He also pointed out that the law ministry had informed a parliamentary committee about the "inequitable representation of backward and minority communities" in the higher judiciary. "Caste is not recorded for Supreme Court appointments, and that silence is itself part of the problem," he added.To underline the historical imbalance, Gavai referred to Professor George Gadbois's study of the Supreme Court's first four decades, which found that a community comprising around one-nineteenth of India's population accounted for more than a third of Supreme Court judgeships between 1950 and 1989.He said the composition of the apex court had remained largely unchanged despite 75 years of the Republic, attributing the persistence of such patterns to familiarity, networks and entrenched perceptions."Seventy-five years into the Republic, the profile of the Court has barely moved. Each of us bears some share of that failure, and I say so plainly. It is because I know how such patterns persist, through familiarity, through networks, and through unexamined ideas of who ‘looks like a Supreme Court judge’, that I can no longer stay silent," he said.Gavai also questioned recent transfers of High Court chief justices, alleging that merit had been overlooked and other considerations had influenced the decisions.He cited the case of a chief justice who was transferred from one High Court to a smaller court and subsequently to one of the country's smallest High Courts before being recommended for transfer to a prominent High Court.Gavai alleged that the latest recommendation came at the expense of another chief justice, whom he described as meritorious and hard-working, who was transferred to a smaller High Court to make way for the former.He said such decisions could demoralise the judges concerned and discourage other hardworking judicial officers, particularly those from marginalised communities.Explaining his involvement in the decisions, Gavai said he was part of the Collegium that recommended the first judge's transfers and headed it when the subsequent transfer was recommended. He also said he had led the Collegium that unanimously recommended the second judge's appointment as chief justice of a prestigious High Court on merit."It therefore raises several unanswered questions as to how a judge transferred multiple times on punitive considerations has for no obvious reasons is now being recommended to be Chief Justice of a much bigger and prominent High Court," he said.Gavai said he had consistently sought to uphold diversity and inclusion during his tenure as a Collegium member and as Chief Justice of India, ensuring representation from forward communities as well as SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women in judicial appointments.However, he alleged that recent recommendations had departed from these principles, with candidates from one particular community being favoured over others."When I was a part of the collegium and was Chief Justice of India, I always followed the principles of diversity and inclusion. Adequate representation was ensured to different sections of the society including those belonging to forward section of the society and also to the marginalised section of the society including scheduled casts, tribes, other backward classes, minorities and women, while considering candidates for recommendation for elevation to High court and Supreme Court collegium of which I was a part and later headed it," he said."However, in the recent past disturbing events have unfolded, showing complete disregard to principles of merit and inclusivity. Candidates belonging to one particular section of the society are being favoured for recommendation/elevation to the exclusion of everyone else including marginalised communities including scheduled casts, tribes, other backward classes, minorities, women and even persons from forward sections of the society who are not from a particular community," he said."I may not be misunderstood as being opposed to any section of the society in so far as the candidate belonging to forward section are duly considered and my endeavour has always been to strike balance between all the sections. However, now there compelling circumstances which support the perception that increasingly recommendations are being made with a focus on appeasing and rewarding a single community," he added.In his concluding appeal, Gavai urged President Murmu to acknowledge the issue and intervene as she deemed appropriate to ensure that all stakeholders were reminded of their constitutional duty to uphold equal representation.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: 'Time to deal with iron hand': SC raps Vijay govt over contempt of its Deepam order
content: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday issued contempt notices to top officers of the Tamil Nadu government over their failure to follow its order to light the Karthigai Deepam lamp atop the Deepathoon.Calling Tamil Nadu government's move a prima facie contempt of SC's order, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi expressed "pain and anguish" and warned that those who try to create constitutional chaos will not be spared."The first thing which comes to our mind is to express the word ALAS! as it would be relevant and appropriate to express in the present scenario. We say so for reasons assigned hereinafter and we say so with pain and anguish," the bench said.Also read: 'Deepam to be lit tomorrow': Furious SC suspends temple trust, asks CRPF to step in"The time has come to deal with the situation with an iron hand as it will lead to constitutional chaos," it added.The apex court said that the executive authorities in the state were "acting on diktats of their political boss" and held that a prima facie contempt case was made out.The bench also suspended the board of trustees of the temple and appointed two retired HC judges, Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthipan, as receivers to take over the management of the temple.The SC also handed over the security of Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and Thiruparankundram hill to CRPF.The Supreme Court also directed that the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit atop the Deepathoon on Saturday.The development came after the ceremonial lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple, rather than at Deepathoon, despite the Supreme Court's order.On November 20, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi permitted the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time interim arrangement. The order came while the Supreme Court was hearing challenges to the Madras High Court's directions on the ritual.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Delimitation row: Kharge calls oppn meet; extends invite to DMK, AAP & BJD
content: NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge has called a meeting of opposition floor leaders at his residence on Saturday.The meeting aims to formulate a joint strategy ahead of the government's likely move to reintroduce a constitutional amendment bill linked to delimitation, as cited by PTI.The meeting is scheduled for 11.30 am at Kharge's residence at 10, Rajaji Marg. Besides INDIA bloc parties, leaders of non-INDIA bloc opposition parties, including the DMK, the AAP and the BJD, have also been invited, sources said, as cited by PTI.The opposition is seeking to coordinate its response to the government's proposed move, with a special sitting of Parliament scheduled to begin on November 30.The Union Cabinet is learnt to have cleared a fresh delimitation-linked women's reservation bill on Friday, raising the possibility of its introduction during the sitting.The Lok Sabha will reconvene on November 30, while the Rajya Sabha will meet on December 2. The sittings are scheduled to conclude on December 3, subject to the requirements of government business. Separate directives for reconvening the Houses were issued by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan.The special sitting will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, as Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13 but the session was not prorogued.Meanwhile, the Congress has issued a whip to its MPs in both Houses, asking them to remain present during the special sitting. The party has also directed its MPs to reach New Delhi by November 29, a day before the Lok Sabha reconvenes.The Congress on Friday alleged that the proposed sitting was primarily aimed at pushing delimitation and had little to do with women's reservation. Describing it as a desperate move by a "nervous and rattled PM who is under siege", the party said it would oppose the move with firm resolve.The DMK has also reiterated its opposition to any change in the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats among states. Party president M K Stalin on Friday said Tamil Nadu's current 7.18 per cent share of seats in the Lower House should not be reduced under any circumstances.He also said the existing proportion of parliamentary representation among states, determined on the basis of the 1971 Census and subsequently frozen, should remain unchanged for another 25 years.In a statement, Stalin said the DMK remained firm on its demand to protect Tamil Nadu's share of seats and its proportion of representation."No change in position, no compromise, the DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu’s interests; nor will it depart from its principles," he said.Kharge's meeting is aimed at bringing opposition parties together ahead of the special sitting, with the participation of parties outside the INDIA bloc also expected to be significant in shaping a coordinated response to the proposed legislation.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 1 mn views on Facebook vs Instagram vs YouTube: Why 2 different paychecks? Why viewer location rules creator economy
content: Two creators get one million views each. One earns a lot. The other earns very little. This confuses many new creators. The views look the same. The money is not. The reasons lie in how each platform pays and who is watching.Note: The figures below are rough ideas, not exact rates. Earnings often vary by niche, season and platform policy. Please check current official rules before planning your income.A view means different things on each platform. On YouTube, a view often means someone chose to watch. They may have searched for your topic. On Instagram and Facebook, many views come from autoplay. People scroll fast, and a video plays for a few seconds. That counts as a view.Advertisers care about attention. A viewer who watches fully is more useful than one who scrolls past. So, the same one million views can carry very different values.How each platform paysYouTube has a long-running ad revenue share. Ads run before, during, or after videos. Creators who qualify for the Partner Programme get a share of ad income. Long videos can carry more ads, so they can earn more per view.Facebook pays through in-stream ads in longer videos and through some monetisation programmes. Rules on length and eligibility apply. Reels and short clips usually earn less than longer content.Instagram has relied less on direct ad sharing. Many influencers earn mainly through brand deals, bonuses and affiliate links. A million views may bring little platform money, but it can attract sponsors.Why viewer location rules the creator economyThis is the biggest reason for pay gaps. Advertisers pay more to reach people in richer markets. A viewer in the US, UK or Australia is worth more to advertisers. Those viewers have higher spending power. So, ad rates there are higher.Now compare two creators. One has a million views, mostly from India. The other has a million views, mostly from the US. The second creator can earn several times more. Same views, different paycheck.The rate advertisers pay is often called CPM. It means cost per thousand views. India's CPM is usually lower than that of Western countries. This does not mean Indian viewers matter less. It reflects how advertisers price their budgets.Suppose a video gets one million views and every view includes an ad. At an illustrative Indian CPM of ₹80, advertisers would pay ₹80,000. At a US CPM of ₹600, they would pay ₹6 lakh. That’s 7.5 times more for the same views.Advertisers often bid more for audiences with greater buying power. Bigger budgets and stronger competition can also push rates up. An Indian finance channel may still earn more than a US comedy channel. Creators receive a share of ad spending, and some views show no ads.Niche matters tooSome topics attract high-paying advertisers. Finance, insurance, software, and education usually pay more. Entertainment and comedy often pay less. A creator who explains investing can earn more than a prank channel with equal views.Advertisers want buyers for costly products. So, they bid more for viewers interested in those topics.Other things that change your incomeWatch time: Longer watch time often helps earnings and reach.Ad inventory: More ad slots can mean more income.Season: Ad rates often rise during festivals and year-end sales.Audience age: Advertisers like working adults with spending power.Content safety: Videos suited for brands attract better ads.What creators can doDo not chase views alone. Look at your analytics. Check where your viewers live and what they watch. Study your audience age and watch time.Build more than one income stream. Use brand deals, affiliate links, courses and memberships or subscriptions. These do not depend on ad rates. Instagram creators, in particular, often earn more from sponsors than from the platform.Create content that serves a clear niche. A smaller, focused audience can earn more than a large, random one.Also be patient. Earnings rise as your channel grows, and your audience becomes more valuable.One million views is a nice number. But it is not a salary. The platform, the viewer's country, the topic and the format all shape your pay. Understand these factors early. Then, you can plan your content and your income with confidence.

headline: Union Cabinet clears fresh women's quota bill linked to delimitation
content: The Union Cabinet met here on Friday and is learnt to have cleared a fresh delimitation-linked women's reservation bill, which is likely to be brought before the special sitting of Parliament beginning next week.Sources said the bill was brought before the special meeting of the Union Cabinet, which is expected to accord its nod to the fresh bill with some amendments to ensure that no state loses its representation in the Lok Sabha in proportion to other states after delimitation.The Cabinet meeting was chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and was convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth to discuss the bill, which the government is keen to get passed in the special sitting of Parliament starting Monday.The bill was brought in Parliament by the government during a special sitting in April, but it could not pass muster in the Lok Sabha.The government has now claimed that it has the numbers to get the legislation through.A two-thirds majority in both houses of Parliament is a must for a Constitutional amendment bill to get cleared.Sources said the DMK and NCP, besides BRS, are expected to support the bill.The opposition INDIA bloc is against the legislation and will be meeting on Saturday to discuss its strategy.

headline: ’Nation will be closely watching Parliament on Nov 30: CJP’s Ashutosh Ranka as Centre plans to take up delimitation bill
content: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leader Ashutosh Ranka on Friday warned political parties against changing their stance on the proposed delimitation exercise ahead of a special Parliament session, alleging that the Centre was using women's reservation in an attempt to manipulate electoral boundaries.What did Ashutosh Ranka say about delimitation?In a social media post, Ranka said that the country would closely watch the proceedings of the special Parliament session, which will commence on November 30. He alleged that the proposed delimitation exercise could disproportionately increase parliamentary representation in states that had lagged in population control.Ranka wrote, "The nation will be closely watching the Parliament proceedings on this Nov 30th. Under the garb of the women reservation bill, which everyone should support, the govt wants to manipulate electoral boundaries, disproportionately increase seats in states which have lagged behind in population control."He added, "While BJP has had its stand clear on both the issues, what the country should watch out for are those parties and politicians who will be switching sides, for either they would have been paid off, or have lost spine completely. Betrayal of people’s mandate won’t be forgiven this time." While the CJP activist maintained that the women's reservation issue deserved support across political parties, he alleged that the Centre was using the legislation as a pretext to push the Delimitation Bill, ANI reported.His remarks come amid an intensifying political debate over the proposed delimitation exercise and the implementation of the women's reservation law ahead of the reconvened Parliament session.Special Parliament session to begin on November 30On Thursday, the Lok Sabha Secretariat announced that the second part of the Eighth Session of the 18th Lok Sabha would begin on November 30 (Monday) and was expected to conclude on December 3 (Thursday), subject to the exigencies of government business.Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju said the Centre had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2, respectively, to take up key government business.The announcement has further fuelled speculation about the possibility of the Delimitation Bill and the Women's Reservation Bill being taken up during the sittings. However, the government has not clarified which Bills will be considered.What is the proposed Delimitation Bill?Parliament last convened during the Monsoon Session, which ended on August 13, with both Houses being adjourned sine die. The proposed Delimitation Bill seeks to increase the total strength of the Lok Sabha to 850 seats.While the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), led by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), has maintained that the proposed delimitation exercise is a constitutional necessity to reflect new census data and facilitate the implementation of 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, the INDIA bloc, led by the Congress, has demanded the immediate implementation of the women's reservation law and opposed linking it to the delimitation exercise.The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, was first introduced in the Lok Sabha on April 16. It seeks to increase the strength of the Lower House to 850 seats and facilitate the implementation of the Women's Reservation Bill, passed in 2023.However, the Bill failed to secure the constitutionally required special two-thirds majority of members present and voting in Parliament and was consequently not passed.(with ANI inputs)

headline: Congress’s Karti Chidambaram asks DMK to explain ‘U-turn’ if it decides to support delimitation bill
content: Congress leader Karti Chidambaram on Friday asked the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) to explain its “U-turn” if it decides to support the proposed delimitation bill, after previously opposing the legislation, ahead of the special sitting of Parliament beginning November 30.“It is really for them to explain what the circumstances and considerations are for them to make a complete U-turn — from opposing the delimitation bill to now supporting it,” he said.Chidambaram called “fair delimitation” a misnomer. “Even though the proportion is maintained, absolute numbers matter, and in absolute numbers, the South will be disadvantaged. Further, this delimitation will lead to gerrymandering, which will completely skew the electoral map in favour of the BJP [Bharatiya Janata Party], particularly in the north of India and in certain other states,” said Chidambaram. He added that while it might not have a direct impact on Tamil Nadu, it will impact all over India, which will affect the outcome of the elections. The comments came a day after the Union government on Thursday said a special sitting of Parliament will be held from November 30, fuelling speculation that it was looking to reintroduce a constitutional amendment and the delimitation bills to roll out women’s quota that did not get the required support earlier in April.A united Opposition defeated the 131st Constitution (Amendment) Bill, which sought to raise the Lok Sabha ceiling to 850 and implement 33% reservation for women in time for the 2029 polls, despite Union home minister Amit Shah’s last-minute offer to incorporate a 50% proportional rise for all states into the bill.The government withdrew two other linked bills, one for delimitation based on the latest available census, effectively the 2011 one, and another implementing the changes in Union Territories.The DMK, which has 22 members, left the Opposition bloc in May after the Congress tied up with ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam in Tamil Nadu.Since April, 20 out of 28 Trinamool Congress lawmakers have joined the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India and said they will support the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance. Six of nine Shiv Sena (UBT) lawmakers joined the NDA constituent, Shiv Sena.The Nationalist Congress Party - Sharadchandra Pawar, which has eight lawmakers, has said it will consider the bill once it reads the text of the legislation and is likely to back the government.

headline: What really happened at Bihar MLA Anant Singh’s daughter’s wedding? Reports say chaos; 25 lakh rasgullas gone in seconds
content: The wedding of Bihar MLA Anant Singh’s daughter, Shivangi Singh, has been drawing attention online, with coverage now extending beyond India. Shivangi married Rishikesh Kumar, son of CRPF Commandant Ranvijay Kumar, and the event became a talking point, not just for the grandeur of the celebrations but also for the chaos that followed.The wedding took place on Wednesday at Singh’s ancestral home in Nadawan village in Patna. The Mokama MLA, also known as ‘Chhote Sarkar’ across the state, reportedly sent out an open invitation for people to attend the wedding, resulting in a massive turnout. He said, "Koi cinema thodi hai jo ticket lagega (this is not a cinema hall, so nobody needs a ticket)," NDTV reported. With nearly half a million people reportedly present, a figure that has not been verified by Mint, what followed was utter chaos.Arrangements made for 5 lakh guests, 150 dishes preparedThe family had made arrangements for an estimated four to five lakh guests, with a spread featuring more than 150 dishes. Over 500 halwais (traditional cooks), assisted by hundreds of workers, had been preparing food for several days across four to five massive pandals. A temporary kitchen stretching over 100 feet was set up, with 12 additional tents added when the arrangements fell short.Milk was brought in through tankers, some carrying as much as 10,000 kg. According to reports, 25 lakh rasgullas have been prepared for guests, while another 50 lakh gulab jamuns were made. By evening, a huge crowd had gathered for the feast, as workers distributed plates to attendees.Videos on social media show guests scrambling for sweetsAccording to NDTV, videos from the wedding surfaced on social media platforms, capturing several aspects of the spectacle, including the chaos. The crowd reportedly overwhelmed the arrangements, after which guests got creative with their eating arrangements. They started using drinking glasses as plates, scooped food straight from giant cooking vessels, and even carried it away in cardboard cartons. Other videos that have taken social media by storm show guests scrambling for sweets. The sweet counter reportedly turned into a battleground, with rasgullas disappearing in the blink of an eye. Describing the situation, one guest in a viral video said, “Getting food here is like winning a war.”The huge turnout also resulted in a massive traffic jam stretching anywhere between five and 10 kilometres, with people arriving in cars, on tractors and on foot.To entertain the guests, Singh did not arrange for a DJ. Instead, a horse race was scheduled. Some spectators found an unusual vantage point atop electricity pylons, where young men climbed the steel structures to watch horses race along a 12-bigha track. Below them, crowds lined the course on all sides, while a new Mahindra Thar stood as the prize for the winner.A total of 52 horses were brought in, with riders from Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Rajasthan and other states. As the contest progressed, the crowd pushed past the edges and spilled onto the track, prompting the organisers to halt the event and reschedule it.The horse race was not the only attraction. Singh also had a specially built helipad for his VIP guests, who included former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, who flew in from Uttar Pradesh.Some of the other highlights included the celebrity-like entrance for Singh himself, who rose through the sunroof of an SUV amid a sea of supporters pressed around it. A report noted that he "was arriving for his daughter's wedding, and he did it in a style that would upstage any groom".The groom, Rishikesh Kumar, who holds an MBA degree from Georgia State University in Atlanta, reportedly received a white Land Rover Defender worth ₹3 crore, along with a 100-gram gold chain and an 80-gram gold bracelet.

headline: Cabinet okays 50% rise in Lok Sabha seats for all states, freeze on current share till 2051 in delimitation move
content: The Union Cabinet on Friday approved a Constitution amendment bill aimed at implementing women's reservation through delimitation, with a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats for all states. Each state's current share of seats will stay frozen until 2051.The move looks to address criticism of the Centre's previous attempt in April, when the Opposition blocked the bill in the Lok Sabha. Critics argued that the promise of a uniform increase was made in speeches but not mentioned in the bill.Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired Friday's cabinet meeting, a day after the Lok Sabha Secretariat announced that a four-day Parliament sitting would begin on November 30 and likely conclude on December 3, subject to exigencies.The move brought the focus back to the 131st Constitution Amendment Bill, which faltered in the Lok Sabha on April 17 during a three-day special sitting of the extended budget session.The bill sought to raise the Lok Sabha seat ceiling from 550 to 850, with up to 815 members from the states and 35 from Union Territories. It also aimed to implement 33% reservation for women in time for the 2029 polls. The Lower House has 543 members.At that time, the bill received 298 votes in favour and 230 against. It needed two-thirds of members present and voting, which was 352. It was the first time a constitutional amendment brought by the government had been defeated since the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) came to power in 2014.A united Opposition thwarted the bill despite a last-minute offer by Union home minister Amit Shah for a 50% rise in seats for every state. Subsequently, the government withdrew two linked bills, which needed a simple majority.One mandated delimitation on the basis of the latest available census, effectively the 2011 one. The other implemented the changes in Union Territories.The biggest sticking point was how the extra seats would be shared among states. If all 850 seats were allotted by population on the 2011 Census, the projection was that the share of southern states in Lok Sabha could drop.Critics argued that North India could gain more seats due to its population, while South India, which contributes around 30-31% of the GDP, could lose out. Southern states have time and again flagged that population alone should not be the criterion for such revisions or additions.The government tried to allay concerns and said every state’s seats would go up by the same proportion, proposing a 50% increase for all states. But the text of the three bills did not explicitly mention a fixed proportion or a freeze on each state’s share.The Opposition said it supported women’s reservation but not the delimitation bill, with its leaders alleging that the government’s promises were spoken in the House, not written into the bills. The ruling side said the Opposition's stand was detrimental to women's empowerment.This time around, because the NDA does not have a two-thirds majority needed for Constitution amendment bills on its own, any fresh attempt will depend on neutral parties and fence-sitters. Every vote, and every absence, will count. The bill is likely to be introduced during the special sitting of Parliament, which begins on November 30.The move brought the focus back to the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, which failed in the Lok Sabha on April 17 during a three-day special sitting. After the defeat, the government withdrew two linked bills, which needed only a simple majority.The delimitation bill would have set up a commission headed by a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge to readjust seats based on the latest published census, effectively the 2011 one. headline: NCP (SP) to first examine delimitation bill before making its stand clear, says Supriya Sule
content: Mumbai, Amid a buzz that the NCP may support the government on the delimitation bill, its leader Supriya Sule on Friday said her party would first examine the draft legislation if it is brought for discussion in Parliament before making its stand clear on it.A special sitting of Parliament has been convened from November 30 to transact essential business, amid indications that the government may reintroduce a constitutional amendment linking the rollout of women's reservation to delimitation.Talking to reporters here, the NCP working president said she had not seen the text of the bill and did not know the session's agenda. "There is no agenda as yet. You will know on the floor of the Lok Sabha," Sule said in response to repeated queries on the party's stand over the delimitation bill.She said she had not received any invitation for any meeting so far.Sule maintained that it was difficult to comment without seeing the document in hand."Until the bill comes in hand, how can I tell?... I haven't even received the syllabus. So only after getting the syllabus can I say something," she said.The NCP on Friday issued a whip directing all its eight Lok Sabha MPs to remain present in the House from November 30 during the special session of Parliament. There is speculation that the party may support the government on the delimitation bill.When asked about coordination within the opposition INDIA bloc, Sule said she speaks to them regularly on issues concerning the country."We speak to each other every day about issues, such as air, water, farmers and inflation," the Baramati MP said.Commenting on Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Raut's remarks warning parties supporting delimitation, Sule described him as a senior leader of the state and country who has the full right to speak.Replying to questions, she clarified her earlier remarks distinguishing between a guardian minister's role and guardianship, saying Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar is the guardian minister for the entire Pune district and not just Pune city.Talking about incidents of crime allegedly on the rise in Pune city, Sule said the responsibility rests with the state's Home Ministry held by the Chief Minister because rising crime harms Pune's image, affects investments, and impacts students coming to study."If crime increases, will anyone invest there?" she asked, adding that she had already raised the issue in detail with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.On protests by the NCP women's wing against Rohit Pawar's remarks targeting Sunetra Pawar, Sule said Rohit had already expressed regret and apologised."Once a person expresses regret, tell me, doesn't the matter end? And he said sorry, right?" she said, appealing to party workers not to stretch the issue and offering an apology on Rohit's behalf if anyone's feelings were hurt.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: BKU (Doaba) leaders meet Punjab Minister Khuddian over pending sugarcane dues; government assures payment of Rs 27.84 cr
content: A delegation of the Bharatiya Kisan Union (Doaba), led by its president Manjit Singh Rai, held a meeting with Punjab Cabinet Minister Gurmeet Singh Khuddian in Chandigarh on Friday to discuss the long-pending payments owed to sugarcane farmers by Golden Sandhar Sugar Mill, Phagwara.Rai told that the state government representatives had assured the union that the outstanding arrears amounting to Rs 27.84 crore would be cleared through the sale of 10 kanals of land situated within the premises of Golden Sandhar Sugar Mill, Phagwara. He added that the Deputy Commissioner, Kapurthala, had been directed to initiate the process for the sale of the land.Rai further stated that the amount generated through the sale of electricity produced by the sugar mill would also be deposited directly into the bank accounts of sugarcane farmers to clear their pending dues.Regarding the additional outstanding amount of Rs 18.93 crore for the 2025-26 crushing season, against the government subsidy of Rs 68.50 per quintal of sugarcane, Rai said that the Cabinet Minister had assured them that the payments would begin reaching farmers’ bank accounts after 10 days.The BKU (Doaba) delegation also raised the demand for taking Golden Sandhar Sugar Mill under the control of the Punjab Government and ensuring its operation during the ongoing 2026-27 crushing season. According to Rai, the state government representatives agreed to the proposal.Describing the meeting as positive and constructive, Rai said that the government representatives had given firm assurances regarding the clearance of pending payments and the future functioning of the sugar mill.He further announced that the union would soon convene a meeting to deliberate on the assurances received from the government and decide its further course of action regarding the pending sugarcane arrears and the operation of the mill.
