headline: ‘One community favoured’: Ex-CJI Gavai writes to President, alleges bias in collegium picks
content: Former Chief Justice of India Bhushan R Gavai has written to President Droupadi Murmu alleging that the Supreme Court collegium is increasingly favouring candidates from “one particular section of the society” for elevation to constitutional courts, to the exclusion of scheduled castes, scheduled tribes, other backward classes, minorities and women.In a strongly worded letter dated November 27, Gavai, who headed the Supreme Court collegium for nearly six months before demitting office in November 2025, alleged that recent recommendations reflected a disturbing disregard for merit, diversity and inclusivity, and appeared increasingly driven by an effort to “appease and reward a single community”. He urged the President to intervene to ensure that all stakeholders discharge their constitutional responsibility of securing adequate representation in the higher judiciary.Although the former CJI did not name the community, his reference to a group accounting for less than 5% of India’s population having secured more than 40% representation in the Supreme Court, with its share rising “manifold in the recent past”, appeared to point to Brahmins. People aware of the matter confirmed that the former CJI’s letter alludes to Brahmins.“While I admit that this is not something new and that is precisely why it is increasingly becoming unforgivable,” he wrote, arguing that the historical pattern of disproportionate representation had persisted for decades without meaningful correction.The collegium in the top court currently comprises CJI Surya Kant, and justices Vikram Nath, BV Nagarathna, MM Sundresh and PS Narasimha.Writing to the President as a former head of the collegium, justice Gavai said he had consistently followed the principles of diversity and inclusion while recommending candidates for elevation to the high courts and the Supreme Court. He maintained that his approach sought to balance representation from forward communities with that of marginalised sections, including SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women.“Candidates belonging to one particular section of the society are being favoured for recommendation/elevation to the exclusion of everyone else including marginalized communities,” he wrote, adding that even persons from forward communities who did not belong to the particular group were being overlooked.To underline the extent of the imbalance, justice Gavai cited parliamentary data on judicial appointments. He referred to the Union law minister’s response in the Rajya Sabha in March 2025, which showed that of the 715 high court judges appointed since 2018, only 22 belonged to the SCs, 16 to the STs, 89 to the OBCs and 37 to minority communities, with roughly three-fourths coming from the general category.He also cited figures for appointments between January 2021 and January 2026, arguing that the share of forward communities was close to 80%, while OBCs, who account for a substantially larger share of the population, received less than 14% representation. The letter pointed out that caste-wise data was not maintained for appointments to the Supreme Court, describing the absence of such information as part of the problem.Justice Gavai’s own tenure as CJI, however, saw the collegium place details of its high court recommendations in the public domain, including the social background of candidates. Between May 14 and November 23, 2025, the collegium headed by him recommended 129 names for high court appointments, of which 93 were cleared by the government, according to the Supreme Court’s published data. These included 10 judges from the Scheduled Caste community, 11 from OBC and backward classes, 13 from minority communities and 15 women.The collegium also recommended five judges for elevation to the Supreme Court during his tenure --justices NV Anjaria, Vijay Bishnoi, AS Chandurkar, Alok Aradhe and Vipul M Pancholi.The former CJI also flagged what he described as questionable decisions in the transfer and subsequent elevation of high court chief justices. Without naming the judges concerned, he referred to a chief justice who, after being transferred successively to smaller high courts, was now being recommended to head a prominent high court, allegedly on account of belonging to the particular community. At the same time, a “meritorious and hard-working” chief justice was transferred to a smaller high court to make way for him, he alleged.Justice Gavai said he had been part of the collegium that recommended the earlier transfers of the first judge and had headed it when the second judge was unanimously recommended as chief justice of a prestigious high court on the basis of merit. He also cited another instance of a judge allegedly being transferred on punitive considerations before subsequently being rewarded with the chief justiceship of a large and prominent high court.While saying that he was aware of the factors that had weighed with the collegium in making these recommendations and transfers, justice Gavai declined to disclose them, citing propriety and judicial discipline. He said the instances nevertheless raised unanswered questions about the criteria being applied and the apparent departure from considerations of merit.Invoking Article 124(2) of the Constitution, which provides for the appointment of Supreme Court judges by the President, Gavai said the judicial interpretation that has made collegium recommendations decisive had neither rendered the collegium unaccountable nor absolved the President of her constitutional responsibility.“The Constitution vests the appointment of judges of Supreme Court in you under Article 124(2),” he said in the letter, adding that the President’s high office continued to have a duty to “preserve, protect and defend the Constitution”.He also underlined that the executive and Parliament were equal stakeholders in judicial appointments and said successive governments had urged the collegium to consider suitable candidates from marginalised communities to improve diversity. The responsibility, he said, was shared by all constitutional stakeholders and could not be left to the judiciary alone.Justice Gavai concluded by urging Murmu to acknowledge the concerns and intervene, as she deemed appropriate, to remind all stakeholders of their constitutional obligation to ensure equal representation in one of the most significant pillars of Indian democracy.The letter was also marked to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal.

headline: Bengal govt schools to introduce biometric attendance from January 2027: Minister
content: The West Bengal government will introduce a biometric attendance system for teachers and students at all state-run and state-aided schools from January 2, 2027, school education minister Dipak Barman has said.There are around 69,000 primary, secondary and higher secondary schools that the West Bengal government either runs or provides funds for.Barman said, the number of students and teachers are around 16 million and 0.4 million respectively.“A modern attendance registration system is necessary. Currently, many students don’t come to school but teachers manually mark their attendance later out of sympathy because they do not want to see the students disqualified from taking board exams. We have to get the actual number of attendees and absentees,” Barman said.Also Read: Over 2 lakh school students in Ludhiana yet to finish biometric update“We will use AI-powered biometric systems for teachers and students in all schools from January 2. It will be installed in 150 schools right now for performance evaluation,” he added.Until now, schools run or aided by the Bengal government have been using roll-call for students and signing of registers for teachers.“Given the poor infrastructure in many district schools, covering all institutions by the January 2 deadline may not be easy. The government is aware of these factors,” a state official said, requesting anonymity.Also Read:Haryana: Remove biometric verification for procurement, says HoodaThe school teachers’ unions in Bengal did not release a statement on the upcoming attendance system till Friday afternoon. The copy will be updated whenever it is received.

headline: EPFOs AIF investment plan could improve subscriber returns, government-backed funds to be initial route: Trustee
content: New Delhi [India], November 27 (ANI): The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation's (EPFO) proposed investment of up to 3 per cent of its fresh annual accretions in alternative investment funds (AIFs) could diversify its portfolio and improve subscriber returns over the long term, Vineet Nahata, Member of the Central Board of Trustees, EPFO, said.Speaking to ANI on the sidelines of the 17th Capital Market Conference organised by ASSOCHAM, Nahata said EPFO was considering government-backed entities such as the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) and SIDBI-managed Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 for initial investments."As far as EPFO is concerned, this is the first time a maiden step is being taken to test the waters in this area," he said.His remarks come after the Central Board of Trustees gave in-principle approval on November 19 to invest up to 3 per cent of fresh accretions in eligible AIFs, within the existing investment ceiling and subject to safeguards.The Rs 10,000-crore Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 invests through SEBI-registered AIFs to support deep technology, innovative manufacturing and early-stage businesses."Both are government-backed. So safety and security is assured and the returns time will tell how the investors can benefit from it," Nahata said.The CBT meeting also approved a voluntary Systematic Withdrawal Plan, allowing retiring members to receive their PF savings in periodic instalments while the remaining corpus continues to generate returns.It also reduced the minimum PF balance requirement from 25 per cent to 10 per cent and the waiting period for final withdrawal from 12 months to two months.On the broader capital market, Nahata welcomed SEBI's efforts to deepen India's debt markets through better bond market-making and wider retail participation. He said these measures could make the market more competitive and resilient while giving retail investors greater access to bonds as an alternative to conventional bank fixed deposits.Nahata further said his company, Powergill Treasuries, had sought wider introduction of a bond margin trading facility and a reduction in the existing 50 per cent haircut to allow financing of up to 95 per cent of bond value. He said this could improve liquidity and make it easier for retail investors to exit bond investments. (ANI)(This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

headline: 8th Pay Commission: Pensioners write to PM Modi, seek equal benefits for pre-2026 retirees, 20% relief among 11 demands
content: The 8th Pay Commission is expected to review the salaries and pensions of central government employees. Ahead of this, a pensioners' association has asked the Centre to ensure that employees who retired before January 1, 2026, also get the benefit of revised pensions.In a memorandum submitted to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 25, the Forum of Civil Pensioners Associations (FCPA) raised 11 demands related to pensions, retirement benefits and healthcare. It has also sought a temporary pension increase of at least 20% until the new recommendations are implemented.These demands cover retired employees and family pensioners from Central government departments, railways, defence, BSNL, MTNL, banks and autonomous bodies. The association said pensioners who retired before January 1, 2026, should get the same benefits as those retiring after that date if they have the same rank and length of service.Here are 11 key demands raised by the association:Include pre-2026 retirees under the 8th Pay Commission - The FCPA has asked the government to amend the 8th CPC's ToR to explicitly include pension revision for employees who retired before January 1, 2026. It has argued that the date of retirement should not determine whether an employee receives revised pension benefits.Withdraw the 2025 pension validation law - The association has called for the withdrawal of the Validation of Pension Rules Act, 2025, enacted through the Finance Act, 2025. It argues that the law goes against the Supreme Court's 1982 D.S. Nakara vs Union of India judgment, which established the principle of pension parity. According to the association, the law could affect the equal treatment of pensioners who retired before 2026.Restore the Old Pension Scheme - The FCPA has demanded the restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) for employees recruited on or after January 1, 2004. It has also called for the discontinuation of the National Pension System (NPS) and the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS).Clear pending BSNL and MTNL pension revision - The association has sought the implementation of pending pension revision for employees absorbed into BSNL and MTNL. It wants the revised pensions to take effect retrospectively from January 1, 2017.Revise pensions of retired bank employees - The FCPA has called for periodic pension revision for retired bank employees on the lines of the system followed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).Extend 8th CPC benefits to autonomous bodies - The association wants employees of autonomous bodies to be covered under the 8th Pay Commission framework. It has also sought Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) facilities for their pensioners, similar to those available to Central government pensioners.Merge 50% DA and DR with basic pay and pension - The FCPA has demanded that 50% of dearness allowance (DA) and dearness relief (DR) be merged with basic pay and pension as an interim measure. It wants this arrangement to remain in place until the 8th CPC recommendations are implemented.Provide at least 20% interim pension relief - The association has sought an additional relief of at least 20% of the existing pension for pensioners and family pensioners. It says the increase should be provided while they wait for the next pension revision under the 8th CPC.Reduce the pension commutation recovery period - Pension commutation allows retirees to receive a portion of their pension as a lump sum in exchange for a reduction in their monthly pension. At present, the commuted portion is restored after 15 years. The FCPA wants the recovery period reduced to 10 years and eight months. It argues that pension deductions recover the commuted amount within this period.Improve CGHS and medical facilities - The association has called for at least one CGHS wellness centre in every district, along with more doctors, medical staff, medicines and empanelled hospitals. It has also sought cashless treatment without administrative hurdles and an increase in the Fixed Medical Allowance to ₹5,000.Ensure pension parity under OROP - The FCPA has demanded equal pension benefits under the One Rank One Pension (OROP) scheme, without discrimination between employees who retired before and after January 1, 2026. The association has urged the government to consider these demands while finalising the 8th Pay Commission's framework and pension-related recommendations.

headline: Kiren Rijiju urges MPs to ensure smooth functioning of Parliament during special sitting
content: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Friday appealed to MPs across party lines to ensure the smooth functioning of Parliament during its four-day special sitting from November 30, amid Opposition criticism of the government's proposed delimitation exercise and changes to the women's reservation framework.The Union minister said the government had called the sitting to discuss important bills and business concerning the country. The Lok Sabha will meet on November 30 and December 1, while the Rajya Sabha will sit on December 2 and 3."When the government calls a session or special session, that means there are important Bills or business for the nation," Rijiju said, reported PTI. ALSO READ | Stalin says won’t compromise on Tamil Nadu's share in Lok Sabha ahead of Parliament sitting He said MPs had an important responsibility to ensure Parliament functions smoothly and that all members get an opportunity to participate in debates."We are proud of our democracy and we must ensure Parliament functions smoothly; India should set an example," he said. Rijiju also said MPs were free to agree or disagree with the government, but their views should be expressed within parliamentary rules and conventions."MPs have rights, all freedom to agree or disagree; but that has to be put in proper perspective, through rules, conventions," he said.What is the government's proposal?The proposed constitutional amendment seeks to increase the Lok Sabha's maximum strength from 550 to 850, with up to 815 seats for states and 35 for Union Territories. The accompanying delimitation exercise would redraw constituency boundaries and determine representation.The government has linked the expansion to implementing 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies ahead of the 2029 general elections.ALSO READ | NDA may be closer to majority on delimitation, women's quota after Opposition churnThe earlier attempt to pass the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, was defeated in the Lok Sabha on April 17. It received 298 votes in favour and 230 against, falling 54 votes short of the 352 needed for a two-thirds majority among the 528 members who voted.The 2023 Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, or the 106th Constitutional Amendment, already provides for 33% reservation for women. However, its implementation is linked to a Census and a subsequent delimitation exercise. The April Bill sought to change this framework.Opposition questions government's plansCongress general secretary Jairam Ramesh on Friday accused the government of trying to secure a “fraudulent two-thirds majority” in the Lok Sabha to pass a constitutional amendment linked to delimitation. He called the proposed move an “assault” on the Constitution and said the party would oppose it.ALSO READ | As delimitation returns to focus, the women’s quota, the seat-share row and the numbersRamesh said the Congress wanted the Lok Sabha's existing strength and the state-wise distribution of seats to remain unchanged for another 25 years. It also wants the 33% women's quota, including a sub-quota for women from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, implemented from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.He argued that the upcoming sitting was focused on delimitation rather than women's reservation, pointing out that Parliament had already passed the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam in 2023. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also criticised the proposed delimitation exercise, saying, “‘Delimitation’ will prove to be the biggest mistake in the BJP’s politics.” DMK president MK Stalin reiterated that the party would not compromise on Tamil Nadu's share of Lok Sabha seats amid the proposed delimitation exercise. “The DMK remains firm on both these positions today and will continue to do so. There is no change in this position, and there is no question of compromise,” he said in a post on X.He demanded that the state's current 7.18% share be maintained even if the total number of seats increases, and that the existing distribution of seats among states, based on the 1971 Census, be frozen for another 25 years.

headline: New Zealand Introduces New Online System For Graduate Work Visa Applications
content: Immigration New Zealand, the operational processing arm of the country's immigration system, announced on November 23 that applications for Post-Study Work Visas and Short-Term Graduate Work Visas had moved to its enhanced Immigration Online system.Applicants for both Post-Study Work Visas and Short-Term Graduate Work Visas must apply within three months of their student visa expiring. The deadline is six months for PhD students. According to the official statement, the enhanced Immigration Online system offers a more streamlined application experience, makes it easier for applicants to track the progress of their applications and reflects the latest visa settings and requirements. Meanwhile, from November 16, 2026, the duration of Post-Study Work Visas was extended for Indian graduates who hold New Zealand PhDs. These graduates are now eligible for visas of up to four years, compared with the previous maximum duration of three years. The Post-Study Work Visa allows international students to stay and work in New Zealand after completing their studies. The duration of the visa depends on the qualification completed and can be up to three years, or four years for eligible Indian PhD graduates. Apply within the permitted period after their student visa expires. The deadline may be three, six or 12 months, depending on the qualification and the student visa held.

headline: Cabinet clears 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across states, ceiling to remain till 2051: Sources
content: NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday approved a proposal to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha by 50% across states, with the revised ceiling to remain in place until 2051, sources told TOI.The decision comes ahead of the special sitting of Parliament beginning November 30, during which the government is expected to take up changes to the delimitation-linked Women's Reservation Bill.The proposed increase in Lok Sabha seats is understood to be part of the government's efforts to address concerns over the impact of delimitation on the representation of states, particularly those in southern India. Earlier reports had indicated that the government was considering a formula to increase seats by 50% across states while retaining their existing inter-state share based on the 1971 Census.The Cabinet meeting, chaired by PM Modi, was convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth, with all ministers asked to remain present, sources told ANI.The government is considering amendments to the earlier legislation, which seeks to provide 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. The proposed changes follow the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha in April.The earlier Bill linked the implementation of women's reservation to delimitation and proposed increasing the strength of the Lok Sabha from the existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850.The special sitting of Parliament will begin with the Lok Sabha reconvening on November 30, while the Rajya Sabha will meet from December 2. The sittings are expected to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Supreme Court dismisses plea against Italian leader’s ‘vote chor’ slogan at Telangana event
content: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a petition seeking action against an Italian political functionary for raising a “demeaning political slogan” at Bharat Summit 2026 in Telangana and to pull down social media posts carrying such derogatory content.A bench of justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh said, “Why have you filed a petition under Article 32 of the Constitution? You can file a complaint against the person,” as it refused to entertain the petition filed by a lawyer Zahid Ali.The petition argued by advocate Syed Rizvan Ahmad said that the objectionable comments were made by Giacomo Filibeck, an Italian political representative and Secretary-General of the Party of European Socialists, at a public event in India and a mechanism should be put in place to regulate the speeches made by foreigners on Indian soil.The controversial sloganFilibeck, while participating at the event organised on November 13 and 14 by the Telangana government, had said, “vote chor, gaddi chhod” – the political slogan coined by the Congress amid controversy over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The bench said, “Let the government regulate freedom of speech of citizens first and then regulate that of foreigners,” while adding, “The petition is dismissed.”‘Petition not politically motivated’Ahmed said that the petition is not politically motivated as it has not mentioned Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, the Indian National Congress or the Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy who were present at the site when the comments were made.“So according to you, they have freedom to say anything,” the bench remarked as Ahmed pointed out that a foreigner cannot make political slogans when the law does not permit him to do so. “The government must regulate the speeches made by foreigners. It can even take steps to pull down social media posts carrying these speeches,” Ahmed said.The petition filed through advocate Pulkit Agarwal said, “The Italian political representative not only raised the vulgar, derogatory and demeaning political slogan but also translated the same for other foreign delegates. The aforesaid derogatory and disrespecting slogan was in bad taste and derogatory to India's democratic processes, and a slogan that has been prominently associated with the Indian National Congress and its political campaign.”The plea sought a direction to the Centre to take action under the provisions of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, the applicable visa conditions and other relevant laws to ensure that foreign political representatives, delegates and dignitaries visiting India do not engage in political or anti- government activities.Under section 7 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, the Centre is empowered to regulate or restrict the presence and activities of foreign nationals in India through appropriate orders, directions and instructions. Further, section 23 provides consequences for violation of visa conditions and other specified statutory requirements.

headline: Government appeals to MPs to ensure smooth special sitting of Parliament
content: New Delhi: The Union government on Friday appealed to all MPs to ensure a smooth special sitting of Parliament that will discuss "very important bills.".A day after a four-day sitting of Parliament was announced, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said it is a joint responsibility of all members to ensure that the world's largest parliamentary democracy, India, sets an example.."My appeal to the members of Parliament is to ensure that Parliament functions smoothly. We are proud of our democracy, and we must ensure that Parliament functions smoothly," he told reporters here..Rijiju said the government has called for a four-day special sitting — November 30 and December 1 in Lok Sabha, and December 2 and 3 in Rajya Sabha..Government plans special session of Parliament to pass women's quota amendment bill: Report."When the government calls a session or a special session, that means there are very important bills or business for the nation," he said..The minister said the members of Parliament have a very special task, an onerous responsibility, in ensuring a smooth run of Parliament.."Members have all the rights, all the freedom to agree or to disagree. But that has to be put in proper perspective through rules, through conventions on the floor of the House," he said..The special sitting was announced on Thursday to transact "essential" business, amid indications that the government may reintroduce a constitutional amendment linking the rollout of women's reservation to delimitation..The government has been keen to push through the Constitution amendment bill for a long time..It seeks to expand the Lok Sabha's strength from the existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. The treasury benches have said it will pave the way for the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and State legislatures ahead of the 2029 general election..The government's earlier move to pass the proposed legislation in Parliament was defeated in April due to a lack of numbers.

headline: "It Was Your Responsibility": Supreme Court Raps Collector Over Deepam Row
content: The Supreme Court on Friday came down heavily on the Tamil Nadu government over the non-compliance of its order on the lighting of Deepam at the Deepathoon pillar in Madurai. The court stated that it is prima facie a case of "contempt of court" and "wilful disobedience" by the state. In a big order on the issue, the court directed Deepam to be lit at the Deepathoon on Saturday and directed deployment of CRPF to ensure peace. The authorities have been directed to maintain peace at both the temple and the adjoining dargah, and ensure that religious activities go on unhindered at both the places. While it criticised the authorities for flouting the court order, the Supreme Court suspended the board of trustees of the temple and appointed the former chief justice of Meghalaya High Court as the receiver of the temple. Hearing contempt pleas filed against the state government and the temple management, the court expressing it "anguish and pain, saying that no one can be allowed to flout a court order. Despite the apex court's permission, the annual Karthigai Deepam was lit only at its customary location, the Uchipillayar Mandapam, at Thiruparankundram on November 24, and not at the stone pillar atop the hill.

headline: What is subvention scheme fraud? Why has SC directed HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank to sanction prosecution of officials
content: The Supreme Court has directed HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital and PNB Housing Finance to grant unconditional sanction for the prosecution of their officials within a week in alleged subvention scheme frauds involving real estate developers and financial institutions, PTI reported.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana warned that the heads of these institutions would have to appear personally before the court if they failed to comply with the order."We direct all the banks or financial institutions referred to above to issue unconditional sanction for prosecution within one week, failing which the CMD and Chairman shall remain present in court to show cause as to why appropriate action be not taken against them," the bench said.The order came while the apex court was hearing a batch of petitions concerning subvention schemes, under which homebuyers were allegedly subjected to loan recovery proceedings after developers failed to meet their financial commitments.What is a subvention scheme?Under a subvention scheme, a bank or financial institution sanctions a home loan and disburses the amount directly into the builder's account. In return, the developer agrees to pay the equated monthly instalments (EMIs) on behalf of the buyer until possession of the flat is handed over.The arrangement is generally governed by a tripartite agreement between the homebuyer, the developer and the lender.The scheme is intended to reduce the immediate financial burden on homebuyers, who do not have to begin paying EMIs while waiting for their homes to be delivered.However, problems arise when developers fail to honour their commitment to pay the EMIs. In such cases, banks can demand repayment from homebuyers, leaving them liable for loans even when they have not received possession of their properties.What is the alleged subvention fraud?The petitions before the Supreme Court concern allegations that banks and developers were involved in arrangements that left homebuyers facing loan recovery proceedings despite builders failing to meet their obligations under the tripartite agreements.The court is examining cases involving alleged collusion between financial institutions and developers to dupe homebuyers, particularly in the National Capital Region (NCR).During Thursday's hearing, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), told the court that the agency was facing difficulties in obtaining prosecution sanctions under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act. This included cases where HDFC Bank had granted conditional sanctions.Bhati also informed the bench that the CBI had filed its sixth supplementary status report. Investigations had been completed in 25 of the 55 registered cases, with 22 chargesheets filed and closure reports submitted in three cases.What has the Supreme Court directed?The bench said granting prosecution sanction was the responsibility of the banking authorities and directed the CBI to complete the remaining investigations within two weeks.The court also said it would prescribe timelines for completing the trials and would not permit delaying tactics.In July last year, the Supreme Court had allowed the CBI to register 22 cases over what it described as an "unholy nexus" between banks and developers to dupe homebuyers in the NCR.

headline: Supreme Court grants bail to former AAP legislator Naresh Balyan
content: The Supreme Court on Friday granted bail to former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) legislator Naresh Balyan in a Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) case for alleged links with UK-based gangster Kapil Sangwan.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh directed Balyan to cooperate with the trial while granting him bail. The Delhi police opposed the bail, calling the charge of organised crime serious.Balyan moved the Supreme Court after the Delhi high court denied him bail. In August, the Supreme Court issued notice to the police after Balyan argued that the high court failed to note that under MCOCA the statutory requirement is not fulfilled, as there should be a continuing lawful activity of the organised crime in which the individual is charge-sheeted in the preceding 10 years.Senior advocate Vikas Singh, who appeared for Balyan along with advocate Vivek Jain, said that the main witnesses in the case rescinded their statements. He pointed out that he had complained to the police, alleging that the person with whom he is alleged to have links was threatening him. Police granted Balyan protection based on his complaint.Balyan said the evidence against him is inadmissible and he was never named originally.The trial court denied bail to Balyan, observing that the criminal nexus between a politician and a gangster is perhaps the “most perilous threat” confronting a nation and its citizens and must be addressed with severity.In his petition, Balyan said that he has been incarcerated since December 2025 and the investigation against him is complete.In May, Delhi police filed a charge sheet against Balyan, alleging that he used his political clout to financially support Sangwan’s syndicate and shield its members from arrest. Balyan allegedly used virtual private networks, an encrypted messaging app to communicate, and phones registered in the name of his family to communicate with Sangwan and to evade detection.Balyan was arrested on December 4 last year on allegations of organised crime, shortly after he was granted bail in the extortion case.

headline: India-US trade pact nears finish as pathway takes shape: Piyush Goyal
content: The India-US trade deal is “close to culmination”, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Friday, indicating progress in negotiations days after Washington proposed a fresh tariff framework for Indian imports. “The US trade deal is close to culmination. The process and pathway, which was always something which held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape,” Goyal said while addressing the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026 organised by TRUST Group. His comments came after the US Trade Representative (USTR) proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods following a Section 301 investigation. Washington has indicated that the rate could be capped at 17 per cent if India and the US conclude a reciprocal trade agreement addressing the issues raised in the investigation. India has disputed the US finding of structural excess capacity in its manufacturing industries and has said trade-related concerns should be addressed through bilateral trade negotiations. Goyal also said the India-European Union free trade agreement was expected to be signed later this year and could come into effect by March or April 2027. The minister said India's FTA coverage had expanded sharply over the past few years. According to Goyal, before 2014, India's trade agreements covered economies with a combined gross domestic product (GDP) of about $10 trillion. Nine agreements finalised in the past four-and-a-half to five years, covering 38 developed countries, have added markets representing about $60 trillion of GDP. Together, India's preferential market access now covers economies with around $70 trillion of GDP, he said. Another eight or nine agreements under negotiation could add around $15 trillion, taking the total to about $85 trillion out of global GDP of $115-120 trillion, Goyal said. “Almost every country in the world wants to do an FTA with India. We will add another $15 trillion. $85 trillion out of $115-120 trillion of global GDP will see India as a trusted partner; will see opportunities for India’s businesses to take forward,” he said. On crude oil, Goyal said markets were sometimes too quick to re-rate or de-rate India based on relatively small movements in global prices. While higher crude prices affected the economy, concerns that may have been significant in the 1990s or early 2000s needed to be viewed differently today given India's larger foreign exchange reserves, remittance flows, foreign direct investment and broader export base, he said. “This could be an important matter of concern when we had much smaller foreign exchange reserves, much smaller remittances coming into the country, much less foreign direct investments coming into the country,” Goyal said. A few dollars of movement in oil prices could not determine India's economic trajectory over the next two or three decades, he said, pointing to the country's expanding exports and economy. The government said India had exported more than $700 billion annually and was targeting $1 trillion of goods and services exports in the current financial year. Goyal also urged large companies, public sector undertakings and infrastructure developers to increasingly use the bond market as their first source of financing, including for long-duration capital expenditure. He called for a broader investor base for long-term debt, asking insurers, pension and provident funds and mutual funds to increase participation in longer-duration instruments and look beyond only AAA-rated issuers. The country's financing ecosystem would need to match the scale and duration of investments expected in areas such as semiconductor manufacturing, power grids, data centres and infrastructure over the coming decades, he said. Goyal also urged exporters and their financiers to turn the market access created through FTAs into investment decisions by adding manufacturing capacity and preparing to serve newly opened markets.

headline: Himachal school forms panel after video of student assault goes viral
content: A video showing a student being assaulted by four to five other students in the boys' hostel of a school in Himachal Pradesh's Kinnaur district has surfaced, prompting the school authorities to constitute a committee to investigate the incident.The incident reportedly took place in September at the Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya in Reckong Peo, but the video went viral on Thursday. It is not clear whether the school management was aware of the incident at the time.The one-minute-three-second video shows the student being kicked and punched. He is first forced onto a bed and then thrown to the floor. The attackers are also heard hurling abuses and issuing threats.Sources said the victim had allegedly been involved in a fight with another student a few days earlier, following which a group of students assaulted him. Preliminary information suggests that the incident involved a group clash in the hostel, they said.Most of the students involved are reportedly in Class XI, while one is in Class XII.Superintendent of Police Sushil Sharma said on Friday that the school management had constituted a committee to investigate the incident.Police are awaiting the committee's findings as the students involved in the assault are minors. Further action will be taken in accordance with the law, he said.

headline: Turkey’s defence paradox — a booming arms industry on a fragile economy
content: The Russia–Ukraine war, which has dominated Europe’s strategic space for nearly five years, had taken a backseat in several discussions I attended during the Athens Security Forum earlier this week. Instead, conversations were either focused on Turkey or kept returning to it amid the wars and rivalries reshaping the Middle East and Mediterranean. Geography shapes not only threat perceptions but also the importance countries attach to different security questions. Despite a shared and unusually strong institutional identity, Europe does not have a common hierarchy of strategic anxieties. Russia remains central to the eastern and northern flanks, and to debates in London, Paris and Berlin. Along the southern flank, the emphasis shifts towards Turkey and the Middle East. But Ankara’s influence now extends much further: the Caucasus, Syria, North Africa, the Sahel and the Horn of Africa. Closer home, India is encountering Turkey across South Asia and, increasingly, Southeast Asia. New Delhi has generally analysed Pakistan’s defence modernisation through a Chinese lens. Operation Sindoor brought the Turkish dimension more sharply into focus. Bangladesh’s purchases of Turkish equipment and Ankara’s expanding partnerships in Indonesia and Malaysia underline why this cannot remain a Pakistan-only discussion for India. There is a paradox here. Turkey is a $1.6 trillion economy, not a poor country, but it faces persistent inflation, expensive credit and structural weaknesses. Yet it possesses NATO’s second-largest military by personnel, after the US, and has built a remarkably active defence industry. Why has this sector performed so differently from the mesh of economic challenges around it? And is Ankara escaping dependence, or getting better at managing it? I outline four propositions to help explain the contradiction. Turkey’s economy combines considerable productive strength with chronic instability. GDP per capita was approximately $18,650 in 2025. Its manufacturing base extends from automobiles and machinery to shipbuilding and construction services. Defence is therefore not an isolated miracle conjured out of an otherwise industrially barren economy.

headline: 22-year-old NEET aspirant dies after falling from hostel’s 4th floor in Kota
content: A 22-year-old NEET aspirant died after allegedly falling from the fourth floor of a hostel in Kota on Friday morning, police said.The deceased was identified as Aman Meena, a resident of the Itawa area in Kota district, who had been preparing for the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) in the coaching hub for around two years.According to preliminary information, Meena had gone to meet his friends at the hostel under the Jawahar Nagar police station limits, on Friday morning."He allegedly fell from the fourth floor of the hostel and sustained critical injuries. He was rushed to New Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead," Ramsagar, a policeman, told reporters.The cops have not ruled out suicide, but said that no suicide note was recovered from his possession.Police were yet to ascertain where Meena had been staying and whether he was attending online or offline coaching classes for NEET, the official said.His cousin Sonu said Meena was good at studies and had previously stayed at the hostel, where the incident took place.

headline: "No Change In Our Position": MK Stalin As Centre Brings Delimitation Bill
content: DMK chief and former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin has reiterated the party's two key demands on the proposed delimitation exercise, insisting that Tamil Nadu's existing 7.18 per cent share of Lok Sabha seats must not be reduced under any circumstances. This amid the possibility of the BJP at the centre bringing the delimitation bill again in parliament next week. In a post on X, Stalin said that if the total number of Lok Sabha seats is increased, the state's present share must remain protected. He also demanded that the existing inter-state proportion of parliamentary representation, based on the 1971 Census and frozen earlier, should continue for another 25 years. "The DMK stands firm on these two demands and will continue to do so. There is no change in our position, and there is no question of any compromise," he said. Stalin also sought to assert the DMK's role in bringing the issue to the national political agenda. He claimed that the party was the first in the country to flag the potential adverse consequences of delimitation and the first to convene a meeting of national political leaders in Chennai to press for a fair exercise. His remarks come amid speculation over the DMK's possible position on the delimitation proposals and allegations by the ruling TVK that the party could be moving closer to the BJP-led Centre. The DMK has denied any move towards an alliance with the BJP, while its spokesperson has declined to commit on whether the party would support the Centre if its demands on delimitation were accepted.

headline: 10-minute blackout mock drill in Sangrur: Shops, offices told to ensure strict compliance
content: The District Administration will conduct a Civil Defence blackout mock drill in the Army Cantonment area and Sangrur city on Friday, November 27 from 8 pm to 8:10 pm.The District Administration has appealed to all residents of Sangrur city to switch off all lights in their homes, shops, offices, commercial establishments and other buildings during the 10-minute mock drill.Residents have also been urged to switch off all lights powered by generators and inverters, as well as illuminated signboards, advertising boards, decorative lights and all other sources of illumination, or to cover them appropriately. Shopkeepers and owners of commercial establishments have been asked to ensure strict compliance with the blackout instructions.The District Administration has clarified that the mock drill is merely a preparedness exercise aimed at assessing arrangements for dealing with emergency situations and that there is no need for the public to panic. People have been advised to remain calm upon hearing sirens or noticing the movement of emergency vehicles and personnel, as these activities will be part of the drill.Residents have been advised to avoid unnecessary movement during the mock drill, cooperate with the police, Civil Defence personnel and other participating teams, and refrain from sharing rumours or unverified information on social media.The District Administration has sought the full cooperation of Sangrur residents to ensure that the mock drill is conducted safely, smoothly and effectively.

headline: Serbia's student-led movement may not form government until new year | World News
content: Serbia's student-led movement may not form a government until the new year, officials said this week, raising the risk that the country will not pass its budget on time and may not have a prime minister soon as it seeks to extend a vital gas supply deal with Russia.Student-backed candidates won the October 25 parliamentary election in a landslide, ousting longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vucic and capping nearly two years of anti-corruption protests.But one month in, the movement still has not nominated a prime minister or a cabinet, and its official stance on key domestic and foreign policies remains unclear.That leaves three deadlines falling before a new government is likely to take office: the December 11 expiry of a US Treasury license that lets Serbia's only refiner keep operating, the December 20 budget cutoff and the December 31 end of the Russian gas contract. Missing them could block new capital spending and leave gas supplies uncertain as winter begins. Oliver Toskovic, a Student List parliamentary deputy, said the movement has a "backbone" of a government, and that it would cut the number of ministries from the current 25."As for the deadline, the idea is not to appoint a government hastily, but to carefully review every decision. My impression is that there is a chance we will have a government by the year's-end," Toskovic told Belgrade's NIN weekly on Thursday.Parliament convened on November 17 and appointed Student List lawmaker Aleksandar Cupic as speaker. He will also serve as interim president until the presidential election on December 27.But Jovo Bakic, the head of the Student List parliamentary faction, said this week that a government would not be formed until the second half of December at the earliest.Under the constitution, the Student List has until February 15 to form a government, or a new parliamentary election must be called.Budget cutoff loomsIf Parliament misses the December 20 cutoff for the 2027 budget, Serbia, an EU membership candidate, will face three months of temporary financing from January 1."Almost certainly there will be temporary financing, even if there’s a government sometime in December," Bakic told Serbia's Masina portal this week.Djordje Djukic, an economist and lecturer at Belgrade University, said moving to temporary financing carries less risk than rushing a budget."The lesser mistake is to go to temporary financing, with an explanation of why that is so, and then form a strong government,” Djukic said.Russian gas dealThe gas supply contract with Russia's Gazprom is especially contentious as Russia seeks to maintain influence over Belgrade, its historic ally.Serbia relies on Russia for around 80% of its natural gas needs, buying it at a discounted price through the TurkStream pipeline via Bulgaria. While this arrangement saves Serbia hundreds of millions of euros each year, it leaves the country exposed to contract renewals and transit risks.Last year, Serbia joined the EU's joint gas-purchasing mechanism. It also imports gas from Azerbaijan via the Bulgaria-Serbia interconnector and plans to build a pipeline to North Macedonia to secure access to liquefied natural gas from Greece.Talks are ongoing between Serbia's state-run Srbijagas utility and Gazprom, but no volumes or duration have been announced.Last week, Aleksandar Vulin, a Vucic ally and the head of Srbijagas’ supervisory board, said he expects an extension of the gas arrangement past December 31, but that it could be a "cautious extension.""Moscow first wants to see who will form the new Serbian government and what kind of policy it will pursue," Vulin told Russia's RT Balkan TV.Since the October election, leading Student List figures have said the movement will not impose sanctions on Russia and wants energy ties to continue on favourable terms, while prioritising the fight against corruption and organised crime, institutional reform and EU alignment.They have also said they see Kosovo, which declared independence from Serbia in 2008, as an integral part of the country.Serbia's only refinery, NIS, is majority-owned by Russia's Gazprom Neft and Gazprom, and its US license runs until December 11. Hungarian oil company MOL is negotiating to buy the majority stake in NIS, but nothing is finalised.

headline: Sebi looks into Tata Steel-Apollo APL deal over minority shareholder concerns
content: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is looking into the Tata Steel–APL Apollo deal, chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Friday, stressing that investor protection remains paramount for the capital markets regulator. "Sebi takes minority shareholder rights very seriously. We are looking into the Tata-APL deal, investor protection is very important,” Pandey said on the sidelines of industry body Assocham’s conference in the national capital. The two-part takeover transaction between Tata Steel and APL Apollo has faced sharp pushback from minority shareholders over related-party transaction (RPT) concerns and the lucrative exit for APL Apollo’s promoters. Shares of APL Apollo rose 3% on Friday afternoon following the remarks. Tata Steel shares gained 0.7%.Deal structureAt the heart of the controversy is the complex structure of the proposed transaction. APL Apollo will acquire two businesses from Tata Steel for a total of ₹28,000 crore, with the purchase largely funded through debt. Tata Steel, meanwhile, will pay ₹15,510 crore to acquire a 26.38% promoter stake in APL Apollo and launch an open offer for an additional 26%, taking its potential total outlay to ₹32,266 crore.Investors have questioned whether the structure effectively leaves APL Apollo shouldering a significant part of the debt burden associated with Tata Steel’s takeover of the tube maker.Separately, Tata Steel and APL Apollo’s promoters have agreed to enter into an exclusive contract-manufacturing arrangement after the promoters exit the company.RPT concernsProxy advisory firms Institutional Investor Advisory Services, Stakeholders Empowerment Services (SES) and InGovern have raised concerns over the transaction structure and urged the market regulator to intervene. They argued that the arrangement ensured Tata Steel was not a related party of APL Apollo when the latter’s board approved the asset acquisitions on Sunday evening, thereby avoiding the requirement of shareholder approval for related-party transactions.Pandey said proxy advisors can raise issues if they strongly feel about them, and “that's what they are there for”.In response to Mint’s email queries on Friday, a Tata Steel spokesperson said: “Tata Steel has complied with the applicable laws in announcing the transactions. However, we have taken cognisance of the feedback received and are carefully examining the concerns raised to determine how best to address them.”Mint had earlier reported that investors and proxy advisory firms had criticised the proposed deal, calling its terms unfair to APL Apollo’s minority shareholders and raising concerns over whether the ₹28,000-crore asset acquisition would secure shareholder approval.Shares of APL Apollo Tubes Ltd have lost just over 30% on the BSE since the deal was announced on Sunday to close at 21,481 on Thursday. Tata Steel has lost just over 8% to close at ·163.35 on Thursday.

headline: Only 20-30% of eligible Indian exports use FTA benefits: RBI Governor
content: Only 20-30 per cent of eligible Indian exports avail tariff benefits under the country's free trade agreements (FTAs), compared with 60-70 per cent of eligible exports from partner countries to India, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra said on Friday. "It is an opportunity we are leaving on the table," Malhotra said at the SME Finance & Investment Summit in Mumbai, urging micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to look beyond domestic markets and make greater use of India's expanding network of trade agreements. The RBI published his address on Friday. He asked MSMEs to familiarise themselves with FTAs relevant to their products and invest in quality, standards and certification to access overseas markets. India's expanding network of FTAs, some of which have dedicated chapters for SMEs, provides access to new markets, lower-cost quality inputs and opportunities to specialise in niche segments of global value chains, Malhotra said. Labour-intensive MSME sectors, in particular, could help spread the benefits of trade more broadly, he added. In a fireside chat following his address, Malhotra was asked about industry demands to extend the period for classifying a loan as a non-performing asset (NPA) from 90 days to 180 days. He said the issue could instead be addressed by borrowers negotiating longer repayment tenures with banks, since the 90-day period begins only after a scheduled repayment becomes overdue. "If you take the repayment period as longer, then the 90-day period will start later," he said. Malhotra also called on banks to create dedicated modules at branches to guide entrepreneurs on the various schemes available to them. Lending, he said, was ultimately built on trust and required relationship banking, where lenders understood businesses as well as the people behind them. Banks should spend more time assessing the needs, capabilities and repayment capacity of enterprises, while borrowers should be persistent in seeking lenders' attention, he said. Bank credit to MSMEs grew 27 per cent year-on-year in the 12 months ended September 2026, compared with 19.4 per cent growth in overall bank credit, Malhotra said. Over the past five years, MSME credit has grown at a compound annual growth rate of around 19 per cent, with outstanding credit rising from ₹17.97 trillion in September 2021 to ₹42.89 trillion in September 2026. "The credit gap has certainly not disappeared, but it has narrowed considerably, and quickly," he said. The focus should now shift towards first-time borrowers, micro enterprises, women-led businesses, and units in smaller towns and rural areas, Malhotra added. The RBI earlier this year raised the mandatory collateral-free loan limit for micro and small enterprises from ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh for loans sanctioned or renewed from April 1, 2026. Banks can raise the limit to ₹25 lakh for borrowers with a strong track record and financial position under their internal policies. Malhotra said this was the first revision of the limit since 2010. The Governor also highlighted the role of India's digital public infrastructure in improving access to finance. The Account Aggregator framework facilitated loans worth around ₹3.5 trillion in FY26, he said, while the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) could potentially replicate in lending the impact that the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has had on payments. However, he stressed that technology should supplement rather than replace relationship banking. Malhotra outlined five priorities for MSMEs: aspiring to scale, investing in productivity, technology and innovation, exploring overseas markets, formalising operations to build lenders' confidence, and using instruments such as the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS). Government support, he said, should be treated as "a catalyst, not a crutch". The productivity of Indian MSMEs, measured by value added per worker, is around 26 per cent of that of large enterprises, according to Malhotra. Raising productivity towards the level of top-quartile firms in advanced economies could add the equivalent of around 11 per cent of India's gross domestic product, he said. He also flagged the relatively low adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) among Indian MSMEs, at around 15 per cent, compared with countries such as China, the US and Germany. Addressing lenders, Malhotra said MSME lending should not be viewed merely as regulatory compliance or a target to be achieved. Digital public infrastructure should strengthen, rather than replace, the personal understanding of borrowers that comes from relationship banking, he said. Similarly, credit guarantees should help lenders share risk but should not become a substitute for proper due diligence. Malhotra said the next phase of MSME development would depend not only on greater access to finance, but also on firms improving productivity, adopting technology, formalising their operations and using trade agreements to compete in overseas markets.

headline: Mint explainer: why HPV vaccination is critical for girls as India crosses 10 million doses
content: India has administered more than 10 million doses of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine to 14-year-old girls in less than nine months under a campaign by the Union health ministry. The drive has covered nearly 87% of the annual target cohort of about 12 million girls, drawing praise from the World Health Organization’s (WHO) South-East Asia Region.

headline: Himachal’s school introduces ‘Honesty Shop’ to promote self-discipline among students
content: A government senior secondary school in Himachal Pradesh's Bilaspur district has launched an 'Honesty Shop', an initiative to promote honesty among students.The shop operates without a shopkeeper and students can take the items they need and deposit the fixed price into a collection box themselves.The school's objective of this initiative is to cultivate honesty, self-discipline and a sense of social responsibility among the students and foster constitutional values, said Principal Madan Lal Sharma on Friday.The event was presided over by Azad Singh Verma, president of the alumni association. During the proceedings, the association gifted an RO water purifier to the school.Many schools in states like Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Punjab have backed such initiatives to teach students integrity, responsibility, and self-discipline using everyday stationery or snacks.

headline: 'Does BJP's defeat rest only on my shoulders?' Masood hits out at SP after Kharge's warning
content: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood refused to temper his criticism of the Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing for the poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, despite party chief Mallikarjun Kharge's call for unity. Claiming he was being "cornered from all sides" and made a "villain", Masood questioned, "Does BJP's defeat rest only on my shoulders?", taking another swipe at the INDIA bloc ally over its approach to the proposed alliance.Speaking to news agency ANI on Friday, Masood said Kharge had acknowledged his efforts and appreciated his work, while maintaining that he would continue to raise concerns in the Congress's interest."Kharge ji has acknowledged my efforts; he is appreciating my work. I am prepared to sacrifice my very life for the progress of my party. I am being cornered from all sides, as if I am a villain."Masood added, "I am making demands for my party; I am fighting for my party. I will always speak in the interest of my party. An alliance is being formed; does the entire responsibility of ousting the BJP rest solely on my shoulders? Does it not rest on yours (SP) as well?"The party MP also questioned the SP's approach to allocating constituencies, arguing that the Congress should not be offered seats where it had little chance of winning.“Give us seats; we can contest and win. We need both quality and quantity... You take the Chief Minister’s post. There is no dispute here regarding the Chief Minister. But why are you trying to undermine your ally? Why do you want to belittle your ally? You started launching direct attacks against me; why? I hadn’t said a single word against you," he said.He further argued that the Congress's contribution to the alliance should not be measured only by its past electoral performance."The Congress is zero. You keep reminding us of our standing, but if you think so little of our standing, why do you even need us? You have the formula for winnability; you have everything, so why do you need us at all?... We are zero—but wherever we align, we multiply the impact tenfold. It was because of Rahul Gandhi that you (SP) managed to win 37 seats (2024 Lok Sabha Elections). We aren’t saying you didn’t contribute; we are saying that we, too, secured victories. We showed a big heart, but must it always be us who shows a big heart, every single time? Can’t you show a bit more generosity?" he told ANI.The disagreement intensified after the SP reportedly offered 26 seats as a starting point and announced five candidates while negotiations were underway. Masood had objected to the move, saying: "We are not beggars... Somewhere, this is very hurtful: that you will dictate terms like this."On Thursday, Kharge, addressing the Congress's Samvidhan Raksha Sammelan in Lucknow, said Masood spoke with enthusiasm but stressed the need for collective effort. "But more than statements, we have to work on the ground," he said.The Congress is reportedly seeking around 130 seats, while the SP's initial offer was 26.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: India's 'AI Kid' Answers Russian President Vladimir Putin's Big Question On AI In Education
content: Raul Jon Aju, a 17-year-old entrepreneur from Kerala, popularly known as India's 'AI Kid', attended an international artificial intelligence conference in Moscow, where he interacted with Russian President Vladimir Putin. During the interaction, Aju explained how artificial intelligence can help personalise education. Giving an example, he said, "Imagine a child like me who likes maths. What if I could learn maths through pictures, through videos, even through games? And I have learned AI through games, by the way." Recalling an incident before his maths examination, Aju said, "One day before my maths exam, my father was like, 'How are you playing a game? Tomorrow you have your exam.' But I said I was studying, and he was like, 'Kids these days.'" Aju said the experience showed how learning could be made more engaging and personalised. "The whole point is that I was able to learn in a fun way, right? I was able to learn in my own, my personalised way. But in a class of 40 children, how is one teacher able to personalise that education? And that's where I believe AI can help," he said.

headline: Opinion: Opinion | When India Went Nuclear, There Was One American Who Helped Change Everything
content: Strobe Talbott's death is an opportunity to look back at a key moment in India-US relations. After India tested nuclear weapons in 1998, the US imposed sanctions, and ties hit a nadir. But the talks that followed helped the two countries progress toward a strategic partnership. Talbott, then the US Deputy Secretary of State, played a central role through his ongoing discussions with India's Jaswant Singh. Their fourteen rounds of talks from 1998 to 2000 helped shift the relationship's direction. For President Bill Clinton, the Pokhran tests were a major setback to his post-Cold War goals. India's decision to test in May 1998 was the first challenge to his efforts to strengthen global non-proliferation, promote nuclear arms control, and secure the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty. When Pakistan tested two weeks later, it torpedoed all hopes of containing the crisis and showed that the Indian subcontinent was now nuclear-armed. The tests also damaged Clinton's broader vision of a peaceful world where political stability and economic cooperation support each other. Indian accounts often focus on security concerns and sanctions, but they tend to overlook this expedient American perspective. Talbott was particularly suited to handle the diplomatic fallout. A Rhodes Scholar educated at Yale and Oxford, he shared a house with Clinton at Oxford. While there, he helped translate Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev's memoirs, something Clinton mentioned in his statement after Talbott's death. Talbott worked at Time for 21 years, including as Moscow bureau chief, which gave him a deep understanding of the Soviet Union and its relationship with the United States. His books reflected these interests:Deadly Gambits examined nuclear arms control; At the Highest Levels, co-written with Michael Beschloss, explored Cold War diplomacy; and The Russia Hand focused on presidential diplomacy and post-Soviet relations. These works show his lasting interest in nuclear strategy, great-power transitions, and political leadership. Clinton inducted Talbott into the government in 1993 as Ambassador-at-Large for the former Soviet republics, and he became Deputy Secretary of State in 1994. In his obituary statement, Clinton described Talbott as analytical, committed to diplomacy, and a source of honest advice. He credited him with helping build trust between former adversaries, reduce nuclear risks, and shape US policy toward Europe and the Balkans. These qualities led Clinton to choose Talbott to lead talks with India after Pokhran. The role required political authority, strategic understanding, and direct access to the President, all of which Talbott had in abundance. Negotiations started in June 1998. The US wanted India to commit to the CTBT, stop making fissile material, follow missile restraint, and tighten export controls. India valued and sought to keep its nuclear independence. While they stayed apart on key non-proliferation issues, their talks grew to include the global order and the future of their relationship. Talbott and Singh built a working relationship based on honesty and respect. The talks opened a strategic communication channel between two governments that had long been wary of each other. Talbott later wrote about these talks in Engaging India: Diplomacy, Democracy, and the Bomb (2004).

headline: Italian leader's 'Vote Chor' slogan row: SC dismisses plea to takedown Filibeck's videos
content: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday rejected a plea seeking the removal of videos showing Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck raising the slogan 'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod' at a Congress-organised event in Hyderabad.The plea had also asked for an independent SIT probe into the participation of foreign delegates and the permissions granted to them for attending the event.During an earlier mentioning before Chief Justic Surya Kant, the petitioner's counsel alleged the secretary-general of the Party of European Socialists (PES), had interfered in India's domestic politics by criticising the government and expressing support for the Opposition.The plea came after Filibeck's remarks at the Bharat Summit 2026, held in Hyderabad on November 13 and 14. He had expressed support for Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and the Congress, saying democracy was "under attack" in India and calling for international support to defend it.His use of the slogan, popularised by Rahul Gandhi, drew criticism from the BJP, which accused the Congress of allowing foreign political representatives to comment on India's internal affairs.Filibeck also said the PES, Congress and other political movements across the world were part of a progressive alliance committed to social justice, climate justice, human rights and democracy."True democracy. Not the corrupted one, not the rigged one, not the fake one," he said.The Party of European Socialists (PES) is a transnational European political party that brings together socialist, social democratic, and labour parties across Europe.Around 1,000 delegates, policymakers and thinkers from 70 countries, were present at The Bharat Summit 2026, which held discussions over geopolitics, democracy, climate change, artificial intelligence and progressive politics.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: 500 cops deployed for Diljit Dosanjh’s Mumbai concert after bomb threat
content: More than 500 Mumbai police personnel will be deployed at Mahalaxmi Racecourse in Mumbai for actor-singer Diljit Dosanjh’s concert on Friday following a threat email warning of possible attacks on the venue and Metro stations, officials said.Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad (BDDS) teams have swept the venue, they said, adding that entry checks will be carried out across all five gates instead of three.Private security personnel have also been roped in to assist police, an official said.An email threatening blasts, grenade attacks and planting of IEDs at the mayor’s office, metro rail stations and Dosanjh’s concert was received on Thursday, the anniversary of the devastating 26/11 terror attacks.The email, sent by an individual identifying herself as Hannah Meler, contained references to Khalistan, the 1984 anti-Sikh riots as well as threats of violence linked to a programme involving Dosanjh and people associated with the event.In view of the threat, the Mumbai police has deployed around 200 constables, 150 women constables and 75 officers, besides plainclothes personnel stationed around the singer. Dog squads and an Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) team will also remain present at the venue, an official said.He said that a no-car zone extending 500 to 700 metres around the racecourse will be enforced, and parking will not be permitted at the event, though no road diversions have been announced.Organisers have been instructed not to disclose details of the singer’s hotel or arrival time as part of the security protocol, sources said.Meanwhile, organisers have prohibited posters, banners, signs and flags of any kind inside Mahalaxmi Racecourse for the concert, which is part of Dosanjh’s RuPay AURA India Tour 2026.

headline: How US Customs caught 440 fake Cartier, Chanel and Tiffany jewellery pieces worth '$2.4 million': Here's what happened
content: US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officers in Cincinnati seized 440 pieces of counterfeit jewellery bearing the trademarks of seven luxury brands after intercepting a parcel sent from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to a residential address in Illinois.The shipment was inspected on November 11, when officers selected the parcel for examination. According to a CBP release issued on November 18, the jewellery carried trademarks associated with Cartier, Tiffany, Chanel, Christian Dior, Van Cleef & Arpels, Bvlgari and Hermes.The agency's Centers of Excellence and Expertise, which employs industry-trained trade specialists, examined the items and determined that they were not authentic. The entire shipment was subsequently seized for carrying counterfeit versions of registered and recorded trademarks.Why the fake jewellery had a potential value of $2.4 millionThe shipment's estimated value of more than $2.4 million refers to what the jewellery could have fetched if the pieces had been genuine.According to CBP, the combined manufacturer's suggested retail price of the items would have exceeded $2.4 million had they been authentic. The figure, therefore, does not represent the actual value of the counterfeit jewellery.The seizure highlights the agency's efforts to prevent counterfeit branded merchandise from entering the US market and protect businesses against trademark infringement.How US Customs can seize counterfeit goodsCBP has the authority to detain, seize, forfeit and ultimately destroy imported merchandise that infringes registered trademarks or copyrights.Under the process outlined by the agency, the relevant trademark or copyright must be registered with the United States Patent and Trademark Office or the US Copyright Office and subsequently recorded with CBP through its e-Recordation programme.Apart from intellectual property violations, the agency also deals with other import-related violations, including incorrect merchandise classification, false country-of-origin markings, health and safety issues, and valuation discrepancies.What CBP says about counterfeit productsCincinnati Port Director Eric Zizelman said counterfeit products impose costs on American businesses through lost revenue, jobs and tax collections."Counterfeit goods are poor quality products that cost the U.S. businesses billions of dollars a year while robbing our country of jobs and tax revenues," Zizelman said.He added that CBP remained committed to preventing counterfeit smuggling, disrupting profits linked to organised crime and protecting communities from potentially hazardous imitation products.The agency also listed several warning signs that consumers should watch for when buying branded merchandise. These include peeling labels, poor-quality printing, spelling errors on packaging and generally substandard packaging.Counterfeit clothing and handbags may have uneven stitching, incorrect sizing or designs that are not part of the original brand's product range. Fake electronic products may also have short battery life or overheat during use.CBP advises consumers to buy products directly from trademark owners or authorised retailers. For online purchases, it recommends checking seller reviews and verifying whether the seller provides a working US phone number and a valid contact address.

headline: Sharad Pawar's health has improved, no word on discharge: Report
content: Mumbai: Nationalist Congress Party (SP) president Sharad Pawar, who was admitted to a hospital in south Mumbai due to dehydration, is doing better, party sources said on Friday..The 85-year-old leader was hospitalised on Thursday, though there is no word yet on when he will be discharged, they said..Earlier, his daughter and NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule had confirmed that Pawar was admitted to the Breach Candy Hospital after suffering dehydration..Sharad Pawar may not join NDA but could extend issue-based support to Centre: Maharashtra min Chhagan Bhujbal."He has to slow down and travel less. He loves his work too much," she had said..Party leader and Pawar's grand-nephew Rohit Pawar also said the veteran leader was fine and there was no need to worry..Rival NCP faction leader Praful Patel had visited Pawar in the hospital on Thursday..This is Pawar's third hospitalisation this month.
