headline: Inside the Tata Sons power struggle: The rules, the rift and the road ahead
content: The battle to lead India's Tata Sons, the owner of marquee brands such as Jaguar Land Rover and Tetley Tea, headed for court on Friday after the sprawling conglomerate flouted the wishes of its controlling charity arm to reappoint ​the chairman.Tata Trusts holds a stake of 66% in Tata Sons, but the latter's board re-appointed chairman ​N. Chandrasekaran and has decided to pursue a possible stock market listing, putting the power struggle at the centre of the standoff.It is the ‌second such fight in a decade for one of India's oldest and most reputed business houses, after a years-long legal battle over Tata Sons' decision to remove earlier chairman Cyrus Mistry ended in the Supreme Court upholding the decision.Here is how the current fight could play out, along with views of both sides and the complex structures, according to people familiar with the matter:TRUSTS WANT CHANDRASEKARAN OUT OF KEY DECISIONSTwo of the seven charitable trusts that control Tata Sons asked the Mumbai high court on Thursday to declare Chandrasekaran's reappointment 'invalid, illegal, null and void', copies of internal memos reviewed by Reuters showed.They also seek court directions that key decisions by Tata Sons require complete support from the charity arm.Reuters has learnt the trusts will tell the court that the board should not have proceeded with the decision as both trust nominees did not back the chairman's reappointment.At Friday's hearing, the trusts are expected to ask for a halt to plans for a November 30 board meeting set to decide next steps towards listing if the chief of the charity arm ‌and family head Noel Tata, as trust nominee, does not vote in favour.The board of Tata Sons agrees to the stock market listing, ordered by the central bank, but the charity arm does not.COURT CASE FOLLOWS BITTER PUBLIC DEBATEBoth sides have hired top lawyers to defend them and explain who can call the shots.Lawmaker and Congress party leader Abhishek Manu Singhvi is representing the Tata Trusts led by Noel Tata.Singhvi has previously said the dispute is about shareholder supremacy and the conglomerate cannot act like a "runaway board" independent of the controlling shareholder.That position is disputed by Tata Group's Chandrasekaran, who has roped in Harish Salve, a former solicitor general of India who often represented the government in global forums.In television remarks Salve has said the board's decision was in line with internal governing rules, urging the charity ​arm to get past the "I control the trusts, I control this group mindset."WHY CAN'T THE TRUSTS CALL A SHAREHOLDER MEETING AND OUST THE CHAIRMAN?The Tata Trusts ‌have problems of their own that weaken their influence. Formed of several affiliated charities, they could have used their voting power to call for a shareholders' meeting to effectively oust Chandrasekaran.But a regulator has barred one of the main charities, the Sir Ratan Tata Trust, from convening its own meetings ​in a dispute over internal ‌appointments.In turn, internal rules mean the charities currently lack the power to call for a meeting of Tata Sons shareholders.The trusts can either wait for the deadlock to ‌lift, once the regulatory inquiry ends, or ask a court to lift the curbs, two people familiar with the matter said.COURT FIGHT CENTRES ON 'ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION'At the heart of the dispute facing the court is the Tata Sons' governance framework known as the "articles of association", since Tata Trusts and Tata Sons ‌disagree on ​the interpretation of ​thee rules, which are not public.The charity arm says Noel Tata's opposition to the reappointment was sufficient to halt the decision. It believes such decisions cannot be made in the absence of support of a majority of the trusts' two board nominees.In this case, "majority amongst two is ‌two and not one," the charity ​arm has publicly argued.Tata Sons' lawyer Salve disagrees, saying both trust nominees voted differently, prompting a casting vote that helped reappoint the chairman under the governance rules.

headline: Delhi: Pollution may be worse in your kitchen than on your balcony; study finds 50% more fine particles in some houses
content: Fine particle pollution was roughly 50% higher inside poorly-ventilated south Delhi homes than outdoors. The study covered 24 homes across four neighbourhoods, PTI reported.Even homes with working kitchen exhaust systems recorded higher air pollution indoors than outside. But their indoor readings were lower than those in homes with poor ventilation.In poorly-ventilated homes, indoor PM2.5 averaged 119.17 micrograms per cubic metre. The outdoor average was 79.34 micrograms per cubic metre. In well-ventilated homes, indoor PM2.5 averaged 77.34, compared with 56.14 outdoors. This put indoor levels about 38% above outdoor readings in those homes.PM10 readings followed a similar pattern. Poorly-ventilated homes averaged 138.63 micrograms per cubic metre indoors and 91.19 micrograms per cubic metre outdoors. That put the indoor reading around 52% higher. Well-ventilated homes averaged 89.51 micrograms per cubic metre indoors and 64.81 micrograms per cubic metre outdoors, a difference of about 38%.Indoor PM2.5 was about 54% higher in poorly ventilated homes than in well-ventilated ones. For PM10, the gap was about 55%. Across all 24 homes, PM2.5 averaged 98.25 micrograms per cubic metre indoors and 67.74 micrograms per cubic metre outdoors.PM10 averaged 114.07 micrograms per cubic metre indoors and 78 micrograms per cubic metre outdoors. The indoor averages were about 45% higher for PM2.5 and 46% higher for PM10.How researchers measured pollutionResearchers monitored homes in Shaheen Bagh, Jasola Vihar, Batla House and Okhla Vihar. They collected readings from February to April 2023.They measured indoor pollution in kitchens and outdoor pollution on balconies. Each home was monitored for 8 hours each day over 3 consecutive days.The researchers skipped night-time monitoring because of privacy concerns. They classified homes according to whether working kitchen chimneys or exhaust fans operated during monitoring.The study linked better ventilation with lower indoor particle levels. Still, both groups recorded higher average particle levels inside kitchens than on balconies.The researchers linked higher indoor readings to household activities and poor ventilation. They also pointed to Delhi pollution entering homes from outside.Cooking, cleaning, smoking and burning incense can add particles to indoor air. Poor ventilation can allow indoor-generated particles to accumulate. The team did not measure how much each contributed to cooking, traffic, or dust.The team included researchers from Jamia Millia Islamia in New Delhi. Researchers from Jazan University in Saudi Arabia also took part. Others came from Baba Ghulam Shah Badshah University in Rajouri, Jammu and Kashmir.The journal Discover Environment published the study in 2025. The researchers said improving ventilation, maintaining exhaust systems and reducing indoor pollution sources could help.

headline: 'Manufacturing fraudulent two-thirds majority': Congress targets Modi govt over delimitation push
content: NEW DELHI: The Congress on Friday accused the government of using the upcoming special sitting of Parliament to push delimitation rather than implement women's reservation, alleging that the move was aimed at securing a "fraudulent two-thirds majority" in the Lok Sabha.Describing the proposed sitting as a desperate move by a "nervous and rattled PM who is under siege", the party said it would oppose the government's move with "all might".Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh alleged that the government, unable to revive the manufacturing sector, was attempting to "manufacture a fraudulent two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha"."Unable to get the manufacturing industry moving, the Modi Govt is moving to manufacture a fraudulent two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha. This is an assault on the Constitution of India. It must and will be resisted with all might. The Indian National Congress has been clear and consistent. Maintain the current strength of the Lok Sabha for another 25 years. Maintain the current state-wise distribution of seats in the Lok Sabha for another 25 years.""Implement one-third reservation for women and reservation within reservation for women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections," Ramesh said in a post on X.Congress deputy leader in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi also questioned the government's decision to convene a short special sitting without provisions for Question Hour, Zero Hour or private members' bills."No question hour, No zero hour, No Private Members bill in Parliament. Yesterday when the entire country paid homage to Dr. BabaSaheb Bhim Rao Ambedkar, the Lok Sabha issued a bulletin for a short 4 day Parliament session without any question hour, zero hour or private member bill."Does the Parliament belong to Modi-Shah?" he asked on X.The Congress's remarks came a day after Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the two Houses on November 30 and December 2, respectively."Subject to exigencies of the business, the sitting of both Houses may conclude on December 3, 2026," Rijiju said in a post on X.The sitting will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, as Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13 and has not been prorogued.Although the government has not officially confirmed the legislative business to be taken up, speculation has centred on the proposed Delimitation Bill and the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections.The Congress has alleged that the government is seeking to revive its delimitation-linked constitutional amendment proposal to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha.On Thursday, Ramesh said the government had made the delimitation Bills public on April 14, Ambedkar Jayanti, but they were defeated in Parliament on April 17."Now on Constitution Day, after 105 days of Operation Lotus, the Modi government announces a special session, hoping that it will get its super-tainted two-thirds majority to pass a Constitution amendment bill," he said.Questioning the timing of the special sitting, Ramesh asked whether there could be a greater insult to and assault on the Constitution, adding, "The fight is on."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

content: VMPLJaipur (Rajasthan) [India], November 27: Reinforcing its commitment to progressive and future-ready education, Neerja Modi School (NMS), Jaipur, has initiated Pragya 2026 - The National Schools Conclave on AI - Humanities and Public Policy, scheduled for 28-29 November at its Jaipur campus.Organised in partnership with Public Policy India (PPI) and STRIDE, a think tank engaged in public policy research and institutional capacity building, the initiative brings together technology, interdisciplinary learning and real-world problem-solving.As artificial intelligence increasingly influences industries, governance and society, Neerja Modi School is taking a proactive approach to integrating emerging technologies with critical thinking, research, ethical reasoning and innovation.What distinguishes Pragya is its emphasis on moving beyond the conventional applications of artificial intelligence. The conclave is intended to encourage students to explore the relationship between technology and society, examine contemporary challenges and develop evidence-based, AI-enabled solutions.Student proposals address a diverse range of issues, including organ donation, agricultural challenges, groundwater management and social welfare, demonstrating the relevance of interdisciplinary learning in addressing complex real-world problems.Through an innovative format that combines policy research, expert engagement and prototype development, students will defend their recommendations before a jury and subsequently translate their ideas into practical solutions.Speaking about the initiative, Ms. Indu Dubey, Principal, Neerja Modi School, Jaipur, said:"At Neerja Modi School, we recognise the importance of staying ahead in an evolving educational landscape. Through initiatives such as Pragya, we are creating opportunities for students to engage with emerging technologies, think across disciplines and develop the confidence to address complex real-world challenges. Our focus is on nurturing informed, innovative and socially responsible young leaders."The collaboration with Public Policy India and STRIDE brings professional expertise and contemporary policy perspectives into the school education ecosystem, creating opportunities for meaningful engagement between young learners and domain experts."The questions these students are asking about AI, on privacy, fairness and who is accountable, are the questions India's policymakers are asking too. Pragya shows that young people can do serious policy work when they are given the evidence, the tools and an audience that takes them seriously," said Yash Agarwal, Founder, Public Policy India and STRIDE.Through Pragya 2026, Neerja Modi School is demonstrating how educational institutions can anticipate emerging global trends and translate them into innovative learning experiences.By bringing artificial intelligence, the humanities and public policy together on a national platform, NMS is reinforcing its position as a forward-thinking institution committed to educational innovation, interdisciplinary excellence and preparing the next generation of leaders.About Neerja Modi School -Established in 2001, Neerja Modi School (NMS), Jaipur, is a co-educational day-cum-day-boarding school offering an educational journey from kindergarten to Grade 12. With approximately 4,600 students and 350 educators, the school brings together students from diverse cultural, socioeconomic and geographical backgrounds. Guided by its commitment to making world-class education accessible and affordable, its progressive educational approach combines academic excellence with sports, visual and performing arts, community engagement and leadership development.(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL. headline: Cashless Mediclaim Policy or Reimbursement: Which Is More Convenient for Planned Hospitalisation? | Hindustan Times
content: Planned hospitalisation gives you time to prepare for treatment, but the payment process still needs attention. Should you use a cashless facility or pay the hospital bill and claim the amount later? The answer depends on your chosen hospital, policy terms and ability to arrange funds. Knowing both options in advance can help you avoid last-minute confusion and focus on treatment. It also helps you plan what you may need to pay yourself.What Happens Under Cashless Treatment?With a cashless mediclaim policy, the insurer or its Third Party Administrator (TPA) settles eligible hospital expenses directly with a network hospital. You do not have to arrange the entire treatment cost upfront and claim it later. HDFC ERGO’s Optima Super Secure plan offers cashless treatment at network hospitals, where eligible expenses are settled directly after approval, subject to policy terms and conditions. For planned hospitalisation, inform the insurer or hospital before admission. The hospital’s insurance desk usually handles the pre-authorisation process by sharing treatment details and estimated expenses with the insurer. Once the request is reviewed, the insurer communicates its decision. However, cashless approval does not mean every hospital expense will be covered. You may still have to pay for: Non-medical expenses: Items and services excluded under the policy.Room rent limits: Charges exceeding the permitted room category or applicable limit.Co-payment: The portion of the approved claim that you must pay.Excluded treatments: Medical expenses that fall outside the policy coverage. The hospital may also ask for a deposit or payment towards expenses that are not covered.When Reimbursement Makes SenseReimbursement allows you to receive the eligible treatment expenses after paying the hospital bill yourself. This option can be useful when your preferred hospital is not part of the insurer’s network or cashless treatment is unavailable. Before admission, check the reimbursement procedure and understand which documents you will need. Keep the following records safely: Original hospital bills and payment receipts.Doctor’s prescriptions and consultation records.Medical reports and diagnostic test results.Discharge summary and treatment details.Completed claim form and other documents requested by the insurer. After treatment, submit the documents within the specified timeline. The insurer reviews the medical records, checks the expenses against the policy terms and determines the payable claim amount. The approved amount is then reimbursed to your account. The payment may be lower than the total hospital bill if certain expenses are excluded or exceed the applicable policy limits.Cashless Treatment vs Reimbursement: Key DifferencesBoth options help you use your health insurance cover, but the payment process and responsibilities are different. BasisCashless TreatmentReimbursementHospital choiceAvailable at eligible network hospitalsCan be used at non-network hospitals, subject to policy termsInitial paymentInsurer settles approved expenses directly with the hospitalYou pay the hospital bill firstClaim processHospital submits the pre-authorisation requestYou submit the claim and supporting documentsPaperworkHospital insurance desk usually handles initial formalitiesYou need to collect and submit the required documentsFinancial planningLess upfront financial burden for approved expensesYou need sufficient funds to pay the hospital billClaim settlementApproved expenses are settled directly with the hospitalApproved expenses are reimbursed to your accountConvenienceGenerally easier during planned hospitalisationRequires more personal involvement in the claim processWhich Route Is More Convenient?Cashless treatment is generally easier when your hospital is in the network, and pre-authorisation is approved. It reduces the need to arrange a large amount for eligible expenses and saves you from paying the entire bill upfront. Reimbursement lets you choose a non-network hospital, but you must have enough funds to pay first. You also need to keep paperwork and complete claim formalities. Settlement time depends on the insurer’s review and whether documents are complete.Make These Checks Before AdmissionUse this checklist: Confirm hospital network status.Ask when pre-authorisation is submitted.Share medical records and treatment details.Read waiting periods, exclusions and limits.Check co-payment, deductible or room restrictions.Set aside money for non-covered expenses.Keep copies of bills, forms and claim messages. Treatment at a network hospital does not automatically qualify for cashless settlement. The insurer’s approval and policy wording decide which expenses are payable.Final ThoughtsCashless treatment is generally more convenient for planned hospitalisation when your chosen hospital is in the network, and the insurer approves the request before admission. Reimbursement may be suitable when you prefer a non-network hospital, but you must arrange the payment and submit the required documents later. Before admission, confirm the hospital’s network status, understand policy limits and exclusions, and keep funds aside for expenses that may not be covered.Note to readers: This article is part of HT's paid consumer connect initiative and is independently created by the brand. HT assumes no editorial responsibility for the content, including its accuracy, completeness, or any errors or omissions. Readers are advised to verify all information independently.

headline: Parliament special session: Delimitation, women's quota, SIR row - what’s on the cards
content: NEW DELHI: A special sitting of Parliament will begin on November 30, with the government expected to consider reviving its push for a constitutional amendment linking women’s reservation to delimitation. The move could set the stage for a fresh political confrontation with the Opposition.The Lok Sabha will reconvene on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2, with the sittings scheduled to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.The government has not officially confirmed which Bills will be taken up. However, speculation has gathered pace over the proposed Delimitation Bill and the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections.What is on the government's agenda?Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha chairman C P Radhakrishnan to reconvene the Houses to transact “essential government business”.“Subject to exigencies of the business, the sitting of both Houses may conclude on December 3, 2026,” Rijiju said in a post on X.The special sittings will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 and subsequently prorogued.The proposed legislation seeks to increase the Lok Sabha's strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation, paving the way for 33 per cent reservation for women in legislative bodies.Why the Bill failed in AprilThe Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha during the special sitting on April 16-17. It received 298 votes in favour and 230 against, with 11 members abstaining. At the time, the House had 528 members and the Bill needed 352 votes to pass.The draft had not provided for a proportional 50 per cent increase in seats across states, a key concern for regional parties, particularly those from southern India. The government has since explored a formula to increase seats by 50 per cent in every state while retaining the existing inter-state share based on the 1971 Census.Protests against SIRThe opposition parties are also expected to carry their protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation into Parliament.Numbers game: DMK, NCP-SP and YSRCPThe BJP leaders are banking on support from the DMK, NCP-SP and breakaway factions of the Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena for the delimitation bill. The DMK has 22 Lok Sabha MPs and the NCP (SP) has eight. Both parties have indicated they could consider backing the proposal if their states' share of seats is protected.NCP-SCP MP Supriya Sule on Wednesday said the proposed Delimitation Bill should first be introduced and its full text made available for scrutiny. “Let the bill be introduced first; let us have the full bill in our hands. Once we have it, we can discuss it—and perhaps it will turn out to be a good one,” she told reporters.YSRCP is also expected to support the Delimitation Bill, according to sources quoted by news agency ANI. Meanwhile, Congress and NCP (SP) are stepping up coordination ahead of the sitting, with the parties summoning their MPs to discuss the proposed legislation and the Opposition's strategy.Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said the government was hoping to secure its “super-tainted” two-thirds majority. “A fight is on,” he said.Cabinet meeting, BJP strategyThe Union Cabinet is scheduled to meet at Sewa Teerth in New Delhi at 1 pm on Friday.The meeting comes as the BJP holds a two-day gathering of its national office-bearers and state in-charges at the PUSA campus on November 27 and 28. Discussions are expected to cover organisational strategy, upcoming Assembly elections and coordination between the Centre, states and the party organisation.The Cabinet meet is also likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's quota, ANI wrote, quoting sources.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: SEBI working to deepen capital markets, simplify regulations to support 2x economy: Chairman Pandey
content: New Delhi [India], November 27 (ANI): The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is working to deepen capital markets, simplify regulations and expand funding avenues as it looks to prepare the country's financial markets to support an economy twice their current size, Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Friday.Addressing the 17th Capital Market Conference organised by ASSOCHAM, Pandey outlined the regulator's priorities, including reviewing disclosure requirements, improving corporate bond market liquidity, widening participation by global investors and adopting emerging technologies with adequate safeguards."A comprehensive review of the LODR framework is underway," he said, adding that it would remove disclosures duplicating government filings and replace multiple exchange penalties for the same violation with a single penalty.SEBI is also reviewing regulations governing IPOs, further public offers, preferential issues, qualified institutional placements and SME listings. It has tightened scrutiny of SME listings and is moving towards risk-based supervision, with fewer routine inspections for compliant entities.The regulator has also introduced the SWAGAT-FI single-window mechanism to ease access for low-risk foreign portfolio investors (FPIs). The framework has registered 740 FPIs, accounting for around 17 per cent of FPI assets under custody.Highlighting its approach to different categories of investors, Pandey said, "We have matched regulations to the investor type. A sophisticated investor and a first-time saver need different protection."SEBI has made direct plans the default option on mutual fund digital platforms, reduced the minimum face value of bonds from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 10,000 and introduced a credit riskometer to help investors assess bond-related risks. It has also reduced the threshold for large-value alternative investment funds from Rs 70 crore to Rs 25 crore.On investor protection, he said, "A smartphone can open a trading account in minutes. It cannot explain risk." SEBI's 'Samaj Se Investing Simple' campaign has recorded around 37 crore social media views and reached 63 cities, with awareness initiatives conducted in 13 languages.On technology adoption, Pandey said, "We have welcomed innovation but with safeguards." SEBI is exploring a domestically governed artificial intelligence model, alongside responsible AI guidelines and a sandbox for testing applications in a controlled environment.The regulator is also developing a corporate bond market-making framework with the Reserve Bank of India and the Ministry of Finance to improve liquidity and access to repo facilities.Its other initiatives include a pilot for tokenised corporate bonds and measures to strengthen market resilience, including faster recovery of critical operations and tighter cyber incident reporting requirements.Outlining its priorities, Pandey said, "First, we will keep simplifying the rulebook" and "Second, we will deepen the markets that finance growth."He added, "Deepening the capital market requires widening the issuer base," urging industry associations to work with stock exchanges to familiarise more enterprises with public capital raising and listing responsibilities."Calibration is a continuing discipline. We will keep measuring, adjusting, and consulting," Pandey said, adding that building capital markets capable of financing the country's ambitions remained a shared responsibility of regulators and industry. (ANI)(This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

headline: Telangana high court clears Moosapet land auction, dismisses PILs challenging sale of 3.15 acres
content: HYDERABAD: The Telangana high court on Friday dismissed two public interest litigations challenging the auction of 3.15 acres of land belonging to the Kukatpally truck yard at Moosapet, clearing the way for the auction scheduled for the day.“Both PILs do not merit consideration. No reasonable public interest has been established that would warrant any interference. The PILs thus fail and are accordingly dismissed,” justice Suddala Chalapathi Rao read out in open court.He pronounced the order on behalf of the division bench comprising acting chief justice P Sam Koshy and justice Suddala Chalapathi Rao.The PILs were filed by BRS MLA from Kukatpally Krishna Rao and social worker Kantha Rao. They alleged that the land had originally been acquired for public purposes but was now being diverted for other reasons, contrary to its intended use.The state government strongly opposed the petitions, arguing that they had been filed with political motives. It contended that public purpose should not be interpreted narrowly and that the proposed truck terminal had never taken off.The land, it said, had not been acquired exclusively for that purpose.The land was acquired nearly four-and-a-half decades ago, when Moosapet was on the outskirts of Hyderabad. The plan was to keep heavy vehicles away from the city by developing a truck terminal.However, the project was never implemented despite attempts to take it forward. The government later formally cancelled the proposal, while residential localities developed in the surrounding areas.The state also argued that, to meet growing parking requirements, dedicated spaces had been allotted at three locations outside the Outer Ring Road (ORR) — Mangalapalli, Ibrahimpatnam and Abdullapurmet — which are now being used by truckers to park their vehicles.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: ED summons four serving IAS officers in DIG Bhullar case; nearly 40 officials under scanner
content: In the ongoing probe into the alleged corruption network involving suspended DIG HS Bhullar, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned four senior Punjab bureaucrats — Krishan Kumar, Ramvir, Varun Roojam and Abhinav Trika.All four officers have been asked to appear before the agency at its Chandigarh office in the first week of December.Earlier, the central agency had summoned Administrative Secretary (Health) Kumar Rahul, PCS officer Anand Sagar Sharma, retired officers Gurpreet Sapra and Arun Sekhri, Fazilka SSP Gagan Ajit Singh, and Special Secretary (General Administration) Neeru Katyal Gupta. Commissioner of Police Swapan Sharma has also been issued a summons to appear on Friday.The summonses have been issued in connection with the agency’s money-laundering investigation into the case involving DIG Bhullar and alleged middleman Krishanu Sharda, who were arrested by the CBI last year.An ED official said, “In the DIG Bhullar case, accused Sharda (liaison) was found to be involved in securing undue favours from these officers of the Punjab Government, indicating large-scale corruption in the state government.”The central agency is expected to summon nearly 40 serving and retired officials in the case.DIG Bhullar and Sharda were arrested by the CBI on October 16, 2025. Sharda was first caught accepting a bribe on behalf of the DIG, leading to the officer’s arrest on the same day.The ED subsequently registered a money-laundering case. Sharda was formally arrested by the ED on September 18, 2026, followed by Bhullar’s arrest on October 9, 2026. A disproportionate assets case against the senior police officer is also being investigated, as the CBI had recovered Rs 7.37 crore in cash and jewellery worth Rs 2.32 crore during his arrest.After interrogating the duo, the ED filed a prosecution complaint against Sharda before the special PMLA court in Chandigarh. In its complaint, the agency alleged that Sharda operated as a conduit for several government officials, facilitating transfers, postings and other official work in exchange for money.The agency attributed around Rs 1 crore in alleged proceeds of crime to him and flagged suspicious financial transactions involving several officers.The ED has also informed the court about the provisional attachment of Rs 26 lakh in cash. Its investigation into the alleged wider network is continuing.In October 2025, scrap dealer Akash Batta had lodged a complaint against Bhullar, alleging that the latter had demanded a bribe through Sharda in exchange for favourable treatment in an FIR registered at the Sirhind police station.CBI sleuths laid a trap and arrested Sharda while he was accepting a bribe of Rs 5 lakh. Bhullar was arrested by the CBI on the same day. The CBI subsequently filed a chargesheet against the accused in December 2025.

headline: 'Don't waste court's time': SC declines urgent hearing on plea against Ranbir's Ramayana
content: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday declined to grant an urgent hearing to a petition challenging the release of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, observing that those who disagree with the film's interpretation of the epic are free to make a film presenting their own perspective.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana questioned the urgency of the plea, noting that the film had already been released in theatres and that those interested in watching it had already done so.The petitioner's counsel told the bench that the plea had been registered on November 23 but was yet to be listed for hearing."The movie has already been released. Those who wanted to watch it have already seen it," the CJI said.The counsel argued that "many facts have been distorted" in the film's depiction of the epic. Responding to this, Justice Bagchi said, "They made a movie as they understand, you make a movie as you understand. Don't waste the time of the court."The CJI also remarked, "If you have a counter-view about the epic, you make a movie on the counter-view. Don't waste time of the Court."As the counsel pressed for an early hearing, the bench said the matter would be listed in due course.The petition alleges that the filmmakers distorted mythological facts in their portrayal of the Ramayana.Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, also referred to as Ramayana: Part 1, is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. The film features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Its ensemble cast includes Sunny Deol, Ravie Dubey, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh and Vivek Oberoi.The film was released in theatres on November 5, 2026.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Punjab Governor Kataria Inaugurates 2-day FAP National Awards 2026 organised by Chandigarh University
content: Drug Menace Biggest Challenge Facing Punjab; Teachers Best Placed to Tackle It and Guide Youth on the Right Path, Says Governor Chandigarh, November 27, 2026: To recognise the invaluable contribution of private schools towards raising the standards of education, sports and culture in the country, Chandigarh University, in collaboration with the Federation of Private Schools and Associations of Punjab (FAP), felicitated 761 principals, teachers and students during the sixth edition of the FAP National Awards 2026, held at the university campus. Punjab Governor and Administrator of the Union Territory of Chandigarh, Gulab Chand Kataria, inaugurated the FAP National Awards 2026 as the chief guest. He was accompanied by Rajya Sabha MP and Chandigarh University Chancellor Satnam Singh Sandhu, former Northern Army Commander and guest of honour Lieutenant General (Retd.) Deependra Singh Hooda, Punjabi writer, singer and actor Happy Raikoti, Chandigarh University Vice-Chancellor Prof. (Dr.) S.S. Sehgal, and FAP President Dr. Jagjit Singh Dhuri, among other dignitaries. Of the 1,525 awards being presented during the FAP National Awards 2026, 761 schools, teachers, principals and meritorious students from 19 states and Union Territories — including Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Delhi, Chhattisgarh, Jammu and Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Chandigarh, Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and Nagaland — were honoured on the opening day. Lifetime Achievement Awards were conferred on 15 school principals and 15 teachers who have devoted a major part of their lives to the teaching profession and made a positive contribution to society. The Best School Award for academic achievements was presented to the top 50 schools whose students recorded the highest percentage of marks, with 97 per cent or above in Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations. For achievements in sports, the Best School Award was also presented to 52 schools that had secured first positions at the state level or won medals in national-level competitions.

headline: Punjab Governor and Administrator UT Chandigarh, GC Kataria Inaugurates 2-Day FAP National Awards 2026 Organised by Chandigarh University
content: PRNewswireChandigarh [India], November 27: To honour the invaluable contribution made by private schools in elevating the stature of education, sports and culture in the country, Chandigarh University in collaboration with Federation of Private Schools and Associations of Punjab (FAP) felicitated 761 principals, teachers and students from over 1157 schools across India during the 6th edition of the FAP National Awards 2026 held at Chandigarh University campus.Punjab Governor and Administrator of Union Territory (UT) Chandigarh, Gulab Chand Kataria inaugurated the FAP National Awards 2026 as the Chief Guest along with Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) and Chancellor, Chandigarh University, Satnam Singh Sandhu, former Northern Army Commander and guest of honour, Lieutenant General (Retired) Deependra Singh Hooda and other dignitaries including Punjabi writer, singer and actor Happy Raikoti, Vice Chancellor of Chandigarh University Prof (Dr) SS Sehgal, President of FAP, Dr Jagjit Singh Dhuri.Of the 1525 awards being conferred during FAP National Awards 2026, 761 schools, teachers, principals and meritorious students from 19 States & UTs – including Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Delhi, Chhattisgarh, Jammu and Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Chandigarh, Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and Nagaland - were conferred with awards on the opening day of 2026 edition. Besides Life Time Achievement Awards conferred on 15 School Principals and 15 Teachers who have given the maximum time of their lives to the teaching profession and contributed positively to society, Best School Award (for academic achievements) was conferred upon the top 50 schools that have the highest percentage of students scoring 97% and above marks in 10th and 12th board examinations. For achievements in sports, Best School Award was also conferred on top 52 schools who have won 1st position at the state level or won medals in national-level games. The Best Student (Pride of India) award was bestowed upon 254 meritorious students who have shown excellence in academics by scoring over 97% marks in the 10th and 12th board examinations. For achievements in sports, The Best Student (Pride of India) award was also conferred upon 368 students for winning medals at national level sports competitions. Seven Appreciation Awards were also given to non-teaching staff members schools for their exemplary contribution in school administration and management.In his inaugural address, Punjab Governor and Administrator of Chandigarh, GC Kataria said, "Punjab is the land of Gurus, great warriors, farmers and the people who save the nation from any calamity. But today drugs are the biggest challenge being faced by Punjab as the youth of the state are getting affected by it. Instead of blaming our youth, it's our responsibility to show the right path to the youth for living a good life. Teachers are the most capable to take up this challenge against drugs. If all teachers make an effort they can drive all the youth in the right direction. We need to make the campaign against drug menace a mass movement,".He said, "Only few people can't make Viksit Bharat by 2047 a reality. India was known as a global hub of education because of the educational institutions like Nalanda and Takshashila (two of the most prominent centers of higher learning in the ancient Indian subcontinent). Today, India is trying to regain its place in the world and it will become reality with the joint effort of all those working in the education sector,". He said the National Education Policy 2020 is transforming India into a global education hub.The Punjab Governor, Kataria said, "In our country's education system, both the public and private sectors play a significant role. Nearly 52% of students in Punjab are part of the private schools who are providing quality education. Therefore, public and private institutions should not act as competitors, but rather as complements to one another,".Commending the award recipients for their significant contributions in shaping the minds of the youth, MP and Chancellor of Chandigarh University, Satnam Singh Sandhu said, "As academic excellence, skill development and entrepreneurship hold immense importance in a country's development, our school teachers will play a pivotal role in establishing India as the skill capital of the world and transform the nation into a knowledge superpower. As we are moving towards the goal of building a Viksit Bharat, this goal can be achieved only through a world-class education system focusing on the intellectual, physical and moral development of children in the early grades. As its not possible for government to do everything or even fulfil the need of quality education, private schools have a big role to play in making the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat by 2047 a reality. So besides recognizing meritorious students, FAP Awards are a due and fitting recognition of significant role being played by private schools and their teachers in the society for providing quality education with utmost dedication and hard work,".In his address, President of FAP, Dr Jagjit Singh Dhuri said, "Private schools are playing a pivotal role in school education but their contribution in India's transformation was ignored and the teachers of private schools were not given due recognition. So the purpose of FAP awards is to give due recognition to private schools, their teachers and students with these awards. This initiative also encourages private schools to compete for achievements in the fields of academics, sports, cultural heritage, infrastructure and facilities," he added.As many as 764 Pride of School Awards will be given to school principals on the concluding day of the 6th edition of FAP National Awards 2026 on Saturday.About Chandigarh UniversityChandigarh University is a NAAC A+ Grade University and QS World Ranked University. This autonomous educational institution is approved by UGC and is located near Chandigarh in the state of Punjab. It is the youngest university in India and the only private university in Punjab to be honoured with A+ Grade by NAAC (National Assessment and Accreditation Council). CU offers more than 109 UG and PG programs in the field of engineering, management, pharmacy, law, architecture, journalism, animation, hotel management, commerce, and others. It has been awarded as The University with Best Placements by WCRC.Website address: https://www.cuchd.in/(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by PRNewswire. headline: Punjab sends panel of 4 doctors for Chandigarh DHS Appointment
content: Chandigarh: Punjab has forwarded a panel of four doctors to the Chandigarh administration for the appointment of the next Director of Health Services (DHS), as the tenure of the incumbent is set to end. Two senior doctors from Government Multi-Specialty Hospital (GMSH), Sector 16, Chandigarh, are among the leading contenders for the position.The panel includes a deputy medical superintendent and a radiologist from GMSH-16, a senior medical officer from Mohali and the head of the paediatrics department at GMSH-16.The current DHS, who has held the position for around five years, is due to retire from Punjab government service on November 30. She had received a one-year extension last year after attaining the retirement age. Her tenure in the Union Territory ended on November 23. Also Read:Class 12 Pass Man Posing as Doctor for 30 Years Arrested in Rs 200 Crore CSR Fraud CaseThe eligibility criteria for the latest selection process stipulate that candidates must be below 56 years of age. The upper age limit has been increased from 55 years, which was applicable during the previous recruitment round. However, only two of the four doctors included in the panel meet the revised age requirement, TOI reported. Under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, the DHS position in Chandigarh has traditionally been filled from the Punjab Civil Medical Services (PCMS) cadre.The selection process has also drawn attention because of a change in the eligibility pool. In 2025, applications were invited from candidates across the country following amendments to the Union Territory's recruitment rules. This time, however, the administration has restricted applications to doctors from Punjab.The development has once again brought into focus concerns over career advancement opportunities for doctors belonging to the UT cadre. Senior UT doctors have been seeking consideration for senior administrative positions, including DHS and Medical Superintendent, since the central service rules were framed in April 2022.An earlier plea before the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), filed by a medical superintendent seeking consideration under the rules, was dismissed as the relevant provisions had not yet been formally notified.Also Read:Rajasthan launches statewide crackdown on Quackery, holds district health officers accountable

headline: Punjab CM launches Smart Ration Card Scheme to benefit 10 lakh beneficiaries
content: Moga (Punjab) Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann launched the Smart Ration Card Scheme on Thursday (November 27, 2026) to extend food-security benefits to 10 lakh beneficiaries, asserting that his government has ensured that only the genuinely needy would receive their rightful entitlements through a transparent selection process. Bhagwant Mann’s journey from comedian to Chief Minister candidate storyline 1 Along with Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Mr. Mann distributed "Meri Rasoi" kits among beneficiaries on stage at an event in Moga. The kits contained pulses, sugar, salt, turmeric and mustard oil. The Chief Minister assured the beneficiaries of five kg of free wheat per family member per month after the completion of e-KYC. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/aam-aadmi-party/ Being Kejriwal storyline 1 "Our government has undertaken a special drive to issue 10 lakh new ration cards to the most deserving and needy families. The entire exercise has been conducted through a digital, transparent and impartial system to ensure that genuine beneficiaries receive their rightful entitlements, without any discrimination or political interference," he said. Mr. Mann noted that 19.25 lakh online applications were received during the special campaign launched in July. "People applied through sewa kendras, common service centres (CSCs) and online platforms, while the district administration conducted door-to-door verification to identify eligible families," he said. Mr. Mann said that under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013, Punjab currently has 1.36 crore beneficiaries belonging to 39.73 lakh families. A timely reset for the Food Security Act opinion 1 https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/punjab/ "All new ration card beneficiaries will receive a special Meri Rasoi kit comprising two kg of pulses, two kg of sugar, one kg of salt, 200 of grams turmeric powder and one litre mustard oil. Besides, they will continue to receive free wheat under the National Food Security Act," he said. The AAP government in Punjab is committed to ensuring food security for every deserving family, the Chief Minister said. These additional benefits will provide meaningful relief to ordinary households and strengthen the welfare support extended to the poorest sections of the society, he added.

headline: Punjab & Haryana High Court tells Centre it can't recommend new judges due to lack of courtrooms
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Friday said that the lack of infrastructure, particularly courtrooms, was preventing it from recommending names for elevation as judges [Vinod Dhattewal and others vs Union of India and others].A Bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Sanjiv Berry made the observation while impressing upon the Central government the urgent need to expand the High Court. The Union government is currently considering a financial plan for a comprehensive plan to create additional infrastructure at the High Court.After perusing the minutes of a recent meeting held under the chairmanship of the Union Home Secretary, the Court observed that some sort of routine procedure was being followed as the bureaucrats appeared to be unaware of the urgent needs of High Court."The officers may not be aware that we are not in a position... there are 85 sanctioned strength of judges. We are not able to recommend names because ... if we say it on record, it will be very embarrassing for the government," the Court observed during a hearing..In the order passed later, the Court recorded that though it has sanctioned a strength of 85 judges, the court halls available are much less. It also said that the parking space is turning out to be inadequate. "The High Court is thus in urgent need of additional infrastructure," the Court said.It asked Additional Solicitor General Satya Pal Jain to personally meet the Home Secretary and emphasize upon the Central government officials to take up the cause in right earnest at the earliest possible time..While the High Court has a sanctioned strength of 85 judges, it has only 69 courtrooms, some of which are also being used by Permanent Lok Adalats and Mediation Centres.The High Court, located in Sector 1 of Chandigarh, falls within the catchment area of Sukhna Lake. It is also a heritage building and part of the Chandigarh Capitol Complex, which has UNESCO World Heritage status. These factors make it difficult to expand the existing structure.A proposal is currently under consideration to construct a few additional courtrooms at the existing site, subject to several restrictions. The broader plan envisages additional courtrooms, expanded parking facilities, rooms for the administrative and judicial branches, and space for lawyers' chambers.The holistic plan has already been sent to the UNESCO and other international institutions for review. In the meantime, the Court has been considering the status of the recommendations sent to the Central Government for financial approval. .Today, the Court said that the minutes of the recent meeting indicate that bureaucrats were under an impression that "some sort of a supervisory functioning" was being done by them."Please tell them that is not their brief," the Court told the Additional Solicitor General Satya Pal Jain.The Court said the governments cannot decide what is needed for the High Court. "Ultimately, it is a project which is imminently needed for the efficient working of the court. It is for the court to assess. It is not for the governments to decide as to what infrastructure would be needed for the court. So let your officers be made very clear that it is not something... otherwise we will pass orders straightaway," the Bench said.It added that most essential activities of the High Court were also getting compromised on account of lack of infrastructure. The government must immediately extend a helping hand and see that the infrastructure is provided at the earliest, the Bench stressed. "The usual bureaucratic approach is not needed...Please tell them that we are not able to have required number of judges. We are not having place for the lawyers," the Court told the ASG..Unless the holistic plan is in place, the administration of justice in the court itself may have to suffer.Punjab and Haryana High COurt.In the order passed today, the Court recorded that the Union government has asked the Chandigarh Administration to share the financial proposal with the governments of Punjab and Haryana and also obtain the views of the High Court on the proposed holistic development plan.The Court said that the holistic plan was conceived by the High Court itself and then processed and forwarded by the UT Administration. "Therefore, we do not find any need for the administration to obtain views of the High Court when the project itself is initiated under its aegis," the Court said. It added that the sharing of costs between State governments of Punjab and Haryana will be done as per the agreed terms settled by the Union government but those aspects will be "adequately addressed at appropriate stage." "Preliminary estimates, therefore, mark the commencement of the project itself," it said. The Court recorded that it expects the concerned officials of the Union government to examine the issue with requisite sensitivity so as to ensure that the required infrastructure is made available for the court at the earliest possible. "We hope and trust that the authorities would give due priority to the imminent concerns of the Court as noticed above," the Bench said.It added that unless the holistic plan is in place, the administration of justice in the court itself may have to suffer. The Court was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by a court employee highlighting the lack of adequate infrastructure. The case will next be heard on December 11.

headline: Punjab News:Punjab Govt Declares Holiday on November 28 for Eligible Workers and Employees to Cast Their Votes in Municipal Corporation Patiala and Municipal Council Elections in Bagha Purana and Dharamkot
content: Punjab News:Punjab Govt Declares Holiday on November 28 for Eligible Workers and Employees to Cast Their Votes in Municipal Corporation Patiala and Municipal Council Elections in Bagha Purana and Dharamkot The Punjab Government has announced a special holiday to enable workers and employees registered as voters to exercise their right to vote in view of the elections to the Municipal Corporation, Patiala and the Municipal Councils of Bagha Purana and Dharamkot. As per the notification issued by the Department of Labour, Punjab, all adult workers and employees working in various establishments situated in the State of Punjab, who are registered as voters in the respective wards falling under the jurisdiction of the concerned Municipal Corporation/Municipal Councils, have been granted a holiday on the day of polling, ie November 28, 2026 (Saturday), to enable them to exercise their right to vote. This exemption has been granted from the provisions of sub-section (1) of Section 26 of the “Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (Central Act 37 of 2020)”, subject to the provisions regarding compensatory holidays under sub-sections (2) and (3) of Section 26 of the said Code. It is pertinent to mention that these elections are being held for 30 wards of the Municipal Corporation, Patiala, 15 wards of the Municipal Council, Bagha Purana and 7 wards of the Municipal Council, Dharamkot in Moga district. The notification further clarifies that the provisions regarding compensatory holidays under sub-section (3) of Section 26 shall remain applicable, thereby enabling the concerned workers and employees to exercise their democratic right to vote.

headline: Akali-BJP | Punjab's anti-incumbency votes have a new home
content: The coming together of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) in Punjab has ended the Congress’ position as the default front-runner in the coming Assembly election. Meanwhile, the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) faces both an eroding vote bank and a consolidated anti-incumbency challenge. The election has suddenly become very interesting. The Congress’ calculations of its position based on poll arithmetic are now threatened. Having won seven of the 13 Lok Sabha seats in the state in 2024, it had hoped to ride anti-AAP sentiment to power. Now it must compete for the anti-incumbency votes with the SAD-BJP alliance, rather than enjoy the benefits of being the sole viable alternative.

headline: Punjab poll on mind, Delhi Govt opens Kejriwal’s former CM residence ‘Sheesh Mahal’ to public scrutiny
content: The Delhi Government is all set to open the original Flagstaff Road residence that former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal had built for himself during his tenure.Pejoratively dubbed ‘Sheesh Mahal’ by the BJP, the opulent government bungalow has been preserved by the incumbent Rekha Gupta-led government, with the complex being opened first to the media today and subsequently to the public.Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Verma, whose ministry oversees the property, said, “Our sole objective is this: since public money — taxpayers’ money — has been invested here, we owe the public an account of every single penny. We must explain exactly where their funds have been spent, and, in fact, every government should do the same.”He said the facility had been opened to the public with this objective."Today, we invited the media; very soon, the people of Delhi will also be able to come and see it for themselves. We have disclosed details exclusively about the items that were purchased for this project," Verma said as the BJP seeks to send a message of Aam Aadmi Party chief's lifestyle to people ahead of Punjab elections.Related: From Rs 88-lakh chandeliers to a Rs 1.5-crore kitchen: What visitors can expect inside Delhi’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’Delhi Culture Minister Kapil Mishra also said that, starting today, people in Delhi and across the country would be able to see the ‘Sheesh Mahal’. "It has been opened to the media today, and through your cameras, the entire nation will witness the sordid game of corruption and plunder that Kejriwal played — at a time when Delhi was gasping for oxygen during the COVID-19 pandemic," Mishra said. He said the very man who once claimed he would live in a single-room house has engaged in massive corruption using public funds."Items have been sourced from various countries around the world: the marble was imported from Vietnam, the crockery from another nation, and the tables from yet another. Today, through your cameras, the whole country will see this truth with their own eyes," the minister added.

headline: Consumer Commission awards Rs 10 lakh compensation to Ludhiana man over delayed rejection of life insurance cover
content: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Ludhiana, has directed ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company to pay Rs 10 lakh compensation to a Ludhiana resident for deficiency in service and unfair trade practices.The commission held that the insurance company failed to take a timely decision on a life insurance proposal and communicated contradictory reasons for declining the insurance cover after the death of the proposed insured.The commission, comprising president Sanjeev Batra and member Monika Bhagat, partly passed the order while deciding a complaint filed by Nayan Chopra, a resident of Janta Nagar, Ludhiana.It directed the insurance company to pay the compensation within 30 days of receiving a copy of the order. In case of default, the amount will carry interest at 8 per cent per annum from the date of the order till actual payment.The dispute arose after Chopra and his family members obtained mortgage loans from ICICI Bank and paid a single premium of Rs 3,70,992 for a proposed group loan insurance cover of Rs 60 lakh in the name of Sangeeta Rani Chopra, one of the co-borrowers.Sangeeta Rani Chopra died on April 22, 2019, barely 23 days after the premium was paid on March 30, 2019. Her family subsequently lodged an insurance claim. However, the insurer declined the payout and refunded the premium amount.The insurance company maintained that no policy had been issued in the deceased’s name as the required medical examination had not been completed. It contended that the proposal was still under underwriting and that the deceased had not completed the formalities necessary for acceptance of the insurance cover.However, the commission observed that the insurance company had communicated different and contradictory reasons for declining the proposal. In an email dated June 13, 2019, it cited medical test findings, while a letter dated July 31, 2019, stated that the medical examinations had not been received. Other communications referred to a past medical history of bypass surgery.The commission noted that all these communications were issued after the death of Sangeeta Rani Chopra and no decision regarding acceptance or rejection of the proposal had been conveyed to her during her lifetime.Holding that the conduct of the insurance company amounted to deficiency in service and adoption of unfair trade practices, the commission observed that the delay and contradictory communications had seriously prejudiced the rights of the deceased and her family.It further observed that the insurer was expected to take a final decision within a reasonable period after receiving the premium, particularly when the insurance proposals of the other co-borrowers were being processed simultaneously.However, since no certificate of insurance had been issued in the deceased’s name, the commission declined to grant the full insured amount of Rs 60 lakh. It considered an award of Rs 10 lakh as just and appropriate, in addition to the premium refund of Rs 3,70,992 already received.The complaint against ICICI Bank and its Ludhiana branch was dismissed. The complaint was partly allowed against ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company and its branch office.

headline: Punjab Assembly elections: Kejriwal, CM Mann attend Shiv Bhajan event in Nangal as AAP eyes Hindu voters
content: With the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections approaching, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government has stepped up its outreach to Hindu voters in the politically significant Anandpur Sahib Assembly constituency. The party organised, ‘Ek Shaam Bhagwan Shiv Ke Naam’, in Nangal on Thursday evening to strengthen its connect with the Hindu community and project its commitment towards Sanatan traditions.AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann attended the religious gathering. Renowned singers Kailash Kher and Hansraj Raghuwanshi sang bhajans dedicated to Lord Shiva, turning the event into a major religious and political spectacle.The choice of Nangal for the programme assumes political significance as it falls in the Anandpur Sahib Assembly constituency represented by Education Minister Harjot Singh Bains. The constituency has a sizeable Hindu population, particularly in the Nangal region.Addressing the gathering, Kejriwal claimed that no government in the country had done as much for Sanatan Dharma as the Bhagwant Mann-led government in Punjab.He also announced that the Mata Kali Temple in Patiala was almost ready and would be inaugurated on December 13. Appealing to devotees to attend the inauguration, Kejriwal said the government was committed to facilitating religious and spiritual activities.Highlighting the expansion of the Chief Minister's 'Teerath Yatra Scheme', he said three new pilgrimage routes had been added. These include journeys to Salasar Balaji and Khatu Shyam, Haridwar and Rishikesh, and Mathura and Vrindavan, besides the existing religious destinations of Anandpur Sahib and Sri Darbar Sahib.CM Mann sought to strike an emotional chord with the gathering by recalling his childhood visits to the Mata Naina Devi temple in neighbouring Himachal Pradesh along with Anandpur Sahib.Mann said that Punjab's tradition of communal harmony shall remain despite attempts by political parties to divide people along religious and caste lines."This is Punjab, where all religious greetings and slogans are raised together. Punjab is an extremely fertile land. Almost every seed can grow in this soil, but the seed of hatred can never take root here," he said.People in Punjab celebrated Ram Navami, Gurpurabs, the Parkash Purabs of Guru Ravidas and Eid together, reflecting the state's shared cultural traditions, he said.The CM added that the Nangal region had remained neglected for decades and was treated as an untouchable area by political leaders who visited it only during elections. The AAP government had given the region the recognition and respect it deserved, he said.Mann claimed that about 78,000 government jobs had been provided transparently by his government. Referring to free electricity for households and the Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna schemes, he said that next installment financial assistance would be transferred directly to women from December 1.

headline: Money laundering probe: ED raids 8 locations in J&K, Punjab against ex-SSB official
content: The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) on Friday conducted searches at eight locations situated in Jammu & Kashmir and Punjab, including Kathua, Udhampur and Pathankot, relating to a fraudulent money multiplier/investment scheme allegedly operated by accused Gurmeet Singh, a former Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel and his associates.The ED investigation originates from multiple FIRs registered by various police authorities in Jammu & Kashmir, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana and Bihar for cheating public at large, including serving and retired SSB personnel who were reportedly persuaded to invest their funds on false promises of high and assured monthly returns.Scrutiny of financial data revealed that substantial amounts, running in crores were reportedly collected from investors through various entities and concerns like M/s Style O Industry, Kathua, M/s Style O Comfort Creations P Ltd and others allegedly controlled and operated by the accused persons.Further investigation is underway in the case, ED sources informed.

headline: Investor ‘fraud’: ED raids in Jammu, Punjab
content: Jammu, Nov 27 (PTI) The Enforcement Directorate on Friday conducted searches at multiple locations in Jammu and Kashmir and Punjab as part of a money laundering investigation against a former SSB official who allegedly duped many investors, including jawans of the paramilitary force, officials said. A total of eight locations in Jammu, Kathua, Udhampur and Pathankot were raided as part of the action under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), the officials said. The probe relates to a fraudulent money multiplier/investment scheme operated by the former Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel Gurmeet Singh and his associates, they said. The ED case stems from multiple FIRs registered by various police authorities in Jammu and Kashmir, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana and Bihar for “cheating” the public at large, including serving and retired SSB personnel who were persuaded to invest after being falsely promised high and assured monthly returns. The officials said substantial amounts, running into crores of rupees, were collected from the investors through various entities and companies.
