headline: Hoshiarpur-origin California martial arts fighter dies after tournament injury, funeral on November 30
content: A California-based Muay Thai fighter, who died on November 21 after suffering a severe head injury during a tournament in Madrid, Spain, was the son of Indian immigrants hailing from Hoshiarpur district of Punjab.Prabhjot Singh Mann (25), whose ancestors hailed from Bigra village in Hoshiarpur, had sustained the injury on November 7 and was airlifted to a local university hospital, where he remained in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) before succumbing to his injuries on November 21.Mann’s last rites and funeral services will be performed at a gurdwara in Fresno, California, on November 30.Mann, who hailed from Fresno, was deeply involved in the Sikh community in the Central Valley. Besides being a mixed martial arts (MMA) fighter, he was also a popular Bhangra performer.He volunteered in the community, mentored local youth and taught traditional Bhangra dance.The Indian community, especially the Sikh community, has expressed deep shock and grief over the incident, paying emotional tributes to Mann. A fundraising campaign was also initiated to support his treatment after he was flown from Spain to the US.

headline: RBI's first state debt switch success opens door for more auctions: Traders
content: The Reserve Bank of India's first ever ​switch of state government securities saw strong participation from lenders, leading to near full subscription. The strong response has market participants anticipating more rounds of such switch auctions. Indian ‌states sold debt worth around ​₹8,000 crore ($864.63 ​million) and bought back securities worth nearly ₹8,300 crore, the Reserve Bank of India said A switch auction allows the issuer to buy back shorter-term bonds with near-term maturities, while selling longer-dated papers ​at the same time. While the Indian federal ‌government holds switch auctions at least once a ​month, such auctions for state government securities have not taken place before. Bonds issued by the states of Madhya ‌Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil ​Nadu and Uttar Pradesh ‌were swapped at Thursday's auction. "Some banks wanted to let ‌go of the papers that are out of (the) ​money," a trader with a private bank said, replacing them with fresh notes that ​are easier to buy and sell. "We could see more such auctions in the ‌remaining part of the financial year," the trader added. Indian states plan to borrow ₹2.78 trillion through bonds in the October-December quarter of the current fiscal year.

headline: Punjab: 6 years on, farmers a strong pressure group but deep divisions a worry
content: Exactly six years ago, on November 26, 2020, farm unions gave the “Dilli Chalo” call, launching a historic protest that forced the Centre to repeal three farm laws. Today, that united front under the Samyukta Kisan Morcha (SKM) has fractured, with unions divided over their demands, loyalties and strategy.However, having demonstrated their ability to mobilise mass protests and force the Centre to roll back its decisions, farmers remain a formidable pressure group in Punjab, especially ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.The SAD-BJP reunion too has brought their demands back into the spotlight and farm bodies are looking toward Prime Minister Narendra Modi for possible announcements when he addresses a joint alliance rally in Moga on December 8. The question remains whether the Centre will use the occasion to address their concerns and whether the divided unions can still exert collective pressure.Alliance a ‘shot in the arm’ for someTwo farm factions, Bhartiya Kisan Union (BKU, Lakhowal) and BKU (Kadian), which had earlier announced support for SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, have welcomed the reunion.“The alliance will give strength to our demands,” said Harmeet Singh, who heads BKU (Kadian).He clarified that his support was for the regional party and said the union had submitted a charter seeking renegotiation of water-sharing agreements, waiver of cooperative-sector farm debt, MSP for all crops, crop diversification and groundwater conservation.Harinder Singh, general secretary of BKU (Lakhowal), said the alliance had brought their demands closer to acceptance. The faction had, interestingly, turned its back on SAD when the Centre announced the three farm laws, despite its president Ajmer Singh having served as Mandi Board chairman during the SAD-BJP government’s tenure.Sukhbir had recently also met BKU (Rajewal) president Balbir Singh Rajewal, seeking his support. Rajewal said his organisation would meet on December 5 to take a decision after reaching a consensus.SAD had initially supported the farm laws, with a video message by its late patriarch and five-time chief minister Parkash Singh Badal also circulating at the time. However, as protests intensified, Harsimrat Kaur Badal quit the Modi cabinet, and SAD subsequently severed its 24-year-old alliance with the BJP and exited the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).No support to any political partyThe left-leaning BKU (Ekta-Ugrahan), however, has rejected the idea of backing any political party.“These parties are anti-farmers and our fight is against them,” said its president Joginder Singh Ughrahan, adding that the agitation would continue until demands were met.The union’s demands include a legal guarantee for MSP on all crops, loan waivers for farmers and labourers, withdrawal of the Electricity Amendment Bill and Seed Bill, repeal of the four labour codes, cancellation of the proposed India-US free trade deal and restoration of the earlier MGNREGA framework.Protests continue, demands unresolvedThe divisions within the movement have become more evident in the agitations that followed the 2020-21 stir.“Since the AAP government took over in Punjab, two farm protests were withdrawn and demands remained unmet,” said Krantikari Kisan Union chief Darshan Pal, attributing the lack of progress to discord and poor coordination among unions.In February 2024, farmers under the Kisan Mazdoor Morcha and SKM (Non-Political) launched the “Delhi Chalo” march, seeking a legal guarantee for MSP, implementation of the Swaminathan Commission recommendations and debt waivers. Stopped by Haryana security forces, they set up protest sites at Shambhu and Khanauri.The agitation took a significant turn when 21-year-old Shubhkaran Singh died during clashes at Khanauri on February 21, 2024. On November 26 that year, SKM (Non-Political) leader Jagjit Singh Dallewal began an indefinite hunger strike at the site.After nearly 400 days of protests, police dismantled the makeshift camps on the intervening night of March 19 and 20, 2025, and detained farm leaders, including Dallewal.In September 2026, SKM, led by Rajewal, organised a seven-day sit-in involving 32 farmer organisations. BKU (Ekta-Ugrahan) stayed away and continued with its separate programme.Agriculture minister Gurmeet Singh Khudian had assured the unions that resolutions accepting their demands would be brought in the Vidhan Sabha, but the session held last month did not see this happen.According to Rajewal, successive governments have repeatedly failed farmers. “But the fight will continue,” he said.

headline: Constitution far greater than power, BJP weakening democratic institutions: Pargat at Amritsar rally
content: The Punjab Congress organised the “Save Constitution-Anti-Drug Rally” to mark Constitution Day on Thursday, with state chief Pargat Singh saying that BR Ambedkar gave the country a Constitution that guaranteed equal rights, dignity and justice to every citizen.Targeting the BJP-led central government, Pargat accused it of weakening constitutional and democratic institutions.“The Constitution is not merely a document but the soul of the nation and the spirit on which democracy rests. However, those in power today, instead of working within the constitutional framework, have started considering themselves above the Constitution. They must understand that power can never be greater than the Constitution; rather, the Constitution is far greater than power,” Pargat said while addressing the party rally in Amritsar.He said the Congress party had always upheld the Constitution above the government. Historic legislations such as the Right to Education and the Right to Information were introduced by the Congress, empowering ordinary citizens with the right to education and the right to seek accountability from the government.“In contrast, today’s governments are weakening constitutional institutions and people’s rights. The world is changing rapidly. Technology and artificial intelligence have ushered in a new era, and major transformations are expected in society, employment and working patterns in the coming years. Unfortunately, instead of receiving employment opportunities, the country’s youth are being forced to struggle from pillar to post,” said Pargat.The state Congress president said the biggest challenge before the country today was to protect the Constitution and democratic institutions. “There is a need for people to unite against forces that seek to crush the rights of ordinary citizens,” he said.He accused the BJP of promoting hatred and social divisions to remain in power, steadily moving the country toward fragmentation. At such a critical time, the Congress party and Rahul Gandhi were the ones fighting resolutely to safeguard the Constitution, democracy and the unity of the nation, he added.Leader of Opposition in the Punjab Vidhan Sabha Partap Singh Bajwa, manifesto committee chairman and MP Dr Amar Singh, MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla and former minister Raj Kumar Verka also addressed the gathering, comprising former MLAs, other senior Congress leaders and a large number of party workers.

headline: Chandigarh: Congress challenges poll panel’s SC certificates decision in HC
content: The Chandigarh Congress on Thursday moved the Punjab and Haryana high court (HC), challenging the state election commission’s decision restricting candidature on scheduled caste category seats to only those with a bona fide caste certificate issued by administration.The petition has been filed by Mamta Dogra and Meenu, two of the ticket aspirants from the party.On November 24, the commission had clarified that only Scheduled Castes certificates issued by the Chandigarh administration on a bona fide basis to residents belonging to the 36 castes notified for the Union Territory would be valid for contesting elections from SC-reserved wards. Certificates issued by the administration to residents who migrated from other states would not be accepted for this purpose, it had said.Lawyers said that a petition has been filed on Thursday and a request will be made on Friday for urgent listing of the matter.Violation of Article 14, claims petitionThe petition terms the commission’s move, a violation of Article 14 (equality before law) of the Constitution. The election commission’s condition is applicable in the case of those seeking employment and admissions to educational institutions in Chandigarh. It is not applicable in the case of fighting elections. Any ordinary voter of a particular state can contest election in that particular area, the petition argues.BJP, election panel conspiring to murder democracy: AAPOn the occasion of Constitution Day and the foundation day of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), the party’s local unit questioned the functioning of the BJP and the election commission. Party leaders alleged that new instructions issued just ahead of the elections are aimed at depriving members of the Scheduled Caste (SC) community of their democratic and political rights.Addressing the press conference, AAP Chandigarh president Vijay Pal Singh said denying electoral rights to their youth and women merely because their roots are linked to Punjab, Haryana or Uttar Pradesh is unjust. He alleged that the BJP, sensing a decline in its political support, was adopting new tactics to restrict the political participation of poor and Dalit communities, following the controversy surrounding the 2024 mayoral elections. AAP too will be moving court, Singh added.

headline: Sukhbir promises solar parks, SGST relief for industry
content: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal on Thursday said that if voted to power, the SAD-BJP alliance would establish solar parks in conjunction with the industry to ensure cheap power supply, besides allowing all new industries to retain the state Goods and Services Tax (SGST).Interacting with trade and industry representatives from Jagraon and Khanna, Sukhbir said the SAD was committed to resolving all pending issues faced by the industry as well as providing relief to traders.The SAD president said the industry would be invited to invest in the proposed solar parks according to their power requirements. “While power would be initially supplied at nominal rates for four years, it will become completely free later,” he said.He also assured industry representatives that the next government would allow multi-fuel use in the steel rolling industry.“We will provide power at ₹5 per unit to the industry besides reintroducing the Rahat scheme, under which small shopkeepers would be required to pay ₹1,000 per year and would be exempted from the requirement of keeping account books,” he said. He also announced that traders would be given a ₹10 lakh medical and fire cover besides a ₹15-lakh life insurance cover.Replying to a question from the Jagraon cold storage association, Sukhbir said the next government would distribute potatoes under the ‘atta-dal’ scheme whenever there was a glut to safeguard farmers as well as the cold storage industry.Badal also assured the arhtiya association that its demand for a 2.5% commission would be taken up for resolution.The SAD president also assured the brick kiln association that its members would not be forced to use pellets as fuel in brick kilns, as was being done now.He further assured Daal Mill association representative Kalpanik Bansal that the next SAD-BJP government would encourage the procurement and milling of pulses in Punjab. “We will start a ‘Grow in Punjab’ movement to encourage local produce,” he added.

headline: Bank holiday today: Are SBI, Canara branches in Bangalore closed on Friday, 27 November, for Kanakadasa Jayanthi?
content: Bank holidays today: Banks in Bangalore, including the State Bank of India, Canara Bank and HDFC Bank, will be closed today on account of Kanakadasa Jayanthi celebrationsas per the Reserve Bank of India calendar.Further, all public and private sector lenders across the country will be shut for the weekend on 28 and 29 November due to the fourth Saturday and Sunday holidays.How are bank hokidays decided?Notably, banks in India are closed for common national and gazetted holidays, weekend offs and local holidays and festivals off, as required. The central bank releases its annual, official bank holiday list in January. Please contact your nearest local bank branch for their confirmed holiday schedule for 2026.As per RBI rules, all scheduled and non-scheduled banks observe listed holidays and mandatory closure on second and fourth Saturdays and every Sunday in a month. In-branch services are shut, but digital services (online net banking, app) will remain operational.Banks will be closed on 16 days this month, including state and regional holidays and weekend offs. This includes:— Weekend offs on November 1, 8, 15, 22, 28, and 29 for Sunday; and November 14 and 28 for second and fourth Saturday holidays, respectively.— Besides these are regional holidays on November 9, 10, 11, 13, 16, 20, 23, 24 and 27.Bank holidays: November 2026 — Check full list of cities, datesBanks, including SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, Punjab National Bank, Canara Bank, Bank of Baroda and other lenders across India will remain closed on the following dates:November 1 (Sunday): Banks will be closed pan India for Sunday holiday.November 8 (Sunday): Banks will be closed pan India for Sunday holiday.November 9 (Monday): Banks will be closed in Agartala, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Gangtok, Imphal and Jaipur. Kanpur and Lucknow for Diwali, Laxmi Puja, Govardhan Pooja and Vishwakarma Day.November 10 (Tuesday): Banks will be closed in Ahmedabad, Belapur, Bengaluru, Dehradun, Gangtok, Mumbai and Nagpur on account of Bali Pratipada, Govardhan Puja, Laxmi Puja and Vikram Samvat New Year.November 11 (Wednesday): Banks will be closed in Gangtok, Imphal, Kanpur, Kolkata, Lucknow and Shimla for Laxmi Puja, Ningol Chakkouba, Bhai Dooj and Chitragupt Jayanti. Notably, Gangtok has three consecutive regional bank holidays.November 13 (Friday): Banks will be closed in Shillong for Wangala Festival.November 14 (Saturday): Banks will be closed pan India for second Saturday holiday.November 15 (Sunday): Banks will be closed pan India for Sunday holidayNovember 16 (Monday): Banks will be closed in Patna and Ranchi on account of Chhath Puja.November 20 (Friday): Banks will be closed in Dehradun to observe Igas-Bagwal.November 22 (Sunday): Banks will be closed pan India for Sunday holiday.November 23 (Monday): Banks will be closed in Shillong for Seng Kut Snem.November 24 (Tuesday): Banks will be closed in Aizawl, Belapur, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Dehradun, Hyderabad, Itanagar, Jaipur, Jammu and Kanpur. Kohima, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, New Delhi, Raipur, Ranchi, Shimla and Srinagar for observances including Guru Nanak Jayanti, Karthika Purnima and Rahas Purnima.November 27 (Friday): Banks will be closed in Bengaluru for Kanakadasa Jayanthi.November 28 (Saturday): Banks will be closed pan India for fourth Saturday holiday.November 29 (Sunday): Banks will be closed pan India for Sunday holiday.What can customers do for services on bank holidays?For customers who face urgent requirements or for daily spends, online banking services and bank mobile apps remain operational across the country even on official holidays and the weekends. You can thus use these uninterrupted services for convenient financial transactions.— UPI transactions: An individual can use UPI or the respective bank's app to make payments and receive money from others. These services work round the clock, whether banks are open or not. Though, at times, it may be down due to scheduled maintenance during which the banks will notify you.— NEFT / RTGS: Additionally, fund transfer requests can be made using NEFT / RTGS transfer forms, demand draft request forms and cheque book forms.— ATM services: Apart from those options, credit cards, debit cards, and ATM cards can also be obtained through card services. Services such as account maintenance forms, setting up standing instructions, and applying for a locker are also available.Disclaimer: This story is for educational purposes only. Check the official RBI or respective bank websites for bank holiday calendar, alerts and notifications.

headline: Drugs seized from medical store, residential premises in Rajpura
content: A major recovery of drugs was made from the residential premises and medical store of the owner of M/s Sapna Medicos, Grain Market, Rajpura, during a joint inspection conducted in connection with the investigation following registration of an FIR.Zonal Drug Licensing Authority Navjot Kaur informed that the joint operation was conducted by Drug Control Officer Patiala-2 Parneet Kaur, along with the SHO, Rajpura city police station and in-charge of the Focal Point Chowki.During the operation, seven types of drugs, containing salts including tapentadol, pregabalin-75, olanzapine and MTP kits, worth approximately Rs 2.39 lakh were allegedly seized from the residential premises by the Drug Control Officer. Three samples were taken for test and analysis, while the police seized nine types of drugs worth approximately Rs 7.99 lakh. The accused was booked under relevant provisions of the NDPS Act.Navjot Kaur further informed that the medical store was subsequently inspected in the evening, during which five types of drugs/items, including secondary packaging of pregabalin-300, tapentadol, clonazepam and alprazolam, worth approximately Rs 4,710, were seized by the Drug Control Officer. Additionally, two types of drugs containing tramadol, worth approximately Rs 19,424, were handed over to the police for further necessary action under the NDPS Act.“In the interest of public safety and to prevent any misuse of drugs, the medical store was sealed on the spot,” she added.

headline: Campaigning ends for Patiala MC re-polls, 165 in fray
content: Campaigning for the re-elections to 30 wards of the Municipal Corporation Patiala ended on a high note on Thursday evening, with major political parties, including the Congress, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), holding separate roadshows and nukkad rallies across various parts of the city to woo voters.Polling for the 30 wards is scheduled for November 28. As many as 165 candidates, including 45 Independents, are in the electoral fray, setting the stage for a keen contest among the four major political parties.The ruling AAP stepped up its campaign with local MLA Ajitpal Singh Kohli leading roadshows in several wards of the royal city.Patiala Mayor Kundan Gogia also campaigned extensively for party candidates, particularly in Ward No. 57, 45 and 58. He also joined a roadshow organised by the ruling party in Ward No. 58 of the city.The BJP, too, intensified its campaign during the final hours. Punjabi film producer and actor Hobby Dhaliwal accompanied BJP Punjab Yuva Morcha president Anuj Khosla, who is contesting from Ward No. 40. Khosla, a former councillor, is locked in a keen contest against Sanjeev Kakkar of the Aam Admi Party.District Planning Board Chairman Tejinder Mehta, who is seeking re-election from Ward No. 34, also held a roadshow in his ward to mobilise voters in his favour.Former Punjab Youth Congress president Mohit Mohindra campaigned for party candidate Gaurav Goyal in Ward No. 34 and a few other wards, seeking support for the party’s nominees.Punjab BJP Mahila Morcha president Jai Inder Kaur also canvassed for party candidates in several wards, urging voters to support the party nominees.With campaigning drawing to a close, candidates and their supporters are now preparing for door-to-door canvassing and the polling day, when the electoral outcome in 30 wards will provide an important political indicator in Patiala ahead of the forthcoming Punjab Assembly elections.

headline: Samyukt Kisan Morcha holds massive rally at PUDA Ground in Patiala
content: In response to a national call by the Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM), the Punjab chapter organised a rally today, at the PUDA Ground in Patiala. Farmers from seven districts of the Malwa region — Patiala, Sangrur, Mohali, Ludhiana, Ropar, Fatehgarh Sahib, and Malerkotla — participated in the event. Leaders from 15 farmer organisations affiliated with the Samyukt Kisan Morcha took part in the rally. It is noteworthy that, on the occasion of the sixth anniversary of the historic “Delhi Morcha” (farmers’ protest), and following a call by the Samyukt Kisan Morcha, four rallies were held in Punjab today — in Patiala, Bathinda, Jalandhar and Amritsar.Addressing the gathering, the speakers urged the public to question political parties during the upcoming elections regarding their future plans to resolve the deepening crisis concerning Punjab’s water resources and its agricultural sector.The leaders sharply criticised both the BJP-led Central government and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab for failing to implement the farmers’ demands that had previously been accepted. They pointed out that the BJP had initially agreed to the demand for a law guaranteeing the procurement of crops at Minimum Support Price (MSP), but subsequently backtracked.“On the other hand, the Punjab Government avoided tabling a resolution in the Legislative Assembly regarding several agreed-upon demands. These included a resolution to repeal Sections 78, 79 and 80 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act —which symbolise the injustice inflicted upon Punjab by the Centre concerning its river waters — as well as the implementation of a one-time settlement scheme for loans taken from cooperative institutions,” said senior leaders Balbir Rajewal and Dr Darshanpal.They said a strategy would be formulated in a future meeting of the Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM) to hold the parties running both the state and Central governments accountable.Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM) leaders termed Rs 15 increase in the sugarcane price as “negligible”. They said by implementing such a meagre hike — despite rising input costs and the skyrocketing prices of sugar — the Punjab Government has played a cruel joke on sugarcane farmers. “The price of sugarcane be set at Rs 500 per quintal and that all outstanding dues be released immediately through the implementation of a ‘single-window, single-payment’ scheme,” they said.Another SKM leader Jagmohan Singh Patiala issued a stern warning to the BJP-led Central government, asserting that any anti-national, duty-free agreement entered into under American pressure would not be tolerated. Describing the US government’s policy of imposing a 25% tariff on India as “imperialist bullying”, they declared that citizens of the country would not forgive the Modi government for its policy of kowtowing to the United States.

headline: Canal water utilisation rises to 82% in Punjab: Minister
content: Punjab Cabinet Minister Barinder Kumar Goyal on Wednesday highlighted the state government’s efforts to improve groundwater management, expand canal irrigation and strengthen the regulation of mining activities, while admitting that Punjab was facing a shortage of police personnel.Interacting with mediapersons at Vishwakarma Mandir in Phagwara, Goyal said the groundwater situation had shown improvement over the past five years, attributing it to increased utilisation of canal water and efforts to reduce farmers’ dependence on tube wells. He said canal-water utilisation had increased substantially during the AAP government’s tenure, reaching approximately 80 to 82 per cent in 2026.Referring to the government’s water conservation initiatives, the minister said canal rehabilitation, restoration of neglected irrigation channels and expansion of pipeline-based irrigation facilities were helping improve the availability of surface water, particularly in areas that had remained deprived of regular canal irrigation for decades.However, when questioned about reports of dry canals and alleged illegal encroachments on canal land, particularly involving two important canals in Phagwara, Goyal initially denied the existence of such encroachments but subsequently assured that the complaints would be examined and investigated at a higher level.On the law-and-order front, the minister acknowledged that Punjab was facing a shortage of police personnel, underlining the need to address the manpower requirements of the police force. Goyal, who also holds the Mining and Geology portfolio, referred to the department’s efforts to curb illegal mining and improve transparency through technology-driven monitoring. According to figures shared by him, the state’s mining revenue had increased to Rs 799 crore in 2025-26, against Rs 123.5 crore in 2017-18.He attributed the growth to improved monitoring, digital mechanisms, drone mapping and stricter enforcement. The minister also criticised the proposed political understanding between the Shiromani Akali Dal and the Bharatiya Janata Party, describing their alliance as “principle-less”. Earlier, Goyal paid obeisance at Vishwakarma Mandir in Phagwara. He was welcomed by temple management committee president Pardeep Dhiman, Gurmukh Singh Chana and Daljit Raju. He also interacted with members of the temple management and mediapersons during his visit.

headline: Kartarpur Corridor to reopen ‘at right time’: Som Parkash
content: Senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and former Union Minister of State Som Parkash stated that the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor will be reopened “at the right time,” maintaining that the ongoing suspension of the cross-border pilgrimage route is guided by national security considerations.Speaking to reporters in Kapurthala, Parkash responded to questions regarding the political debate surrounding the closure of the corridor, which links Gurdwara Dera Baba Nanak in Punjab’s Gurdaspur district to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Pakistan’s Narowal district. “There are security reasons and keeping those in mind, the corridor was built specifically for devotees to pay obeisance. It will be opened at the right time,” Parkash told reporters.His comments echo remarks made in New Delhi on Tuesday by Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Addressing a media briefing, Shah stated that the corridor—inaugurated in November 2019—was temporarily shut following Operation Sindoor in May 2025 due to security concerns and would be reopened “with full honour” once those concerns are addressed. Shah also urged political parties not to politicise matters related to national security.The 4.1-kilometre visa-free transit route has remained suspended since May 2025, despite India and Pakistan having renewed the bilateral Kartarpur Corridor Agreement for a five-year term in October 2024.Meanwhile, opposition parties in Punjab have continued to press the Union government for the resumption of pilgrim movement. Earlier this month, Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi requesting the reopening of the corridor ahead of Guru Nanak Dev’s Parkash Purab.On Tuesday, Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh also urged the Prime Minister to take steps toward restoring access, stating that the pilgrimage holds deep spiritual significance for devotees and calling for a balanced approach between security imperatives and religious access. He described the SAD-BJP alliance as a step toward stability in the state while criticising the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government over law and order and state finances.

headline: Employee leaders’ detention ahead of Moga rally sparks protest in Faridkot
content: The detention of several employee union leaders and the placement of some others under house arrest by the Faridkot police ahead of the Aam Aadmi Party’s rally in Moga on Thursday triggered resentment among various employee organisations.Representatives of several unions gathered at the city police station and staged a protest. Following nearly two hours of confrontation, the police released the detained leaders on Thursday morning.Employee representatives said the unions had not planned any protest or other programme during the AAP rally in Moga. Despite this, the police detained several of their colleagues and placed some union leaders under house arrest.They said Karan Jain, district president of the DC Office Employees Union, was picked up from his residence early on Thursday morning and taken to the city police station. Sukhwinder Singh Sukhi, district president of the Democratic Teachers’ Front, was also placed under house arrest.On learning about the police action, employees from various organisations, led by Gurnam Singh Virk, a state-level leader of the Ministerial Employees Union, gathered at the police station and raised slogans against the police. The police subsequently released Jain and the other detained employees.Addressing the protesters, Virk alleged that the AAP government had failed to fulfil even a single promise made to employees and pensioners. He said several rounds of meetings had been held with the government following prolonged protests, but none of the major demands had been addressed.He further alleged that even the demands accepted by the government had not been implemented.Virk said detaining employee leaders and placing others under house arrest, despite no protest being planned during the Moga rally, amounted to a violation of their democratic rights.He said employee organisations had decided to intensify their agitation against the government and asserted that the employee community would oppose the AAP in the forthcoming Assembly elections.However, police authorities denied arresting any union leader. A senior police officer, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said the police had formally requested employee union leaders not to disrupt law and order by blocking roads during the rally.

headline: Denied ticket, Punjab Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khuddian gets front-row seat at AAP Moga rally
content: Even though the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has decided not to field Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khuddian from the Lambi Assembly segment and instead announced the candidature of his nephew Randhir Singh Dhira, the minister was given a prominent place in the front row on the stage during the state government’s smart ration card distribution programme, which the party has projected as a ‘Khushhaal Punjab’ rally in Moga on Thursday.Khuddian arrived early at the venue and occupied his seat alongside other Cabinet ministers, including the party’s Punjab affairs in-charge Manish Sisodia, Aman Arora, Lal Chand Kataruchak, Dr Balbir Singh and Harbhajan Singh.Notably, Khuddian has already extended his support to Dhira. He was also present during Dhira’s roadshow in Lambi on November 20, when he formally kick-started his election campaign in Lambi.Khuddian’s name has not figured in the two lists of 71 candidates announced by the AAP so far. However, speculation continues over whether the party may field him from another constituency.Khuddian, meanwhile, has maintained that he is content with the opportunities given to him by the party. He contested from Lambi in the 2022 Assembly elections and defeated former Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal. He was later fielded against SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal’s wife and senior SAD leader Harsimrat Kaur Badal in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Bathinda, but lost.

headline: Juba Sangha: The grassroots club aiming to surprise India in the IWL
content: CHENNAI Susanta Deb and a few of his seniors from Delhi’s Zakir Husain College started the Juba Sangha club at CR Park back in 1999 as a passion project. “When the club began, we used to win almost 95 per cent of the local tournaments we took part in. Football is all about networking, and we used to have a strong network comprising students. Juba Sangha used to be a local team famous all over Delhi,” Deb tells Sportstar. In 2022 the club registered with the Delhi Soccer Association (DSA) with the hopes of going to the next level in the sport. Two years later, Juba Sangha created its senior women’s team, which has swiftly climbed the ladder and earned promotion to the Indian Women’s League this season. Incidentally, the first tournament the club as a whole took part in was the 2022-23 Women’s Under-17 League under the aegis of the DSA. The club got together some local children to make the team and finished third. “After that a year passed since I started researching women’s football. Whatever limited knowledge we had, at least in India, about football, we realised women’s football is a completely different concept than men’s. If you think you can run a women’s team in the way you do a men’s, then the chances of being successful are quite slim,” Deb explains. Help from Haryana “At that U-17 tournament, we saw that players from Haryana are quite good. When we saw them play, we noticed they had power in their shots, their passes crossing the halfway line. The champion side largely comprised players from the State. Then we began researching Haryana. After more than a year of this, we found Chuli Bagriyan village in Hisar district,” he continues. Vinod Kumar had been running his girls academy in that village since 2015. Deb and Co. travelled to the village, and that was the start of an instrumental collaboration which would see Juba Sangha form its senior women’s team in 2024. From then on, the side has earned a promotion in each season in professional football — from the Delhi Women’s Championship to the Delhi Premier League before entering the Indian Women’s League 2. A runner-up finish in the 2025-26 IWL 2 season saw Juba Sangha get promoted to IWL. The team’s players hail from primarily three places — Delhi, Haryana, or Habra in West Bengal. “Whatever teams we make for any league, we have a mix of players from these regions. Across these three spots, we have around 300 girls in the ecosystem,” Deb reveals. But it’s Vinod’s wards which make up the majority of Juba Sangha’s IWL squad in the ongoing campaign. On August 16, 2015, Vinod started a girls’ team. His students have been selected for national team camps in the past. Eight of them were part of the SAFF U-15 Championship-winning Indian side in 2018 — Manisha, Ritu Devi, Poonam, Anju, Kavita, Nisha, Varsha, and Kiran (current Juba Sangha captain). Vinod remembers that someone in Delhi had told Deb that to beat a particular team, which Vinod didn’t want to name, they would need his players. This is how the friendship between them began. READ: IWL 2026-27: Maimouna’s brace guides Sethu FC to 5-1 win over HOPS, lifts Madurai side to top of table https://sportstar.thehindu.com/football/womens-football/iwl-2026-27-sethu-fc-vs-hops-fc-5-1-victoire-maimouna-brace-kalyani-stadium-top-of-table/article71747934.ece#google_vignette “Susanta sir is a great man. He doesn’t really interfere with football matters and completely gives me the responsibility in things like forming a team and all,” Vinod says. The Haryana man is not the Juba Sangha head coach on paper — it is Kulbhushan Manderwal who’s also been associated with the club for some time — but he insists he’s a man who works on the ground and with the grassroots. Juba Sangha might be a debutant in IWL, but Vinod’s students have already experienced the rigours of the top-flight. They have played for teams like Sribhumi FC, Ara FC, Odisha Sports, Sethu FC, Odisha FC, NITA FA, and HOPS FC in the past. A dark horse? “We have an all-Indian team. We have put our trust in our own girls, and if you look at the squad in the last three years, 90 per cent of them are the same. Most of the children coming through the trials come from poor families. It’s not that children from well-to-do backgrounds aren’t coming, but they don’t stay too long. Even if you look at our main team, they come from poor families. Football is their life. They give their best,” Deb says. “Till now, we haven’t been able to get a sponsor. I have been footing the bills so far. Whatever money I earn from my construction business, I put in football. I have spent more than five crores in the last four years across the boys and girls teams. We don’t really get much help from AIFF. The passion keeps driving us. We had thought that when we reached a higher level, we would get a sponsor. Let’s see,” he adds. With these limitations and faith in its academy players, Juba Sangha had a dream IWL debut with a 2-0 win over HOPS FC, a city rival. However, it was soon brought back to reality after suffering a 0-8 thrashing by another city rival in Garhwal United. Vinod believes that the result was an aberration and backs his girls to improve. “We have worked on our defensive position. They are young children. Many of the first-team players were not available due to their NIS Diploma commitments. But we have motivated the players and said haar ke baad hi jeet hai (There’s victory after defeat),” he says. Before Juba Sangha’s campaign opener, Deb had a bold prediction. “We will surprise India. Like how at the World Cup, you have a dark horse. I hope that our girls will do just that.”

headline: Supreme Court grants three weeks interim bail to AAP leader in money laundering case
content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday gave three weeks interim bail to Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Deepak Singla in a money laundering case arising from a 2018 CBI complaint related to an alleged Rs 155 crore banking fraud..A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of the submissions of senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for Singla, that he had been in jail for more than six months and there was a family medical emergency as his father had undergone a "high risk liver transplant"..The apex court asked the Punjab and Haryana High Court to decide his plea for regular bail in two weeks from today and said the gravity of the offence can be taken to a logical conclusion in the trial..“We have not expressed any observations on the merits of the case,” the CJI said and disposed of the plea..Singla's plea was opposed by Additional Solicitor General S V Raju, appearing for the Enforcement Directorate, who said Rs 155 crore bank money was found deposited in his bank accounts..Supreme Court grants bail to former AAP MLA Naresh Balyan in MCOCA case.Singh countered this by saying that a key accused, Ashok Kumar Mitta, is already out on bail..“Then let him also remain in jail for 11 months,” the law officer replied..The senior advocate said the Punjab and Haryana High Court has so far not heard Singla's main plea seeking regular bail in the case..The AAP leader had contested the Delhi Assembly elections from Vishwas Nagar constituency and taken on organisational roles in Delhi, Goa, and Maharashtra..The plea, filed through lawyer Rajat Bhardwaj, had sought setting aside of the Punjab and Haryana High Court's refusal of bail..According to the plea, the ED arrested him eight years after the original FIR, with no fresh evidence and no permission from the trial court..Singla challenged the high court's September 9 order dismissing his regular bail plea under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA)..The plea sought interim bail while the appeal is pending and said he was not an accused in the CBI's main case. He was also not named in the ED's 2019 ECIR, its July 20, 2022 prosecution complaint or its September 1, 2025 supplementary complaint, it said.

headline: Delhi-Karnal Travel Time Set to Fall with Rs. 330.51 bn Corridor
content: The route will run parallel to NH-44, linking Delhi with Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal. The project has received clearances from the Centre and the Haryana government, while NHAI has granted land-use permission for pier construction, stations and the relocation of high-tension power lines. Preliminary work has begun on an approximately 22-km stretch between Narela and Murthal. The corridor is planned to have 22 stations, with most elevated and selected stations in Delhi and Panipat underground or at ground level. Trains will have a design speed of 180 kmph and an operating speed of 160 kmph, with proposed intervals of five to 10 minutes. The network will connect with the existing Delhi-Meerut corridor and several Metro, railway, bus and expressway links. Travel between Delhi and Panipat, which currently takes about two to two-and-a-half hours by road or regular train, is projected to fall to nearly one hour. The journey to Karnal, now requiring about three-and-a-half to four hours, is targeted at around 90 minutes. The planned interchanges at Sarai Kale Khan, Kashmere Gate, Kundli and the KMP Expressway could improve access to workplaces, educational institutions, markets and healthcare facilities. The project is also expected to influence residential and commercial development in Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal. Property industry representatives have said improved connectivity could support housing, offices, retail outlets, hotels and mixed-use projects, particularly around stations such as Kundli, Bahalgarh, Murthal and Ganaur. Haryana’s proposed Transit-Oriented Development policy could encourage denser development near stations, although the eventual impact will depend on construction progress, station accessibility, supporting infrastructure and the corridor’s actual travel times. headline: Haryana Board announces 2027 class X, XII exams; check dates
content: The Board of School Education Haryana (BSEH) has announced the examination schedule for the 2027 class X and class XII board examinations, with the Senior Secondary examinations beginning on March 3 and the Secondary examinations starting a day later, on March 4. The board has announced the overall examination windows, while the subject-wise date sheet is still awaited. According to the schedule, class XII examinations will be conducted from March 3 to April 8, 2027. The class X examinations will begin on March 4 and conclude on March 26. The announcement covers the start and end dates for both examinations but does not specify when individual subject papers will be held. The dates were announced through an official press release issued on November 26. BSEH chairman Shankar Lal Dhoopar and secretary Deepak Babulal Karwa jointly shared the schedule from Bhiwani, Haryana. The announcement provides students with the broad examination timeline ahead of the release of the detailed timetable. The detailed subject-wise date sheet will list the examination dates for individual papers in both classes. Students will be able to check the schedule on the board's official website, bseh.org.in , once it is published. The board has not yet announced a date for releasing the detailed timetable. For students appearing in class X, the examination period will span 23 days, from March 4 to March 26. The class XII examination window will extend over a longer period, beginning on March 3 and ending on April 8. These are the overall examination periods announced by the board and should not be treated as the dates for any particular subject paper. The board's announcement gives students, parents and schools an advance indication of the examination schedule for the 2026-27 academic session. However, candidates will need to refer to the subject-wise date sheet to confirm the date of each paper and plan their preparation around the individual examinations.

headline: NEWS RECEIVED FROM HARYANA STATE UNDER THE LEADERSHIP OF C.M.SH.NAYAB SINGH SAINI AND OTHER NEWS
content: *Providing Better and Modern Healthcare Facilities Close to People’s Homes State Government’s Top Priority- Arti Singh Rao* *Additional Rs 170.32 Lakh Approved for Construction of Healthcare Facilities in Karnal and Yamunanagar Districts* Chandigarh, November 27 – Haryana Health Minister, Ms. Arti Singh Rao said that providing better and modern healthcare facilities to every citizen close to their homes is the top priority of the State Government. Strengthening Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Sub-Health Centres (SHCs) and Block Public Health Units (BPHUs) in rural and semi-urban areas will further strengthen the healthcare security network for the people. The Health Minister said that an additional amount of Rs 170.32 lakh has been approved, taking into account the revised requirements for the construction of Primary Health Centres at Popra, Uplana and Jalmana in Karnal district, a Sub-Health Centre at Chamrori and a Block Public Health Unit at Pratap Nagar in Yamunanagar district, to expedite the execution of these projects. She directed the officers to pay special attention to the quality and timely completion of all construction works so that residents of the respective areas can avail themselves of the benefits of these healthcare facilities at the earliest. Sharing further information in this regard, a spokesperson of the department said that the revised rough cost estimates had been received from the Civil Surgeons of the districts concerned. These estimates were prepared by the Executive Engineers of the respective Zila Parishads, taking into account site-specific requirements and revised cost assessments.

headline: Delhi's AQI continues to remain poor; DTU records highest reading at 304
content: Delhi’s air quality remained in the ‘poor’ category on Friday, with the city-wide Air Quality Index (AQI) at 220 at 8 am, according to real-time data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). The reading was slightly lower than Thursday’s 226, while PM2.5 remained the prominent pollutant. Of the 59 monitoring stations, 55 reported valid readings. Of these, 38 recorded AQI levels above 200, while two entered the ‘very poor’ category, with readings above 300. Under the CPCB's National Air Quality Index classification, readings between 0 and 50 are categorised as ‘good’, 51 and 100 as ‘satisfactory’, 101 and 200 as ‘moderate’, 201 and 300 as ‘poor’, 301 and 400 as ‘very poor’, and 401 and 500 as ‘severe’. Delhi Technological University (DTU) recorded the highest AQI at 304, followed by CRRI Mathura Road and North Campus of Delhi University at 292 each. Ghoga recorded 289, followed by IGI Airport (T3) at 289, Burari Crossing at 287, ITO at 285, Pusa (IITM) at 282 and Sirifort at 280. Meanwhile, Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium recorded the lowest AQI at 125, followed by Pusa (DPCC) at 135 and Lodhi Road at 141. IMD Lodhi Road recorded 142, while Najafgarh stood at 146. These locations were in the ‘moderate’ category. Air quality across the National Capital Region (NCR) remained largely in the ‘poor’ category. Gurugram recorded the highest AQI among the neighbouring cities at 291, followed by Faridabad and Greater Noida at 231 each. Noida's air quality index stood at 229. Sirsa in Haryana recorded the highest AQI among the 286 cities covered in the CPCB’s latest national bulletin, issued on November 26 at 4 pm. Its AQI stood at 355, placing it in the ‘very poor’ category. Anpara in Uttar Pradesh followed at 310, while Ballabgarh in Haryana recorded 305.

headline: Haryana rights panel seeks report on playground land at Gohana school
content: Gohana: The Haryana Human Rights Commission has expressed concern over the lack of adequate playground facilities for 862 students of Government Senior Secondary School, Gohana, despite 27 kanals and 10 marlas (around 3.44 acres) being recorded in the education department’s possession since 1976-77.Commission chairperson Justice Lalit Batra (retd) directed the principal secretary (school education) to coordinate with the Sonipat deputy commissioner and district education officer and submit a detailed report on the land’s status, possession and availability for students at least a week before the next hearing.A four-member committee inspected the school and submitted a report dated Nov 2, 2026, with photographs, a site map and records. It found 28 shops, a police post and Government Primary School, Mughalpura, operating on portions of the land. The primary school occupies around 430 square yards. Shopkeepers told the team that rent was deposited with the SDM’s office. The Municipal Committee holds the playground’s entrance key, while the SDM permits public events there.Revenue records classify the land as ‘Gair Mumkin Maidan’ (playground), with the possession column carrying the entry ‘Makbuja Mahkama Taleem’ since 1976-77.The school operates from two campuses about 170 feet apart, housing 581 and 281 students. The Commission said the nearby Shaheed Madan Lal Dhingra Stadium, 350-400 metres away, could not justify denying students access to land recorded as being in the education department’s possession.The district education officer recommended joint demarcation and examination of the shops and police post. The next hearing is scheduled for Feb 10, 2027. headline: Haryana Congress holds ‘save Constitution’ march in P’kula
content: The Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee (HPCC), following directions from the Congress high command, organised a “Samvidhan Raksha March” (save Constitution march) in Panchkula on Thursday to mark Constitution Day. Senior leaders accused the BJP government of undermining democratic institutions and citizens’ voting rights.The march started from Maharana Pratap Bhawan and culminated at Dr BR Ambedkar Chowk. It was led by All India Congress Committee (AICC) in-charge for Haryana Sanjay Dutt, HPCC president Rao Narender Singh and Congress Legislature Party leader and former chief minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda. MPs, MLAs, district and block Congress committee presidents, office-bearers of various party wings and a large number of workers participated.During the programme, party leaders and workers collectively read out the Preamble to the Constitution and took a pledge to protect its fundamental values and the country’s democratic framework.Addressing the gathering, Dutt said protecting the Constitution and democracy was no longer merely a political issue but a question concerning the nation’s future and citizens’ rights. He accused the BJP government of weakening constitutional institutions and undermining voting rights. Raising concerns over electoral rolls, the alleged deletion of voters’ names and transparency in elections, he said these developments posed a serious threat to democracy.Rao Narender Singh said the Constitution was not merely a document but a guarantee of citizens’ rights, dignity, equality and justice. Referring to BR Ambedkar’s vision, he stressed the importance of social justice, equal opportunities and fraternity.Hooda said any attack on the Constitution amounted to an attack on democracy and citizens’ rights. He said ensuring free and fair elections was the Election Commission’s constitutional responsibility. The Congress, he added, would continue its struggle to protect constitutional institutions, electoral transparency and democratic rights, both on the streets and inside legislatures.

headline: Haryana minister Goel divested of civil aviation portfolio, CM to keep it | Hindustan Times
content: In a surprise development, Haryana revenue minister Vipul Goel was on Wednesday night divested of the civil aviation portfolio by chief minister Nayab Singh Saini. Goel who is also revenue and urban local bodies minister however continues to be so.Saini will now hold the charge of the civil aviation department in addition to his existing ones with immediate effect. Orders to this effect were issued by chief secretary Anurag Rastogi and secretary to the governor, Vijay Kumar Bhavikatti.When asked, Goel told HT that the decision to take away his portfolio was mutually agreed by him and the CM. “Since the civil aviation department looks after the state aircrafts – a 10-seater Beechcraft King Air 250 purchased in 2018 for VVIPs luxury travels and an Airbus H145 D3 chopper bought in 2024 – which are used by the CM and governor, it was decided that the CM should keep the civil aviation portfolio in the interest of efficient functioning,’’ Goel said while downplaying the development.The shift however has come in the backdrop of a Hindustan Times investigation on July 7 that found Hisar airport handled only 9,559 passengers and recorded 474 aircraft movements between April 2025 and March 2026 despite a nearly ₹1,457-crore investment, according to Airports Authority of India (AAI) data. The figures placed Hisar among the least-utilised commercial airports in the country.The statistics highlighted the gap between spending on the airport and its actual use. At present, the airport operates seven arrivals and seven departures a week, connecting Delhi, Chandigarh, Jaipur and Ayodhya, with Ayodhya accounting for nearly 47% of passenger traffic. A former IAS officer who once handled the civil aviation department told HT that Hisar airport is an expensive showpiece—a marquee project yet to justify its investment. “It is a case of dream selling backed by massive public investment but limited utilisation, a grand vision confronting ground realities,” the officer said.The airport did not handle any cargo during 2025–26, and passenger traffic declined by 8.3% during April and May 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier. Hisar airport faces headwinds from a limited passenger catchment and proximity to Delhi airport, which offers wider connectivity.The scale of spending is also reflected in the state’s budget allocation. The ₹315-crore capital outlay for the integrated aviation hub accounts for about 63% of the civil aviation department’s ₹495-crore capital allocation for 2026–27.Responding to the July investigation, Goel had said the numbers reflected the early phase of commercial operations, which began in April 2025. He cited limits on daylight operations, terminal capacity constraints and the lack of instrument approach facilities as factors affecting flights.Goel had said the government was working to upgrade navigation and landing systems, expand flight routes and build passenger and cargo infrastructure, while engaging with airlines, maintenance firms and logistics operators to draw aviation-linked businesses to the airport.

headline: After Punjab, Haryana has highest exploited groundwater in country, cites NGT report | Hindustan Times
content: Haryana has the second-highest proportion of over-exploited groundwater assessment units in the country, with nearly 64% of its assessed areas falling in the category, according to a report submitted before the National Green Tribunal (NGT).The report of a joint committee constituted by the NGT shows that 91 of Haryana’s 143 groundwater assessment units, or 63.64%, are over-exploited. The number has increased from 88 units, accounting for 61.54%, in the earlier assessment placed before the tribunal.Whereas the neighboring state Punjab has the highest proportion with 111 of its assessment units (72.55%) classified as over-exploited. Haryana is followed by several states facing varying degrees of groundwater stress, including Rajasthan and Delhi, while the committee’s comparative assessment shows a marginal increase in Haryana’s over-exploited units.The report was prepared by a five-member joint committee comprising representatives of the Union environment ministry, the CSIR-National Geophysical Research Institute, the Geological Survey of India, IIT-Roorkee and the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA). The report was submitted on Wednesday in compliance with an NGT order dated April 23, 2026.The findings assume significance for Haryana, where agriculture remains heavily dependent on groundwater for irrigation and several districts have been grappling with falling water tables.According to the report, the committee examined state-wise data on over-exploited assessment units, regulatory mechanisms, illegal groundwater extraction, enforcement action and environmental compensation. It noted considerable variation among states in the implementation of groundwater regulations and the recovery of environmental compensation.The panel report also flagged shortcomings in the information supplied by several states and union territories, including inadequate identification of groundwater extraction units in stressed areas, lack of uniform criteria for granting permissions, insufficient monitoring of groundwater abstraction and the presence of illegal extraction structures. It also pointed to gaps in the collection and utilisation of environmental compensation and weak links between groundwater extraction and recharge measures.Even as Haryana has a state-level groundwater regulatory framework through the Haryana Water Resources Authority (HWRA), the report noted that states which have established their own regulatory authorities need to ensure that enforcement mechanisms are adequately equipped and that there is no regulatory gap in monitoring groundwater extraction.The committee stressed that the effectiveness of groundwater regulation should not be measured merely by the number of no-objection certificates (NOCs) issued, notices served or compensation recovered. Instead, it should be assessed through a measurable reduction in unauthorised groundwater extraction, stabilisation of water levels and restoration of stressed aquifers.The report also highlights the scale of groundwater dependence nationally. In 2025, irrigation accounted for 215.10 billion cubic metres (87.01%), of the country’s total groundwater extraction. Domestic use accounted for 27.89 billion cubic metres (11.28%), while industrial use stood at 4.23 billion cubic metres (1.71%), reveals the report. It also recommended crop diversification, promotion of short-duration paddy varieties, drip and sprinkler irrigation, and better irrigation scheduling to reduce pressure on groundwater.

headline: Lawmakers discuss constitutional values, devp in Haryana assembly | Hindustan Times
content: Amid mild bickering and disagreements, lawmakers from the ruling BJP and the Opposition Congress on Thursday spoke at length on constitutional values and state’s development trajectory during the day- long special session of Haryana assembly. The special session was convened to mark Constitution Day. Congress MLA, Raghuvir Singh Kadian who spoke first from the opposition benches made certain remarks with reference to the RSS but was asked to refrain from doing so by the Speaker, Harvinder Kalyan.The Speaker asked Kadian not to deviate from the subject. Chief minister Nayab Singh Saini also urged the opposition MLAs not to stick to the topic. Pointing to the Congress benches, Saini reminded who the founder of the Congress was, stating that even Mahatma Gandhi proposed disbanding the Congress after India attained independence.Congress Legislature Party (CLP) leader, Bhupinder Singh Hooda said if the Speaker was asking Kadian to stick to the subject, then the same rule should apply to the ruling party MLAs also.Kadian said that until a decade ago, fingers were never pointed at the constitutional bodies. “But it is happening now,” he said. The Congress MLA said the manner in which attempts are being made to gain control over the functioning of the autonomous bodies is a cause of deep concern. “Samvidhan Raksha marches are being held across the country. Why have things come to this,” he asked. State energy minister Anil Vij during his address targeted the Congress saying the opposition which claimed that the Constitution was under threat should explain who actually had undermined the spirit of Constitution and democratic institutions. Vij said the country had witnessed a period when democratic rights were violated, citizens’ voices were suppressed and the spirit of the Constitution was deeply hurt. Referring to the Emergency imposed in 1975, he said that citizens’ rights were curtailed, the press was subjected to censorship, and leaders and workers of opposition parties were imprisoned. He said that during that period, even expressing one’s views had become difficult and people were denied the freedom to speak.Leader of Opposition Hooda said that the Constitution was not merely a book, it was the nation’s soul.Hooda said there was a need to keep our institutions like Election Commission, media autonomous because if any one of these become weak then democracy cannot survive. “If democracy does not survive, the constitution will not survive. And this country won’t be there,” Hooda said.Saini in his address said that the Constitution was the guiding force for our present and future. Over the past 77 years, the Constitution has shown the country the right path in overcoming every challenge. Respecting the Constitution is not the responsibility of any one political party or government, but the duty of every individual whom the people have entrusted with the opportunity to serve them, Saini said.The CM said it was a matter of pride that seven eminent personalities from Haryana — Captain Ranjit Singh, Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava, Rao Bahadur Chaudhary Suraj Mal, Pandit Shri Ram Sharma, Master Nand Lal, Chaudhary Ranbir Singh Hooda and Lala Deshbandhu Gupta — contributed to the deliberations of the Constituent Assembly. The CM said that while commemorating this significant occasion, everyone must also remember that November 26 marked the anniversary of the 2008 Mumbai terror attack.Saini said that the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on December 9, 1946. After nearly three years of deliberations, the Constitution was adopted on November 26, 1949. At that time, it comprised 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules. The Constituent Assembly deliberated on several important issues during its 11 sessions, while thousands of amendments proposed to the draft Constitution were given serious consideration. During this extensive process, the voices of every section of Indian society and every region of the country were heard. The framing of the Constitution was not merely an exercise in preparing a document, but a powerful endeavour to find a path of consensus, dialogue and democratic decorum for a nation marked by immense diversity.“The Constitution was not the creation of any one individual, but the outcome of the collective wisdom of the Constituent Assembly and the collective aspirations of the nation. On January 24, 1950, 284 members signed the Constitution, bearing testimony to India’s democratic commitment,” he said.

headline: Himachal to Recruit 661 Data Entry Operators, Junior Office Assistants for Digitalisation of Hospitals
content: The Himachal Pradesh Government is set to introduce a Hospital Management Information System (HMIS) across healthcare institutions in the state to strengthen digital healthcare services and streamline hospital administration. Under the initiative, the government has approved the recruitment of 661 Data Entry Operators and Junior Office Assistants (IT) to ensure the smooth implementation and operation of the system. With the introduction of HMIS, doctors will be able to access patients’ medical histories, treatment records and medical reports with a single click. The system will facilitate the digitisation of patient information and hospital-related records, making the treatment process more efficient and improving coordination among healthcare institutions. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said the HMIS initiative aims to bring greater transparency, efficiency and accountability to the healthcare system. He added that the government is strengthening IT-related human resources in medical institutions to ensure the effective implementation of technology-driven services. The Chief Minister said the state government is continuously working towards modernising healthcare infrastructure, improving patient care and ensuring that people across Himachal Pradesh benefit from technological advancements. Of the 661 approved positions, 20 will be filled at the Directorate of Medical Education, Shimla, while 100 posts have been allocated to Indira Gandhi Medical College (IGMC), Shimla. Similarly, 61 positions will be filled at Lal Bahadur Shastri Government Medical College, Nerchowk; 50 at Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Government Medical College, Chamba; 100 at Dr. Rajendra Prasad Government Medical College, Tanda; and 90 at Dr. Radhakrishnan Government Medical College, Hamirpur.

headline: Himachal School Introduces 'Honesty Shop' for Student Integrity
content: In a unique initiative aimed at instilling core values, a government senior secondary school in Himachal Pradesh's Bilaspur district has introduced an 'Honesty Shop'. This novel concept operates on a trust-based system, allowing students to select items they require and deposit the stipulated payment into a collection box, thereby fostering a sense of self-discipline and integrity.Information was available with The Chenab Times that the primary objective behind establishing the 'Honesty Shop' is to cultivate honesty, self-discipline, and a robust sense of social responsibility among the student body. School Principal Madan Lal Sharma articulated on Friday that the endeavor is designed to nurture constitutional values through practical application. The shop is managed entirely by the students, who are expected to take items and make payments without direct supervision, emphasizing the importance of personal accountability.The initiative saw its formal launch with the presence of Azad Singh Verma, the president of the alumni association, who presided over the proceedings. During the event, the alumni association demonstrated its commitment to the school's welfare by donating an RO water purifier, further supporting the school's infrastructure and student well-being. This collaboration between the school administration and its alumni underscores a shared vision for holistic student development.The 'Honesty Shop' model, while new to this particular school, is not unprecedented in educational institutions across India. Similar initiatives have been successfully implemented in schools located in states such as Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Punjab. These existing programs have typically involved the sale of everyday stationery items or snacks, with the underlying principle remaining the same: to teach students integrity, responsibility, and the practice of self-governance in everyday transactions. The Bilaspur school's adoption of this model aims to replicate these positive outcomes within its own student community.The operational mechanism of the 'Honesty Shop' is straightforward yet profound. Students are provided with access to essential stationery supplies or other designated items. They are then expected to self-assess their needs, take the required articles, and subsequently deposit the fixed price of each item into a secure collection box. This system relies entirely on the students' inherent sense of morality and their understanding of fair practice. The school administration believes that this hands-on experience will be more impactful than theoretical lessons in developing these crucial life skills.The introduction of such programs is seen as a vital component of modern education, going beyond academic curricula to address the ethical and social development of young minds. In an era where integrity and accountability are increasingly valued, equipping students with the tools to practice these virtues from an early age is considered paramount. The 'Honesty Shop' provides a tangible environment for students to exercise ethical decision-making and understand the consequences of their actions, or inactions, in a low-stakes setting. This fosters a proactive approach to ethical conduct that can translate into various aspects of their lives.Principal Madan Lal Sharma further elaborated that the establishment of the 'Honesty Shop' is also aligned with broader educational goals of promoting civic sense and responsible citizenship. By entrusting students with the responsibility of managing their transactions, the school is encouraging them to think critically about fairness, honesty, and the collective good. This approach aims to create a generation of individuals who are not only academically proficient but also morally upright and socially conscious. The alumni association's support, including the donation of the RO water purifier, highlights the positive impact such community partnerships can have on educational institutions and the students they serve.The success of similar 'Honesty Shops' in other states has provided a positive precedent for this initiative. These models have consistently demonstrated improvements in student behavior, a reduction in petty pilferage, and a heightened sense of community within schools. The Bilaspur school administration is optimistic that this program will similarly contribute to a more disciplined and responsible student culture. The emphasis is on creating a learning environment where ethical behavior is not just taught, but actively practiced and reinforced through daily interactions and responsibilities. The long-term vision is to see these instilled values extend beyond the school gates into the wider community.The introduction of the 'Honesty Shop' is a step towards a more holistic educational paradigm, where character building is given as much importance as academic achievement. The school administration is confident that this trust-based system will yield significant positive results in shaping the character and conduct of its students, preparing them for the responsibilities of adulthood and active participation in society.

headline: Himachal's school introduces 'Honesty Shop' to promote self-discipline among students
content: A government senior secondary school in Himachal Pradesh's Bilaspur district has launched an 'Honesty Shop', an initiative to promote honesty among students. The shop operates without a shopkeeper and students can take the items they need and deposit the fixed price into a collection box themselves. The school's objective of this initiative is to cultivate honesty, self-discipline and a sense of social responsibility among the students and foster constitutional values, said Principal Madan Lal Sharma on Friday. The event was presided over by Azad Singh Verma, president of the alumni association. During the proceedings, the association gifted an RO water purifier to the school. Many schools in states like Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Punjab have backed such initiatives to teach students integrity, responsibility, and self-discipline using everyday stationery or snacks. headline: Two killed, three injured as vehicle plunges into gorge in Himachal’s Mandi
content: Shimla/Mandi (HP), Nov 27 (PTI) Two people were killed and three others injured after the vehicle they were travelling in veered off the road and plunged into a deep gorge in Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi district, police said on Friday. The accident occurred near the Pandar police outpost in the Nihri area of Sundernagar when the vehicle, carrying five people, was returning from a wedding ceremony. The occupants were part of the wedding procession (baraat), police said. The procession had travelled from Jaidevi to Kindar. The deceased have been identified as Vijay Kumar alias Rinku (36), son of Ramdas and a resident of Khagrao village, and Puneet Kumar alias Anku (34), son of Kewal Krishan and a resident of Bodlidhar village. The injured have been identified as Manoj Kumar, Surender Kumar and Pankaj Kumar, all residents of Bodlidhar. They were taken to a hospital, where they are undergoing treatment. One of them has been referred to AIIMS Bilaspur, police said. According to reports, the driver lost control of the vehicle near the Pandar outpost, causing it to plunge into the gorge. Local residents launched rescue efforts and helped pull the occupants out of the vehicle. Police personnel faced difficulties in extricating the victims from the wreckage due to darkness, Deputy Superintendent of Police Bharat Bhushan said.
