headline: Himachal forest fire: 200 hectares gutted, Kinnaur woman killed after burning branch falls on car
content: A massive forest fire has ravaged over 200 hectares of forest land in Nichar block of Kinnaur district, leaving a woman dead and several others injured.The woman was killed after a burning branch fell on a car passing through the affected area last evening. The driver lost control of the vehicle, which met with an accident, leaving two others injured. Several people have also sustained injuries while trying to douse the blaze.The fire has been raging for the past two to three days despite efforts by multiple agencies, including the Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), to bring it under control.“The fire broke out at a high altitude, where the slopes are extremely steep. This is making it difficult to contain the blaze,” said Kinnaur Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) Arvind Kumar. He said firefighting teams were now close to bringing it under control.The fire broke out at two locations — Urni and Chagaon. While the blaze at Urni has been brought under control, efforts are underway to douse the fire at Chagaon by noon on Thursday.Forest officials suspect human activity to be the cause of the fire. An FIR has been registered against unidentified persons.“There is a practice of setting fire to grasslands to promote the growth of fresh grass for cattle fodder. Someone may have set fire to a grassland, from where it spread uncontrollably,” the DFO said.The blaze spread rapidly due to the high-altitude location and strong winds that further fanned the flames. Army and ITBP personnel joined forest department officials and local residents in the firefighting operation.“The slopes are extremely steep, and there are no motorable roads to transport water tankers to the affected areas. Falling rocks from the heights have added to the challenges. Several firefighters were also injured while trying to control the blaze,” he said.The fire has caused extensive damage to forest resources and wildlife. The extent of the losses will be assessed after the blaze is completely extinguished.

headline: Prosecution sanction cannot be reversed without fresh evidence: Supreme Court
content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has held that a sanctioning authority cannot reverse its earlier decision refusing prosecution sanction merely on a change of opinion based on the same material, and quashed criminal proceedings against two Customs officials accused of facilitating the misdeclaration of imported air conditioners.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said that reconsideration of a decision refusing sanction could be permitted only when fresh material was subsequently collected and placed before the competent authority."Merely on a nudge by the Vigilance Commission, the opinion was changed which, as held in the cited decisions, was not permissible," the bench said.The court relied on its judgment in State of Himachal Pradesh Vs Nishant Sareen (2010), which held that a sanctioning authority cannot review or reconsider its earlier decision on the same material.The November 26, 2026 judgment came on appeals filed by P Kathirvel, an Assistant Commissioner of Customs, and S Gugan, an Examiner, challenging orders of the Madras High Court refusing to quash criminal proceedings arising from a CBI investigation.The case originated from an FIR registered by the CBI's Anti-Corruption Branch, Chennai, on February 29, 2012. It was alleged, M/s Majestic Impex had imported complete air conditioners but declared them as 'parts of air conditioners' in a Bill of Entry dated September 2, 2011, allegedly causing a revenue loss of Rs 42.05 lakh.Four Customs officials were initially accused of colluding with the importer.Examining Gugan's appeal, the court noted that the Commissioner of Customs had initially refused sanction after finding no prima facie evidence of criminal conspiracy, abuse of official position or receipt of illegal gratification.The Commissioner had concluded that the alleged failure to discharge official duties could attract disciplinary action under the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965, but did not warrant criminal prosecution.However, following the Central Vigilance Commission's agreement with the CBI's recommendation, sanction was subsequently granted without any fresh material being placed before the Commissioner..Supreme Court sends journalists’ police abuse allegations to inquiry panel; flags need to define journalist status.Setting aside the sanction order of September 30, 2013, the bench directed that no proceedings be taken against Gugan.The court then examined Kathirvel's role as Assistant Commissioner and the procedure followed for assessment and examination of imported goods.It noted that Kathirvel had assessed the Bills of Entry based on the importer's declaration, while physical examination of the goods was the responsibility of the examining officials. If any discrepancy was found, the Bills of Entry had to be returned to the Assessment Wing for reassessment.The bench observed that Gugan had reported the goods as air conditioners but failed to return the Bills of Entry despite the alleged discrepancy in their description.Kathirvel, therefore, was removed from the physical examination of the goods and could have verified the alleged misdeclaration only if the documents had been returned to him.The court also found that the chargesheet merely alleged deliberate intention on Kathirvel's part without substantiating it."There is no allegation of any illegal enrichment or even a dishonest intention of the appellant in assessing the goods, as per the description shown in the Bill of Entry," the judgment said.The bench thus held that mere dereliction of duty could not establish criminal culpability."A mere power conferred, coupled with a duty to random checking of goods cannot lead to inference of criminal culpability," it observed, adding that any duty lapse could have been dealt with departmentally.The court consequently quashed the proceedings against both officials pending before the Principal Special Judge (CBI), Chennai.However, it clarified that the prosecution against the importers, who were accused of knowingly misdeclaring the goods, would continue in accordance with law.

headline: Himachal fixes Rs 100 rate for 1,000 cubic feet of surplus raw water
content: Shimla: The Himachal Pradesh govt has approved a uniform policy fixing the rate for the sale and supply of surplus raw water to neighbouring states, govt agencies and industries at Rs 100 per 1,000 cubic feet. The rate will be revised periodically in line with the Wholesale Price Index (WPI).The policy will cover all existing and future water resources and projects, including interstate multipurpose projects, while ensuring that Himachal’s present and future water requirements remain the priority. It will not apply to water used for domestic purposes within the state.The move assumes significance in view of the Kishau Multipurpose Project, under which Himachal has an allocated share of 3.154% of the dam’s live storage, amounting to around 42 million cubic metres.The state also has an allocated share of Yamuna waters under a memorandum of understanding among Upper Yamuna Basin states for developing the Lakhwar, Kishau and Renuka Ji dam projects.Chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said the policy would establish a transparent and uniform mechanism for determining water prices and protect the state’s long-term financial interests.He said drinking water, irrigation, agriculture, environmental and developmental requirements would remain paramount before surplus water was supplied to other states or agencies. The policy aims to ensure appropriate economic returns from Himachal’s natural resources.

headline: Five killed, five injured in three road mishap across HP
content: Five persons were killed and five others injured in three separate road accidents reported from Mandi, Lahaul-Spiti and Una districts of Himachal Pradesh in past 24 hrs. The latest accident occurred around 7 pm on Thursday when an Alto taxi carrying five wedding guests plunged into a deep gorge near Pandar Chowki in the Nihri area of Sundernagar subdivision in Mandi district. Two occupants died in the accident, while three others sustained injuries. The victims were taken by ambulance to the Community Health Centre (CHC) at Rohanda, where two of them were declared dead on arrival. The injured were admitted for medical treatment. According to preliminary information, the occupants were returning from a wedding ceremony at Basek village in Bandli panchayat. They had travelled from Jaidevi to attend the function when the vehicle reportedly went out of control and plunged into the gorge. In another accident on Thursday evening, a young couple lost their lives when their pickup vehicle skidded off the road and fell into a waterlogged drain near Tandi in Lahaul-Spiti district. The accident occurred around 4 pm on the Tandi-Pukar link road while the vehicle was travelling from Gojang village towards Tandi. The deceased were identified as Ajay (24), son of Diwan Chand, and his wife Anjali, both residents of Katarain. Another occupant, Saksham, son of Jawahar Lal, a resident of Lapshak, sustained injuries and is undergoing treatment at Regional Hospital, Keylong. His condition was stated to be out of danger.

headline: Himachal to sell surplus water to other states as policy gets nod | Hindustan Times
content: The state government has approved a uniform state policy for the valuation, determination and periodic revision of rates for the sale and supply of surplus raw water from all existing and future water resources and projects of the state, including inter-state water projects.Under the policy, an initial benchmark rate of ₹100/1,000 cubic feet has been approved for the valuation and supply of surplus raw water. The rates will be revised periodically on the basis of the wholesale price index (WPI), ensuring that the economic value of water is protected against changes in prevailing price levels.In a statement issued on Thursday, the state government said the policy will ensure transparent and economically rational valuation of the state’s water resources while safeguarding its financial interests.It also provides a uniform mechanism for determining the rates of surplus raw water supplied to neighbouring states, government agencies and industries, wherever permissible, after meeting the present and future requirements for the state. However, this framework will not apply to water utilised for domestic purposes within the state.The matter assumes significance in the context of the Kishau Multipurpose Project, under which Himachal Pradesh has an allocated share equivalent to 3.154% of the live storage of the dam, amounting to approximately 42 million cubic metres. The state also has an allocated share of Yamuna waters under the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed among the upper Yamuna basin states. The MoU envisages the development of Lakhwar, Kishau and Renuka Ji Dam projects for optimum utilisation of the basin’s water resources.The policy also covers all existing and future projects of Himachal Pradesh from which surplus raw water is supplied to other states or eligible agencies.Chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said that the state government was committed to protecting Himachal Pradesh’s natural resources and ensuring that the state received appropriate economic returns from its valuable water resources.He said that water was one of the most important assets of the state and its economic value must be recognised while entering into any arrangement for supplying surplus water to other states or agencies. The policy would establish a transparent and uniform mechanism for determining water rates and their periodic revision, thereby protecting the long-term financial interests of the state.The CM said that the government would ensure that the interests and requirements of the state were fully safeguarded before making any surplus water available to other states. He said that the state’s drinking water, irrigation, agricultural, environmental and developmental needs would remain paramount.

headline: ‘Himachal Feels Like Home’: CJI Surya Kant Reconnects with State, Praises Clean Air at Dharamshala University Convocation
content: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Justice Surya Kant’s emotional association with Himachal Pradesh found a special expression during the 10th convocation of the Central University of Himachal Pradesh in Dharamshala on Sunday, as he described the hill state as his home and recalled his brief but memorable tenure as Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court. Speaking before students, faculty members and distinguished guests, Justice Surya Kant said that although he had spent only around seven months in Himachal Pradesh as Chief Justice of the state High Court, his emotional connection with the state had endured. “I have some emotional attachment with Himachal Pradesh. I feel that Himachal is my home,” he remarked, drawing thunderous applause from the gathering. Recalling his appointment in October 2018 as Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court, he said that despite having had limited time in the state, his association with Himachal had continued over the years. Expressing his pleasure at returning to Dharamshala, the CJI said the invitation from the state government and the Central University had provided him an opportunity to spend at least a day amidst the natural beauty of Himachal. In a particularly candid observation, apparently contrasting the experience with the deteriorating air quality in the national capital, Justice Surya Kant said he had the opportunity to breathe clean, crisp air and enjoy clean oxygen in Himachal Pradesh.

headline: Congress, BJP trade charges over Constitution in Himachal
content: Shimla: The Himachal Pradesh Congress and BJP traded charges over the Constitution and democratic institutions on Thursday, with the Congress holding a Constitution protection march in Shimla and leader of opposition Jai Ram Thakur accusing the party of undermining constitutional provisions.The Congress march began at Chaura Maidan, from the statue of Dr BR Ambedkar, and culminated at the Ridge, near Mahatma Gandhi’s statue. Party leaders and workers read the Preamble and pledged to protect the Constitution, alleging that democratic institutions and citizens’ rights were under threat.Deputy chief minister Mukesh Agnihotri, Congress state in-charge Rajani Patil, state party president Vinay Kumar and former state Congress president Pratibha Singh participated. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, who was expected to join, did not attend, while chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu skipped the programme due to health reasons.Addressing the gathering, Vinay Kumar said Rahul Gandhi had taken up the task of safeguarding the Constitution and urged party workers to pledge their support.In a statement, Thakur accused the Congress of misusing constitutional provisions to dismiss elected state govts and curtail fundamental rights. He alleged that the party had invoked Article 356 nearly 90 times to remove majority govts for political reasons.Citing Indira Gandhi’s tenure as Prime Minister, Thakur claimed President’s Rule was imposed 51 times during her nearly 16 years in office, accounting for 12,943 days across states. He also criticised the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, alleging that the Congress had made sweeping changes to the Constitution, including its Preamble.Thakur said the Constitution, adopted on Nov 26, 1949, was the foundation of India’s democracy and citizens’ rights. He credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi with initiating nationwide Constitution Day celebrations in 2015 to promote constitutional awareness.

headline: BJP releases list of 23 candidates for Chandigarh MC polls
content: Chandigarh, Nov 27 (PTI) The BJP on Friday released a list of 23 candidates for the December 23 general elections for the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation, including sitting Mayor Saurabh Joshi. Senior party leaders Devender Babla and Gurbax Rawat also figure in the list. Seven of the 23 candidates announced are women. The names of the candidates were finalised by the BJP’s Central Election Committee. The elections to elect councillors to the 35 wards of the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation will be held on December 23, while the counting of votes will take place on December 26. The filing of the nominations began on November 26, with December 3 being the last date for filing papers. The scrutiny of nominations will be held on December 4, while the last date for withdrawal of candidature is December 7. Following the announcement of the poll schedule on November 20, the model code of conduct came into immediate effect in all 35 wards, and will remain in force till the completion of the electoral process.

headline: Chandigarh: Auto-rickshaw driver gets five-year jail for 2023 crash | Hindustan Times
content: Nearly three years after a road accident at the Sector 16/17 light point claimed a cyclist’s life, a local court sentenced the auto-rickshaw driver to five years of imprisonment for culpable homicide, not amounting to murder. The court also convicted him for driving without a valid licence.The convict, Sonu, had rammed the auto-rickshaw into two cyclists, one of whom later succumbed to his injuries. Additional sessions judge Amit Kumar Grover held him guilty under Section 304 Part II (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Section 181 (driving a motor vehicle without a valid driving licence) of the Motor Vehicles Act, sentencing him to five-year imprisonment.The accident took place around 7.15 am on September 11, 2023, when Dr Lakhwinder Singh, 48, and his friend Satyajeet Kundra were returning from Sukhna Lake on their bicycles. An autorickshaw hit them near the Sector 16/17 light point, throwing both cyclists onto the road. The autorickshaw also overturned, injuring its passengers.Lakhwinder was initially taken to the government multi-specialty hospital in Sector 16, and subsequently shifted to Max Hospital in Mohali, where he died on September 28, 2023. Kundra had also sustained injuries in the mishap.The court placed considerable reliance on CCTV footage of the accident, which showed the autorickshaw hitting both cyclists from behind. One of them was dragged for around 30-40 metres before the vehicle skidded and overturned. The court observed that the vehicle was being driven at such a speed that the driver could not bring it under control.Rejecting the defence’s argument that the cyclists were responsible for the accident for using the main road instead of a cycle track, the court noted that the footage showed them riding on the extreme left side of the road.The court further observed that the accused was driving a commercial passenger vehicle without a valid licence and had overloaded it beyond its permissible seating capacity. It also took note of the testimony of an injured passenger, who stated that the driver had been cautioned to drive slowly but paid no heed to their advice.Holding that these circumstances established the driver’s knowledge that his actions were likely to cause death, the court ruled that the case went beyond mere rash and negligent driving and attracted Section 304 Part II of the IPC (punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder where the accused had knowledge that the act was likely to cause death, but no intention to cause death or such bodily injury).

headline: Chandigarh: PU to focus on filling vacancies, additional revenue, says new V-C | Hindustan Times
content: Filling vacant faculty and non-faculty posts, and finding alternate revenue sources will be his key priorities, said Tankeshwar Kumar on Thursday, a day after assuming charge as the vice-chancellor of Panjab University.Talking about financial distress that PU is facing, the vice-chancellor said that the university would explore alternative revenue sources without increasing the financial burden on students. He emphasised that he would prefer not to burden students through fee hikes.He further said that rather than asking for an increase in aid from the central government, the university would develop online courses and other alternative resources.“Asking for funds from the government is not the only option. We have to see how to earn money. We can start online courses. PU has made a name for itself. Given its A++ grade from National Assessment Accreditation Council (NAAC), many would be interested in studying online from PU,” he added.Kumar has assumed charge as the Panjab University V-C at a time when the university is grappling with faculty shortage, fall in global rankings, outdated infrastructure and safety concerns due to financial constraints.Around 50% of its 1,378 sanctioned faculty posts are lying vacant across its 74 departments. The V-C said advertisements had already been issued for 50 teaching posts, while 100 non-teaching positions would be advertised soon.Taking note of key administrative posts – including registrar, controller of examination, dean college development council – lying vacant, Kumar said these posts would be filled by regular recruitment. “Teachers shouldn’t be given charge of these administrative posts as it hinders their teaching. Teachers should give their quality time to students,” he stated.Besides, the university could not even make it to the top 1,000 universities in QS World University Rankings-2027. It slipped from the 901-950 band to 1001-1200.In Times Higher Education (THE) World University Ranking-2027, PU slipped from 601-800 band to 701-800 band. It had managed to be in the 226-250 band in THE rankings in 2013-14.Even in the National Institute Ranking Framework-2025 (NIRF), PU was ranked 57 in the overall category, against 33rd spot in 2018.Regional private universities – including Chandigarh University, Lovely Profession University, Shoolini University, Chitkara University, and Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology – are outshining PU in these rankings.Kumar did his postgraduate degree as well as doctorate in physics from PU. He has also taught in the university, and has been a member of senate and syndicate. He also has 11 years of experience as vice-chancellor in two universities.Kumar said the university would work towards improving its performance in the QS World University and Times Higher Education rankings. Kumar also emphasised on the need to improve gross enrolment ratio (GER).Highlighting the growing relevance of artificial intelligence (AI), the V-C said AI-enabled courses need to be integrated into the university curriculum to equip students with skills relevant to the changing job market. Referring to his experience at other universities, where he had introduced AI-based courses for all subjects, he stressed that AI skills were becoming essential across sectors.He also listed students’ well-being, particularly mental health and prevention of substance abuse, among his priorities. He urged teachers to maintain direct communication with students and identify early signs of depression or substance abuse.

headline: Chandigarh employees, teachers seeks health coverage, benefits as per central rules | Hindustan Times
content: Nearly four years after the central government service rules were implemented in Chandigarh in 2022, employees and teachers are still waiting for several corresponding benefits.Employee organisations have alleged selective implementation of the rules, claiming that while certain leave facilities were restricted, benefits such as healthcare coverage and financial upgradation remain pending.The issue has resurfaced after the Centre rejected the Chandigarh administration’s proposal to extend the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) to around 66,500 serving employees and their dependents. The proposal reportedly included issuing around 18,600 new CGHS cards. The rejection was cited on grounds of financial burden and limitations in existing infrastructure, said the joint action committee of teachers, UT Chandigarh.Employees and teachers are also demanding the implementation of the Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP) scheme. It provides financial upgradation to employees who do not receive regular promotions at specified stages of their service. The employee unions want Chandigarh employees to receive this benefit on the pattern of central government. Employees have also raised concerns over changes to casual leave, medical leave and other leave entitlements after the adoption of central government rules. They claim that half pay leave (HPL) accumulated up to 2022 has not been credited to their accounts.The unions have questioned why restrictions were implemented without extending the corresponding benefits. They are demanding CGHS coverage, MACP, settlement of pending HPL and protection of leave entitlements.The joint action committee, along with other employees’ and teachers’ unions, is preparing to hold a joint press conference to collectively raise this issue. It has also sought a clear, time-bound policy from the Chandigarh administration on the pending benefits.

headline: Rs 462cr station revamp set to miss yet another deadline
content: Chandigarh: Nearly three years after work began, the Rs 462 crore redevelopment of Chandigarh railway station is staring at yet another missed deadline, with key works on the Chandigarh side yet to take off.The project, which began in Jan 2023 with a 15-month completion target, has already slipped past several deadlines. While the Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA) is still aiming for completion by Dec-end, unfinished parking, entry and exit infrastructure on the Chandigarh side could push the finish to Jan 2027.The latest target is Dec 26, 2026. However, work on beautification and renovation of the Chandigarh-side parking area, entry and exit points and associated infrastructure has not begun, making completion of the entire project within the remaining month difficult.Saurabh Singh, joint general manager (projects), RLDA, Chandigarh, said major infrastructure works were nearing completion and efforts were on to meet the Dec deadline.Three of the four lifts planned for each of platforms 3, 4 and 5 have been installed and made operational, he said. The remaining lift is expected to become operational by Dec 10, while installation of escalators across the platforms is targeted for completion by the end of Dec.The Chandigarh-side works, however, remain the biggest hurdle. Besides parking and entry-exit infrastructure, internal roads, separate vehicle lanes and repairs to the existing station building are pending.The project was awarded to Ahluwalia Contracts (India) Ltd by RLDA in Dec 2022 under the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) model. Work began on Jan 11, 2023, with an original completion period of 15 months, putting the first deadline at April 10, 2024.Since then, the project has gone through a succession of revised targets, including Dec 2024, May and Oct 2025, and March and July 2026, before the latest Dec deadline.Once complete, the station is planned as a modern transport hub serving Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula. The redevelopment includes new G+3 station buildings on the Chandigarh and Panchkula sides, a 72-metre-wide covered air concourse, two 12-metre-wide foot overbridges, expanded parking, 30 lifts and 10 escalators.Upgraded waiting halls, food courts, retail outlets, paid lounges and retiring rooms are also part of the plan. The revamped station is designed to cater to a projected daily footfall of more than one lakh passengers by 2061.

headline: Delhi plans 180 new EV charging stations, 540 points
content: New Delhi: Delhi is set to expand its public electric vehicle charging network with 180 new charging stations and 540 charging points across the city, offering more options to owners of electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers and cars.Delhi Transco Limited (DTL) will engage private operators to develop and operate the facilities for 10 years and has designed the project to improve access to charging infrastructure and support the adoption of EVs.The project, estimated to cost Rs 125.7 crore, has been divided into two packages, each comprising 90 sites. The charging points will have a combined capacity of around 34.6 MW. Each station will be equipped with three chargers: a 12-kW unit for light EVs, including two- and three-wheelers, and 60-kW and 120-kW fast chargers for cars.CM Rekha Gupta said, ”Delhi is developing one of India’s largest EV charging networks, with a vision to expand the number of charging points to 32,000 through seamless coordination between Centre, Delhi Government, MCD and other agencies. With over 9,000 charging points already operational, we are steadily strengthening the infrastructure required to make the transition to electric mobility easier and more accessible. Our objective is to encourage more people to adopt EVs and contribute towards reducing vehicular pollution. Delhi is making the transition to clean mobility simpler, while strengthening our collective commitment to a cleaner and greener future.”Delhi already has over 9,000 operational charging points.DTL has invited bids for the rollout of the project, which will not be like a conventional procurement exercise under which govt purchases and installs equipment. It will be based on a design, build, finance, operate, maintain and transfer model. Private charging point operators will be responsible for everything — from site surveys, securing electricity connections and civil works to installation, maintenance and customer support.“DTL will act as the nodal agency and facilitate the availability of identified sites in coordination with respective site-owning agencies. The operators will have to make each station commercially operational within 150 days of the site being handed over. They will recover their investments through charging fees collected from users and financial support available under Centre’s PM e-DRIVE scheme,” said an official.According to plans, the operators of the charging points must provide mobile apps and web interfaces showing the location of stations, charger availability and applicable tariffs. The users will be able to make payments through UPI, debit and credit cards, RFID cards and mobile wallets. “Owning a particular vehicle brand or subscribing to an operator’s network cannot be made a condition for using a station,” said an official.The facilities will have to remain operational between 6 am and 10 pm every day, including public holidays. Operators will also be required to provide CCTV surveillance, adequate lighting, fire safety arrangements, emergency contact details and a 24-hour toll-free customer helpline. Special attention has been prescribed for the safety of women users, particularly at night.To ensure that chargers do not remain dysfunctional for extended periods, DTL has proposed performance-linked service standards. Operators will have to progressively increase system availability from 90% in the first year to 95% from the third year onwards. Accordingly, faults will have to be rectified within 24 operating hours, failing which financial penalties will be charged.The official said the operators will be responsible for protecting equipment against theft and vandalism, maintaining spare parts in Delhi and undertaking preventive maintenance at least once every six months.“At the end of the 10-year contract, the charging stations, electrical infrastructure and associated assets, including the charger management system, will be transferred to DTL at zero cost. The arrangement is intended to ensure that the public charging network remains available beyond the initial operating period,” said the official.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. headline: Keeping eye on Delhi developments: Jharkhand CM on special sitting of Parliament
content: Ramgarh (Jharkhand), Nov 27 (PTI) Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren on Friday said the JMM was keeping an eye on developments in Delhi, amid a buzz that the Centre may reintroduce a constitutional amendment linking women’s reservation rollout to delimitation in the upcoming special sitting of Parliament. The Union Cabinet met on Friday and was learnt to have cleared a fresh delimitation-linked women’s reservation bill ahead of the special sitting of Parliament, beginning next week. Sources said the bill was brought before the special meeting of the Union Cabinet, which is learnt to have accorded its nod to the fresh bill with some amendments to ensure that no state loses its representation in the Lok Sabha in proportion to other states after delimitation. “We are keeping an eye on the developments in Delhi. This is not the only special session; other sessions have come and gone too. The way laws are being passed and the poor state they end up in are right in front of everyone,” Soren told reporters in Ramgarh. He, however, did not comment on the JMM’s stand on the proposed delimitation bill. The delimitation-linked women’s reservation bill was brought in Parliament by the government during a special sitting in April, but it could not pass muster in the Lok Sabha. The government has now claimed that it has the numbers to get the legislation through.

headline: World-class travel? Pull that chain of thought
content: The ordeal of a train journey often begins much before you board a train. In the first part of this new series, we look at how Delhi Cantt station’s revamp has left behind a trail of rubbleNEW DELHI: Heaps of construction debris, piles of garbage and iron pieces strewn around have become part of the landscape at Delhi Cantonment railway station, where ongoing infrastructure work and poor upkeep have left large stretches of the premises looking neglected.During a spot visit, several stretches along the tracks could be seen littered with broken construction material, discarded objects, plastic and iron waste, and heaps of earth.In some places, large mounds of debris were covered with green tarpaulin, while construction material and dismantled scaffolding lay scattered.A guard at the station said, “A foot overbridge is being constructed here, which is why all these things have piled up.”Adding to the grim picture are jhuggi clusters abutting the railway tracks, with most locals using the area as an extension of their living space and going about their routine amid the clutter and debris.Clothes are hung out to dry, household belongings are stacked along the boundary, and residents, including children, can be seen sitting on the tracks or moving around dangerously close to the railway lines.The proximity of these settlements to an active railway line raises serious questions about safety. “These tracks are mostly used for goods wagons, not for regular trains,” said Bablu, a resident of Khajan Basti, adding simply: “We move when we hear the horn.”Under the Amrit Bharat Station scheme, the Delhi Cantt railway station is undergoing major redevelopment, estimated at about Rs 335 crore.The upgrades include new station buildings with dedicated arrival and departure zones, a spacious concourse, and an elevated road to ease traffic flow.Outside the terminal, circulating areas and parking facilities are being expanded for smoother multimodal connectivity.Inside, platforms will get fresh resurfacing, upgraded shelters, new lifts, escalators, modern waiting lounges, accessible toilets, and digital passenger information systems. However, infrastructure work at the station is far from complete.Concrete pillars with exposed steel reinforcement bars jut out at the platform, surrounded by scaffolding. At other locations, construction material, metal rods and discarded equipment lie scattered around unfinished structures.Anita Jaiswal, who had come to drop off her relative, said, “Look at the iron rods. What if someone falls on these after getting off the train?Right now, the station is not crowded, but when the train comes, many people come in at the same time.”A senior Northern Railway official said, “Major renovation work is under way at the station, but we had asked the station authorities to ensure all construction material is covered.The mounds of construction material and iron bars are in the non-passenger areas. Due to the festive season, many workers had gone home, resulting in a temporary halt in the work. However, contractors have been instructed to see that all material in passenger areas is properly covered.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. headline: IIT Delhi admissions open for AI and entrepreneurship programme: Check eligibility, fees and course detai
content: IIT Delhi AI Programme 2027: The Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi) has opened admissions for the first batch of its five-month online programme, Design Thinking with AI for Innovation-Based Entrepreneurship. Offered through the institute's Continuing Education Programme (CEP) in association with TimesPro, the course will begin on March 20, 2027, and conclude on July 24, 2027.The programme is designed for graduates interested in combining artificial intelligence, design thinking and entrepreneurship to develop business ideas and solutions to real-world problems. Candidates from any academic discipline can apply. The programme fee is Rs 1,59,000, excluding 18% GST.IIT Delhi AI programme 2027: Key detailsParticularsDetailsInstituteIIT DelhiProgrammeDesign Thinking with AI for Innovation-Based EntrepreneurshipBatch1DurationFive monthsModeOnlineService providerTimesProStart dateMarch 20, 2027End dateJuly 24, 2027EligibilityGraduates from any disciplineProgramme feeRs 1,59,000 + 18% GSTApplication statusAdmissions openWhat will the programme cover?The curriculum combines design thinking principles with practical applications of AI and business development. Participants will learn how to identify user requirements, define problems, conduct AI-assisted research, generate ideas and develop prototypes.The programme also covers Generative AI, machine learning, prompt engineering, no-code AI tools, agentic technologies and user validation. Further modules focus on business model innovation, financial planning, revenue strategies and go-to-market approaches.A dedicated capstone project will allow participants to develop and validate an AI-enabled business venture. The programme follows a learning structure comprising 60% practical work and 40% theoretical instruction.Eligibility and class scheduleGraduates from any discipline are eligible to apply, with selection based on application review. headline: Delhi Court Bars Rohini Satsang House From Using "Guruji Ka Ashram" Name And Guruji's Photographs
content: The District Judge (Commercial Court)-03 at Saket Courts, New Delhi, has restrained a Rohini-based satsang house from using the name "Guruji Ka Ashram", displaying photographs of the late spiritual leader Shri Nirmal Singh Maharaj, known to devotees as "Guruji", and collecting donations in his name. The court found that a prima facie case of trade mark infringement, copyright infringement and passing off was made out.Passing the ex parte ad interim order on 26 November 2026, Judge Balwant Rai Bansal was dealing with an application under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 CPC, filed by Guruji Ka Ashram Trust against Sarva Samarpit Awam Samarpan Trust and a "John Doe/Ashok Kumar", who represents the unknown persons managing it. The suit seeks permanent and mandatory injunction, delivery up, rendition of accounts and damages.Appearing for the plaintiff trust were Advocates Sandeep Kapur, Senior Partner, Manmeet Kaur, Partner, Gurtejpal Singh and Parth Gupta, Advocates, Karanjawala & Co.Name, photographs and donation boxesThe plaintiff is a public charitable trust formed on 14 May 1999 by Guruji and his mother, and manages the "Bade Mandir" at Bhatti Mines, Mehrauli. It told the court that the name "Guruji Ka Ashram" has been in use since 1 January 1999 and that it is the registered proprietor of the word mark in Classes 45, 41 and 16 (Registration Nos. 3821140, 3821141 and 3821142), along with a device mark in Class 45 (Registration No. 6120985).It also claimed copyright in 120 photographs of Guruji, taken by photojournalist Raghu Rai between 1997 and 2007 and assigned to the trust through a registered agreement dated 13 February 2024. Devotees revere these images as "Swaroops" of Guruji.According to the trust, the defendants run a "Satsang House" that presents itself as linked to Guruji and the trust, though no such connection exists. It alleged that photographs identical or similar to the assigned works are prominently displayed at the premises and on an Instagram account, "guruji_satsang_house". It further claimed that donations are collected through QR codes placed on donation boxes in front of Guruji's photographs, and that members are enrolled in a monthly "investment committee" scheme requiring instalments of Rs 1,00,000 for 20 months. The trust said it learnt of this on 29 October 2026 and relied on an affidavit from a devotee, Ankit Mendiratta, who visited the premises.Comparing the photographs side by side, the court found that "the defendants have reproduced the photographs of Guruji" and displayed them prominently at the premises and on social media. These images, it added, were also "identical with or deceptively similar to the registered device mark of the plaintiff."On donations, the court said the screenshots of QR codes and linked UPI IDs, placed on record, showed "prima facie" that the defendants were soliciting donations in Guruji's name "for commercial gain."Since both sides were rendering identical services, the court saw "every likelihood of confusion and deception" among the public and devotees about who runs the services. It held that the balance of convenience lay with the plaintiff and that refusal of an injunction would cause it "irreparable loss and injury in terms of goodwill and reputation."The defendants and all persons acting on their behalf are restrained, till further orders, from:1. using "GURUJI KA ASHRAM" or any identical or deceptively similar mark for any goods or services, including at the Rohini premises and on the Instagram page;2. reproducing, displaying or communicating to the public any of the assigned photographs, or a substantial part of them, in any form; and3. soliciting or collecting donations, subscriptions or instalments, including under the investment committee scheme, on the representation that these are for or associated with the plaintiff trust or Bade Mandir, and passing off their services as the plaintiff's.The plaintiff has also been directed to comply with Order 39 Rule 3 CPC. The court clarified that nothing in the order amounts to an expression on the merits of the case at this stage.Case Title: Guruji Ka Ashram Trust vs. Sarva Samarpit Awam Samarpan Trust & Anr. Order Date: November 26, 2026Bench: District Judge (Commercial Court)-03 Balwant Rai Bansal

headline: Kejriwal’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’ opens to scrutiny: A look inside the controversial bungalow
content: The controversy over the renovation of former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal’s official residence has now acquired a public viewing dimension, with the Delhi Government opening the bungalow at 6, Flagstaff Road, to the media on Friday and preparing to charge visitors around Rs 20 to see its interiors.The government’s move is aimed at putting the property, dubbed ‘Sheesh Mahal’ by the BJP, on public display before deciding its longer-term use. An online booking facility is expected to be introduced this week, with the public likely to get access in the coming days. Senior citizens and college students may be allowed free entry.Delhi Government's PWD minister Parvesh Verma, while speaking to The Tribune, said, "This is what happens when public is bluffed by an imposter. This is a live example of how corrupted Arvind Kejriwal has spent taxpayers' valuable money for his own comforts." He added, "It is not just the high expenditure at such ultra luxurious residence but the way its construction went on without NOC."Along with Verma, minister Kapil Mishra was also leading the tour to Sheesh Mahal.Mishra said, "They (AAP) have done similar corruption in Punjab too, they have destroyed the state completely." During the media tour, he showcased furnishings whose individual prices have become central to the political controversy. These included a chandelier costing Rs 11.56 lakh, a sofa worth Rs 5.47 lakh, chairs priced at Rs 5.58 lakh, a centre table costing Rs 6.79 lakh and curtains valued at Rs 5.69 lakh. The overall renovation and furnishing expenditure has been pegged at Rs 58.83 crore.Visuals from AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal's former residence as the CM of Delhi. Tribune photos: Mukesh AggarwalThe bungalow, which served as Kejriwal’s official residence from 2015 to 2024, has eight bedrooms, 12 toilets, a jacuzzi bath, a spa, expensive carpets and five OLED televisions. Its upkeep now falls under the Public Works Department (PWD), which has deployed around 10 staff members for cleaning and maintenance.Verma had announced the media visit on Thursday, while Minister Kapil Mishra said the opening would allow people across the country to see the property and judge the alleged misuse of public funds. BJP has repeatedly accused the former Chief Minister of excessive spending on the renovation.However, the proposed public exhibition may be only a temporary arrangement. The government is considering handing over the property to a private hospitality company after a limited viewing period. The bungalow could subsequently be used for official conferences, meetings and lunches.Government sources informed The Tribune that it will become ultimately a hospitality venue as a state guest house.The PWD had conducted a thorough audit of the interiors after Kejriwal and his family vacated the premises. The proposed ticketing system could offer visitors access to the property, but the government is yet to announce the final booking arrangements, viewing duration or management model.For now, the ‘Sheesh Mahal’ controversy is moving from political speeches to a physical space that visitors will soon be able to inspect themselves.

headline: 87.5% girls, women, LGBTQ+ people feel unsafe in Delhi local parks, says new report
content: New Delhi: More than 87 per cent of women, girls, and LGBTQ+ persons in Delhi feel unsafe in their neighbourhood parks after dark, while more than 14 per cent do not visit these parks at all, a new report has found. Titled ‘Everyday Journeys: Women’s and Girls’ Access to Footpaths and Public Parks in Delhi’, the study was launched on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women and Girls. The Centre for Equity and Inclusion (CEQUIN), which published the report, works to prevent gender-based violence across Delhi-NCR, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Bihar. According to the report, 87.5 per cent of women, girls, and queer persons feel unsafe while walking to the nearest bus stop or metro station after dark. “A woman should not have to explain why she is outside, whether she is there for work, leisure, pleasure or nothing at all. She has a right to be there. The more women occupy these spaces, the safer and more accessible they become,” said Laura Prabhu, co-founder of CEQUIN. “By keeping women away, we are not solving the problem. We are curtailing their rights, limiting their participation in public life and, ultimately, holding back half the population that contributes to the economy.” On Wednesday evening, the annual gathering, Hain Haq Hamara Hissedari, was attended by hundreds at Vasant Udyan in Delhi’s Vasant Vihar, refusing to let darkness drive them out of a neighbourhood park. The gathering came in the wake of the alleged rape of a 17-year-old girl at Ashta Kunj Park in September. The incident brought the safety of women in Delhi’s public parks under scrutiny. These green spaces, often the only breathing room in the choking capital, have since seen access restrictions, with several parks that have multiple gates shutting some of their entrances in the evening.

headline: Elderly prisoners’ inclusion to fixed review window, new Delhi jail rules modify emergency parole system
content: New Delhi: Prisoners over 70, as well as those who are infirm or terminally ill, have been brought within the ambit of Delhi’s emergency parole regime as the government moves to widen the circumstances in which temporary release from prison can be considered.The change is part of the Delhi Prisons (Amendment) Rules 2026, notified on 25 November. The amendments make three principal interventions in the existing parole framework: they widen the scope of emergency parole under Rule 1212A, recast the process for obtaining police and probation reports under Rule 1213, and substitute Rule 1219 governing cases where a convict is unable to furnish surety (a financial guarantee furnished to secure compliance with the conditions of release). The most substantive change is to Rule 1212A. The provision now expressly permits emergency parole to be considered in situations involving an epidemic or natural disaster, or old age (only for prisoners above 70), infirmity or terminal illness, as well as other circumstances warranting an immediate easing of the prison population. This does not mean that emergency parole, or even the eight-week period contemplated by the rule, has been introduced for the first time. Rule 1212A already allows the government to grant up to eight weeks of emergency parole in one spell, in addition to regular parole, in the event of an epidemic, natural disaster or other circumstances requiring an immediate easing of the prison population. The rule also left it to the government to decide whether the period spent outside prison would count towards the prisoner’s sentence. Those features have been retained. The amended rule also states that the number of emergency-parole spells may be increased where the situation warrants. The release, however, is not automatic. Rule 1212A uses discretionary language, providing that the government “may” grant parole, subject to prescribed conditions.

headline: US tariffs: India gets an edge over China, Vietnam, Bangladesh—but what must New Delhi do to secure it?
content: The Trump administration on Wednesday announced plans to increase tariffs on more than a dozen countries, including India, China and Vietnam. The proposed change comes as Washington and New Delhi continue negotiations on a long-pending trade deal.USTR proposes new tariff rates on India, Asian peers: What we knowAccording to reports, the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed a 17% tariff on Indian exports under a reciprocal trade agreement . In the absence of a deal, Indian exports could face tariffs of up to 25% under Section 301 investigations into excess production capacity that allegedly harms US interests.In comparison, the USTR has proposed a tariff rate of 18% on Bangladesh, Cambodia and Thailand, and a 20% duty on China and Vietnam, subject to their respective trade deals.Citing an expert, CNBC reported that Washington expects the announcement of a lower tariff rate to prompt New Delhi to sign the trade deal before the G20 Summit, scheduled for next month in Florida. The expert added that India has got a "better bargain with Washington than its main competitors", and that it may be enough for the Indian government to declare victory and secure domestic backing for the deal.The lower tariff rate will come into effect if India accepts a trade deal, which has been on hold since both sides have indicated that there was little to no room to grant concessions.The US has cited several concerns behind its investigation into India's trade and industrial policies. These include government plans to expand manufacturing, inadequate labour protections, financial repression policies, continued barriers to market access, and India's failure to address global excess production capacity. Washington has also raised concerns about imports and foreign direct investment from non-market economies.According to the USTR, these policies and practices restrict US commercial interests by limiting opportunities for American producers and exporters in India and other markets. The office also claims that they contribute to losses in US manufacturing production, exports, jobs and investment, while increasing economic security risks through dependence on inputs from non-market economies. The concerns are particularly significant in sectors such as pharmaceuticals and medical devices, steel, solar energy, and information and communications technology (ICT).India's response to US allegationsIn response to the USTR's findings, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry said the Indian government had taken note of the notice of determination and the request for comments and was currently examining them. India said it had engaged constructively throughout the investigation and that the Department of Commerce maintained during the proceedings that the country did not have structural excess capacity in any sector.The government also said that India and the US were engaged in negotiations for a Bilateral Trade Agreement, and maintained that trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations. It reiterated its commitment to working closely with Washington towards the early conclusion of the agreement.What will India have to do to secure a lower tariff rate?According to an Indian Express report, while New Delhi has a chance to gain a tariff advantage over its ASEAN peers, it will have to accept steep demands made by the US under the trade deal.According to a joint statement released by the two sides, India agreed to "eliminate or reduce" tariffs on a wide variety of goods from the US, including all industrial goods and US food and agricultural products such as dried distillers’ grains (DDGs), red sorghum for animal feed, tree nuts, fresh and processed fruit, soybean oil, wine and spirits, among other products.The statement read, "India agrees to address long-standing barriers to the trade in US medical devices; eliminate restrictive import licensing procedures that delay market access for, or impose quantitative restrictions on, U.S. Information and Communication Technology (ICT) goods; and determine, with a view towards a positive outcome, within six months of entry into force of the Agreement whether US-developed or international standards, including testing requirements, are acceptable for US exports entering the Indian market in identified sectors."(With agency inputs)

headline: Gwalior man undergoes prostate cancer treatment in Delhi, Star Health rejects Rs 26,803 claim over OPD ca
content: BHOPAL: A 68-year-old Gwalior man’s Rs 26,803 health insurance claim for prostate cancer treatment has been allowed by the district consumer commission, which held Star Health and Allied Insurance Company guilty of deficiency in service for rejecting it on the ground that the treatment was taken on an outpatient basis.In an order dated November 5, the Gwalior District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission directed the insurer to pay Brijmohan Shrivastav Rs 26,803 within 45 days. It also ordered the company to pay Rs 2,000 as compensation for mental agony and Rs 1,500 towards litigation expenses.Shrivastav had approached the commission after the insurer rejected his claim for expenses incurred during treatment at Rajiv Gandhi Cancer Institute in Delhi. He said he was undergoing treatment for prostate cancer and submitted a claim of Rs 26,803 after medical examinations and treatment.The insurer rejected the claim, saying Shrivastav had not been admitted to hospital and had received outpatient treatment. It argued that the policy covered only eligible inpatient treatment expenses and that outpatient treatment was not payable.The company also contended that each claim had to be assessed on its own merits and that settlement of earlier claims did not automatically entitle the policyholder to reimbursement.However, the commission noted that the insurer had not specifically disputed Shrivastav’s claim that it had earlier paid claims relating to day-care treatment under the same policy. It also failed to draw the commission’s attention to any specific policy condition that justified rejecting the present claim.Holding that the insurer had failed to establish a valid basis for repudiation, the commission set aside the rejection and directed payment of the claimed amount.The order said that if the insurer failed to pay within 45 days, it would have to pay 6% annual interest on the amount from the expiry of the stipulated period until actual payment.The order was passed by commission president Rajendra Prasad Sharma and member Revati Raman Mishra.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhopal | Silver Rate in Bhopal | Bank Holidays in Bhopal | Public Holidays in Bhopal | Petrol Price in Bhopal | Diesel Price in Bhopal | CNG Price in Bhopal | LPG Price in BhopalStay updated with the latest Bhopal news. headline: Delhi plans 540 new EV charging points at a cost of Rs 125.7 crore
content: Delhi’s public electric vehicle (EV) charging network is set for a major expansion, with 180 new stations comprising 540 charging points to be developed across the city at an estimated investment of Rs 125.7 crore. The move comes amid the government’s push to accelerate the shift towards electric mobility, including a phased transition of school bus fleets to electric vehicles.Delhi Transco Limited (DTL) has invited bids for the project, which will be implemented in two packages covering 90 sites each. Private agencies will be responsible for setting up and operating the facilities for 10 years under a Design, Build, Finance, Operate, Maintain and Transfer (DBFOMT) arrangement. The proposed network will have a combined capacity of around 34.6 MW.Each station will have three charging units, a 12 kW charger for light electric vehicles, including two-wheelers and three-wheelers, and two fast-charging units with capacities of 60 kW and 120 kW for cars. The selected operators will have to make the stations commercially operational within 150 days of receiving the sites.Delhi currently has more than 9,000 operational charging points, while the government aims to increase the number to 32,000.Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has said the expansion is intended to make EV adoption easier and reduce vehicular pollution through coordinated efforts involving the Centre, Delhi Government, Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) and other agencies.To ensure easy access, operators will have to develop mobile applications and web platforms providing information on charging station locations, charger availability and tariffs. Payments will be accepted through UPI, debit and credit cards, RFID cards and mobile wallets.Charging facilities cannot be restricted to customers of a particular vehicle manufacturer or subscribers of a specific operator, an official said.The project also lays down safety and maintenance requirements, including CCTV cameras, adequate lighting, fire safety measures, emergency contact details and a 24-hour-toll-free helpline. Operators will have to resolve technical faults within 24 operating hours or face financial penalties.School bus fleets to adopt EVs in phasesSeparately, Delhi’s 2026 EV policy for school bus fleets, effective from July 1 and applicable until March 31, 2030, requires schools to convert at least 30 per cent of their total bus fleets to electric vehicles.The policy provides for a phased transition, with schools required to achieve 10 per cent EV adoption within two years of the notification, increase it to 20 per cent by the third year and reach the 30 per cent target by March 31, 2030.The mandate covers school buses operating under all arrangements, including those owned, leased or hired by schools. The Education Department has been designated as the nodal authority responsible for overseeing the implementation of the transition.

headline: 'Rs 5.47 lakh sofa, Rs 11 lakh chandelier': Delhi govt opens doors of Arvind Kejriwal's 'Sheesh Mahal'; h
content: NEW DELHI: The Delhi government on Friday opened former chief minister Arvind Kejriwal's controversial 'Sheesh Mahal' residence on Flagstaff Road to the media, showcasing its interiors and furnishings, which the BJP has alleged were purchased using public money at exorbitant prices.The government plans to open the bungalow to the public through a ticketing system in the coming days.During the media tour, officials displayed expensive furnishings, including a chandelier worth Rs 11.56 lakh, a sofa priced at Rs 5.47 lakh, chairs costing Rs 5.58 lakh, a central table worth Rs 6.79 lakh and curtains valued at Rs 5.69 lakh. The total cost of the renovation and furnishings has been pegged at Rs 58.83 crore.Public Works Department (PWD) minister Parvesh Verma had announced on Thursday that the media would be given access to the bungalow first, followed by public visits. The government is expected to introduce an online booking system this week.The bungalow, under the PWD's maintenance, has eight bedrooms, 12 toilets, a jacuzzi bath, spa, expensive carpets, five OLED TVs, and other amenities.Delhi minister Kapil Mishra said the opening would allow people across the country to see the property and alleged that public funds had been misused during Kejriwal's tenure."Starting today, the public in Delhi and across the country will be able to see this 'Sheesh Mahal'. It has been opened to the media today, and through your cameras, the entire nation will witness the sordid game of corruption and plunder that Kejriwal played," Mishra said.He alleged that the furnishings and materials had been sourced from different countries, citing marble imported from Vietnam and crockery and tables procured from abroad. Mishra also accused the former chief minister of spending lavishly on the residence while Delhi was struggling during the Covid-19 pandemic.Officials said the entry ticket is likely to cost around Rs 20, while senior citizens and college students may be allowed free entry.The government is also considering hiring a private hospitality company to manage the property, which is proposed to host official conferences, lunches and meetings."The public viewing will be for a limited period of time. After that, the plan to hand it over to a private hospitality company is in the works. It will be finalised soon," a senior government official said.Located at 6, Flagstaff Road, the bungalow served as Kejriwal's official residence during his tenure as Delhi chief minister from 2015 to 2024. The BJP coined the term 'Sheesh Mahal' during its campaign for the February 2025 Assembly elections, alleging that public money had been spent excessively on its renovation.After Kejriwal and his family vacated the bungalow, the PWD conducted an extensive audit of its interiors. headline: Gold, silver prices today, 27 November: Check retail rates of 24K, 22K gold, 999 silver in Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata
content: Gold and silver prices, 27 November: Gold and silver prices rose in early domestic trading on Friday amid a strong dollar and bets on tighter Fed policy. In the international market, gold prices drifted lower on Thursday, as lingering inflation concerns and the market's growing expectations that the US Federal Reserve will hike interest rates again pressured the precious metal. Spot gold was down 0.4% at $3,566.99 per ounce by 1901 GMT. Prices briefly fell below the psychologically important $3,500 level on Wednesday for the first time since September 2025. US gold futures for December delivery rose 0.9% to $3,565.90, as per a report by Reuters. In the domestic futures market, MCX gold futures rose 1.63% to ₹1,24,790 per 10 grams, while MCX silver futures rallied by around 4.06% to ₹1,52,530 per kg at around 9:13 am. Gold is available in different purities in the retail market, with 24-karat gold being the purest form and 22-karat gold commonly used to make jewellery due to its greater durability. Silver 999, also known as 99.9% pure silver, is a high-purity form of silver commonly used for investment purposes, including silver bars and coins.
