headline: Delhi court frames charges against 4 teens for gangraping, killing 16-year-old
content: A Delhi court on Wednesday filed charges against four teenagers, including three minors, in connection with the gang rape and murder of a 16-year-old girl whose partially decomposed body was found nearly two months ago in Swaroop Nagar, police said.Senior police officers said the involvement of the four teenagers in the cases was established using DNA profiling coupled with a watertight investigation. Police are also trying to appeal to the court to try the three juveniles as adults due to the heinous crime.Raped, stabbed over six timesThe incident took place on September 11 when the minor had left home to meet a friend. Police said the accused took her to a field where they took turns to rape her. When she threatened to report them, they stabbed her more than six times and left her body in the field. Her body was found two days later, decomposing and partially eaten by dogs.On Friday, DCP (Outer North) Shobhit D Saksena confirmed a Delhi court had framed charges in the case and the case will now be in the prosecution evidence stage.During prosecution evidence, police said the court will summon doctors, complainant, witnesses and police. Cross examination of all the witnesses will be done.Senior officers said a “major” piece of conclusive evidence in the case is the Central Forensic Science Laboratory (CFSL) report confirming the presence of “human semen” and “a mixed male DNA profile corresponding to four males on swabs collected from the victim”.How the investigators cracked the caseInvestigators said these scientific tests were essential to link the victim to the accused as when DNA is “possibly contaminated” and there’s multiple DNAs, the tests help.A police officer aware of the matter said that the report found that the Y-chromosome short tandem repeat (Y-STR) profiles of all the four accused strongly matched the mixed male DNA profile recovered from the victim’s swabs, corroborating the allegations of sexual assault. The CFSL report confirmed the presence of human semen on the victim’s swabs and a mixed DNA profile corresponding to four different males, said police.The Delhi Police on October 12 had submitted a 365-page chargesheet in the case with statements from 54 witnesses and mentions a gait analysis conducted on the accused.Gait analysis involves studying a person’s walking or running pattern, usually through video recordings, to assess whether their movements correspond with those captured in surveillance footage. The technique can help investigators examine whether a suspect’s physical movements are consistent with those of a person seen at a crime scene.The investigation initially hit hurdles because the body was severely mutilated, with the skull and rib cage exposed and the right arm severed. Investigators were initially unable to establish the deceased’s gender. A breakthrough came when an assistant sub-inspector noticed a tattoo of three stars in a row on the victim’s left arm. Missing-person records and CCTV footage from the surrounding area was analysed to crack the case.

headline: 22,000 stray dogs microchipped under the pilot project to track status:MCD
content: New Delhi: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), in partnership with NGO Friendicoes-SESCA, has microchipped around 22,000 stray dogs in a pilot project at two Animal Birth Control (ABC) centres, said senior municipal officials said on Thursday. The centres are located in Bijwasan and Ghazipur.“The rice-grain sized chips are injected under the skin. They store information on sterilisation, anti-rabies vaccination, the NGO responsible for the dog and their characteristics, colour and location. The data can be accessed using a handheld scanner and may also help the corporation conduct a dog census,” an official said.The MCD has set a target of sterilising 80% of the dog population in each ward to stabilise numbers and prevent births.Officials said the MCD has sought a report from the NGO on the project’s operation and effectiveness. The report will help determine whether microchipping should be expanded to other areas.MCD has faced allegations of poor sterilisation drives and inflated figures. A civic official said the chips can also help audit the sterilisation as penalties can be imposed on the NGO concerned if fresh breeding in such a case is reported.The project is part of a series of measures the corporation has promised to take following the Supreme Court orders on stray dogs and dog-bite prevention.MCD officials said the microchips are procured from agencies listed on Bharat Pashudhan portal of National Digital Livestock Mission.“We are also exploring the possibility of funding the expanded microchipping project through a CSR model. We are in advanced discussions with an NGO to carry out ward-wise microchipping using the CSR funds. Estimates of the expenditure and the methodology for the survey have also been sought,” officials said.The last dog census conducted by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) was in 2009, when the population of community dogs was estimated to be 560,000.

headline: Safdarjung Hospital under scrutiny over fake doctor’s recruitment
content: Safdarjung Hospital has not explained how a man who police say had not passed Class 12 got through its checks to work there as a junior resident on forged papers, including a fake Delhi Medical Council (DMC) registration certificate.The Rajasthan Police’s special operations group arrested Ramkishor Mahawar and three others in an interstate racket that sold forged medical degrees. Police said Mahawar registered with DMC using forged MBBS and MD degrees and joined Safdarjung as a contractual junior resident in June 2025.A Rajasthan police official said Mahawar was arrested from Delhi on November 8, following which the agency traced the others to Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. The chain of events that led to their covers being blown began in Jaipur after Rajasthan Medical Council’s registrar filed a police complaint in October, 2024 reporting “individuals had secured registration as medical practitioners with the Rajasthan Medical Council by submitting false and forged documents”.Safdarjung has 397 sanctioned junior resident posts, each with a one-year tenure, according to recruitment guidelines on its website. Candidates need an MBBS degree from a recognised university, registration with the DMC, and an internship completed within two years of applying. The hospital selects them through a written examination and then allots seats in departments by counselling based on their exam scores. “The selection of junior resident is through written exam followed by counselling on the basis of merit score in written exam for allotment of seats in various departments and no interview shall be conducted,” the guidelines state.HT asked Safdarjung how it verifies documents, how Mahawar was selected without the required qualifications, which department he worked in, and whether it had acted against the officials responsible for recruitment or verification. The hospital declined to respond.DMC never registered Ramkishor Mahawar, the council told the Rajasthan Police. HT has seen DMC’s letter to the police. In it, the council said its records show no registration in Mahawar’s name under certificate No. 33624, dated July 10, 2025, and that it did not issue that certificate. DMC was replying to an SOG letter dated November 25, 2026, which asked for details of the registration.To be sure, HT could not verify whether Mahawar produced multiple DMC registrations, since he appeared to have joined Safdarjung prior to the registration date (July 10, 2025) in the certificate referenced in the DMC and Rajasthan Police communication.To register with the DMC, applicants upload their educational qualifications and other certificates on the council’s portal and then bring the originals to its office for physical verification on an assigned date. A DMC official, who asked not to be named, said the council then writes to the university named by the applicant. “Registration is granted only after the university’s acknowledgement is received,” this person said.HT asked DMC acting registrar Dr Atul Kochar how Mahawar obtained registration and whether the council had confirmed his degrees with the universities that supposedly issued them. Kochar had not responded by the time of publication.“This is extremely worrisome, that a fake doctor was working at a prestigious hospital in the national capital. Imagine what must be happening in smaller towns. This is a grave error on the part of the hospital. Hospitals can easily verify a candidate’s DMC certification by rechecking the candidate’s DMC registration number on the DMC portal or by directly reaching out to DMC. This will avoid any major medical negligence,” Dr Arun Gupta, senior paediatrician, who was the DMC’s president from 2015 to 25.

headline: Sarai Kale Khan road rage: Accused held after 160-km chase
content: New Delhi: Even swapping their car’s number plate for a fake one and sticking a bogus MLA sticker could not save a 23-year-old law student and his 25-year-old accomplice. The two accused of attacking two bikers with a hammer and baseball bat in a fit of road rage were nabbed on Wednesday night in northeast Delhi’s Khajuri Khas after a 160-kilometre chase, police said on Thursday.Police identified the accused as Armaan, a law student, and his friend Abhishek, a construction worker.On Wednesday, they allegedly assaulted Vikram, 39, and Arun, 22, after the victims’ motorcycle brushed against the accused SUV near the Sarai Kale Khan flyover in south Delhi. The accused also snatched Vikram’s phone and, when Arun called, threatened them with dire consequences if he filed a police complaint, said additional deputy commissioner of police (southeast) Utkarsha. “To evade detection, the accused replaced the SUV’s number plate with a fake. They also affixed a fake Member of Legislative Assembly (MLA) sticker to the vehicle’s front windscreen to mislead the police. We recovered the hammer, the wooden stick and the car used in the crime. The phone has also been recovered,” said Utkarsha.Police said the two were booked under sections 109 (attempt to murder), 309 (robbery) and 3 (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).During the investigation, police traced the SUV’s owner, who told them that Abhishek, one of the accused, rented the vehicle from him a few days ago. “The accused kept their locations across Haryana and Delhi. After tracking them for nearly 160 kilometres, we nabbed the duo from Khajuri Khas,” the officer saidPolice said the accused are contractual employees at Safdarjung Hospital. Both were admitted to AIIMS Trauma Centre. While Arun was discharged on Thursday, Vikram was undergoing treatment.

headline: Delhi, Bihar to ink pact for year-round bus services
content: New Delhi: The Delhi and Bihar governments are set to sign a reciprocal transport agreement for year-round bus services between the two states via 18 proposed routes, Delhi transport minister Pankaj Kumar Singh said on Thursday.The proposed routes will connect Delhi with destinations including Patna, Gaya, Muzaffarpur, Darbhanga, Bhagalpur, Buxar, Araria, Purnia, Kishanganj and Madhubani, among others. Under the agreement, 12 bus permitseach will be allocated to Delhi and Bihar on every route.According to officials, the agreement is expected to benefit nearly two million people from Bihar and Purvanchal living and working in Delhi, in addition to other passengers travelling between the two states.Singh said both governments would mutually finalise timings and schedules to ensure convenient services, adding that the network could be expanded in the coming years.The initiative follows the operation of around 76 buses between Delhi and Bihar during Diwali and Chhath this year, which highlighted demand for a permanent arrangement.The Bihar State Road Transport Corporation has procured 75 non-AC and 74 AC buses for interstate operations. Another 150 buses will be deployed under the public-private partnership model.

headline: NGT seeks explanation from DJB over discharge in drains, orders DPCC to conduct spot inspections
content: The National Green Tribunal (NGT), in an order issued on November 25, has sought an explanation from the Delhi Jal Board (DJB) over the continued discharge of untreated sewage into drains in the city. It also directed the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) to inspect the affected locations, collect and analyse samples, and submit a report before the next hearing.The tribunal headed by chairperson justice Prakash Shrivastava was hearing the case Nizamuddin West Association vs Union of India.During the hearing, DJB submitted that work to trap sewage in certain drains had been completed. However, advocates presented photographs allegedly showing untreated sewage flowing into Drain No. 22 (Pant Nagar/Lajpat Nagar), despite the board reporting the work as complete.Taking note of the submissions, the tribunal directed the DJB chief engineer, who filed a progress affidavit on November 21, to submit a response. It observed that if the affidavit is found to be incorrect or false, appropriate legal action may follow.The DPCC has been asked to conduct spot inspections, particularly at the locations shown in the photographs, and submit its findings within four weeks. The tribunal also expressed concern over the vague status reports submitted by the DJB on sewage treatment plants (STPs) and decentralised sewage treatment plants (DSTPs).The DJB has been given two weeks to file a further affidavit detailing the progress of STP and DSTP projects, reasons for delays and revised timelines. It has also been directed to clarify whether the nano-bubbles plant being set up near Defence Colony is functional, when it began operations and how effective it has been.A DJB official said that the agency will submit its stance before the tribunal on the matter.The tribunal also took note of revised deadlines for completing work on 22 identified drains as several projects have been pushed to March or June 2027.In a separate case, the NGT took note of the Delhi Development Authority’s (DDA) submission on action against illegal groundwater extraction on the Yamuna floodplains, including the removal of 87 illegal borewells.According to the DDA’s affidavit, the authority removed 40 illegal borewells from Mayur Nature Park between July 18 and 22, 2024, along with around 200 cattle sheds, 20 illegal nurseries and four farmhouses. It also stated that it had reclaimed around 1,337.666 acres of floodplain land through anti-encroachment operations between May 26, 2022, and May 31, 2026.

headline: Delhi SIR filing window ends with 337,970 Form 6 submitted
content: New DelhiThe office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Delhi, received nearly 502,000 claims and objections until the deadline under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, following which the exercise of processing applications and disposing of notices issued to voters over mapping discrepancies and logical errors has started, according to data released by the CEO’s office on Thursday.The filing window, which began on August 31, ended on November 25. The CEO’s office said all forms received by the deadline will be disposed of by December 15, ahead of the publication of the final electoral roll, scheduled for December 22.As per the data shared, 501,880 forms were received during the SIR period, while 525,990 applications were received before August 31. Under the SIR, 337,970 Form 6 applications for inclusion of names were filed, 631 Form 6A applications were filed, 37,038 Form 7 applications for deletion of names were filed, and 126,241 Form 8 applications for correction or shifting of entries were filed.Before August 31, election authorities received 212,400 Form 6 applications, 1,351 Form 6 A applications, 51,471 Form 7 applications and 260,768 Form 8 applications.Officials said that the election office has made progress in disposing of notices issued to voters whose details were flagged during the mapping exercise. As of November 26, of 3,314,032 electors under the “no-mapping” and “logical discrepancy” categories, 3,300,164 electors have been parked for inclusion in the final electoral roll, the CEO’s office said. This means that only 13,868 cases were yet to be parked for inclusion, according to the latest figures.The office also said it disposed of 303,353 Form 6 applications, 36,373 Form 7 applications and 276,498 Form 8 applications during the ongoing disposal process.Meanwhile, the election office is also continuing a special drive to enrol voters whose names could not be included in the draft electoral roll because they were categorised as ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate).Under the drive, booth-level officers (BLOs) are visiting households to distribute enumeration forms to such electors. The distribution and collection exercise, which began on November 18, will continue until November 30. The forms will be disposed of by December 10, according to the schedule.The CEO’s office said BLOs would make efforts to trace these electors in coordination with residents’ welfare associations and booth-level agents of recognised political parties. Forms are being delivered physically or through electronic means such as WhatsApp and SMS wherever contact details are available.Electors can also download and submit enumeration forms through the ECINET app or the Election Commission’s website using the EPIC number they held before their names were deleted.The office clarified that voters who have already submitted Form 6 do not need to submit a separate enumeration form, as their applications will be processed under the Election Commission’s November 3 instructions. Those willing to enrol as voters can fill Form 6 even now, but their applications will only be disposed of after the final roll is published.SIR began in Delhi on June 30. At the time, the electoral roll comprised 14.5 million people. The draft roll was released on August 31, removing nearly 4.76 million people – all under the absent, shifted, dead or duplicate (ASDD) categories.

headline: Pocso convict held for sexually assaulting 10-year-old girl in Delhi park | India News
content: Police on Thursday said they had arrested a 40-year-old man, recently released from prison after serving an eight-year sentence for sexually assaulting a minor in 2018, for allegedly attempting to sexually assault a 10-year-old girl at a park in northwest Delhi’s Sangam Park.The accused, identified as Rajesh Kumar, works as a carpenter, police said.According to the police complaint, the girl, a Class 4 student at a private school, went to Ismail Khan Wala Bagh, a Delhi Development Authority (DDA)-maintained park, around 11am on Tuesday to play with her friends. Schools were closed for the Gurpurab holiday.“According to the survivor’s statement, she was inside the park playing hide and seek. She was standing in one of the corners when the accused, who was urinating nearby, spotted her and dragged her. He forced her and started disrobing her. She screamed for help, and people nearby rushed to assist her. They caught the accused, assaulted him and made a PCR call,” said an officer aware of the case.Also Read: East Delhi gang-rape case: Cafe sealed, owner detained; 3 accused on the runDeputy commissioner of police (northwest) Akanksha Yadav said Rajesh was arrested at the spot. The survivor was counselled and her statement recorded, she added.Based on her statement, a case was registered under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.Police said the accused had been arrested in 2018 for sexually assaulting a minor in Swaroop Nagar, north Delhi. He was convicted and sentenced to eight years in prison, and released around six months ago.“We are checking whether he targeted others as well. We have also collected his blood samples to check if he was under the influence of alcohol or drugs. He is unmarried and was near the park for some work,” the officer said.According to police, there was only one guard in the 22-acre park at the time of the incident. A police officer, who did not wish to be named, said they had asked DDA to deploy more guards.However, DDA, in a statement, said its security personnel had acted promptly after noticing the alleged incident. “The security guard immediately alerted the police, facilitating swift police intervention and the subsequent arrest of the accused.Also Read: Fast-track courts take 4 years for POCSO cases, says Delhi High Court reportDDA has already put in place requisite safety and security arrangements at the park, spread over 22.80 acres, including 47 functional light points, a boundary wall, entry/exit gates, women and child safety awareness boards and round-the-clock deployment of six security guards, with two guards in each shift,” the statement said.Just two months ago, grave security lapses were found in Aastha Kunj Park of southeast Delhi, where a 17-year-old girl was gang-raped allegedly by three men. The park had limited streetlights, no guards, and hardly any police deployment.The incident prompted authorities to step up security at the public parks.

headline: Give sanction to prosecute officials within a week: Supreme Court to banks, NBFCs
content: The Supreme Court on Thursday set a two-month deadline for the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to complete its investigation into the pending subvention scheme scam cases. It directed the banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) under scanner to grant sanction for prosecution of their officials within one week.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, and comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, passed the order while hearing a clutch of petitions by homebuyers. The court had entrusted the CBI with a probe into 55 cases involving a builder-bank nexus.A subvention scheme is a tripartite agreement between the builder, homebuyer and bank. Under it, banks agree to release loans to builders, who pay the EMIs till a specified cut-off or till the date of handing over possession of the flat.Investigation complete in 25 of 55 casesThe CBI told the court that investigation is complete in 25 of the 55 cases, in which final reports have been filed. According to its status report, charge sheets were filed in 22 of these and closure reports in the remaining three. Additional solicitor general (ASG) Aishwarya Bhati appeared for the agency. She said in the completed investigations, four banks/NBFCs had either not granted sanction for prosecution of their officers named in the charge sheet or had granted conditional sanction. The status report named four banks/institutions: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, PNB Housing Finance Limited and Sammaan Capital.Sanction was sought under section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, which requires prior sanction before a person is prosecuted under the Act. The CBI named officials of banks and financial institutions because the Act’s definition of a public servant also includes persons performing a public function. In this case, that function is the grant of loans to homebuyers. Disapproving of such conduct by banks and financial institutions, the bench said, “We direct all banks and financial institutions to issue unconditional prosecution sanction failing which the chairman-cum-managing director (CMD) shall be present in court.”Bhati said that HDFC had issued a conditional sanction, subject to its officials being public servants. The court set aside the conditional sanction and said, “We direct HDFC and other financial institutions to issue unconditional sanction for prosecution within one week.”CBI cites three-month period to wrap investigationWhen the bench asked about the timeline for completing the probe into the remaining cases, Bhati said the agency requires three months to complete the probe in the 30 pending matters. The court said, “We impress upon the CBI to complete its investigation within two months.”Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, appearing for one of the NBFCs under probe, said they do not perform any public function as they only provide loans. Other private banks also argued that they cannot be required to give sanction for prosecution of their officials.Also Read I Supreme Court tightens food labelling norms, gives FSSAI four months to finalise themThe bench said, “These are cases where FIRs were registered on orders of the court and it was the court which has monitored the investigations.” It made clear that sanction has to be granted, and warned further, “Those who are not concerned can say no sanction is required but you cannot deny. We will direct the registration of FIR against CMD of the bank if they do not give sanction.”The CBI had told the court that the 55 cases involve 25 banks/housing finance companies and 56 builders, spread across multiple projects in the country.The agency invoked the Prevention of Corruption Act against officials of six banks: Bank of India, State Bank of India, UCO Bank, HDFC, ICICI Bank and Sammaan Capital. In all, 34 prosecution sanctions are awaited, and the banks have not responded till date.

headline: Delhi AQI today: National Capital's air quality worsens to 273 on Friday, hovers in 'severe' category | Details inside
content: Delhi AQI today: A smoky haze covered the national capital on Friday, 27 November, as the air quality index (AQI) hovered in the 'severe' category at 273 at 6:11 AM. It fell nearly 120 points from the overnight peak of 393, recorded at 2:00 AM. Delhi's air quality improved through Thursday afternoon before worsening again in the evening. The AQI fell to 121 at 5:01 PM, its lowest reading in the previous 24 hours. It rose above 300 around 8:00 PM and reached 393 at 2:01 AM on the intervening night of Thursday and Friday. Readings remained above 300 until after 5 AM before easing later in the morning, according to AQI.in.Delhi's seven-day AQI peaked at 465 at 6 AM on 20 November. The seven-day period ended on 26 November. The lowest reading in that series was 170 at noon on 26 November. Early morning readings generally hovered between 350 and 450 on several days during that period.At 6:11 AM on Friday, Delhi's PM10 level stood at 274 micrograms per cubic metre, compared with the World Health Organization's (WHO) guideline of 45 micrograms per cubic metre. Carbon monoxide was reported at 2,208 parts per billion (ppb), while nitrogen dioxide measured 23 parts per billion and sulphur dioxide nine parts per billion. Ozone was recorded at two parts per billion. The temperature was 14℃, humidity was 57%, wind speed was 3.6 km/h, and the UV index was zero.According to PTI, citing data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Delhi's air quality was in the 'poor' category on Thursday, with an AQI of 224. Of the 55 monitoring stations across the capital, at least 40 were in the 'poor' category, 14 in the 'moderate' category, and one in the 'very poor' category. The monitoring station at ITO recorded 'very poor' air quality.The CPCB data also showed that Thursday was the 12th consecutive day when the national capital recorded 'poor' air quality. On Tuesday, Delhi's AQI was 227. It later declined to 220 on Wednesday, then rose to 224 on Thursday.ncPTI, citing real-time source apportionment estimates for Delhi on Thursday, reported that secondary organic aerosols were the largest contributors to PM2.5 pollution, accounting for roughly 24.8% of the estimated load. These aerosols form in the atmosphere when gases released by sources such as vehicles, industries and other combustion activities react with other compounds in the air to produce fine particles. Vehicular emissions accounted for 20.6% of the total. Biomass burning accounted for 19.7%, while secondary inorganic pollutants accounted for 12.5%. Other sources included waste burning (11.4%), road dust, soil and minerals (4.5%), industrial activity (2.7%), coal burning (1.6%), firecrackers (1.4%) and mixed combustion (0.6%). According to the report, between 1 October and 25 November, Delhi ranked first among the 10 most polluted cities in the National Capital Region (NCR) for both PM2.5 and PM10 levels. It reportedly moved up from third and fourth positions, respectively, during the corresponding period last year. An analysis of the India Air Quality Portal by EnviroCatalysts found that Delhi recorded the highest average PM2.5 concentration at 113 micrograms per cubic metre during the period under review. Gurugram followed with 109 micrograms per cubic metre, while Noida and Ghaziabad recorded 105 and 103, respectively. Meerut reported 96, Baghpat and Greater Noida 95 each, Panipat 90, Bulandshahr 82 and Faridabad 69 micrograms per cubic metre. CPCB AQI classification The CPCB classifies an AQI reading of 0-50 as 'good', 51-100 as 'satisfactory', 101-200 as 'moderate', 201-300 as 'poor', 301-400 as 'very poor' and 401-500 as 'severe'. AQI.in classification AQI.in follows the US AQI scale, under which readings of 0-50 are classified as 'good', 51-100 as 'moderate', 101-150 as 'poor', 151-200 as 'unhealthy', 201-300 as 'severe ', and 301 and above as 'hazardous'. (With agency inputs)

headline: Petrol, diesel prices today, November 27: Check fuel rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and other cities
content: Petrol and diesel prices remained largely stable across major cities on Friday, November 27, even as crude oil prices headed for their first weekly gain this month amid escalating tensions in the Middle East.In Noida, petrol prices increased by ₹0.16 to ₹102.12 per litre, while diesel rates rose by ₹0.12 to ₹95.56 per litre, according to Goodreturns data.In Delhi, petrol was priced at ₹102.12 per litre, while diesel retailed at ₹95.20 per litre. In Mumbai, petrol cost ₹111.21 per litre and diesel ₹97.83 per litre.In Kolkata, petrol was priced at ₹113.51 per litre and diesel at ₹99.82 per litre. Meanwhile, Chennai recorded petrol prices of ₹107.76 per litre and diesel rates of ₹99.55 per litre.Petrol and diesel prices in major Indian cities on November 27Why are crude oil prices rising?Oil prices are heading for their first weekly gain this month as attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers in the Middle East have raised concerns about an escalation in hostilities, according to a Bloomberg report.West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose to nearly $85 per barrel, while Brent crude closed below $97 in the previous session.Tehran-backed Houthi militants attacked Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery on the Red Sea, temporarily halting some operations. The attack came after the group targeted the Ras Tanura oil hub in the Persian Gulf earlier this week.Concerns over shipping routes have also persisted. A tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations, following unconfirmed Iranian claims that other vessels had hit mines.However, increased traffic through the waterway this month has helped keep oil prices in check.Despite the recent recovery, Brent crude is down nearly a fifth this month following a revival in Middle Eastern exports. The International Energy Agency expects this to push the oil market into a surplus this quarter.Oil-product markets have also seen some relief, with diesel futures in Europe and pump prices in the US declining. Diesel had rallied more sharply than crude oil amid disruptions linked to the US-Iran war and escalating Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries.Traders will also be watching Sunday's OPEC meeting, where the group is expected to discuss its supply strategy for 2027. The alliance is considering maintaining its existing output quotas through January, even as members remain divided over their sustainable production capacities.What has the Centre said about fuel prices?On Monday, Hardeep Singh Puri reiterated that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's policies had shielded Indian consumers from global fuel price shocks, with domestic retail prices remaining largely stable despite international crises.Inspecting petrol pumps in Indore on Sunday, the Rajya Sabha member from Madhya Pradesh said the Centre had reduced excise duty three times -- in November 2021, May 2022 and on March 10, 2026 -- limiting the increase in domestic fuel prices to "around seven per cent against a 50-70 per cent surge globally".Puri also praised state-run oil marketing companies — Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) — for absorbing heavy losses when crude oil prices rose from $60-65 to $120 per barrel.

headline: From Rs 88-lakh chandeliers to a Rs 1.5-crore kitchen: What visitors can expect inside Delhi’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’
content: A modular kitchen estimated at Rs 1.5 crore, chandeliers costing up to Rs 88 lakh, curtains worth nearly Rs 95 lakh, a jacuzzi, sauna and around 50 air-conditioners are among the extravagant household fittings and amenities that visitors could see when the Delhi Government opens former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal’s official residence, popularly dubbed ‘Sheesh Mahal’, to the public this week.Nearly two years after Kejriwal vacated the bungalow at 6, Flag Staff Road, the BJP government plans to showcase its lavish interiors and facilities to highlight what it describes as extravagant spending of taxpayers’ money.The government has decided to retain the premises in their existing condition, without undertaking any special arrangements for the viewing experience. Visitors will be allowed to walk through the bungalow on a 15-20-minute tour, with labels placed alongside various installations, fittings and other features explaining their details.The proposal to develop the property as a State Guest House-cum-Cultural Centre has been dropped. Instead, the government plans to turn it into a public viewing attraction, allowing visitors to see the premises and judge for themselves the scale of construction and facilities.Among the most talked-about features are the property's elaborate interiors and high-value household installations. According to details disclosed by PWD Minister Parvesh Verma during a video walkthrough of the premises earlier this year, the residence has a modular kitchen estimated at Rs 1.5 crore, a chimney costing nearly Rs 5 lakh, chandeliers valued at up to Rs 88 lakh and curtains estimated at around Rs 95 lakh.The list of amenities also includes a jacuzzi reportedly costing Rs 6 lakh, a sauna room estimated at Rs 10 lakh, premium recliners, designer furniture, automated curtains and smart lighting systems. The lighting arrangements can reportedly change colours through remote controls, with different shades available across rooms.The minister had also highlighted television units reportedly costing up to Rs 28 lakh, a sound system, luxury bathroom fittings and imported Vietnamese marble. Around 50 air-conditioners were reportedly installed across bedrooms, living areas, dressing rooms and bathrooms.The premises also reportedly feature gym equipment, including a treadmill valued at Rs 14 lakh.Talking to The Tribune, an official said the idea was to show visitors what was already present inside the bungalow. The labels would carry details about the various items and installations, explaining what they were and providing information about them.“The objective is simply to show people how this grand palace, built at a cost of Rs 60 crore using taxpayers’ money, came into existence,” the official said.The arrangements for opening the property, including the visitor management system, are still being finalised. Details regarding public access, ticketing and reservations are expected to be announced separately.The controversy over the bungalow's renovation gained further traction after a Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) report, tabled in the Delhi Assembly in March 2026, pegged the construction and renovation expenditure at Rs 33.66 crore against the initial estimate of Rs 7.91 crore. The audit flagged expenditure of Rs 18.88 crore on items involving superior specifications, artistic and antique features and ornamental works.It also pointed to an increase in the built-up area from 1,397 square metres to 1,905 square metres and procedural lapses in the award of additional works.While BJP leaders have repeatedly raised allegations about extravagant installations, the Aam Aadmi Party has rejected the charges, calling them politically motivated.With the government planning to open the bungalow in its existing condition, the public tour is expected to offer a closer look at the fittings and facilities that have so far featured largely in political exchanges and video walkthroughs.The ‘Sheesh Mahal’ controversyArvind Kejriwal moved into the bungalow at 6, Flag Staff Road with his family in March 2015, after becoming Chief Minister for a second consecutive term. Built in 1942, the property reportedly had five bedrooms and a separate office.Renovation was proposed in 2020 after portions of the roof, including that of a toilet, collapsed during the Covid-19 pandemic, raising concerns over structural safety. However, the scope of the project expanded, prompting the BJP to allege that public funds were being used to turn the official residence into a luxury property. Allegations of imported marble, designer fittings, chandeliers and other high-end amenities became central to its criticism. The term ‘Sheesh Mahal’ featured prominently in the BJP’s campaign against Kejriwal ahead of the February 2025 Assembly elections.Kejriwal vacated the bungalow on October 4, 2024, after resigning as Chief Minister. His successor, Atishi, moved in on October 6 but was asked to vacate it three days later amid a dispute over its formal handover to the Public Works Department (PWD). Though allotted the property again on October 11, she never took physical possession. The allotment was withdrawn in January 2025.After coming to power in February 2025, the BJP government considered transferring the property to the Centre or converting it into a State Guest House. In July 2026, it moved towards developing the premises as a guest house-cum-cultural centre, with accommodation for visiting officials, conference facilities and spaces for cultural events. The latest decision to open the property to the public marks a departure from that plan, giving the controversial bungalow a new identity as a public viewing attraction.

headline: ''Threat To Communal Harmony': MK Stalin Blames Vijay For Deepam Row Escalation
content: DMK president MK Stalin launched a sharp attack on Tamil Nadu's ruling TVK and Chief Minister Vijay on Friday, following the Supreme Court's intervention in the Thiruparankundram Karthigai Deepam controversy, describing the developments as shocking and calling them a "blatant failure" of the state government. The former chief minister expressed shock over the disbanding of the temple's Board of Trustees, the deployment of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) on the hill and the Supreme Court's direction to the Chief Secretary and senior police and administrative officials to appear before it. He described these developments as an "unprecedented threat to communal harmony and state rights". The DMK Chief placed the responsibility for the situation squarely on the state government, shifting the blame to the temple trustees. "Instead of taking responsibility, the state government blamed the temple trustees and hid behind cowardice," he alleged. The Supreme Court on Friday directed that the Karthigai Deepam be lit at the disputed hilltop stone pillar on November 28, following the Tamil Nadu government's failure to implement its November 20 interim order permitting a one-time lighting of the lamp at the location. The court also permitted devotees to access the hilltop for the lighting, subject to the conditions laid down in its order, and directed the CRPF to provide security. It suspended the temple's Board of Trustees and appointed two former Madras High Court judges as receivers to oversee the temple administration and ensure compliance with its directions.

headline: The need for financially informed governance | Hindustan Times
content: A country's economic progress depends not only on the strength of its financial institutions but also on the regulatory and judicial frameworks that govern them. As economies become increasingly interconnected and financial markets grow more sophisticated, decisions involving banks, investors and commercial institutions can have consequences that extend far beyond the parties directly involved. In such an environment, the relationship between law and economics assumes particular significance. Legal certainty remains essential, but so does an understanding of the economic realities within which institutions operate.Financial institutions perform a critical role in sustaining economic activity. They facilitate investments, support businesses, mobilise savings and provide credit to individuals and enterprises. However, their operations also expose them to risks arising from market volatility, inadequate capital, poor governance and changing economic conditions. When a financial institution encounters distress, the challenge is not simply to determine who is legally responsible but also to establish a resolution mechanism that protects the wider financial system from instability.This makes regulatory frameworks particularly important. Financial regulations are designed to establish accountability, maintain institutional discipline and ensure that financial institutions have adequate safeguards against potential crises. However, regulations must also be sufficiently clear, consistent and adaptable to address situations that may not follow conventional patterns. Ambiguity in regulatory provisions can create uncertainty among financial institutions, investors and regulators, complicating decision-making precisely when timely intervention becomes necessary.One of the most important considerations during a financial crisis is the allocation of losses. When an institution becomes financially distressed, the consequences must be distributed among different stakeholders, including shareholders, creditors, investors and, in certain circumstances, the public sector. The manner in which these responsibilities are allocated influences the incentives of market participants and determines how much risk is ultimately transferred to the wider economy. A well-designed resolution framework must, therefore, establish a transparent hierarchy of responsibilities while ensuring that the burden of institutional failure does not disproportionately fall on taxpayers.Financial instruments designed to absorb risk are an important part of this architecture. They provide institutions with mechanisms to manage financial stress without immediately depending on external assistance. However, their effectiveness depends on the certainty that contractual provisions and regulatory safeguards will operate as intended. If investors remain uncertain about how such instruments will be treated during a crisis, the resulting risk perception can influence investment decisions, increase borrowing costs and weaken confidence in the financial system.The Supreme Court's decision in the AT1 verdict involving Yes Bank illustrates how judicial interpretations of financial instruments can have wider implications for banking stability and investor confidence. The case also highlights the importance of clearly defined regulatory authority and procedures during the resolution of distressed financial institutions. Such disputes demonstrate why legal reasoning in financial matters must engage with the economic purpose of the instruments and the potential consequences of their interpretation.This does not mean that economic considerations should override established legal principles or that judicial scrutiny should be weakened in the interests of financial institutions. The protection of contractual rights, procedural fairness and institutional accountability remains fundamental to the rule of law. However, legal decisions involving complex financial arrangements also require an appreciation of how individual outcomes can influence market behaviour, institutional balance sheets and the broader economy. The objective should be to develop an approach in which legal safeguards and economic stability reinforce rather than undermine each other.Investor confidence is particularly sensitive to uncertainty. Financial markets function on the understanding that rules will be applied consistently and that risks can be assessed with reasonable predictability. When regulatory interpretations change or institutional responsibilities remain unclear, investors may demand higher returns to compensate for the additional uncertainty. This can increase the cost of capital, discourage long-term investments and make financial institutions more vulnerable during periods of economic stress.Consequently, economic literacy within regulatory institutions and the judiciary deserves greater attention. Financial disputes increasingly involve sophisticated instruments, interconnected markets and complex risk-sharing arrangements. A deeper understanding of these mechanisms can help decision-makers assess not only the immediate legal questions but also the possible implications for employment, credit availability, business continuity and financial stability. Specialised training and greater engagement with financial experts could strengthen the quality of institutional decision-making without compromising judicial independence.The speed at which financial disputes are resolved is equally important. Unlike many conventional commercial disagreements, disputes involving distressed financial institutions can have immediate implications for market confidence and the availability of capital. Prolonged uncertainty can affect business operations, investor sentiment and the ability of institutions to plan their future. Specialised mechanisms and time-bound procedures for resolving complex financial disputes could help minimise these disruptions while preserving the necessary scope for judicial scrutiny.As India advances towards its ambition of becoming a developed economy, the resilience of its financial institutions will remain central to sustainable growth. This requires more than robust banks and well-capitalised markets. It demands regulatory clarity, accountable institutions, predictable legal processes and a judiciary equipped to appreciate the economic dimensions of financial disputes. Ultimately, the strength of a financial system lies not merely in its ability to withstand crises but also in the quality of the institutions that respond to them. Bridging the understanding between law and economics is, therefore, essential to building a financial architecture that inspires confidence, distributes risk responsibly and supports long-term economic progress.(The views expressed are personal)This article is authored by Dr Charan Singh, former RBI Chair, professor of economics, IIM Bangalore and Dr Atul Mehta, associate professor, UNSW Bengaluru.

headline: First time in 1952, a 1976 freeze: Tracing the journey of delimitation in India
content: The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, which seeks to pave the way for delimitation in the country to implement women's reservation in Parliament and state legislative assemblies. The proposed amendment comes three years after the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, was enacted, providing for one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.Under the delimitation process, constituency boundaries are redrawn and seats are allocated among states and Union territories based on their population. The exercise is key to implementing women's reservation, as the 2023 law's rollout is linked to a delimitation exercise following a Census.ALSO READ: Govt’s delimitation plan: 50% seat hike for every state, Lok Sabha strength ceiling rises to 850 Article 81 of the Constitution provides for the principle of “one person, one vote, one value” by seeking to ensure, as far as practicable, an equal ratio between a state's population and the number of Lok Sabha seats allotted to it. Article 81(2)(a) states: “There shall be allotted to each State a number of seats in the House of the People in such manner that the ratio between that number and the population of the state is, so far as practicable, the same for all States.”The only exception to this provision is for states with a population not exceeding six million. They are exempt from the requirement of maintaining the same population-to-seat ratio as other states, allowing them to retain adequate representation in the Lower House despite their smaller populations.ALSO READ: How Centre's delimitation plan could change India's electoral map: A look at state-wise numbersArticle 82 of the Constitution provides for the readjustment of the allocation of seats and the division of states into territorial constituencies after every Census. Article 81(3), meanwhile, defines the population to be considered for the purpose of seat allocation and delimitation. It states: “In this article, the expression ‘population’ means the population as ascertained at the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published.”Delimitation exercises in India over the yearsThe first delimitation exercise was carried out in 1952, based on the 1951 Census. Since then, four delimitation commissions have been constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002. The 29-year gap between the last two commissions was the result of the Constitution (42nd Amendment) Act, 1976, which froze the allocation of Lok Sabha seats among states, based on the 1971 Census, until the publication of figures from the first Census conducted after 2000.According to an earlier Hindustan Times report citing former chief election commissioner SY Quraishi, the freeze was intended to ensure that states which had performed well in family planning programmes did not lose their proportional political representation in the Lok Sabha.In 2002, under the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led government, the delimitation exercise was taken up again. However, the decision was to allow constituency boundaries within states and Union territories to be redrawn based on population, without changing the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to each state or UT. This was intended to ensure that states which had made progress in population control did not lose their share of parliamentary representation to states with higher population growth.The Delimitation Commission, headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Kuldip Singh, was constituted in 2002. Its exercise was completed in 2008, with delimitation orders coming into effect in most states and Union territories in February that year. The erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir was excluded from the exercise. The process was also deferred in four northeastern states of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Manipur through presidential orders issued on February 8, 2008, citing concerns over security and public order.The Constitution (84th Amendment) Act, 2001, extended the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha seats among states until the publication of figures from the first Census conducted after 2026. It, however, allowed the redrawing of constituency boundaries based on the 1991 Census. The Constitution (87th Amendment) Act, 2003, subsequently provided for the use of the 2001 Census for this purpose, without altering the total number of seats allotted to individual states.The existing constitutional freeze is linked to the publication of the relevant figures from the first Census conducted after 2026. It is not triggered merely by the completion of the Census exercise.Southern states have argued that a fresh population-based allocation of Lok Sabha seats could reduce their relative share of parliamentary representation, as states such as Uttar Pradesh and Bihar have recorded higher population growth than several southern states. However, the latest proposal seeks to retain the existing proportional share of states while increasing their Lok Sabha seats by 50 per cent.

headline: Delimitation Bill proposes formation of commission, SC judge, CEC nominee among members
content: A delimitation commission will be immediately constituted after The Delimitation (Second) Bill takes effect, according to a copy of the document accessed by HT.According to the document, the proposed three-member delimitation commission will include a serving or former Supreme Court judge, the Chief Election Commissioner or one of the Election Commissioners (ex-officio) appointed by him and a state election commissioner.Section 3 of the Bill provides for the constitution of a delimitation commission. Here's what it reads: “(a) one member, who shall be a person who is or has been a Judge of the Supreme Court, to be appointed by the Central Government, as the Chairperson of the Commission; (b) the Chief Election Commissioner or an Election Commissioner nominated by the Chief Election Commissioner, ex officio: ….. and (c) the State Election Commissioner of the State concerned, ex officio.”The proposed Bill, which is expected to be introduced in the Lok Sabha during the special Parliament sitting scheduled from November 30, says that the panel will be formed if the Bill passes both Houses of Parliament and becomes an Act with the President's assent.Also Read | Govt’s delimitation plan: 50% seat hike for every state, Lok Sabha strength ceiling rises to 850A serving or former Supreme Court judge will be appointed as the panel's chairperson.The government is expected to bring the fresh delimitation bill alongside the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, which seeks to amend constitutional provisions to enable the implementation of the one-third quota for women after the first delimitation exercise following its commencement. The Union cabinet had cleared the revised legislation on Friday, ahead of the special sitting of Parliament.However, the bill clarifies that after the nomination of an Election Commissioner as a member under the relevant clause, the nomination of an Election Commissioner as a member under will be made except to fill the casual vacancy of such member under section 6.For Meghalaya and Nagaland, the third member will be a person nominated by the respective state governor. The bill also mentions the constituencies of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir under Pakistan's occupation. “The Election Commission shall act as delimitation commission for the purpose of delimiting constituencies in the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir falling under the occupation of Pakistan, when the area of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir under the occupation of Pakistan ceases to be so occupied,” the bill states.Delimitation commission to also include MPs, MLAs as associate membersThe bill which is expected to be introduced in Parliament proposes that the delimitation commission will associate ten members from each state to assist it – five Lok Sabha MPs representing that state and five members of its legislative assembly. In states with five or fewer MPs, all such MPs will be associate members, and the total number of associated members will be reduced accordingly.However the associate members will not have voting rights or the power to sign any decision of the commission. The MPs part of the panel will be nominated by the Lok Sabha speaker, while the speaker of the respective state legislative assembly will nominate the MLAs, keeping in mind the composition of the House concerned.The panel can also seek assistance from the registrar-general and census commissioner, surveyor general, government officials geographical information system experts and other relevant individuals.Also Read | How Centre's delimitation plan could change India's electoral map: A look at state-wise numbersTerm and functions of the delimitation commissionThe term of the commission will be specified by the Centre through a notification if the Bill is passed and becomes an Act. The Union government can, on the request of the commission, extend its term “by such further period as it may consider necessary.”The delimitation commission will readjust:(a) the allocation of seats in the House of the People to the States and Union territories and the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State, in accordance with the provisions of this Act;(b) the division of each State and Union territory into territorial constituencies, on the basis of the latest census figures

headline: High oil, gas prices add Rs 6-7 lakh crore burden to economy annually: PMO advisor
content: NEW DELHI: As India’s dependence on imported oil and gas continues to remain high, surging energy prices have added an estimated Rs 6-7 lakh crore annually to the financial burden on the Indian economy, said Tarun Kapoor, advisor in the Prime Minister’s Office, on Friday.Speaking at the 16th Energy Security Conference organised by CII, Kapoor advocated a structural shift towards electric vehicles for both freight and passenger transportation to reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels.“Our large dependence on imports has shown that we are so vulnerable that we may be caught in a tight situation and it can be disastrous for the country. High prices of crude and natural gas are costing us at least Rs 6-7 lakh crore extra every year. Imagine the impact this has on the economy,” Kapoor said.He added that if govt and oil companies had not absorbed the increase in oil and gas prices, and the higher costs had been passed on to consumers, as is done in many countries in Europe and the US, the impact on consumer goods and supplies would have been disastrous.In the first half of the 2026-27 financial year (Apr-Sept), India imported 122.7 MT of crude, marginally higher than the 121.8 MT imported during the corresponding period last year. The import bill, however, jumped to $90.6 billion from $61.9 billion due to elevated crude oil prices amid global uncertainties.Referring to the Prime Minister’s appeal to citizens to reduce energy consumption, Kapoor said some reduction was observed initially, but rising incomes, economic growth and increased travel and transportation requirements subsequently pushed consumption upwards.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

headline: Bihar student found dead in Sangrur; several detained for questioning
content: A Bihar-origin student was found dead under mysterious circumstances near a drain outside an engineering institute here on Saturday, with police saying they are probing the circumstances behind his death.Sunam deputy superintendent of police Kulwinder Singh said as per preliminary information, an argument allegedly broke out between a group of students outside the Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology (SLIET) campus the previous day, which purportedly escalated into a physical altercation.Whether the deceased, Ayush Kumar, originally from Bihar’s Muzaffarpur, was attacked by some students is a matter of investigation, he said.The DSP said police are waiting for Ayush’s parents to reach, after which a case will be registered based on their complaint.A senior police official said information was received at Longowal police station on Saturday morning that a body was found lying near a drain adjoining SLIET.Investigation has revealed that during the clash, Ayush may have been pushed around, he said.Some students have been rounded up in connection with the incident and are being questioned, he added.The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) in a statement said it condemns “murder of SLIET student Ayush Raj and demands impartial probe and strict action against culprits”.The RSS-affiliated students’ organisation expressed grief over the death of Ayush, a third-year B Tech student at SLIET. “A native of Muzaffarpur, Bihar, Ayush Raj was found dead near the institute’s main gate on November 27. Preliminary information suggests that the murder was linked to drug abuse and personal rivalry.”

headline: Fazilka SSP Gagan Ajit, former Ludhiana CP Swapan Sharma, ex-IAS officer Gurpreet Sapra appear before ED
content: Former Ludhiana police commissioner Swapan Sharma, who was recently appointed Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of the Ropar Range, appeared before the Enforcement Directorate (ED) at its Sector 17 office in Chandigarh on Friday.Sharma, who arrived at around 11.15 am, remained at the ED office for over eight hours before leaving at around 7.25 pm.Former IAS officer Gurpreet Kaur Sapra also appeared before the agency. She reached the ED office at 2.15 pm and left at 7.25 pm.Jaspal Singh, father of Moga MLA Amandeep Kaur Arora, appeared before the ED at 10.15 am and left at 5.45 pm. Speaking to media after the questioning, he said the agency had questioned him about a land deal.Fazilka SSP Gagan Ajit Singh also appeared before the ED at its Chandigarh office in connection with an ongoing investigation.The summonses were allegedly issued to them in connection with the agency's investigation into the money-laundering case involving suspended DIG HS Bhullar and alleged middleman Krishanu Sharda, both of whom were arrested by the CBI last year.The ED had summoned Administrative Secretary (Health) Kumar Rahul, PCS officer Anand Sagar Sharma, retired officers Gurpreet Sapra and Arun Sekhri, Fazilka SSP Gagan Ajit Singh, Special Secretary (General Administration) Neeru Katyal Gupta and former Ludhiana police commissioner Swapan Sharma.Bhullar and Sharda were arrested by the CBI on October 16 last year. Sharda was caught allegedly accepting a bribe on behalf of Bhullar, who was then DIG of the Ropar Range. Bhullar was arrested the same day.
