headline: Punjab govt launches Mission Clean Punjab 3.0 across 166 urban local bodies
content: While elected representatives will closely monitor the campaign in their respective constituencies, the daily progress of every urban local body will be reviewed at the state level to ensure zero laxity, Local Government Minister Harjot Singh Bains said. !Image 1: Of the 31,802 complaints received during the campaign, 28,686 were resolved, while 2,935 remained pending and 181 were declared invalid or rejected, Local Government Minister Harjot Singh Bains said. Of the 31,802 complaints received during the campaign, 28,686 were resolved, while 2,935 remained pending and 181 were declared invalid or rejected, Local Government Minister Harjot Singh Bains said. The Punjab government on Friday launched 'Mission Clean Punjab 3.0' across all 166 urban local bodies (ULBs), aiming to improve urban governance and civic infrastructure by addressing eight key civic issues in every urban ward. Local Government Minister Harjot Singh Bains, who launched the campaign, said it builds upon the "resounding success" of earlier cleanliness drives by moving beyond routine garbage collection to identify and resolve eight critical day-to-day civic problems across every urban ward.

headline: Delhi government opens Arvind Kejriwal’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’ to media ahead of public viewing
content: New Delhi: The Delhi government on Friday opened 6, Flagstaff Road, the official residence allotted to former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, to the media ahead of plans to open it to the public next month. Mr. Kejriwal lived in the bungalow with his family from 2015 until October 2024, when he vacated it after stepping down as Chief Minister. The preview comes ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly election, in which Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) is seeking another term. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta urged people in Delhi and Punjab to visit the bungalow and see how, in her words, AAP had “looted” Delhi and was now “looting” Punjab. “Today, the veil has been lifted once more, exposing all their misdeeds to the public. People can now see how they misused the hard-earned money of the public, earned through the blood and sweat of the common man, to build a ‘Sheesh Mahal’ for themselves, while the people of Delhi remained homeless and destitute,” Ms. Gupta said. She alleged that AAP had plundered Delhi over the past 12 years, causing it considerable economic harm, and had delivered little in the name of development. Instead, she said, the party had spent crores on propaganda and advertisements, besides spending lavishly on its own “extravagant lifestyle”. The bungalow in Civil Lines has been dubbed ‘Sheesh Mahal’ by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) over allegations that an “exorbitant” amount was spent on its renovation. The alleged irregularities are under scrutiny by central investigative agencies while AAP has denied the allegations. The BJP claims that the Public Works Department (PWD) built the bungalow at a cost of ₹58 crore during the COVID-19 pandemic. The residence, spread over 1,905 square metres, has eight bedrooms and 13 bathrooms. The media tour included details of the prices and bills for its furniture and fittings. ‘Public has right to know’ During the tour, PWD Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh said the purpose of opening it to the public is to ensure accountability. “We have only one objective: every government should provide a full account of where Delhi residents’ money, or taxpayers’ money, has been spent and how much has been spent. The public has the right to know how the former Chief Minister spent their money, meant for Delhi’s development. We have no political motive here,” he said. He said the bungalow was being built when Delhi was battling COVID-19. “The people of Delhi were struggling to breathe, and here a sauna, a jacuzzi and a steam room were being fitted,” Mr. Singh said. The Minister said several homes meant for government officials and two adjoining government bungalows had been demolished and merged to build the residence. “The entire house is exactly as it was before; nothing in it has been moved around. Therefore, the public has every right to know where their money was spent,” he said. AAP did not comment on the issue.

headline: Jalandhar DC Office Blackout Drill | Civil Defence Mock Exercise
content: A multi-agency civil defence mock drill and blackout exercise was conducted at Jalandhar DC Office, with SDRF, Punjab Police, Fire Brigade and Health Department teams demonstrating emergency rescue operations. Jalandhar, November 27: A multi-agency civil defence mock drill and blackout exercise was conducted at the District Administrative Complex in Jalandhar as part of Punjab's statewide emergency preparedness initiative. The exercise aimed to assess the readiness of various government departments and emergency response teams to deal with situations such as air raids, fires and other major disasters. The drill was organised under the directions of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to strengthen coordination among different departments and prepare civilians to respond effectively during emergency situations. The exercise began with a simulated air raid warning, following which red warning sirens were sounded and a blackout was implemented within the DC Office complex. Officials clarified that the blackout was restricted to the administrative complex and that electricity supply across the rest of Jalandhar city remained unaffected. After the simulated threat ended, a second green all-clear siren was sounded, signalling the commencement of emergency response operations. Teams were then deployed to handle staged disaster situations involving fires and simulated structural collapses. Several departments participated in the coordinated exercise, including the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), Punjab Police, Fire Brigade, Civil Defence volunteers, Home Guards and the Health Department.

headline: After Patiala-Sangrur bridge collapse, Punjab orders safety audit of all bridges
content: Days after the collapse of a national highway bridge on the Patiala-Sangrur road triggered a war of words between the ruling AAP government in Punjab and the BJP-led Centre, the state government has ordered a comprehensive safety inspection of bridges across Punjab.Taking serious note of the incident, Public Works Minister Harbhajan Singh ETO has directed senior field engineering officers of the PWD (B&R) to inspect all bridges falling under their respective jurisdictions and identify any structural deficiencies that could pose a risk to commuters.The minister has asked the officers to pay particular attention to the condition of foundations, piers, abutments, decks and other critical structural components. Any cracks, deterioration or signs of structural distress must be assessed promptly, with preventive measures initiated wherever necessary.He has also directed the department to engage specialised agencies, reputed technical institutions or structural engineering experts, wherever required, to conduct detailed safety audits and non-destructive testing, particularly of old and vulnerable bridges.Harbhajan Singh ETO emphasised that the exercise should be undertaken on priority and inspection findings, along with recommendations for necessary repairs, strengthening or rehabilitation, should be properly documented to ensure public safety and prevent any untoward incident.A 60-metre-long steel truss bridge over Bhakra Main Line Canal near Passiana village on the Patiala-Sangrur highway collapsed early on November 20, trapping two sand-laden trucks in the mangled structure. One of the vehicles caught fire, leaving its driver injured.The incident occurred around 6 am on the Patiala bypass section of National Highway-64 (now NH-07), the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) said. Parts of the trapped vehicles were left hanging precariously over the canal.The bridge collapse had triggered a political confrontation between the AAP government and BJP, with both sides trading charges over responsibility for the incident and the condition of the national highway infrastructure.BJP and SAD accused the ruling AAP of neglecting safety maintenance and allowing rampant illegal sand mining on canal and river beds near the bridge, which they said was weakening its structural strength.The AAP leaders, including Punjab media in-charge Baltej Pannu and spokesperson Neel Garg, pointed out that the bridge was built about a decade ago during the previous SAD-BJP government. Pannu targeted BJP and NHAI over construction standards, maintenance, and heavy toll collection without adequate safety or commuter facilities.Harbhajan Singh had urged Union Minister Nitin Gadkari to order a structural safety audit of all national highway bridges across Punjab.Meanwhile, during a review meeting, the minister also assessed the constituency-wise and division-wise progress of ongoing state highway and link road projects being executed by PWD.He directed officials to ensure that projects under various schemes, including SASCI, Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) and NABARD, were completed within the stipulated timelines.With winter setting in, he also instructed officials to expedite the installation of lane markings and other road safety equipment on stretches where the work remained pending, keeping in view the reduced visibility during foggy conditions.The minister said the state government was undertaking construction and renovation of around 45,000 km of roads across Punjab.PWD Secretary Ravi Bhagat, Joint Secretary Amarbir Sidhu, Engineer-in-Chief Gagandeep Singh, Chief Engineer Arshdeep Singh, and other senior engineering officers attended the meeting.

headline: Mock drill conducted in Punjab to test civil defence preparedness, emergency response
content: Chandigarh, Nov 27 (PTI) A mock exercise across all districts of Punjab was conducted on Friday evening to test the civil defence preparedness in the state and emergency response, officials said. The exercise was conducted at 8 pm in all districts of the state according to the directives of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). The mock exercise commenced with an air raid warning signal, which was disseminated through sirens featuring a high-low pitch for a duration of two minutes. During the course of the exercise, a simulated blackout was enforced in specific areas identified by the respective deputy commissioners-cum-controllers, civil defence. The public in these identified areas had been instructed to switch off all non-essential lighting during the blackout period. However, essential services remained functional during the blackout. The exercise concluded with an ‘all clear’ signal, characterised by a continuous high-pitch siren for two minutes, marking the formal termination of the drill.

headline: From Punjab’s fields to the Canadian prairies
content: At dawn in the quiet chill of Saskatchewan, a single thought can spark a profound shift in perspective. For nearly five decades, my life has spanned two far-off corners of the globe — from my roots in Punjab to building a new life over the last decade on the Canadian Prairies.Before immigrating, I had living a comfortable life. I had a stable teaching position in my hometown in Malout, built a new house, bought a car, and enjoyed a vibrant social life surrounded by extended family. Yet, despite the contentment, a quiet restlessness persisted — an inner calling to step into the unknown.With the unwavering support of my wife, Meenakshi, we took a leap of faith. Leaving behind our newly built home, established careers, and close-knit family, we travelled to the other end of the world to begin anew.Relocating across the globe is rarely seamless. For us, it meant starting from scratch — enduring sub-zero Prairie winters, and adapting to stark contrasts between rural and urban landscapes. As a high school teacher who has stood in classrooms in both India and Canada, I witnessed firsthand how educational philosophies and everyday mannerisms shift across borders. In Punjab, respect is often expressed through formal deference; in a Canadian classroom, it is built through open dialogue, mutual curiosity, and informal warmth. Wisdom and courtesy, I quickly learned, are not static — they evolve across languages and cultures.Beyond the classroom, the true test of adaptation unfolded inside our home. Raising two teenagers in a new land offered a deeply personal lens into the immigrants’ journey. Balancing our Punjabi values and mother tongue with the realities of growing up in North America required constant conversation, patience, and an open mind. Every cultural hurdle — from navigating school traditions to bridging generational expectations — became a lesson in unlearning old assumptions and listening without judgment.Today, as both Meenakshi and I serve as permanent high school teachers and call Saskatoon our home, people often ask if the sacrifices were worth it. My answer is an unequivocal ‘yes’.Still, rebuilding a life comes with a quiet ache. Video calls can never fully replace the warmth of spontaneous chai and gupshup or festive family gatherings back in Punjab, neither do the taste of samosas and butter chicken here seems genuine. Yet, those very hardships cultivate a profound empathy. Stepping outside one's comfort zone strips away inherited biases and fosters genuine respect for diverse faiths, traditions, and races. It shapes you into a true global citizen — someone whose compassion transcends man-made borders, even while carrying an enduring love for their homeland. We do visit Punjab regularly so our children remain deeply connected to the soil and spirit of their origin.Through this journey, I have come to realise that the Almighty blessed me to travel across the earth, carrying goodness, compassion, and positive change wherever I go. For the Punjabi diaspora, this spirit turns migration from a simple relocation into a purposeful responsibility.In a fast-paced world, pausing to reflect is a quiet act of empowerment — a reminder that wherever life takes us, every transition offers a wider lens through which to view our shared humanity.Deep Kamal, Saskatchewan (Canada)/MaloutTribuneindia.com invites contributions to SHAHARNAMA. Share anecdotes, unforgettable incidents, impressionable moments that define your cities, neighbourhoods, what the city stands for, what makes its people who they are. Send your contributions in English, not exceeding 450 words, to shaharnama@tribunemail.comDo include the name of your city and your social media handles (X/ Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn)

headline: Punjab no longer chases hollow promises, it chooses development: Mann tells 2 lakh in Moga
content: Moga, Nov 27: “Punjab no longer believes in empty promises. It chooses progress, development and prosperity.” With these words, CM Bhagwant Singh Mann addressed a record crowd of over 2 lakh at the ‘Khushhaal Punjab’ Maha Rally in Moga on Thursday, thanking people for what he called a historic endorsement of performance politics. In a post on X, Mann said the massive sea of humanity was proof that when people see zero electricity bills, 77,000 jobs without bribery, canal water at tail ends, ₹10 lakh health cover and dignity for mothers and daughters, they come forward on their own. At the rally, Mann presented his government’s report card and asked opposition parties to present theirs. “Those who ruled for decades must also tell people what they did,” he said. He said his government gave 77,182 jobs on merit. “Youth do not have to approach a minister or pay bribes. Earlier they had to leave Punjab and spend parents’ savings to go abroad. Now opportunities are being created here,” he said. He said 90% households now get zero bills, farmers get daytime power and canal water, and health cards have reached 54-55 lakh families.

headline: Beware of fake visa agents: Mohali admin warns job aspirants against social media offers
content: The district administration has advised Indian nationals, particularly those aspiring to travel abroad for employment or residency, to exercise utmost caution while dealing with visa and migration processing agencies.Referring to an advisory issued by the Embassy of India, Abu Dhabi, and the Consulate General of India, Dubai and Northern Emirates, District Magistrate Aaditya Dachalwal stated that complaints have been received from Indian nationals against certain visa and migration processing agencies operating outside India, including in the UAE. These agencies advertise third-country employment and residency visa services through social media platforms, collect fees from applicants and subsequently fail to provide the promised services or refund the money.The administration advised people not to rely solely on social media advertisements or blindly trust private visa processing agencies, particularly those operating outside India. Applicants have been urged to verify visa requirements, application procedures and authorised channels for obtaining employment or residency visas directly with the concerned embassy or consulate of the country they intend to visit, located in their country of residence.It was further emphasised that no agency can guarantee visa approval, as the decision to grant a visa rests solely with the government of the issuing country. Therefore, applicants should never pay any amount merely on the basis of promises of visa approval.The District Magistrate also advised prospective applicants to always consult the official government and embassy websites of the concerned country for accurate and updated visa-related information instead of relying on third-party sources.The public has been urged to remain vigilant and verify all relevant information through official channels before making any payment to visa or migration processing agencies.

headline: Is stubble burning in Punjab affecting Sri Lanka’s air quality?
content: In the months of October and November, farmers in Punjab and Haryana burn leftover rice stalks to clear their fields for wheat. The smoke chokes Delhi, but it does not stay there. In mid-November 2026, Sri Lanka’s Central Environmental Authority reported raised levels of fine dust (PM2.5 and PM10) across the Northern Province and in Anuradhapura, Puttalam, Trincomalee, Kurunegala and Colombo. It blamed much of this on winds blowing in from outside the island.

headline: 'Dead letter' comes alive 135 times; all govts used Article 356, highest under Indira Gandhi
content: New Delhi: B R Ambedkar hoped Article 356 would stay a "dead letter" but it was used 135 times since 1951 to dismiss State governments. The Congress has invoked it 90 times while in power with Indira Gandhi's dispensation alone accounting for 50 of these instances, according to an analysis..In an article published in newspapers on Thursday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, without naming the Congress, accused it of weakening the Constitution during its rule and said that repeated misuse of Article 356 to dismiss elected State governments presents another troubling chapter..The Modi government has also used Article 356 as many as 10 times..'Her strength lives on in women of my family': Rahul Gandhi hails Indira on birth anniversary.According to the government analysis, since 1950, President's Rule has been imposed about 135 times and the Congress governments account for around 90 of these cases, or two thirds of the total. The Indira Gandhi government alone accounts for 50..The Janata Party and other coalitions governments used Article 356 as many as on 28 occasions and BJP-led governments 17..During Jawaharlal Nehru's government, Article 356 was used eight times, including in Punjab (1951), PEPSU (1953), Andhra State (1954), Travancore-Cochin (1956), Kerala (1959), Odisha (1961), Goa (1964)..PEPSU (Patiala and East Punjab States Union) was an amalgamation of the pre-independence princely territories of Patiala, Jind, Nabha, Faridkot, Kapurthala, Kalsia, Malerkotla (Maler Kotla), and Nalagarh..During Nehru's tenure, when Article 356 was used in Kerala to dismiss EMS Namboodiripad's elected Communist government, it was widely criticised as the first major political use of the constitutional provision..During Lal Bahadur Shastri's government, it was used once — in Kerala (1964), after the ruling Congress lost its majority due to internal party splits..Indira Gandhi used Article 356 a total of 50 times — Haryana (1967), West Bengal (1968, 1970, 1971), Tamil Nadu (1976), Gujarat (1976) and nine Opposition states in 1980..She often used the provision to dismiss non-Congress governments, notably Tamil Nadu (1976) during the Emergency despite DMK's majority and nine states in February 1980 (UP, Bihar, Rajasthan, MP, Punjab, Odisha, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu) upon returning to power following the general elections, the analysis said..Late prime minister Moraraji Desai used the provision 16 times — first nine Congress-ruled states Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal after the Janata Party's Lok Sabha victory, arguing they had lost the public mandate..The Desai government also dismissed seven more state governments, including Karnataka, Manipur, Tripura, Mizoram, Puducherry in 1978..Late prime minister Charan Singh used Article 356 four times — Sikkim (1979), Manipur (1979), Kerala (1979), Assam (1979) — triggered by shifting coalition loyalties, defections, and the onset of the Assam Agitation..Rajiv Gandhi used the provision six times — Punjab (1987), Tamil Nadu (1988), Nagaland (1988), Mizoram (1988), Karnataka (1989)..When the S R Bommai's Janata Dal government in Karnataka was dismissed in 1989 it was later struck down by the Supreme Court in a landmark ruling..Government appeals to MPs to ensure smooth special sitting of Parliament.During V P Singh's regime, the Article 356 was used twice — Jammu and Kashmir in 1990, and Karnataka (1990). Jammu and Kashmir was placed under central rule due to escalating militancy while Karnataka saw a brief spell amid Congress internal turmoil..The provision was used five occasions when Chandra Shekhar was the prime minister — Assam (1990), Goa (1990), Tamil Nadu (1991), Haryana (1991), Puducherry (1991)..Tamil Nadu's (1991) M Karunanidhi-led DMK government was dismissed over alleged LTTE links despite holding a clear Assembly majority..When PV Narasimha Rao was the prime minister, Article 356 was used 12 times, including Nagaland (1992), Manipur (1993), Bihar (1995), UP (1995)..Rao also dismissed four BJP-led State governments following the Babri Masjid demolition Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh in 1992..During H D Deve Gowda's tenure, the provision was used only once in Uttar Pradesh in 1996 following a hung Assembly after the Assembly elections..During Atal Bihari Vajpayee's tenure as prime minister, Article 356 was used six times, including Goa (1999), Manipur (2001), Uttar Pradesh (2002), J&K (2002)..Vajpayee dismissed Rabri Devi's RJD government in Bihar in 1999 citing law-and-order collapse, but revoked it within 26 days after facing defeat in the Rajya Sabha..The Manmohan Singh government used the provision on 13 occasions, including in Karnataka (Twice in 2007), J&K (2008), Jharkhand (2009, 2010, 2013), Delhi (2014; Article 239AB instead of Article 356) and Andhra Pradesh (2014)..The Congress-led UPA also dissolved the hung Assembly in Bihar allegedly to prevent the NDA from staking a claim. The Supreme Court later declared the dissolution unconstitutional..The same government also dismissed the Manohar Parrikar government in Goa in 2005..The Modi government has used Article 356 as many as 10 times, including in Maharashtra twice (2014, 2019), Arunachal Pradesh (2016), Uttarakhand (2016), J&K (2015, June 2018, Dec 2018, 2019 UT), Puducherry (2021), Manipur (2025)..Article 356 was used in Maharashtra due to political instability, in Arunachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand after the respective government faced party rebellions. In Manipur, the provision was used after the then chief minister N Biren Singh's resignation following ethnic conflict.

headline: 3 crushed under overloaded truck in Ropar identified as Delhi residents
content: The driver of the multi-axle truck that overturned onto a car near Bharatgarh on the Ropar-Manali National Highway, killing three Delhi residents, has been arrested.The deceased have been identified as Vaibhav, Amaritanshu Gupta (29) and Gaurav Gaur (28), all residents of Delhi.The truck driver, identified as Parwinder Singh alias Bareta, a resident of Dhobiana Road, Preet Nagar, Bathinda, is in police custody.SSP Ropar Maninder Singh said the truck driver had fled the accident spot after the mishap but was subsequently arrested by the police.The three victims were travelling in a Maruti Baleno (DL 3CC-X-4582), which was crushed under the overloaded multi-axle truck (PB 03 BL-2107) carrying washed sand. Vaibhav was the resident of Block B, Sant Nagar, Burari, North Delhi. Amaritanshu Gupta lived at SFS DDA Flats, Gulmohar Enclave, South Delhi, while Gaurav Gaur was a resident of 43-D, Pocket A-I, Tiranga Enclave, Delhi.The truck allegedly went out of control and hit around eight vehicles before overturning onto the Baleno, crushing all three occupants to death on the spot. A newlywed couple travelling in another car had a narrow escape after their vehicle was engulfed by gravel spilling from the overturned truck.The accident triggered a massive traffic jam on the busy highway, leaving thousands of commuters stranded for several hours. Even ambulances travelling towards Chandigarh from different parts of Ropar district and neighbouring Himachal Pradesh reportedly remained stuck in the congestion.The tragedy has once again exposed the growing risk of accidents on the Bharatgarh-Sirsa Nangal stretch of the Ropar-Manali National Highway, where sharp curves, high-speed traffic and poorly managed road cuts have made driving increasingly hazardous.Sources said nearly 80 per cent of the FIRs registered at Kiratpur Sahib police station, under whose jurisdiction the stretch falls, pertain to road accidents. Despite repeated mishaps, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has allegedly failed to take effective measures to eliminate identified accident-prone spots and improve road safety.The accident has also raised serious questions about the enforcement of traffic regulations in the district. Police officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Ropar district had only nine traffic police personnel to manage its entire road network.The district police force was also reportedly functioning with barely 40 per cent of its sanctioned strength, making effective traffic regulation a major challenge.The unchecked movement of overloaded trucks and tippers carrying mined material has emerged as another major concern. Several such vehicles allegedly operate without number plates, while in other cases, registration numbers are deliberately covered with mud to evade enforcement agencies.The latest accident has intensified criticism of the state government's failure to curb overloading and the illegal transportation of mined material.Under existing provisions, police and Mining Department officials can impose fines of up to Rs 2 lakh on overloaded vehicles. However, the continued movement of such trucks has raised questions about the effectiveness of enforcement.The deaths of three young Delhi residents have once again highlighted the urgent need for highway safety audits, the removal of accident black spots, adequate deployment of traffic personnel and strict action against overloaded vehicles.

headline: Civilian injured in exchange of fire between police, suspects in Punjab’s Hoshiarpur
content: A civilian was injured in an exchange of fire between a Crime Investigation Agency (CIA) team of Hoshiarpur police and suspected criminals at Balagan Chowk in Dasuya on Friday. Police apprehended one accused, but another managed to escape, police said.The injured person, Mohammad Rafi (30), sustained a bullet injury in his arm while he was at his dry-cleaning shop near the chowk. He was admitted to the Civil Hospital in Dasuya and is stated to be out of danger, police said.Deputy Superintendent of Police (Detective) Parneet Singh said the CIA Hoshiarpur team had proceeded to the Dasuya area to apprehend suspects in connection with a firing incident for which an FIR was registered at Garhdiwala police station on November 15.Acting on leads developed during the investigation, the police team spotted the suspects' vehicle near Balagan Chowk. The occupants allegedly attempted to flee, ramming their vehicle into the CIA team's vehicle and damaging several other vehicles amid traffic, he said.The suspects also opened fire at the police party, prompting the personnel to retaliate, Singh said, adding that one accused was apprehended along with the suspected vehicle, while the other managed to escape.A hunt to nab the absconding accused is underway, police said.

headline: Ajnala sparks first SAD-BJP seat-sharing tussle as Bony stakes claim against Samra
content: Even as the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and BJP are yet to decide on seat-sharing after their alliance, the two parties could face their first test over the Ajnala seat, with BJP leader Amarpal Singh Bony Ajnala on Friday staking his claim to it.He said the party high command had called him and sought his views on contesting the poll from Ajnala. He said he had expressed his willingness to contest.His claim comes at a time when SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal has already announced Jodh Singh Samra as the party’s candidate during a Punjab Bachao rally at Ugar Aulakh village in September. Earlier, SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia had also publicly backed Samra’s candidature.Nevertheless, former MLA Bony Ajnala staking claim to the same seat on the BJP ticket has brought the question of seat-sharing between the two parties into focus.Bony, who recently met senior party leaders, including Union Home Minister Amit Shah, said he had conveyed his willingness to contest from Ajnala and was confident of winning the constituency if given an opportunity.“I have been active in politics for 21 years, while my family has been associated with active politics for 45 years. Ajnala is my ‘Janmabhoomi’ as well as my ‘Karmabhoomi’. If the party gives me an opportunity to serve, I will win the seat for it,” he said.Ajnala has traditionally remained an Akali stronghold and was contested by SAD in the 2007, 2012, 2017 and 2022 Assembly election. Bony himself had represented the constituency as an SAD MLA. His claim on the BJP ticket could, therefore, complicate negotiations if the two parties decide to contest the elections together.Maintaining that no final decision on seat-sharing or ticket allocation had been taken, Bony said BJP’s central leadership would take a call after consultations with senior leaders of both parties, including Sukhbir Singh Badal and Amit Shah.He also cautioned party workers against believing claims that tickets had already been allotted, saying the high command would consider the winnability of candidates before taking a decision.Making a pitch for his candidature, Bony said he had deep roots in the constituency and questioned the rationale of imposing an outsider when local leaders were available. He said Ajnala needed a representative who had a direct connection with its people and ground realities.He also advocated a BJP-led government in Punjab, claiming that it could address issues concerning farmers, employees, drug abuse, law and order, the release of Bandi Singhs and the welfare of weaker sections.“The people of Punjab want peace, communal harmony and prosperity. BJP can deliver on these issues,” he said.

headline: Mann pitches AAP’s Punjab record at Moga rally ahead of 2027 polls
content: Punjab has put its record on jobs, electricity, irrigation and healthcare at the centre of its political pitch ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann addressed the Aam Aadmi Party’s ‘Khushhaal Punjab’ rally in Moga, where the party claimed two lakh people had gathered. Mann called the turnout support for “Kaam Di Rajneeti” and said voters should judge governments by delivery. Mann said his government was presenting its report card to the public and challenged parties that had governed Punjab for decades to explain their record. He accused the Congress, Shiromani Akali Dal and BJP of making promises but failing to resolve the state’s problems. Jobs, power and healthcare The chief minister said the government had provided 77,182 government jobs through merit-based and transparent recruitment, without bribes. He said nearly 90% of households in Punjab were receiving zero electricity bills. Farmers, he added, were now getting daytime power, allowing them to visit fields in the morning and switch off their motors by evening instead of working at night. Mann also said canal water was reaching areas that had gone without supplies for years, including the tail ends of canals in Moga. He said the effort was intended to ensure farmers received their rightful share of water and reduce pressure on groundwater. On healthcare, Mann said eligible families could receive treatment worth up to ₹10 lakh under the state’s health insurance scheme. He put the number of eligible families at around 65 lakh and said 54-55 lakh health cards had been issued. He also claimed that approximately 50,000 stent procedures and 35,000 knee replacement procedures had been carried out under the scheme. Opposition and election pitch Mann accused the Congress, Akali Dal and BJP of taking turns in power without addressing Punjab’s problems. He alleged that the parties were now coming together because they were concerned about AAP’s work. Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s proposed December 8 rally at the same Moga ground, he questioned what the leaders expected to share the platform had done for Punjab. He also accused the Akali Dal of compromising farmers’ trust by joining hands with the BJP for a ministerial position. Mann said voters would give the opposition an answer in 2027 and urged them not to let political parties influence their votes with money. AAP Punjab president Aman Arora said traditional parties had betrayed public trust. Senior party leader Manish Sisodia highlighted the government’s claims on public schools, clinics, health insurance and welfare schemes. Sisodia said Aam Aadmi Clinics treated around 90,000 people daily and cited free medicines, tests and consultations across the state.

headline: Kejriwal makes welfare continuity central to AAP’s Punjab poll pitch
content: Arvind Kejriwal’s appeal to Punjab women to mobilise male relatives behind the Aam Aadmi Party put welfare spending at the centre of its 2027 election pitch. Addressing an AAP Foundation Day rally in Moga, the party’s AAP national convenor said the Mawan-Dheeyan Satkar Yojana, free electricity, health insurance and pilgrimage programmes would remain in place if Bhagwant Mann returned as Chief Minister. Kejriwal said the monthly payment to women was intended to provide relief from inflation, which he blamed on the Centre. Under the scheme, women receive ₹1,000 a month, while Scheduled Caste beneficiaries receive ₹1,500. Payments are credited quarterly, at ₹3,000 and ₹4,500, respectively. He said beneficiaries who registered earlier received payments first and pending eligible beneficiaries would receive their dues on December 1. Payments would then be made quarterly. Kejriwal acknowledged that the scheme had started later than promised, attributing the delay to the state treasury being depleted by previous governments. Funding and implementation The AAP convenor said his government took four years to replenish Punjab’s finances by saving public money. He alleged that the Centre withheld funds and tried to prevent the women’s scheme from being implemented, adding that the state had approached the court. He presented the scheme alongside initiatives that he said fulfilled the party’s 2022 election guarantees: free electricity, pilgrimage travel, mohalla clinics, ₹10 lakh health insurance and improvements to government schools. He acknowledged that some schools still required improvement and said the government would work on them over the next five years if re-elected. Kejriwal also claimed that the Mann government had provided more than 70,000 government jobs without bribery and that recruitment was based on merit. He cited canal water reaching fields and daytime electricity for irrigation as benefits for farmers and households throughout rural Punjab as well. Opposition and policy continuity The AAP leader warned that the Congress, Akali Dal and BJP would discontinue the Mawan-Dheeyan scheme and free electricity if they formed the government. He cited a senior Congress leader’s criticism of the scheme as a burden on the exchequer. He alleged that the BJP government in Delhi had shut down AAP-era mohalla clinics, free medicines and pilgrimage facilities, and was preparing to end free electricity. Kejriwal framed the 2027 contest as a choice over whether existing benefits would continue. He urged women to ask husbands, sons and other male relatives to vote for AAP, arguing that free power, health cover, agricultural electricity and household assistance benefited entire families. He said another AAP government would continue existing schemes and said they depended on Mann’s return.

headline: Surplus Treasury Claims Meet Debt Reality As AAP Launches Punjab Campaign
content: Arvind Kejriwal told a Moga rally that the AAP government spent four years filling Punjab's "sarkari khajana". The fiscal record points the other way. Between March 2022 and March 2026, the state's net outstanding debt rose by approximately Rs 1.35 lakh crore, from Rs 2.73 lakh crore when AAP took office to roughly Rs 4.08 lakh crore by the end of FY 2025-26. Gross borrowings look larger still because budget documents include short-term Ways and Means Advances from the RBI and rollover repayments. The treasury was not filled. It was leveraged. A ruling party that funds its doles with fresh loans and then presents the arrangement as a filled treasury is not merely campaigning. It is asking voters to treat borrowed money as earned surplus. On its foundation day, the AAP government chose this path: protect an inflated image of plenty, keep the monthly transfers flowing, and leave the rising interest burden for later. Whether that bargain produces a khushhaal Punjab or simply postpones a darker reckoning is no longer a question of accounting. It is a question the electorate will answer when it decides if the immediate gain is worth the deferred cost. Economists say freebies retain electoral pull because most voters experience them as immediate cash or free power, not as entries in the state budget. Delayed salaries and unpaid arrears affect a limited set of government employees; the wider electorate sees the monthly transfer or the zero electricity bill. AAP's promise to continue these schemes therefore converts fiscal strain into a simple choice: keep the benefit or risk losing it. With interest payments already taking 17.2 per cent of expenditure and new women's cash transfers budgeted at Rs 9,300 crore, committed liabilities crowd out capital spending. The political calculation is that short-term household relief will outweigh long-term development shortfalls at the ballot box. Welfare and subsidy bills explain much of the rise. The power subsidy stood at roughly Rs 19,657 crore in FY 2025-26 and is budgeted above Rs 20,000 crore for FY 2026-27. Over four years the cumulative power outlay reached Rs 76,000-Rs 78,000 crore. Free agricultural tubewell electricity accounted for about Rs 10,413 crore a year. The 300-unit free domestic power scheme, covering nearly 90 per cent of households, cost Rs 6,859-Rs 7,614 crore annually. Industrial concessions added another Rs 2,384 crore. Social security pensions for 33-35 lakh beneficiaries formed the second-largest recurring outflow at Rs 6,132 crore a year, or Rs 23,500-Rs 24,000 crore over four years. Subsidised ration and nutrition kits cost Rs 800-Rs 900 crore annually. Zero-ticket bus travel for women cost the exchequer Rs 2,042 crore across the term. Cashless healthcare top-ups and Aam Aadmi Clinics absorbed Rs 1,046 crore in FY 2025-26 and Rs 3,500-Rs 4,000 crore over four years, rising to Rs 2,000 crore in FY 2026-27. The Mukh Mantri Maavan Dheeyan Satkar Yojana, offering Rs 1,000 a month to women and Rs 1,500 to Scheduled Caste women, was budgeted at Rs 9,300 crore from FY 2026-27 after remaining unlaunched through the first four years. Comparisons with earlier governments sharpen the picture. AAP's four-year net addition of roughly Rs 1.35 lakh crore already exceeds the approximately Rs 1.31 lakh crore added across the full ten-year SAD-BJP term from 2007 to 2017. Stripping out the one-off UDAY power-bond takeover of about Rs 15,628 crore brings the SAD-BJP ten-year figure down to roughly Rs 87,000 crore. Against that adjusted total, AAP's four-year borrowing is higher by about Rs 48,000 crore. Projected forward to the FY 2026-27 Budget Estimate of Rs 4.47 lakh crore, AAP's five-year net addition reaches Rs 1.65-Rs 1.74 lakh crore. Congress added roughly Rs 91,000-Rs 1 lakh crore over its five years from 2017 to 2022. The annual pace under AAP averages about Rs 33,750 crore, compared with Rs 18,200-Rs 20,000 crore under Congress and Rs 13,100 crore under SAD-BJP (or Rs 8,700 crore excluding UDAY).

headline: The importance of Moga: Why all parties choose it as their poll campaign launchpad
content: Chandigarh: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) launched its campaign for next year’s Punjab assembly elections with a big show of strength rally in Moga on Thursday. Organised officially by the Punjab government as a smart card distribution ceremony, the ‘Khushhaal Punjab Maha Rally’ as it was christened, turned into the formal launch of the ruling party’s campaign. Moga has also been chosen by the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) combine for its first joint rally on 8 December that will be addressed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Union Home Minister Amit Shah had virtually kickstarted the BJP’s campaign from Moga in March. But why Moga? What is it about this city, 170 km west of Chandigarh, that every party seeks to make it a launchpad for the assembly elections? Moga is considered the epicentre of Malwa, the region that accounts for 69 of Punjab’s 117 assembly constituencies. Over the years, it has emerged as a preferred spot for political parties seeking to make statewide political and electoral statements. Its location, though central to Malwa, connects it closely to the two other regions of Punjab—Majha and Doaba. With Jalandhar only 80 km away and Amritsar a little over 100, Moga is a convenient mobilisation point for political parties.

headline: Ludhiana Sports Park Faces Criticism Over Proximity to Garbage Dump
content: Ludhiana: A recently inaugurated sports park in Ludhiana, developed at a cost of over Rs 91 lakh, is drawing criticism due to the unhygienic conditions surrounding it, primarily stemming from an adjacent garbage dump. The accumulated waste is emitting a foul odour, causing concern among visitors about health hazards and detracting from the facility's intended purpose of promoting sports and recreation.Information was available with The Chenab Times that the mini sports park, situated behind the Civil Hospital and within the Ludhiana Central Assembly constituency, was established on a parcel of land previously notorious for anti-social activities. This site, which once housed the city's former jail, had served as a dumping ground for waste for more than a decade before its transformation into a sports facility a few months prior. The park offers amenities for basketball, volleyball, pickleball, and box cricket, and its development was initially met with appreciation from residents who had long awaited proper sports infrastructure in the area.However, the continued presence of a static compactor adjacent to the park, which receives substantial amounts of garbage daily, has rendered the surroundings unpleasant for those seeking to utilize the facility. Residents have voiced their concerns over the prevailing conditions.Vishal Kumar, a resident residing on Civil Hospital Road, stated that he regularly visits the park with his children for morning and evening activities, as there are limited alternative sports facilities in the vicinity. He highlighted that the garbage collected in the static compactor makes it difficult for visitors to enjoy the park. Kumar noted that the compactor receives tonnes of waste daily, leading to a strong stench from the heaps of refuse, which complicates playing in such an environment. He suggested that the static compactor should be relocated to prevent potential diseases among park visitors.Senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Parveen Bansal also inspected the site and drew attention to the deteriorating condition of the facility. He alleged that the polluted surroundings pose a significant health risk, particularly to children and the elderly. Pointing to the piles of waste lying next to the sports ground, Bansal questioned the rationale behind developing a recreational area in such an environment. He remarked that a sports park, intended for children and elders to visit for physical activities, is instead exposing them to unsanitary conditions. He further questioned the planning, suggesting that those responsible for the development work should reconsider the chosen location.Bansal critically questioned the concept of developing a sports facility adjacent to a garbage dump, stating that it contradicts the objective of promoting health and well-being. He expressed doubt about the vision of the authorities who allocated funds for the park's development, suggesting that an alternative location would have prevented visitors from enduring a foul-smelling environment during their recreational visits.He appealed to the concerned authorities to prioritize better planning and ensure adequate sanitation around public spaces, especially those designated for sports and recreation, to prevent unhygienic conditions from undermining their intended purpose.For regular users of the park, the issue has also brought to the fore ongoing concerns about the maintenance of newly developed public facilities. Residents feel that the proximity of a garbage collection point to a sports ground negates efforts to encourage young people to engage in outdoor activities. They indicated that the pervasive foul smell and accumulating waste discourage families from spending time at the park and urged for the relocation of the static compactor to a more appropriate site.The situation also brings into focus persistent complaints regarding garbage accumulation near parks and other public areas across the city. Residents and elected representatives have consistently raised concerns about the detrimental impact of such unhygienic conditions on public health.

headline: Punjab Govt Funds Ludhiana Vet University Startup
content: Herbspark Nutraceuticals Pvt Ltd, a startup incubated and supported by the Veterinary and Livestock Innovation and Incubation Foundation (VLIIF) of Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal Sciences University, has received Rs 3 lakh in seed funding from the Punjab Government. The funding is part of the state's Industrial and Business Development Policy-2022.Information was available with The Chenab Times that the grant aims to bolster entrepreneurial ventures within the state's agricultural and veterinary sectors.The Vice-Chancellor of the university, Dr JPS Gill, extended his congratulations to the startup. He acknowledged the efforts of VLIIF in fostering entrepreneurship through financial support, mentorship, and institutional backing. Dr Gill reaffirmed the university's dedication to promoting innovation, encouraging new businesses, and facilitating the commercialisation of research-driven technologies.Dr RS Sethi, the Director of VLIIF and Dean of the College of Animal Biotechnology, stated that the foundation had previously provided an initial grant of Rs 4 lakh to Herbspark Nutraceuticals. This earlier funding was instrumental in supporting the startup's initial entrepreneurial activities and business development phases.Dr Sethi further elaborated that the newly secured seed funding acknowledges the significant potential of Herbspark Nutraceuticals. The additional financial assistance is expected to play a crucial role in accelerating the startup's growth trajectory and expanding its operational capacity. The initiative underscores the Punjab Government's commitment to nurturing a vibrant startup ecosystem, particularly within specialised fields like veterinary sciences and nutraceuticals.The Veterinary and Livestock Innovation and Incubation Foundation, established under Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal Sciences University, serves as a crucial platform for translating scientific research into viable commercial products and services. Its incubation programs provide aspiring entrepreneurs with the necessary resources, guidance, and infrastructure to develop and scale their innovative ideas.The Industrial and Business Development Policy-2022 of Punjab aims to create a conducive environment for industrial growth and business expansion by offering various incentives and support mechanisms to eligible enterprises. The inclusion of seed funding for innovative startups like Herbspark Nutraceuticals highlights the policy's focus on fostering a new generation of businesses driven by technology and research.Herbspark Nutraceuticals is anticipated to leverage this funding to advance its product development, enhance its market reach, and contribute to the economic development of Ludhiana and the wider Punjab region. The success of such startups is vital for diversifying the state's economy and creating high-value employment opportunities.The veterinary university has been actively involved in promoting applied research and encouraging its faculty and students to pursue entrepreneurial ventures. This focus on innovation is crucial for addressing contemporary challenges in animal health, livestock management, and food safety, while also contributing to the broader goals of sustainable agriculture and rural development.The seed funding represents a significant milestone for Herbspark Nutraceuticals, validating its business model and the potential impact of its proposed nutraceutical products. The collaboration between academic institutions, government bodies, and private enterprises is seen as a key driver for innovation and economic progress in Punjab.

headline: Youth Killed in Ludhiana; Friend Critical, Police Probe Threats
content: A young man has died in Ludhiana, Punjab, after being attacked with sharp weapons, while his friend remains in critical condition. The incident, which occurred in the Bindra Colony area of Daresi on Thursday night, has prompted a police investigation into prior threats allegedly made against the deceased. Information was available with The Chenab Times that the attack took place late Thursday night. Residents of the neighbourhood reported hearing a commotion and discovering two youths lying on the street, bleeding profusely. Alerted by the disturbance, neighbours rushed the injured individuals to CMC Hospital. Medical personnel at the hospital pronounced Honey Bansal deceased, while his companion, Pawan, continues to receive intensive care for his severe injuries. Eyewitness accounts suggest that a group of six to seven assailants were involved in the attack. Naginder, a local resident, stated that the incident occurred while many in the area were asleep. Upon investigating the noise, residents saw several individuals fleeing the scene after assaulting the two youths. Further details indicate that Honey Bansal may have been targeted due to a long-standing rivalry. Rakesh Kumar, another resident, claimed that Bansal had received explicit threats of death earlier on the same day as the attack. These threats were reportedly disseminated through social media groups, signaling a premeditated motive for the assault. The police have begun their investigation into the matter and have identified several suspects in connection with the stabbing. The individuals named by preliminary police sources include Rahul, also known as Golu; Prince, alias Lalla; Daljit; Gaurav; and Manjit Mani, along with other unnamed accomplices. ASI Sukhwinder, along with other police personnel, visited the crime scene to gather evidence and assess the situation. Following initial inquiries and the inspection of the site, the Daresi police station has reportedly detained some suspects in connection with the fatal attack. The investigation is ongoing as authorities work to apprehend all individuals involved and establish the full sequence of events leading to the violence. The incident has sent shockwaves through the local community, highlighting concerns about the prevalence of targeted violence and the use of social media for issuing threats. Police are reportedly working to trace the origin of the social media messages and gather further evidence to build a strong case against the perpetrators.

headline: BJP accepted ‘younger brother’ role in SAD reunion to save Punjab: Dhillon
content: Chandigarh: Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon on Thursday defended the party’s decision to play the role of a “younger brother” in its alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), saying the tie-up was aimed at rescuing Punjab from administrative, economic and social decline rather than pursuing power.“When a national party governing 22 states and forming the Union govt for a third consecutive term willingly steps into the role of a younger brother in Punjab, it makes it abundantly clear that its foremost priority is saving the state,” Dhillon said in a statement, describing the alliance as a commitment to “Punjab First”.He said Punjab was grappling with drugs, gangsterism, corruption and deteriorating law and order, with drug abuse putting the future of its youth at risk, weakening the workforce and pushing families into financial distress and migration.Dhillon said an NDA govt in Punjab would provide MSP on 25 crops and vegetables on the Haryana model and implement central schemes to upgrade rural roads and village infrastructure.He also flagged pending dearness allowance dues of govt employees, estimated at Rs 15,000-20,000 crore, alleging these remained unpaid despite high court orders. He said central support would be needed to clear the dues.On the business front, he promised to end alleged harassment of traders over state GST demands, release stalled refunds and restore a secure environment for traders and industrialists. Dhillon said the BJP-SAD alliance was aimed at safeguarding the future of Punjab’s youth, farmers, traders and industrialists.

headline: INLD leader alleges Haryana universities saddled with ₹16,052 crore debt
content: GURUGRAM: Former Haryana Cabinet Minister and Indian National Lok Dal national patron Sampat Singh has accused the State government of pushing 22 public universities into a debt burden of ₹16,052 crore over the past four years by converting grants-in-aid into perpetual loans. In a press statement, Mr. Singh termed the move a calculated withdrawal from public higher education and warned that the growing financial liabilities could pave the way for the commercialisation, closure or privatisation of public universities. He said the government had initially replaced grants with loans through an order issued on April 29, 2022, but withdrew a month later following protests. However, he alleged that the rollback was merely an “eyewash”, as the government released grants for only two quarters in 2022-23 and subsequently continued funding universities under alternative heads such as non-recurring expenditure. Under different head The funds, he alleged, were being booked under Budget Head 6202 (Loans for Education, Sports, Art and Culture) instead of Head 2202 (Grants for Education), effectively turning government assistance into liabilities for the universities. Mr. Singh told The Hindu that the government was creating a loan liability on paper so that, eventually, they could say that the universities had accumulated such huge debts and could no longer be run. “Gradually, they could wind them up or shut them down. That is precisely the intention. ‘It is a perpetual loan. We do not want to take it back,’ they say. If you are not going to recover the money, why call it a loan? Give it as a grant instead. Why change the budget head?” said Mr. Singh. ‘Would affect EWS students’ He said the policy would disproportionately affect students from middle-class and economically weaker sections who depend on affordable public education. Mr. Singh said the universities had been asked to mobilise their own resources through alumni contributions, Corporate Social Responsibility funds, patents and commercial utilisation of surplus land to meet their academic and operational expenses. ‘56.5% vacancies’ The financial squeeze had also affected staffing, he said, pointing out that only 2,733 of the 6,290 sanctioned regular teaching positions across the universities were filled, leaving 3,557 vacancies. This meant that nearly 56.5% of the sanctioned teaching posts were vacant. He further flagged a government directive issued on August 17 stipulating that newly created posts remaining vacant for four years from the date of Finance Department approval would be deemed abolished. He demanded that the State government restore full grant-in-aid under Budget Head 2202, stop converting grants into loans, waive the existing liabilities of universities and release adequate funds to fill vacant teaching and non-teaching posts. “There are two universities where the situation is particularly bad -- Sports University, Rai, and Sanskrit University in Kaithal. They have barely five to seven regular teaching staff members. The rest are part-time or engaged through other arrangements,” said Mr. Singh. (EOM)

headline: Waste piles up across Haryana's Faridabad after HC order shuts Aravalli dumping site
content: NEW DELHI: Faridabad is facing an acute waste disposal crisis after the dumping site at ecologically sensitive Bhakri village was shut down following a Punjab and Haryana High Court order, even as municipal officials claim to have identified alternative sites for disposing of the city’s unsegregated waste.With waste piling up along roadsides in several parts of the city, residents have complained of foul smells and deteriorating sanitation. The problem has been reported in residential neighbourhoods as well as industrial areas, including NIT, Mewala and Sectors 24, 28, 31, 32, 59, 66-69 and 74.Ravinder Bhatti, a social media influencer and resident of NIT Market 5, said municipal waste was lying along roads at several locations in the area despite protests by residents. He said they had repeatedly brought the matter to the authorities’ attention, but their concerns remained unaddressed.Another resident said sanitation was poor even in what is considered one of the city’s posh localities.The situation is reportedly worse in industrial areas, with huge piles of waste lying behind the Faridabad railway station. Residents of Mewala told the TNIE that garbage accumulating at several locations, including near the underpass, had caused a persistent stench.Madan Kumar, a resident of the area, said the smell from household waste, coupled with toxic air, had made it difficult for people to step out for morning walks. Sector 28, adjacent to Mewala, is facing similar problems, while heaps of residential and industrial waste have also been found along roadsides in Sector 24.Faridabad Municipal Corporation (MCF) officials, however, said the civic body would continue dumping fresh waste at the Mirzapur site until the processing capacity of the Pratapgarh waste management facility was increased from 200 tonnes to 650 tonnes a day.The city generates around 1,200 tonnes of solid waste daily. However, the two existing waste disposal facilities have a combined capacity of handling only 300 tonnes a day, with each processing 150 tonnes, leaving a substantial gap between waste generation and processing capacity..Environment activists have questioned the civic body’s continued reliance on dumping unsegregated waste, arguing that the practice violates the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, which mandate segregation at source and scientific management of municipal waste.Ranbir Singh, joint commissioner of the MCF’s NIT zone, said the civic body had not faced any problems with waste disposal so far. “Sanitation work in the city is going on as usual, and we have identified some places, including the Pratapgarh waste management facility, for disposing of the waste. We have stopped dumping waste at Bhakri village following the High Court’s orders,” he said.Satish Kumar Phagna, MLA from Faridabad NIT (Assembly Constituency No. 86), said the authorities were setting up processing plants to reduce pressure on dumping grounds. Ten new waste processing units would come up at various locations in the city, he said, without specifying where they would be located.Haryana Urban Local Bodies Minister Vipul Goel said he was unaware of the waste lying on roadsides. “I am not aware of this. I will enquire about it and ask the authorities to take appropriate action,” he said.Earlier, environmentalists and villagers had protested against the dumping of municipal waste on Aravalli land near Bhakri village, demanding proper segregation and disposal.Acting on a complaint filed by Anil Arora of the Save Aravallis Trust, the Punjab and Haryana High Court on November 5, 2026, directed the Haryana government to stop further dumping of waste on 152 acres of ecologically sensitive Aravalli land near Bhakri village along the Gurugram-Faridabad Road. The order followed nearly a month of protests by local residents against the alleged dumping of municipal and industrial waste by the MCF.The National Green Tribunal had earlier taken suo motu cognisance of reports about municipal waste being dumped in the Aravalli hills and forest area near Bhankri village in Faridabad and sought responses from government agencies..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Airline cancels Delhi-Bengaluru flight; passenger spends ₹48,719 on new ticket, court orders ₹66,491 compensation
content: A West Bengal Consumer Commission has directed an airline to pay ₹56,491.78, along with 9% annual interest, to a passenger after cancelling her Delhi-Bengaluru flight without providing an adequate explanation for the decision. The passenger had to arrange another flight at a higher cost and spend two days at a hotel in Gurugram. The commission also ordered the airline to pay ₹10,000 towards litigation expenses, according to a report by Indian Express. The bench, comprising President Shivarama K and members Suma Anil Kumar and Rekha Sayannavar, held that the airline could not avoid responsibility as it had failed to explain the operational difficulties that led to the cancellation. Observing that “the unforeseen operational exigencies have not been explained”, the commission concluded that the airline was guilty of deficiency in service. In its November 19 order, the commission said, “It is not explained as to what kind of unforeseen operational exigencies it has faced. Therefore, mere saying that, because of unforeseen operational exigencies, it has affected the travel and theflight did not take off is not sufficient”. Why did the passenger approach the consumer commission? According to the complaint, the passenger booked a Delhi-Bengaluru flight on November 4, 2025, for travel on December 5, paying ₹7,497 for the ticket, Indian Express reported. The complainant asserted that the flight was cancelled without prior notice or alternative arrangements. She also claimed that the crew did not provide any assistance to help her reach her destination by another mode of transport. The cancellation disrupted her doctor's appointment and also resulted in a financial loss of ₹50,000. She also had to stay in Gurugram, Haryana, for two days before undertaking her return journey. The passenger said she stayed at a hotel from December 5 to December 6 and paid ₹15,269 for the accommodation. She later booked another flight for December 7, 2025, and paid ₹48,719 for the replacement ticket.After incurring these losses, she approached the consumer commission seeking compensation. Airline responds The airline claimed that the flight was cancelled on December 5, 2025, due to operational reasons and that the passengers had been informed immediately. It further alleged that the passenger had refused to travel on the alternative flight offered by the airline and that the full ticket amount had been refunded, the report added.The airline also argued that the circumstances leading to the cancellation were unforeseen and beyond its control.What did the consumer commission order?The commission observed that the passenger's flight ticket showed that she had travelled on another flight on December 7, 2025. It also noted that the hotel invoice submitted by her covered accommodation expenses alone.After examining the documents, the bench held that she was entitled to reimbursement of the additional expenses incurred because of the cancellation.

headline: Haryana clears Rs 455-crore 6-lane elevated corridor to ease Gurugram traffic
content: In a major move to ease traffic congestion in Gurugram, the Haryana Government has approved a Rs 455.22-crore six-lane elevated corridor that will also improve connectivity towards Jhajjar and the Kundli-Manesar-Palwal (KMP) Expressway.The 2.24-km corridor will be constructed along National Highway-352W, between Hero Honda Chowk and Umang Bhardwaj Chowk. It is expected to provide a crucial connectivity link and ease congestion along the stretch.The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) will execute the long-pending project as a deposit work of the Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority (GMDA).The approval follows GMDA’s resubmission of a revised proposal to the state government. According to the authority, its Chief Executive Officer, Dushmant Kumar Behera, IAS, reviewed the project after taking charge and pursued the matter on priority.Earlier, on October 1, it was reported that the government had entrusted the project to GMDA, which was to prepare a fresh detailed project report.Following a detailed examination with the engineering officers concerned, GMDA recommended that the elevated corridor be developed and executed by NHAI. The proposal has now been approved in accordance with the decision taken in this regard.The corridor will help segregate local and through traffic, increase road capacity and facilitate smoother movement towards Jhajjar and the KMP Expressway.The stretch is significant for Gurugram’s road network as it connects a key junction on the Delhi-Jaipur highway with the road towards Jhajjar. Daily commuters as well as through traffic are expected to benefit once the corridor is completed.GMDA has already spent around Rs 116.55 crore on land acquisition and the shifting of utilities for the project.Behera said the approval marked a significant step towards implementing the crucial infrastructure project. He said it would strengthen Gurugram’s road network and improve convenience for commuters.The official statement did not specify when tenders would be floated, when construction would begin or the deadline for completing the corridor.

headline: Haryana CM Saini to take education pitch to Oxford, Cambridge & a Barnet school on UK-Germany tour
content: Chandigarh: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini will spend part of next week sitting down with Indian students at the University of Oxford. He wants to hear what they think of Haryana, and whether they see a place for themselves in its growth. The meeting is one of the more unusual items on the agenda for a UK-Germany tour that begins on 28 November and ends on 5 December. Saini will lead the delegation. Industries and Commerce Minister Rao Narbir Singh and senior officers of the department will travel with him. During the UK leg of the tour, CM Saini and team plan to pitch cooperation in education. At Cambridge, the chief minister will interact with representatives of the Centre for Science and Policy. He will also visit Queen Elizabeth’s School in Barnet, where the talks will be about cooperation in education and the possibility of setting up an educational campus in Haryana. On 30 November and 1 December, Saini will hold one-to-one meetings with representatives of leading companies, industries and educational institutions. Roundtables are also planned on trade and investment under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA). Education, skill development and vocational training will get dedicated sessions. Industries and Commerce Department Commissioner and Secretary Dr Amit Kumar Agrawal told ThePrint that the chief minister would also meet members of the Indian diaspora with roots in Haryana. They will be invited to invest in the state. UK members of Parliament and other prominent figures will be asked to attend the Global Investors Summit that Haryana proposes to hold in April 2027. The delegation will also meet a Confederation of Indian Industry team to discuss investment opportunities in the state. Saini will attend a special International Gita Jayanti Mahotsav in London, which the government says will showcase the heritage of Kurukshetra.

headline: Haryana CM unveils mascot of ‘Khel Mahakumbh Haryana-2026’
content: Chandigarh, Nov 27 (PTI) Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini on Friday unveiled the mascot of ‘Khel Mahakumbh Haryana-2026’ and said 18,000 sportspersons would showcase their talent, skills and sporting spirit across 30 sports disciplines during the state-level sports event. Inspired by the Blackbuck, the state animal of Haryana, the mascot symbolises the state’s identity and cultural heritage, as well as the agility, alertness, balance and unwavering commitment of Haryana’s sportspersons to achieving their goals, Saini said. On the occasion, former Indian hockey captain Sardar Singh, Asian Games medallist Parveen Hooda and boxer Narender were also felicitated. Addressing the sportspersons at the event, Saini said that the passion and enthusiasm of Haryana’s sportspersons were the state’s greatest strength. It is a matter of pride that Haryana consistently figures at the top of medal tallies, he said. Congratulating the sportspersons, he said that the Khel Mahakumbh would provide them with a major platform to hone their talent and bring laurels to the state.
