headline: Construction on village pond? NGT seeks Haryana govt reply
content: Gurgaon: National Green Tribunal (NGT) has sought responses from Haryana govt and other respondents over alleged encroachment and construction on a village pond in Rewari.The water body is recorded in official revenue records as a Gair Mumkin talab and johad. The petitioner, Rattan Lal Saini, alleges that private individuals are carrying out construction on the pond land.On Wednesday, a bench headed by NGT chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and expert member Dr Afroz Ahmad observed that the application raises a substantial issue relating to compliance with environmental norms, and issued notices to the respondents.Saini submitted a copy of the jamabandi to establish the land’s recorded status as a water body, along with photographs to support the allegation of illegal construction. He also told the tribunal that complaints had been submitted to various authorities but no action had been taken. A copy of one such complaint was placed on record.Seeking protection of the water body, the applicant relied on two Supreme Court judgments: Hinch Lal Tiwari vs Kamala Devi (2001) and Jagpal Singh vs State of Punjab (2011). Both dealt with the protection of village ponds and common lands against encroachment.The tribunal directed the applicant to serve the respondents and file an affidavit of service at least a week before the next hearing. The matter will be heard on March 5, 2027.Village water bodies serve as traditional water-retention structures and form part of common village resources. Their encroachment can affect local drainage and water conservation.

headline: NEWS RECEIVED FROM SH ANIL VIJ HARYANA MINISTER FOR ENERGY, TRANSPORT AND LABOUR
content: *Vij expresses gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Constitution Day; says the occasion provides an opportunity to reflect on the Constitution’s values, rights and duties* *“The Constitution provides a strong foundation for the country’s unity, integrity and equality. Despite our diversity, India remains united—unity in diversity is our greatest strength”: Anil Vij* *“Democratic rights were curtailed during the Emergency, the press was censored and opposition leaders were jailed”: Anil Vij* *“The Bharat Ratna was conferred on Dr. B.R. Ambedkar by a BJP-supported government, and his portrait was installed in Parliament in 1990”: Vij* *“Haryana’s progress is the result of the collective efforts of hardworking farmers, youth, teachers and an effective governance system”: Vij* Chandigarh, November 26: Haryana Energy, Transport and Labour Minister Sh. Anil Vij said that the essence of the Indian Constitution lies in the words “We, the People of India” and that the ultimate power in a democracy rests with the people. Expressing his gratitude to Prime Minister Sh. Narendra Modi for the initiative to celebrate Constitution Day, Vij said the occasion provides an opportunity to reflect on the values enshrined in the Constitution, as well as the rights and duties of citizens. He said that India, despite being home to people belonging to different religions, castes, languages and cultures, remains united, and that “unity in diversity” is the country's greatest strength. The Constitution has provided a strong foundation for India's unity, integrity and equality. He added that Haryana's development journey, too, is the outcome of the collective efforts of its hardworking farmers, talented youth, teachers and an effective governance system.

headline: IIT Mandi Design Practicum Showcases 75 Student-Built Prototypes With Over 1,200 School Students Witness Innovation In Action.
content: Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, 27th of November 2026 : The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Mandi organised its Design Practicum Open House and Hack for Social Cause (HSC) Project Demonstration on campus, showcasing 75 working prototypes developed by more than 450 second-year BTech students. The event brought together young innovators, industry and domain experts, public officials, and over 1,200 school students from across the region to explore technology-driven solutions to real-world challenges. The projects addressed a wide range of issues in healthcare, education, energy, social development, community awareness, national defence, robotics, artificial intelligence and automation. Developed by interdisciplinary student teams over the semester, the prototypes demonstrated how engineering knowledge can be translated into practical solutions for society. A major highlight of the event was the participation of over 1,200 students from nearby schools. Moving from one demonstration station to another, the young visitors interacted with student teams, learned about the problems behind each innovation and watched the prototypes in action. The experience offered them an inspiring glimpse into engineering, creativity and problem-solving. The projects were evaluated by more than 25 experts representing diverse fields, including officers from the Indian Air Force, doctors from AIIMS Bilaspur, officials from the Election Commission in Mandi, and IIT Mandi faculty members. Their participation brought valuable real-world perspectives to the evaluation process and enabled student teams to receive feedback from professionals with direct experience in the areas their projects seek to address. Several prototypes demonstrated promising potential for commercialisation and startup development. IIT Mandi will extend financial support to selected projects to help teams take their ideas beyond the prototype stage and develop them further. Design Practicum is a core course at IIT Mandi that encourages students to identify real-world problems and develop practical solutions through hands-on engineering and innovation. The initiative aims to nurture an entrepreneurial mindset by providing students with the resources, mentorship and funding needed to transform ideas into viable products and potential businesses.

headline: 6 students suspended for assaulting Class 9 boy at Navodaya Vidyalaya in Reckong Peo
content: Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Reckong Peo, has suspended six students accused of assaulting a Class 9 student after a video of the incident circulated on social media. Kinnaur DC Sonakshi Tomar said the district administration has issued a show-cause notice to the school principal.Tomar said the victim was a Class 9 student, while the six accused students were studying in Classes 9 and 12. After the video emerged, the district administration sent teams from the Education Department and Child Welfare Committee (CWC) to the school for a preliminary inquiry.“A detailed investigation is underway. The victim and his parents are being provided counselling,” she said.Tomar said the role of the school management and the responsibility of teachers and wardens on duty at the time of the incident were also being examined. The inquiry will establish which teachers and wardens were present and the circumstances in which the assault took place.The administration is also investigating how students were allowed to carry mobile phones into the school premises. Some other irregularities have also come to light, including students leaving the school campus without permission. She added that the police have also started investigating the possible reasons behind the assault.The incident came to light when a video of the assault surfaced on social media on Thursday. According to officials, the incident took place around two months ago.

headline: Two bears trapped in water tank rescued in Shimla’s Rampur
content: Two adult bears, which accidentally fell into an empty water tank at Gaura panchayat in the Rampur subdivision of Shimla district, were rescued by the Forest Department on Thursday evening. The bears remained trapped in the tank throughout the day, repeatedly attempting to climb out but failing because of its height.A team from the Forest Department's Rapid Rescue Team reached the spot after receiving information about the incident. However, officials decided against carrying out the rescue during the day as the area witnesses considerable public movement.“To avoid an accidental encounter between the bears and schoolchildren, farmers and others in the area once the animals got out, the rescue was delayed until evening, when human movement decreases,” said an official who was part of the rescue team. Before starting the rescue operation late in the evening, the team made announcements over loudspeakers, asking everyone to stay indoors.A ladder was then placed inside the tank to help the animals climb out. Both bears managed to get out safely and ran towards the nearby forest. The operation lasted around 40 minutes.“Once the bears got out of the tank, we burst crackers and sounded sirens to scare them away so that they would not venture out of the forest again,” the official said.Bear sightings have become increasingly common in the Rampur subdivision. In the recent past, as many as four incidents of bear attacks on humans have been reported from the subdivision.

headline: Delhi govt notifies dates of Census to be held next year
content: New Delhi, Nov 27 (PTI) Delhi government has notified January 25-February 28, 2027 as Census dates for population enumeration in the national capital, officials said on Friday. Earlier, the Ministry of Home Affairs in a notification on October 28, notified the dates of population Census in the country, barring Manipur, Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, the Union territories of Ladakh and Jammu and Kashmir and the snow-bound, non-synchronous areas of Himachal Pradesh. According to a recently-published Revenue department notification, in pursuance of the MHA notification, Census will be conducted from January 25, 2027 to February 28, 2027 with a revisional round to be held from March 1, 2027 to March 5, 2027. The option of self-enumeration will be available from January 10 to January 24, ahead of house to house population enumeration. The reference date for the census will be 00:00 hours of the first day of March, 2027, it said. The first phase of the census exercise in Delhi concluded in June this year, covering nearly 76 lakh houses and around 55 lakh households.

headline: Patients’ details to be accessible at single click as Himachal moves to implement HMIS
content: Shimla, Nov 27 (PTI) Doctors will soon have access to patients’ complete medical reports at the click of a button, streamlining treatment and improving healthcare delivery as the Himachal Pradesh government is set to implement the Hospital Management Information System (HMIS) in various health institutions across the state. This system aims to enhance efficiency, transparency and accountability in hospital administration and healthcare delivery. It will facilitate digitisation and effective management of patient records, hospital-related information, data entry, report generation and other essential institutional processes, a statement issued here on Friday said. To ensure the effective implementation of HMIS across the state, the government is deploying trained data entry operators and the necessary manpower. This will ensure timely entry, maintenance and updating of information, enabling health institutions to make better use of digital technology and improve patient care. In this direction, the state government has approved the engagement of 661 data entry operators/junior office assistants (IT) for the implementation and smooth functioning of HMIS. The government will fill up 561 posts of junior office assistants (IT)/data entry operators in the Directorate of Medical Education and various government medical colleges across the state. These personnel will support various technology-driven administrative and institutional activities, including operation of e-office, e-governance, online correspondence, HMIS operations, data management, report and return preparation, government portals, e-salary-related tasks, online recruitment and establishment matters, and procurement through the government e-marketplace (GeM).

headline: Himachal BJP demands re-exam after Sikh youth barred from patwari exam over kara, kirpan
content: Nahan The Himachal Pradesh unit of the BJP on Friday (November 27, 2026) demanded a re-examination for the patwari post exclusively for an Amritdhari (baptised) Sikh candidate who was allegedly barred from appearing in the exam over his kara and kirpan. Addressing the media in Poanta Sahib in Sirmaur district, State BJP Minority Morcha chief Gurmeet Singh sought an explanation from the Congress government over the incident at the ‘Devbhoomi Online Examination Centre’ in Solan. He demanded that the State government conduct an inquiry, hold a special patwari (revenue official) examination for the affected candidate, and amend the examination guidelines so that no candidate is deprived of taking an exam because of their religious beliefs. Mr. Gurmeet Singh said the matter concerned not only the future of a student but also his religious freedom and constitutional rights. He said he had spoken to the candidate, who told him he had been asked to remove his kara (iron/steel bangle) and kirpan (ceremonial sword). The Sikh youth told him that the examination centre operator cited “government instructions” for disallowing those articles, but when asked for the relevant notification, the authorities failed to provide a copy, he said. The candidate’s father, Vichitra Singh, who was also present at the press conference, demanded that the government clarify the specific order under which the candidate was barred from the examination. Mr. Gurmeet Singh said a father invests his hard-earned money in his child’s education, dreaming of a bright future for him, and being barred from the examination had come as a severe blow to the family. Referring to Article 25 of the Constitution, which guarantees the right to religious freedom, he said carrying a kirpan is an integral part of the Sikh faith, and that while establishing security protocols for examinations, constitutional rights and religious beliefs must be respected. He also raised concerns about alleged restrictions on mangalsutras (sacred necklaces) and bangles worn by women under the examination guidelines, and urged the government to review directives that interfere with religious and cultural practices. The patwari recruitment examinations began on November 23, 2026, and are scheduled to conclude on November 30, 2026.

headline: Education & Skilling Conclave 2026 Emphasises Industry–Academia Partnership for a Future-Ready Workforce
content: Chandigarh, November 27, 2026: The Chandigarh Skill Development Mission (CSDM), in collaboration with ASSOCHAM Northern Region, organised the Education & Skilling Conclave 2026 at Hotel Taj, Chandigarh. Shri Gulab Chand Kataria, Governor of Punjab and Administrator, UT Chandigarh, graced the occasion as the Chief Guest. The conclave brought together policymakers, industry leaders, academicians and skill development experts to deliberate on emerging trends in education, technology and industry-linked skilling. Education and skilling have also been identified as a priority area for this year’s 6th Chief Secretaries’ Conference, underscoring the need for a coordinated approach among the Centre, States, industry and educational institutions to prepare a workforce equipped with emerging skills and competencies. Addressing the gathering, Shri Kataria emphasised that skilling is essential to prepare youth for the challenges and opportunities of a rapidly evolving economy. He highlighted the significant role of industry in strengthening the skills ecosystem through industry-oriented training and closer collaboration with educational institutions. He called for concerted efforts by Government, industry and academia to equip youth with relevant skills and enhance their employability. The thematic sessions explored the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence and digital learning, emerging technologies, advanced manufacturing, green skills and sustainable MSME growth. Discussions also focused on digital transformation to enhance MSME competitiveness and strengthen linkages between education, industry and employment. Dr. Palika Arora, PCS, Mission Director, Chandigarh Skill Development Mission, highlighted the Chandigarh Administration’s commitment to building a skilled and industry-ready workforce in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. She emphasised the need for greater industry participation in curriculum development, practical training, internships, apprenticeships and research.

headline: Parents’ Group Calls for PM’s Direct Intervention to Tackle Delhi-NCR’s Year-Round Air Pollution
content: New Delhi: A parent-led citizens’ collective has demanded a coordinated mechanism involving Centre and govts of Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, with regular reviews led by Prime Minister to ensure accountability and effective enforcement to control air pollution.Arguing that air pollution has worsened over the past decade despite repeated govt interventions, Parents and People Against Pollution (PPAP) called for urgent intervention by Prime Minister to address what it described as a year-round public health emergency in Delhi-NCR.PPAP said the problem could no longer be addressed through seasonal or emergency measures alone. It called for tough policy decisions, strict implementation of existing laws and visible improvement in air quality within the next year.Among its key proposals is a permanent, year-round ban on firecrackers across Delhi-NCR, covering their manufacture, sale, storage, distribution and use. The group also called for a fundamental overhaul of the city’s transport policy, shifting the focus from private vehicles to an extensive, reliable and affordable public transport network, including 16,000-20,000 buses, better last-mile connectivity and a revival of Delhi Ring Railway.Calling for stronger enforcement, PPAP sought the filling of vacancies in Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) and the deployment of 24-hour rapid response teams comprising pollution control officials, police personnel and elected representatives to identify and address violations on the ground.The group also proposed changing the way air quality is communicated to citizens, replacing the existing AQI descriptions such as poor, very poor and severe with more health-oriented categories such as unhealthy, very unhealthy and hazardous.Other recommendations include stricter monitoring of construction and road dust, honest environmental impact assessments of infrastructure projects, better waste segregation and management, monitoring of pollution from thermal power plants and aviation, and a scientific approach to protecting and expanding Delhi-NCR’s tree cover.Highlighting the gap between India’s National Ambient Air Quality Standards and World Health Organization guidelines, the collective pointed out that India’s annual PM2.5 limit is 40 micrograms per cubic metre, compared with the WHO guideline of 5 micrograms. For PM10, the corresponding limits are 60 and 15 micrograms.Emphasising that the right to clean air is part of the fundamental right to life, PPAP appealed to citizens across Delhi-NCR to write to Prime Minister through letters, postcards and emails, urging his direct intervention.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. headline: Delhi: Civil defence volunteers, multiple agencies participate in air raid mock drills
content: New Delhi, Nov 27 (PTI) Civil defence volunteers participated in a large-scale mock drill on Friday, showcasing their training and preparedness for simulated emergency scenarios such as air raids, fires, and building collapses at various locations across the national capital. In the New Delhi district, a mock drill for an air raid was conducted at Dhaulakuan Metro station, where civil defence volunteers (CDVs) followed standard operating procedures that began with the sound of an air raid siren and a blackout, according to officials. The drills took place at select venues in 13 districts by the Civil Defence Directorate of the Delhi government. Delhi Police, Delhi Disaster Management Authority, Fire Service, Revenue Department and other agencies concerned also took part in the drills. The drills were conducted at several locations, including a hospital in southeast Delhi, an apartment building in Dwarka, an interstate bus terminal, a DTC depot in North East Delhi, a mall in West Delhi, Gaffar Market in Karol Bagh, among others. Similar mock drills were held in the national capital in May last year, in the backdrop of ‘Operation Sindoor’ which targeted terror camps in Pakistan. Officials stated that the current mock drill was part of a civil defence training and preparedness programme led by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) across various states and Union Territories.

headline: Fake job offers, seized passports, threats: Inside Delhi's international human trafficking and cyber fraud racket
content: New Delhi Lured to India with promises of lucrative jobs, 164 foreign nationals from Indonesia and Malaysia allegedly found themselves trapped in a network of human trafficking and cybercrooks, with their passports seized upon arrival, movement restricted and lives reduced to making fraudulent calls to people back home, Delhi Police said on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Kept in paying guest (PG) accommodations, allegedly served substandard food and subjected to physical assault if they refused to work, the foreign nationals were forced to follow written scripts to cheat unsuspecting people in their own countries through fraudulent investment platforms, police said. Delhi Police arrests 10 more suspects linked with interstate child-trafficking racket Delhi Police arrests 10 more suspects linked with interstate child-trafficking racket Police said the fresh arrests exposed an organised network that allegedly procured infants from biological parents and sold them to childless couples for several lakhs in multiple States. Delhi Police arrests 10 more suspects linked with interstate child-trafficking racket storyline 1 In a major crackdown in southwest Delhi's Dwarka on an alleged international human trafficking and cyber fraud network, the Crime Branch of Delhi Police has rescued 164 foreign nationals, including 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians, from premises allegedly being used to operate the racket. A 25-year-old Malaysian national, identified as Tan Guan Wei, has been arrested in connection with the case. According to police, the network specifically targeted people in Indonesia and Malaysia by offering them employment opportunities in India, promising attractive salaries and better career prospects. However, their ordeal allegedly began soon after they landed in the country. Their passports were taken away upon arrival, leaving them without control over their identity documents and restricting their ability to leave, police said. They were subsequently shifted to PG accommodations and allegedly forced to work to cheat others. Those who resisted or refused to participate in the fraudulent activities were allegedly thrashed by members of the network to ensure compliance, a senior police officer said, adding that so far they got to know that around two people were thrashed. The living conditions at the accommodations were also allegedly poor, with the foreign nationals being provided substandard food. Despite a fleet of around 40 cabs being used to ferry them between the PG accommodations and the cyber fraud call centre, they were not allowed to venture out independently or move around as they wished, the officer said. "The cabs were allegedly deployed to transport them to the call centre and bring them back to their accommodations, ensuring that their movement remained under the control of the handlers," the officer said. The foreign nationals were not merely made to operate computers and mobile phones but were allegedly trained to execute a specific pattern of cyber fraud. They were provided written scripts containing conversations that they had to follow while approaching prospective victims. The targets were primarily people in Malaysia and Indonesia. The operators allegedly created fictitious female identities and social media profiles to establish contact with unsuspecting individuals. "Using these profiles, the foreign nationals were instructed to initiate conversations, develop online relationships and gradually gain the confidence of their targets. Once trust was established, the victims were persuaded to invest money through fraudulent trading and investment platforms," the officer added. The syndicate allegedly used websites and APK-based applications to lure people with promises of high returns. The victims were made to believe that they were investing in legitimate financial opportunities, while the money was allegedly siphoned off through the fraudulent network. "We got to know about the fraud after the crime branch received an email alert about the alleged racket around a week ago, following which its officers began developing intelligence about the network," the officer said. Special Commissioner of Police (Crime Branch) HGS Dhaliwal said, "As soon as we received information about the cyber racket, I personally constituted a specialised team and directed the officers to take immediate action." Initial information suggested that around 60 to 70 foreign nationals were being held and forced to work in the cyber fraud operation. However, when the police team conducted the operation at the suspected premises, the actual number turned out to be significantly higher. The operation led to the rescue of 164 foreign nationals, exposing the scale of the alleged racket. The police are now investigating how the foreign nationals were recruited, who facilitated their travel to India, and how their passports were taken away. "During the entire investigation, two names, Sunil Kumar and Sushil Bhati, cropped up. Bhati used to arrange the PG accommodations and transportation facilities. Both are absconding, both will be arrested soon," the officer said. Certain bank accounts allegedly maintained by Kumar and Bhati have been identified as being used to meet rental and other operational expenses of the network. The financial trail is being examined to establish the flow of money, identify the beneficiaries and trace the proceeds generated through the alleged cyber fraud. The arrested Malaysian national, Tan Guan Wei, a resident of Negeri Sembilan, is being questioned about his alleged role in the network, his association with other members and the extent of his involvement in operating the fraudulent platforms. The police have seized a substantial digital infrastructure allegedly used to run the operation. The recoveries include 355 mobile phones, 168 desktop computers, 26 laptops, 53 SIM cards and 174 passports. Of the 355 mobile phones, 335 were old or used handsets and 20 were new phones in sealed packaging. The 53 SIM cards include 31 international and 22 Indian connections. The recovered passports comprise 95 Indonesian and 79 Malaysian documents. Servers and other electronic material have also been seized. Investigators are examining the devices to identify the victims, establish the communication channels used by the syndicate and trace financial transactions linked to the fraudulent platforms. Special CP Dhaliwal further said the conditions in which the foreign nationals were being held were deplorable. Praising the team for its work, Mr. Dhaliwal added, "Our team has done a commendable job in this case. We will extend all possible assistance to the rescued foreigners and ensure that they can return to their respective countries safely." A case has been registered at the Crime Branch police station under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Further investigation is underway to identify other members of the international network and establish the extent of the alleged human trafficking and cyber fraud operation.

headline: 'My father has passed away': Passenger pleads with SpiceJet staff amid flight delay, video goes viral
content: A prolonged SpiceJet flight delay left a grieving passenger pleading with airline staff at an airport as he struggled to reach home in time for his father's last rites.A video of the incident, shared by Yash Dabas, president of the Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU), showed the distressed passenger asking ground staff for help while other travellers waited amid the disruption.In the video, Yash was seen confronting SpiceJet employees as a crowd gathered at the airport. Pointing towards the flight information display, he said, “You can see that the flight to Patna is supposed to depart from gate number 34, but boarding hasn’t started yet.”As the passenger broke down, Yash questioned the airline's handling of the delay.“Ek beta apne baap ke antim sanskaar pe nahi pahunch paa raha hai, kyun itna bada paap le rahe ho (A son is unable to reach his father's funeral. Why are you committing such a grave sin)?” he told the ground staff.He also questioned why the airline continued accepting bookings if it allegedly lacked the resources to operate flights as scheduled.“Jab aapke paas sansadhan nahi hai, toh phir booking kyun le rahe ho (If you don't have the resources, why are you accepting bookings)?”Meanwhile, the passenger was seen showing a video on his phone and pleading with the airline staff for assistance.“Mere papa ki death ho gayi hai. Humko pohacha dijiye (My father has passed away. Please get me there).”Yash Dabas criticises SpiceJet over passenger's ordealSharing the video on social media, Yash criticised SpiceJet over the distress caused to passengers and called for accountability from the airline.“Shame on you for putting passengers through such distress. A grieving son, trying to reach home after his father’s demise, was left struggling amid prolonged flight delays. Take responsibility. Show some accountability and compassion,” he wrote, tagging the airline.Watch the viral video here:SpiceJet faces operational and financial challengesThe latest incident comes amid a series of disruptions affecting SpiceJet's operations. Earlier this month, chaos erupted at Delhi airport after a SpiceJet flight scheduled to operate from Delhi to Mumbai on November 19 was delayed for hours before being cancelled, according to India Today.The disruption led to confrontations between frustrated passengers and airline employees as travellers demanded answers.The airline's operational difficulties have also raised concerns about its ability to maintain services. SpiceJet's crisis has reached a critical point, with the cash-strapped carrier left with just five operational aircraft against a fleet of nearly 50 on paper, Business Today reported.On November 22, the Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) urged the government to intervene urgently in the airline's ongoing financial and operational crisis, warning of potential implications for aviation safety.

headline: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta flags off interstate bus services to Bihar on 18 routes
content: New Delhi, Nov 27 (PTI) Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Friday flagged off interstate bus services between Delhi and Bihar under an MoU signed by the two sides, covering 18 routes to destinations across Bihar. The initiative aims to ease travel between the two states, particularly during festivals when many Bihar residents living in Delhi travel to their native places, putting pressure on existing transport services, including trains and private buses, officials said. Gupta said the buses would ply on 18 identified routes connecting Delhi with various cities in Bihar, which would be gradually increased as per requirements. The 18 destinations in Bihar include Patna, Araria, Bhagalpur, Buxar, Darbhanga, East Champaran, Gaya, Kishanganj, Madhubani, Muzaffarpur, Nawada and Purnia, among others. “Under the MoU, the Delhi government’s transport department has issued 216 permits to Bihar for operating buses on 18 routes connecting the capital with various cities there,” Gupta said. The agreement reflected the growing cooperation between the two states and would benefit lakhs of people from Bihar who live and work in the capital, including students, she said.

headline: This Delhi startup lets people plan their own funerals while alive; packages range from  ₹29,999 to  ₹1.5 lakh
content: A Delhi-based startup is giving people the option to plan their own funerals while they are still alive. Moksha Voyage, a professional last rites service provider, helps individuals and families with funeral arrangements, transportation, logistics and post-funeral rituals. The company describes its services as “compassionate and professional assistance for last rites, funeral logistics and related services”, according to its website. Currently operating across Delhi NCR, including Ghaziabad, the startup offers comprehensive funeral arrangements, from dignified transportation to conducting Antim Sanskar in accordance with an individual's traditions and preferences. Its services cover several aspects of the last rites, including transportation, mortuary and preservation facilities, cremation and Antim Sanskar, Asthi Sanchayan (collection of ashes), Asthi Visarjan (immersion of ashes) and other associated rituals.An initiative of Namo Gange Wellness, Moksha Voyage also helps families organise post-funeral ceremonies, including Tehravin and Pind Daan.What funeral packages does Moksha Voyage offer?The company has introduced three funeral service packages, each designed to cover different stages of the last rites and the ceremonies that follow.The entry-level package, Samman Sewa, offers “cremation day sewa support”. It covers coordination and guidance for family members, a pandit to perform rituals at home and at the crematorium, pooja samagri and assistance with the necessary documentation.The second package, Shraddha Sewa, covers the period from “cremation day to Asthi Visarjan”, which generally takes between one and three days. Along with all the services included in Samman Sewa, this package provides arrangements for Asthi Sanchayan and Asthi Visarjan. These include a vehicle, a pandit, a kalash and the required documentation.The most extensive package is Moksha Sankalp Sewa. It provides assistance to the family throughout the 13 days following a person's death. The package also covers Brahmin Bhoj and travel arrangements to Haridwar for the immersion of ashes.According to a report by Jagran, the funeral packages are priced between ₹29,999 and ₹1.5 lakh. Samman Sewa, the basic package, costs ₹29,999, while the comprehensive Moksha Sankalp Sewa package is priced at ₹1.5 lakh. How can people plan their own funerals in advance? Beyond organising last rites after a person's death, Moksha Voyage also allows individuals to communicate and document their funeral preferences while they are alive. “Your preferences are clearly understood and documented,” the company states on its website. According to the company, planning funeral arrangements in advance offers several benefits, including financial clarity, less stress for family members and the assurance that the final rites will be performed in accordance with an individual's wishes. The initiative aims to help people make these decisions beforehand, rather than leaving their families to deal with funeral arrangements, expenses and logistical challenges during an emotionally difficult period. What is Moksha Voyage's free funeral service initiative? Alongside its paid packages, Moksha Voyage runs a programme called Moksha Sewa, which provides funeral assistance to economically disadvantaged families, as well as abandoned and destitute individuals. The company says it offers these services free of cost to ensure that everyone receives a dignified final farewell, regardless of their financial circumstances or support system. Vijay Sharma, chairman of Moksha Sewa, said: “Moksha Sewa is a humble step towards a more compassionate society, where every life – known or unknown, supported or unsupported – receives a dignified final journey.” Actress and Bigg Boss 19 contestant Tanya Mittal, who is also a member of the Moksha Sewa board, said she was “honoured” to be associated with the initiative. “Every individual deserves respect and a dignified final journey. I encourage more people and organisations to come forward and support this noble cause, so that together we can build a kinder, more compassionate society,” she said.

headline: Delhi HC asks Satyendar Jain to respond to ACB’s plea challenging bail in corruption case
content: New Delhi, Nov 27 (PTI) The Delhi High Court on Friday sought AAP leader Satyendar Jain’s response on a plea by the Anti-Corruption Branch challenging an order granting him bail in a corruption case involving the Delhi Jal Board. Justice Sachin Datta issued notice to Jain on the petition by the Delhi government’s ACB and listed the matter for further hearing on December 22. The ACB has challenged the trial court’s September 3 order granting bail to the former Delhi minister saying the evidence before it is “prima facie insufficient” to deny the relief. The trial court had pulled up the ACB saying that “a sudden arrest at the tail end of the investigation, without strong reasons and without a change in circumstances, tends to invite criticism that it is arbitrary”. During the hearing on Friday, the ACB’s counsel submitted that the trial court’s bail order was in the nature of discharging the accused and several observations were made by the special judge even when the investigation was going on and charge sheet was yet to be filed. Jain was arrested in the case on August 18 and remanded in judicial custody on August 19.

headline: Delhi govt opens Kejriwal’s former residence as ‘Sheesh Mahal’ row returns to focus | India News
content: The Delhi government on Friday opened the former official residence of Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convener and former chief minister Arvind Kejriwal at 6 Flagstaff Road to the media.The chief ministerial bungalow, which the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) calls “Sheesh Mahal”, has been a political flashpoint over allegations of excessive expenditure on its renovation.Visuals showed purported price tags on several items inside the bungalow, including a centre table, television, sofa and powder room fittings. The residence will soon be opened to the public, people aware of the matter said. The bungalow became a major political issue ahead of the February 2025 Delhi assembly elections, with the BJP repeatedly accusing the then AAP government of spending public money on lavish renovations of the chief minister’s residence. Kejriwal and his family lived in the bungalow for nearly a decade, from 2015 until October 2024. The controversy gained fresh traction after a Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) report, tabled in the Delhi Assembly in March this year, pegged the expenditure on renovation and construction at ₹33.66 crore, against an initial preliminary estimate of ₹7.91 crore.The BJP has cited the audit findings to accuse the previous AAP government of irregularities in the renovation. AAP, however, rejected the allegations, describing them as baseless and politically motivated.
